FJ3176.name: Atlas
FJ3176.details: First cervical vertebra; ring-shaped, lacking body and spinous process; lateral masses carry occipital condyles above and axis below; vertebral artery grooves its posterior arch.
FJ3176.clinicalCondition: Jefferson burst fracture — axial load through the skull splits the ring, displacing lateral masses outward.
FJ3176.clinicalScenario: A 22-year-old dives into shallow water and strikes his head; he has severe neck pain and CT shows a four-part burst fracture of C1.

FJ3177.name: Axis
FJ3177.details: Second cervical vertebra; its odontoid process (dens) projects upward and is held against the atlas by the transverse ligament, forming the pivot for head rotation.
FJ3177.clinicalCondition: Odontoid fracture — elderly falls; type II fractures risk nonunion and spinal cord injury.
FJ3177.clinicalScenario: An 82-year-old woman falls face-first at home; CT reveals a type II dens fracture and she is fitted with a rigid cervical collar.

FJ3178.name: Body of sternum
FJ3178.details: Flat central segment of the sternum between manubrium and xiphoid process; articulates with costal cartilages two to seven; overlies the heart and great vessels.
FJ3178.clinicalCondition: Sternal fracture — blunt steering-wheel trauma; a marker for underlying cardiac and pulmonary contusion.
FJ3178.clinicalScenario: A driver whose chest struck the steering wheel has midsternal bruising and pain; CT shows a transverse sternal fracture and troponin is checked.

FJ2440.name: Cricoid cartilage
FJ2440.details: Signet-ring-shaped hyaline cartilage of the larynx at C6 level; the only complete ring of the airway; connected above to thyroid cartilage by cricothyroid membrane.
FJ2440.clinicalCondition: Post-intubation subglottic stenosis — pressure injury at this narrow, rigid ring scars and narrows the airway.
FJ2440.clinicalScenario: A child extubated after prolonged ventilation develops progressive stridor; endoscopy shows subglottic narrowing precisely at the cricoid level.

FJ2769.name: Cricoid cartilage
FJ2769.details: Surface landmark at C6: here pharynx becomes esophagus and larynx becomes trachea; the carotid pulse is palpated against the adjacent transverse process of C6.
FJ2769.clinicalCondition: Cricoid pressure (Sellick maneuver) — compresses the esophagus during rapid-sequence induction, reducing aspiration risk.
FJ2769.clinicalScenario: During emergency intubation of a vomiting trauma patient, an assistant applies firm cricoid pressure while the anesthetist secures the airway with a cuffed tube.

FJ3182.name: Distal phalanx of left big toe
FJ3182.details: Terminal bone of the hallux; supports nail and pulp; flexor and extensor hallucis longus tendons insert around its base, aiding balance and push-off.
FJ3182.clinicalCondition: Tuft fracture with subungual hematoma — crush injury traps painful blood beneath the nail.
FJ3182.clinicalScenario: A warehouse worker drops a crate on his left foot; X-ray shows a tuft fracture of the great toe with a tense subungual hematoma.

FJ3181.name: Distal phalanx of left fourth toe
FJ3181.details: Small terminal bone of the fourth toe; flexor digitorum longus inserts on its plantar base; protected dorsally by the nail.
FJ3181.clinicalCondition: Stubbing fracture — axial impact against furniture commonly fractures lesser-toe phalanges.
FJ3181.clinicalScenario: A woman catches her left fourth toe on a bedpost at night; she has swelling and X-ray confirms a distal phalanx fracture treated by buddy taping.

FJ3183.name: Distal phalanx of left index finger
FJ3183.details: Terminal bone of the index finger; flexor digitorum profundus inserts on its palmar base and the extensor expansion dorsally, balancing fingertip motion for pinch.
FJ3183.clinicalCondition: Mallet finger — extensor tendon avulsion here leaves the fingertip drooping, unable to extend.
FJ3183.clinicalScenario: A cricketer struck on the left index fingertip by a ball cannot straighten the tip; a mallet splint is applied in extension for six weeks.

FJ3184.name: Distal phalanx of left little finger
FJ3184.details: Smallest terminal finger bone; profundus tendon inserts on its palmar base; the ulnar digits contribute most to power grip strength.
FJ3184.clinicalCondition: Jersey finger — forced extension avulses flexor digitorum profundus from this phalanx.
FJ3184.clinicalScenario: A rugby player's left little finger is caught in an opponent's jersey; he cannot flex the fingertip and is referred urgently for tendon repair.

FJ3185.name: Distal phalanx of left little toe
FJ3185.details: Tiny terminal bone of the fifth toe, often partly fused with the middle phalanx; bears little weight during gait.
FJ3185.clinicalCondition: Fifth-toe phalanx fracture — the commonest toe fracture, usually from stubbing, needing only buddy strapping.
FJ3185.clinicalScenario: A barefoot teenager stubs her left little toe on a door frame; X-ray shows a nondisplaced distal phalanx fracture managed conservatively.

FJ3186.name: Distal phalanx of left middle finger
FJ3186.details: Terminal bone of the longest digit; profundus and extensor insertions balance fingertip flexion and extension; its pulp is richly supplied with sensory receptors.
FJ3186.clinicalCondition: Subungual hematoma — a trapped fingertip causes throbbing pain relieved by nail trephination.
FJ3186.clinicalScenario: A carpenter slams his left middle finger in a car door; a tense blood collection under the nail is drained by trephination with instant relief.

FJ3187.name: Distal phalanx of left ring finger
FJ3187.details: Terminal bone of the ring digit; profundus inserts on the palmar base while the nail complex protects the spongy tuft dorsally.
FJ3187.clinicalCondition: Tuft fracture — crush mechanisms comminute the distal tuft, often with nail-bed laceration.
FJ3187.clinicalScenario: A mechanic crushes his left ring fingertip under machinery; imaging shows a comminuted tuft fracture and the torn nail bed is repaired under ring block.

FJ3179.name: Distal phalanx of left second toe
FJ3179.details: Terminal bone of the second toe, the longest toe in many people (Morton's toe); flexor digitorum longus inserts on its plantar surface.
FJ3179.clinicalCondition: Hammer toe — interphalangeal flexion contracture overloads this segment, producing painful dorsal corns.
FJ3179.clinicalScenario: A woman with a long second toe develops painful corns over the left foot and is fitted with orthotics for an established hammer toe deformity.

FJ3180.name: Distal phalanx of left third toe
FJ3180.details: Terminal bone of the middle toe; with its neighbors it spreads forefoot load and assists balance during push-off.
FJ3180.clinicalCondition: Stress injury — repetitive loading in runners and dancers can produce a phalangeal stress reaction.
FJ3180.clinicalScenario: A ballet dancer reports three weeks of aching left third-toe pain; MRI reveals a stress reaction of the distal phalanx and she is rested from pointe work.

FJ3188.name: Distal phalanx of left thumb
FJ3188.details: Stout terminal thumb bone; flexor pollicis longus inserts palmarly and extensor pollicis longus dorsally; essential for pinch, grip, and opposition.
FJ3188.clinicalCondition: Tuft fracture with nail-bed injury — crush impact is the commonest mechanism in manual workers.
FJ3188.clinicalScenario: A joiner strikes his left thumb with a hammer; X-ray shows a tuft fracture and the lacerated nail bed is sutured after removing the nail.

FJ3192.name: Distal phalanx of right big toe
FJ3192.details: Terminal bone of the right hallux; supports the nail and pulp and anchors the hallucis longus tendons; receives much of forefoot load at push-off.
FJ3192.clinicalCondition: Ingrown toenail (onychocryptosis) — the nail edge penetrates periungual tissue over this bone, causing infection.
FJ3192.clinicalScenario: A teenager has a red, swollen right great-toe edge with pus; partial nail avulsion is performed for a recurrent ingrown toenail.

FJ3191.name: Distal phalanx of right fourth toe
FJ3191.details: Terminal bone of the right fourth toe; flexor digitorum longus inserts on its plantar base; capped by the toenail.
FJ3191.clinicalCondition: Mallet toe — flexion deformity at the distal interphalangeal joint makes the toe tip bear weight painfully.
FJ3191.clinicalScenario: An elderly man develops a downward-curling right fourth toe that rubs in shoes; podiatry confirms mallet toe and debrides a painful tip callus.

FJ3193.name: Distal phalanx of right index finger
FJ3193.details: Terminal bone of the right index finger; profundus inserts palmarly; its pulp works with the thumb in precision pinch and fine manipulation.
FJ3193.clinicalCondition: Felon — closed pulp-space infection causes tense, throbbing fingertip pain and abscess.
FJ3193.clinicalScenario: A gardener develops an exquisitely tender, swollen right index fingertip after a thorn prick; incision and drainage releases a felon abscess.

FJ3194.name: Distal phalanx of right little finger
FJ3194.details: Terminal bone of the right fifth digit; profundus insertion on its palmar base; ulnar-sided digit vital for cupping and power grip.
FJ3194.clinicalCondition: Mallet finger — sudden forced flexion avulses the extensor insertion, drooping the tip.
FJ3194.clinicalScenario: A volleyball player jammed her right little finger on the ball; the tip droops and she is splinted continuously in extension.

FJ3195.name: Distal phalanx of right little toe
FJ3195.details: Tiny terminal bone of the right fifth toe; frequently fused with the middle phalanx as a normal variant; minimal load-bearing role.
FJ3195.clinicalCondition: Stubbing fracture — painful but benign; displaced fractures are rare and surgery almost never needed.
FJ3195.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman trips barefoot and fractures her right little toe's distal phalanx; buddy taping and stiff shoes relieve her pain within weeks.

FJ3196.name: Distal phalanx of right middle finger
FJ3196.details: Terminal bone of the right middle finger, the hand's central axis digit; balanced by profundus and extensor tendon insertions at its base.
FJ3196.clinicalCondition: Mallet (baseball) finger — a ball striking the fingertip avulses the extensor tendon here.
FJ3196.clinicalScenario: A baseball fielder misjudges a catch and the right middle fingertip droops; radiographs exclude a bony avulsion and a stack splint is fitted.

FJ3197.name: Distal phalanx of right ring finger
FJ3197.details: Terminal bone of the right ring digit; the ring finger's profundus is the one most commonly avulsed in grabbing injuries.
FJ3197.clinicalCondition: Jersey finger — profundus avulsion from this phalanx, classically affecting the ring finger.
FJ3197.clinicalScenario: A football player grabbing a jersey feels a pop in his right ring finger; he cannot flex the tip and undergoes flexor tendon reinsertion.

FJ3189.name: Distal phalanx of right second toe
FJ3189.details: Terminal bone of the right second toe; flexor digitorum longus inserts beneath; toe length often exceeds the hallux.
FJ3189.clinicalCondition: Heloma (corn) formation — chronic shoe pressure over this segment produces painful keratotic lesions.
FJ3189.clinicalScenario: A saleswoman on her feet all day develops a hard, painful corn over her right second toe and is advised on footwear and padding.

FJ3190.name: Distal phalanx of right third toe
FJ3190.details: Terminal bone of the right middle toe; shares forefoot load during stance and contributes to balance corrections.
FJ3190.clinicalCondition: Hammer toe deformity — fixed flexion crowds this toe against footwear, causing ulceration in diabetics.
FJ3190.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man is found to have a small ulcer under his right third toe tip from a hammer toe; offloading and vascular review are arranged.

FJ3198.name: Distal phalanx of right thumb
FJ3198.details: Terminal thumb bone; flexor pollicis longus inserts on its palmar base; broad pulp supports strong pinch against the fingers.
FJ3198.clinicalCondition: Subungual hematoma — crush injury raises painful pressure under the thumbnail.
FJ3198.clinicalScenario: A builder traps his right thumb under a paving slab; trephination of the nail releases blood and X-ray excludes a tuft fracture.

FJ3174.name: Eighth thoracic vertebra
FJ3174.details: Typical thoracic vertebra with heart-shaped body, costal facets, and long overlapping spinous process; the T8 level corresponds to the inferior vena cava opening of the diaphragm.
FJ3174.clinicalCondition: Osteoporotic wedge compression fracture — mid-thoracic bodies collapse anteriorly, causing kyphosis and height loss.
FJ3174.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman develops sudden mid-back pain lifting shopping; lateral X-ray shows an anterior wedge compression fracture of the T8 body.

FJ3155.name: Eleventh thoracic vertebra
FJ3155.details: Transitional vertebra near the thoracolumbar junction; bears a single whole costal facet and lacks a transverse-process facet; the junction concentrates mechanical stress.
FJ3155.clinicalCondition: Burst fracture — the thoracolumbar junction is the commonest site for unstable burst fractures.
FJ3155.clinicalScenario: A roofer falls four meters onto his feet; CT shows a burst fracture of T11 with retropulsed fragments narrowing the spinal canal.

FJ3199.name: Ethmoid
FJ3199.details: Light, spongy bone between the orbits; its cribriform plate forms the olfactory roof of the nose, the crista galli anchors the falx cerebri, and its air cells drain into the nasal cavity.
FJ3199.clinicalCondition: CSF rhinorrhea — cribriform plate fracture tears the dura, leaking cerebrospinal fluid through the nose.
FJ3199.clinicalScenario: After a frontal head injury, a man notices clear watery fluid dripping from one nostril; testing for beta-2 transferrin confirms a CSF leak.

FJ3167.name: Fifth cervical vertebra
FJ3167.details: Typical cervical vertebra with bifid spinous process and transverse foramina transmitting the vertebral artery; the C5 root exits above it and supplies deltoid.
FJ3167.clinicalCondition: C5 radiculopathy — disc or foraminal narrowing causes shoulder pain and weak arm abduction.
FJ3167.clinicalScenario: A man has neck pain radiating to the shoulder with weak abduction; MRI shows a C4/C5 foraminal stenosis compressing the C5 root.

FJ3168.name: Fifth lumbar vertebra
FJ3168.details: Largest lumbar vertebra; its broad transverse processes anchor the iliolumbar ligaments to the ilium; the lumbosacral junction bears the greatest spinal load.
FJ3168.clinicalCondition: Spondylolisthesis — L5 slips forward on S1, commonly through bilateral pars defects.
FJ3168.clinicalScenario: A teenage gymnast with chronic low back pain has imaging showing grade I anterolisthesis of L5 over S1 from pars defects.

FJ3169.name: Fifth thoracic vertebra
FJ3169.details: Typical mid-thoracic vertebra; articulates with the fifth rib; the thoracic canal at this level is relatively narrow, leaving little room around the cord.
FJ3169.clinicalCondition: Pott disease (tuberculous spondylitis) — infection destroys thoracic bodies, collapsing them into a kyphotic gibbus.
FJ3169.clinicalScenario: A man with months of thoracic pain, night sweats, and weight loss has MRI showing T5 body destruction and a paravertebral abscess from tuberculosis.

FJ3157.name: First lumbar vertebra
FJ3157.details: First lumbar vertebra, lacking costal facets; the conus medullaris of the spinal cord typically terminates at the L1/L2 level in adults.
FJ3157.clinicalCondition: Burst fracture with conus injury — causes saddle anesthesia, bladder dysfunction, and mixed leg signs.
FJ3157.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist with an L1 burst fracture develops urinary retention and saddle numbness, indicating a conus medullaris injury requiring urgent neurosurgery.

FJ3158.name: First thoracic vertebra
FJ3158.details: Transitional cervicothoracic vertebra with a complete costal facet for the first rib; the stellate ganglion lies just anterior, near the neck of the first rib.
FJ3158.clinicalCondition: Pancoast tumor invasion — apical lung cancers invade this level, injuring the T1 root and sympathetic chain.
FJ3158.clinicalScenario: A smoker presents with shoulder pain radiating down the inner arm and a drooping eyelid; imaging shows an apical lung tumor invading the T1 region.

FJ3164.name: Fourth cervical vertebra
FJ3164.details: Typical cervical vertebra; the C4 segment contributes to the phrenic nerve (C3–C5), and the C4 dermatome caps the shoulder region.
FJ3164.clinicalCondition: High cervical cord injury — lesions around C4 threaten diaphragmatic function and spontaneous ventilation.
FJ3164.clinicalScenario: A diver with a fracture-dislocation at C4 cannot breathe adequately on arrival and requires intubation and ventilatory support in intensive care.

FJ3165.name: Fourth lumbar vertebra
FJ3165.details: Typical lumbar vertebra; a line joining the highest points of the iliac crests (Tuffier's line) crosses its spinous process, guiding lumbar puncture level selection.
FJ3165.clinicalCondition: Lumbar spinal stenosis — degenerative narrowing around L4 causes neurogenic claudication of the legs.
FJ3165.clinicalScenario: An elderly man whose leg pain eases when leaning on a shopping trolley has MRI showing severe stenosis at the L4/L5 level.

FJ3166.name: Fourth thoracic vertebra
FJ3166.details: The T4/T5 disc level corresponds anteriorly to the sternal angle, the surface landmark for the second costal cartilage and approximate tracheal bifurcation level.
FJ3166.clinicalCondition: Metastatic vertebral disease — thoracic bodies are common deposit sites that can compress the cord.
FJ3166.clinicalScenario: A woman treated for breast cancer develops mid-back pain and leg weakness; MRI shows a T4 metastatic deposit compressing the spinal cord.

FJ3200.name: Frontal bone
FJ3200.details: Forms the forehead, floor of the anterior cranial fossa, and orbital roofs; contains the frontal sinuses; meets the parietal bones at the coronal suture.
FJ3200.clinicalCondition: Frontal sinus fracture — posterior-table involvement risks CSF leak, meningitis, and intracranial injury.
FJ3200.clinicalScenario: A cyclist struck on the forehead has CT showing a depressed frontal bone fracture involving the posterior wall of the frontal sinus.

FJ1253.name: Gingiva of lower jaw
FJ1253.details: Fibromucosal tissue covering the mandibular alveolar processes and necks of the lower teeth; attached gingiva is keratinized and firmly bound to periosteum.
FJ1253.clinicalCondition: Drug-induced gingival hyperplasia — phenytoin, ciclosporin, and nifedipine cause firm lower gum overgrowth.
FJ1253.clinicalScenario: A man on long-term phenytoin presents with enlarged lower gums burying the tooth crowns; drug-induced gingival hyperplasia is diagnosed and oral hygiene intensified.

FJ1252.name: Gingiva of upper jaw
FJ1252.details: Mucosa investing the maxillary alveolar ridge and upper tooth necks; continuous medially with the hard-palate mucosa and drained by regional lymphatics.
FJ1252.clinicalCondition: Acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis — painful, punched-out interdental papillae in stressed or immunosuppressed patients.
FJ1252.clinicalScenario: An exhausted student develops painful, bleeding upper gums with foul breath; examination shows necrotic interdental papillae typical of acute necrotizing gingivitis.

FJ2772.name: Hyoid bone
FJ2772.details: U-shaped bone suspended by muscles and ligaments in the anterior neck at C3; the only bone articulating with no other; anchors the tongue musculature.
FJ2772.clinicalCondition: Hyoid fracture — classically associated with manual strangulation; causes pain on swallowing and speaking.
FJ2772.clinicalScenario: An assault survivor has anterior neck pain and painful swallowing; CT of the neck demonstrates a fracture of the greater horn of the hyoid.

FJ3201.name: Hyoid bone
FJ3201.details: Gives attachment to suprahyoid and infrahyoid strap muscles; moves upward during swallowing; its greater horns are palpable on either side of the neck.
FJ3201.clinicalCondition: Thyroglossal duct cyst — the embryological tract passes through the hyoid region, so the Sistrunk operation removes its central portion.
FJ3201.clinicalScenario: A teenager's midline neck lump rises when she protrudes her tongue; the excised specimen includes the central hyoid, confirming a thyroglossal cyst.

FJ3211.name: Intervertebral disk
FJ3211.details: Fibrocartilaginous joint between vertebral bodies: tough outer anulus fibrosus surrounds the gelatinous nucleus pulposus; provides spinal flexibility and shock absorption.
FJ3211.clinicalCondition: Disc prolapse — nucleus herniates through a torn anulus and compresses adjacent nerve roots.
FJ3211.clinicalScenario: A warehouse worker lifts a heavy box and feels back pain shooting down his leg; MRI confirms a posterolateral lumbar disc prolapse.

FJ3202.name: Intervertebral disk of axis
FJ3202.details: The C2/C3 disc below the axis is the first true intervertebral disc of the spine (none exists between atlas and axis); it permits flexion below the atlanto-axial pivot.
FJ3202.clinicalCondition: High cervical disc protrusion — uncommon; may cause suboccipital headache and neck stiffness.
FJ3202.clinicalScenario: A man with persistent suboccipital headache after a whiplash injury has MRI showing a small central C2/C3 disc protrusion irritating the C3 root.

FJ3207.name: Intervertebral disk of eighth thoracic vertebra
FJ3207.details: The T8/T9 thoracic disc; thin relative to its vertebral body, reflecting limited thoracic mobility; lies close to the spinal cord within a narrow canal.
FJ3207.clinicalCondition: Thoracic disc herniation — rare, but a calcified protrusion can produce progressive myelopathy.
FJ3207.clinicalScenario: A woman with gradually stiff, clumsy legs and a thoracic sensory level has MRI showing a calcified T8/T9 disc compressing the cord.

FJ3210.name: Intervertebral disk of eleventh thoracic vertebra
FJ3210.details: The T11/T12 disc at the thoracolumbar transition; nearby cord segments and the conus region make herniations here neurologically significant.
FJ3210.clinicalCondition: Thoracolumbar disc prolapse — can mimic conus or cauda equina syndromes.
FJ3210.clinicalScenario: A man presents with low back pain, patchy leg numbness, and urinary hesitancy; MRI reveals a large central T11/T12 disc prolapse.

FJ3219.name: Intervertebral disk of fifth cervical vertebra
FJ3219.details: The C5/C6 disc, the most mobile and commonly degenerated cervical level; its herniation typically compresses the exiting C6 root.
FJ3219.clinicalCondition: C6 radiculopathy — pain into the thumb and index finger with weak wrist extension.
FJ3219.clinicalScenario: An office worker has neck pain radiating to her thumb with a reduced brachioradialis reflex; MRI shows a C5/C6 prolapse compressing C6.

FJ3217.name: Intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra
FJ3217.details: The L5/S1 lumbosacral disc; wedge-shaped, bearing heavy load; herniation classically compresses the traversing S1 root.
FJ3217.clinicalCondition: S1 radiculopathy (sciatica) — calf pain, weak plantarflexion, and loss of the ankle jerk.
FJ3217.clinicalScenario: A gardener develops back pain radiating to the sole of the foot with an absent ankle reflex; MRI confirms an L5/S1 disc prolapse.

FJ3204.name: Intervertebral disk of fifth thoracic vertebra
FJ3204.details: The T5/T6 mid-thoracic disc; thoracic discs are thin and stabilized by the rib cage, so herniation is uncommon.
FJ3204.clinicalCondition: Girdle pain from thoracic disc disease — a band of pain wrapping around the chest wall.
FJ3204.clinicalScenario: A woman describes a tight band of pain encircling her chest at nipple level; cardiac tests are normal and MRI shows a T5/T6 disc protrusion.

FJ3212.name: Intervertebral disk of first lumbar vertebra
FJ3212.details: The L1/L2 disc, just below the conus medullaris; herniation affects upper lumbar roots supplying hip flexors and the front of the thigh.
FJ3212.clinicalCondition: Upper lumbar radiculopathy — groin and anterior thigh pain easily mistaken for hip disease.
FJ3212.clinicalScenario: A man treated for presumed hip arthritis has normal hip imaging; MRI instead shows an L1/L2 disc prolapse compressing the L2 root.

FJ3222.name: Intervertebral disk of first thoracic vertebra
FJ3222.details: The T1/T2 disc at the cervicothoracic junction; a herniation here can affect the T1 root supplying intrinsic hand muscles.
FJ3222.clinicalCondition: T1 radiculopathy — medial forearm pain with wasting of small hand muscles.
FJ3222.clinicalScenario: A woman notices clumsiness and wasting of her hand muscles; MRI reveals a rare T1/T2 disc prolapse compressing the T1 root.

FJ3218.name: Intervertebral disk of fourth cervical vertebra
FJ3218.details: The C4/C5 disc; herniation compresses the C5 root, weakening deltoid and biceps and dulling sensation over the shoulder.
FJ3218.clinicalCondition: C5 radiculopathy — shoulder abduction weakness after cervical disc prolapse at this level.
FJ3218.clinicalScenario: A painter cannot lift his arm overhead and has pain over the deltoid; MRI shows a C4/C5 prolapse compressing the C5 root.

FJ3216.name: Intervertebral disk of fourth lumbar vertebra
FJ3216.details: The L4/L5 disc, among the most frequently herniated; a posterolateral prolapse compresses the traversing L5 root.
FJ3216.clinicalCondition: L5 radiculopathy — weak great-toe and foot dorsiflexion producing a partial foot drop.
FJ3216.clinicalScenario: A nurse develops back pain with numbness over the dorsum of the foot and cannot extend her big toe; MRI shows an L4/L5 prolapse.

FJ3203.name: Intervertebral disk of fourth thoracic vertebra
FJ3203.details: The T4/T5 disc in the upper-mid thoracic spine; pain from this level projects around the chest and may imitate cardiac pain.
FJ3203.clinicalCondition: Thoracic disc protrusion — an uncommon but recognized mimic of angina pectoris.
FJ3203.clinicalScenario: A man with recurrent exertional-sounding chest pain has normal angiography; spinal MRI later reveals a T4/T5 disc protrusion as the pain source.

FJ3208.name: Intervertebral disk of ninth thoracic vertebra
FJ3208.details: The T9/T10 lower thoracic disc; herniations at lower thoracic levels are the commonest thoracic prolapses and may affect the cord or roots.
FJ3208.clinicalCondition: Thoracic radiculopathy — dermatomal band pain misdiagnosed as shingles or abdominal disease.
FJ3208.clinicalScenario: A woman with a burning band of pain below the ribs is treated for gallstones before MRI shows a T9/T10 foraminal disc prolapse.

FJ3214.name: Intervertebral disk of second lumbar vertebra
FJ3214.details: The L2/L3 disc; herniation compresses the L3 root, affecting hip flexion, knee extension, and sensation over the anterior thigh.
FJ3214.clinicalCondition: L3 radiculopathy — anterior thigh pain with a reduced knee jerk and quadriceps weakness.
FJ3214.clinicalScenario: A retired teacher complains of front-thigh pain and knee buckling on stairs; MRI shows an L2/L3 disc prolapse compressing the L3 root.

FJ3223.name: Intervertebral disk of second thoracic vertebra
FJ3223.details: The T2/T3 high thoracic disc; herniation is rare; root pain radiates around the upper chest and into the axilla.
FJ3223.clinicalCondition: High thoracic disc prolapse — may present as interscapular pain with myelopathic signs.
FJ3223.clinicalScenario: A man with interscapular ache and brisk leg reflexes has MRI showing a small T2/T3 disc herniation indenting the spinal cord.

FJ3221.name: Intervertebral disk of seventh cervical vertebra
FJ3221.details: The C7/T1 disc at the cervicothoracic junction; herniation compresses the C8 root, which supplies finger flexors and hand intrinsics.
FJ3221.clinicalCondition: C8 radiculopathy — numbness of the little finger with weak finger flexion.
FJ3221.clinicalScenario: A typist develops aching into the ring and little fingers with clumsy grip; MRI confirms a C7/T1 prolapse compressing the C8 root.

FJ3206.name: Intervertebral disk of seventh thoracic vertebra
FJ3206.details: The T7/T8 mid-thoracic disc; pathology here can project pain to the upper abdomen, imitating visceral disease.
FJ3206.clinicalCondition: Thoracic disc disease mimicking cholecystitis — referred pain confuses the initial diagnosis.
FJ3206.clinicalScenario: A woman undergoes normal gallbladder ultrasound for right upper abdominal pain; MRI later identifies a T7/T8 disc protrusion causing referred pain.

FJ3220.name: Intervertebral disk of sixth cervical vertebra
FJ3220.details: The C6/C7 disc, a common degeneration site; herniation compresses the C7 root supplying triceps and wrist flexors.
FJ3220.clinicalCondition: C7 radiculopathy — middle-finger paresthesia with triceps weakness and lost triceps reflex.
FJ3220.clinicalScenario: A mechanic has neck pain shooting to his middle finger and cannot push himself up from a chair; MRI shows a C6/C7 prolapse.

FJ3205.name: Intervertebral disk of sixth thoracic vertebra
FJ3205.details: The T6/T7 mid-thoracic disc; the narrow thoracic canal means even modest protrusions can threaten cord function.
FJ3205.clinicalCondition: Thoracic myelopathy — slowly progressive gait disturbance from a central disc protrusion.
FJ3205.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman reports two years of worsening balance and stiff legs; MRI shows a T6/T7 disc herniation compressing the thoracic cord.

FJ3209.name: Intervertebral disk of tenth thoracic vertebra
FJ3209.details: The T10/T11 disc; the T10 dermatome lies at the umbilicus, so root pain here wraps around the abdomen.
FJ3209.clinicalCondition: Thoracic radicular pain mimicking appendicitis or renal colic — dermatomal distribution is the clue.
FJ3209.clinicalScenario: A young man has right-sided abdominal pain with normal scans; careful examination maps it to the T10 band and MRI shows a T10/T11 prolapse.

FJ3213.name: Intervertebral disk of third cervical vertebra
FJ3213.details: The C3/C4 disc; herniation affects the C4 root, and this level lies near the phrenic nerve contributions to the diaphragm.
FJ3213.clinicalCondition: C4 radiculopathy — neck and shoulder-cape pain, occasionally with diaphragmatic irritation.
FJ3213.clinicalScenario: A woman with neck pain over the shoulder cape and unexplained hiccups has MRI showing a C3/C4 disc prolapse irritating the C4 root.

FJ3215.name: Intervertebral disk of third lumbar vertebra
FJ3215.details: The L3/L4 disc; herniation compresses the L4 root, weakening knee extension and tibialis anterior and numbing the medial leg.
FJ3215.clinicalCondition: L4 radiculopathy — anterior thigh and medial shin pain with a diminished knee jerk.
FJ3215.clinicalScenario: A postman develops pain down the front of the thigh to the inner shin and trips over his foot; MRI shows an L3/L4 prolapse.

FJ3224.name: Intervertebral disk of third thoracic vertebra
FJ3224.details: The T3/T4 high thoracic disc; protected by rib-cage stiffness, so symptomatic herniation is rare but can compress the cord.
FJ3224.clinicalCondition: Upper thoracic disc herniation — presents with interscapular pain and possible cord signs.
FJ3224.clinicalScenario: A woman with pain between the shoulder blades and brisk reflexes has MRI demonstrating a central T3/T4 disc herniation touching the cord.

FJ2775.name: Left arytenoid cartilage
FJ2775.details: Pyramidal laryngeal cartilage riding on the cricoid; its vocal process anchors the vocal ligament and its muscular process receives intrinsic laryngeal muscles, pivoting to open and close the glottis.
FJ2775.clinicalCondition: Arytenoid dislocation — traumatic intubation subluxes the cricoarytenoid joint, causing persistent hoarseness.
FJ2775.clinicalScenario: After a difficult intubation, a patient has breathy hoarseness for weeks; laryngoscopy shows the left arytenoid displaced and immobile.

FJ3256.name: Left calcaneus
FJ3256.details: Largest tarsal bone forming the heel; receives the Achilles tendon posteriorly, articulates with the talus above and cuboid in front, and transmits body weight to the ground.
FJ3256.clinicalCondition: Calcaneal fracture — falls from height; associated lumbar spine fractures must be excluded.
FJ3256.clinicalScenario: A man jumps from a wall and lands on his heels; X-ray shows a comminuted left calcaneal fracture, so his lumbar spine is also imaged.

FJ3257.name: Left capitate
FJ3257.details: Largest carpal bone, central in the distal row; its rounded head sits in the lunate cup, and the hand's longitudinal axis passes through it and the third metacarpal.
FJ3257.clinicalCondition: Scaphocapitate syndrome — capitate neck fracture combined with scaphoid fracture after hyperextension injury.
FJ3257.clinicalScenario: A snowboarder falls on an outstretched left hand; CT reveals fractures of both the scaphoid waist and the capitate neck needing fixation.

FJ3237.name: Left clavicle
FJ3237.details: S-shaped strut linking sternum to scapula, first bone to ossify; the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus pass behind its middle third.
FJ3237.clinicalCondition: Midshaft clavicle fracture — among the commonest fractures, from falls onto the shoulder.
FJ3237.clinicalScenario: A cyclist thrown over the handlebars has a deformed, tender left mid-clavicle with a drooping shoulder; X-ray confirms a displaced midshaft fracture.

FJ2776.name: Left corniculate cartilage
FJ2776.details: Small conical elastic cartilage capping the apex of the arytenoid within the aryepiglottic fold; contributes to the posterior laryngeal inlet.
FJ2776.clinicalCondition: Supraglottic edema — swelling of the aryepiglottic fold tissues around it narrows the airway inlet.
FJ2776.clinicalScenario: A child with drooling, stridor, and a tripod posture has imaging showing swollen supraglottic structures including the aryepiglottic folds — acute epiglottitis.

FJ3258.name: Left cuboid bone
FJ3258.details: Lateral midfoot tarsal wedged between calcaneus and the fourth and fifth metatarsals; the fibularis longus tendon grooves its plantar surface.
FJ3258.clinicalCondition: Cuboid (nutcracker) fracture — compression between calcaneus and metatarsals in crush injuries disrupts the lateral column.
FJ3258.clinicalScenario: A forklift wheel crushes a worker's left foot; CT shows a cuboid nutcracker fracture with midfoot dislocation requiring surgical fixation.

FJ2773.name: Left cuneiform cartilage
FJ2773.details: Small rod-shaped elastic cartilage within the aryepiglottic fold, just anterior to the corniculate; seen at laryngoscopy as the cuneiform tubercle.
FJ2773.clinicalCondition: Laryngomalacia — floppy supraglottic tissues around these cartilages prolapse inward, causing infant stridor.
FJ2773.clinicalScenario: A two-month-old has noisy breathing worse when feeding and lying flat; flexible laryngoscopy shows prolapsing aryepiglottic folds diagnostic of laryngomalacia.

FJ3235.name: Left eighth rib
FJ3235.details: A false rib whose cartilage joins the seventh above, forming the costal margin; left lower ribs overlie and protect the spleen.
FJ3235.clinicalCondition: Lower rib fractures with splenic injury — this association mandates abdominal imaging after left-sided fractures.
FJ3235.clinicalScenario: After a road accident, a man with fractures of left ribs eight to ten develops shoulder-tip pain; CT confirms a splenic laceration.

FJ3226.name: Left eleventh rib
FJ3226.details: Floating rib with a single costal facet and no anterior attachment, its tip free in the abdominal wall; the kidney lies posterior to it.
FJ3226.clinicalCondition: Floating rib fracture with renal injury — flank trauma here can contuse the underlying kidney.
FJ3226.clinicalScenario: A rugby player kicked in the left flank fractures the eleventh rib and passes blood-stained urine; imaging shows a renal contusion.

FJ3259.name: Left femur
FJ3259.details: Longest and strongest bone; its head sits in the acetabulum at a neck angle near 125 degrees, the shaft bears the linea aspera, and the condyles form the knee.
FJ3259.clinicalCondition: Femoral neck fracture — in the elderly, displaced fractures threaten the head's blood supply, causing avascular necrosis.
FJ3259.clinicalScenario: An 84-year-old falls at home and cannot bear weight; her left leg lies shortened and externally rotated, and X-ray confirms a fractured neck of femur.

FJ3260.name: Left fibula
FJ3260.details: Slender lateral leg bone; its head takes the biceps femoris tendon, the common fibular nerve winds around its neck, and its lateral malleolus stabilizes the ankle mortise.
FJ3260.clinicalCondition: Fibular neck fracture with nerve injury — the superficial common fibular nerve is easily damaged here.
FJ3260.clinicalScenario: A footballer tackled on the outer knee develops foot drop and numbness over the dorsum of the foot; X-ray shows a left fibular neck fracture.

FJ1409M.name: Left fibularis brevis
FJ1409M.details: Origin: lower two-thirds of lateral fibula; insertion: base of fifth metatarsal; everts and plantarflexes the foot; supplied by the superficial fibular nerve (L5–S2).
FJ1409M.clinicalCondition: Fifth metatarsal base avulsion — sudden inversion makes this tendon tear off its insertion fragment.
FJ1409M.clinicalScenario: A dancer inverts her left ankle stepping off a stage and has lateral foot pain; X-ray shows an avulsion fracture at the fifth metatarsal base.

FJ1410M.name: Left fibularis longus
FJ1410M.details: Origin: fibular head and upper lateral fibula; its tendon crosses the sole obliquely to insert on the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform; everts the foot and supports the arches; superficial fibular nerve.
FJ1410M.clinicalCondition: Fibular tendon subluxation — the tendon snaps over the lateral malleolus in runners and skiers.
FJ1410M.clinicalScenario: A marathon runner reports painful snapping behind the left lateral malleolus; dynamic ultrasound confirms fibularis longus subluxation over the malleolus.

FJ1411M.name: Left fibularis tertius
FJ1411M.details: Small anterior-compartment muscle arising with extensor digitorum longus; inserts on the dorsal base of the fifth metatarsal; dorsiflexes and everts the foot; deep fibular nerve (L5, S1).
FJ1411M.clinicalCondition: Acute anterior compartment syndrome — bleeding or swelling in its compartment threatens muscle and the deep fibular nerve.
FJ1411M.clinicalScenario: Hours after a tibial fracture, a patient develops severe pain on passive toe stretch with a tense shin; fasciotomy is performed for compartment syndrome.

FJ3251.name: Left fifth costal cartilage
FJ3251.details: Hyaline cartilage joining the fifth rib directly to the sternum, as for all true ribs one to seven; contributes to chest-wall elasticity.
FJ3251.clinicalCondition: Costochondritis — inflammation of costal cartilages produces localized anterior chest pain reproducible by palpation.
FJ3251.clinicalScenario: A woman with a tender, slightly swollen left fifth costochondral junction and a normal ECG is reassured with a diagnosis of costochondritis.

FJ3252.name: Left fifth metacarpal bone
FJ3252.details: Metacarpal of the little finger; its carpometacarpal joint is relatively mobile, and its neck is the classic weak point in punching injuries.
FJ3252.clinicalCondition: Boxer's fracture — neck fracture of this metacarpal from a clenched-fist blow.
FJ3252.clinicalScenario: A man punches a wall and presents with a swollen left hand and dropped knuckle; X-ray shows an angulated fifth metacarpal neck fracture.

FJ3253.name: Left fifth metatarsal bone
FJ3253.details: Lateral forefoot bone; its base tuberosity receives fibularis brevis; the metaphyseal–diaphyseal junction (Jones zone) has a watershed blood supply.
FJ3253.clinicalCondition: Jones fracture — fracture at this junction heals poorly and risks nonunion in athletes.
FJ3253.clinicalScenario: A basketball player lands awkwardly and has lateral foot pain; imaging shows a Jones fracture of the left fifth metatarsal, so a cast and non-weight-bearing are advised.

FJ3232.name: Left fifth rib
FJ3232.details: A true rib articulating with the sternum through its own cartilage; the cardiac apex beat is palpated in the fifth intercostal space just below it.
FJ3232.clinicalCondition: Multiple rib fractures with flail segment — three or more contiguous fractures impair ventilation.
FJ3232.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist with fractures of left ribs four to six shows paradoxical movement of that chest segment and is managed as a flail chest.

FJ3239.name: Left first costal cartilage
FJ3239.details: Joins the first rib to the manubrium by a synchondrosis allowing no movement; the subclavian vein passes immediately behind it.
FJ3239.clinicalCondition: Effort thrombosis (Paget–Schroetter) — subclavian vein compression in the costoclavicular space behind this cartilage.
FJ3239.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter develops a swollen, bluish left arm after training; venography shows subclavian vein thrombosis at the costoclavicular space.

FJ3240.name: Left first metacarpal bone
FJ3240.details: Shortest, stoutest metacarpal; its saddle-shaped base joint with the trapezium permits thumb opposition; axial load on the thumb injures its base.
FJ3240.clinicalCondition: Bennett fracture — two-part intra-articular fracture-dislocation at this base from axial loading.
FJ3240.clinicalScenario: A man falls onto his abducted left thumb during skiing; X-ray shows a Bennett fracture at the first metacarpal base requiring surgical fixation.

FJ3241.name: Left first metatarsal bone
FJ3241.details: Short, thick weight-bearing bone of the great-toe ray; two sesamoids sit beneath its head within the flexor hallucis brevis tendons; vital for push-off.
FJ3241.clinicalCondition: Hallux valgus (bunion) — lateral drift at the first metatarsophalangeal joint overloads this bone's medial eminence.
FJ3241.clinicalScenario: A woman with a painful medial bump and a great toe drifting toward the others has X-rays confirming hallux valgus of the left foot.

FJ3228.name: Left first rib
FJ3228.details: Shortest, broadest, most curved rib; bears the scalene tubercle; subclavian vein passes in front of scalenus anterior, artery and lowest brachial plexus trunk behind it.
FJ3228.clinicalCondition: Thoracic outlet syndrome — compression of neurovascular structures between this rib and the clavicle.
FJ3228.clinicalScenario: A young woman has left arm heaviness, hand tingling, and a diminished pulse on arm elevation; imaging confirms compression at the first-rib outlet.

FJ3248.name: Left fourth costal cartilage
FJ3248.details: Cartilage connecting the fourth rib to the sternum; lies over the cardiac silhouette, so pain here frequently raises cardiac concern.
FJ3248.clinicalCondition: Costochondritis mimicking angina — reproducible parasternal tenderness distinguishes chest-wall pain from cardiac pain.
FJ3248.clinicalScenario: A patient with left parasternal pain is found tender precisely over the fourth costal cartilage; with normal cardiac tests, costochondritis is diagnosed.

FJ3249.name: Left fourth metacarpal bone
FJ3249.details: Metacarpal of the ring finger; shaft fractures must be checked for rotational malalignment by observing the finger cascade during flexion.
FJ3249.clinicalCondition: Metacarpal shaft fracture — unrecognized rotation makes the ring finger cross its neighbors on gripping.
FJ3249.clinicalScenario: A goalkeeper jams his left ring finger on the ball; X-ray shows a spiral fourth metacarpal shaft fracture and rotation is carefully corrected before splinting.

FJ3250.name: Left fourth metatarsal bone
FJ3250.details: Slender forefoot bone of the fourth ray; shares transverse-arch load with adjacent metatarsals; its neck is a recognized stress-fracture site.
FJ3250.clinicalCondition: Metatarsal stress fracture — insidious forefoot pain in runners and new military recruits.
FJ3250.clinicalScenario: A recruit develops aching over the left forefoot after weeks of route marches; MRI confirms a stress fracture of the fourth metatarsal neck.

FJ3231.name: Left fourth rib
FJ3231.details: A true rib of the upper chest wall; fractures here lie adjacent to pleura and lung apex region, so pneumothorax must be excluded.
FJ3231.clinicalCondition: Rib fracture with pneumothorax — a displaced fragment can puncture the underlying pleura.
FJ3231.clinicalScenario: A scaffolder falls onto scaffolding tubes and fractures the left fourth rib; chest imaging reveals a small pneumothorax managed with observation.

FJ3261.name: Left hamate
FJ3261.details: Distal-row carpal bone whose hook projects palmarly, forming the medial wall of Guyon's canal transmitting the ulnar nerve and artery into the hand.
FJ3261.clinicalCondition: Hook of hamate fracture — golfers and baseball players; fragments can injure the ulnar nerve and flexor tendons.
FJ3261.clinicalScenario: A golfer who struck the ground hard develops hypothenar pain and weak grip; CT shows a fractured hook of the left hamate.

FJ3288.name: Left hip bone
FJ3288.details: Formed by fused ilium, ischium, and pubis meeting at the acetabulum; transmits trunk weight to the femur and anchors gluteal and abdominal wall muscles.
FJ3288.clinicalCondition: Pelvic ring fracture — high-energy disruption risks life-threatening hemorrhage from the presacral venous plexus.
FJ3288.clinicalScenario: A crushed motorcyclist arrives hypotensive with an unstable pelvic fracture; a pelvic binder is applied and massive transfusion begun.

FJ3262.name: Left humerus
FJ3262.details: Upper-arm bone; head articulates with the glenoid, the radial nerve winds in the spiral groove against its midshaft, and trochlea and capitulum form the elbow.
FJ3262.clinicalCondition: Midshaft fracture with radial nerve palsy — the nerve's groove contact makes wrist drop a classic sign.
FJ3262.clinicalScenario: A man with a left humeral shaft fracture cannot extend his wrist or fingers; a cock-up splint is fitted for radial nerve palsy.

FJ1423M.name: Left iliotibial tract
FJ1423M.details: Lateral thickening of fascia lata receiving tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus; runs over the lateral femoral epicondyle to insert on the lateral tibial condyle; stabilizes the extended knee.
FJ1423M.clinicalCondition: Iliotibial band syndrome — repetitive friction over the epicondyle causes lateral knee pain in runners.
FJ1423M.clinicalScenario: A cyclist training for a race reports left lateral knee pain appearing thirty minutes into every ride, settling with rest — iliotibial band syndrome.

FJ3264.name: Left intermediate cuneiform bone
FJ3264.details: Smallest cuneiform, recessed between its neighbors so the second metatarsal base keys into it — the mortise at the heart of the Lisfranc joint complex.
FJ3264.clinicalCondition: Lisfranc injury — tarsometatarsal disruption centered on this mortise destabilizes the midfoot arch.
FJ3264.clinicalScenario: A rugby player twists his planted left foot and develops midfoot swelling and plantar bruising; weight-bearing X-rays show Lisfranc diastasis.

FJ3267.name: Left lateral cuneiform bone
FJ3267.details: Wedge-shaped tarsal between the intermediate cuneiform and cuboid, articulating with the third metatarsal base; part of the transverse arch of the foot.
FJ3267.clinicalCondition: Midfoot arthrosis — degeneration at the cuneiform–metatarsal joints causes activity-related midfoot ache.
FJ3267.clinicalScenario: An older walker reports dorsal midfoot pain and a bony prominence; imaging shows arthrosis at the left lateral cuneiform–third metatarsal joint.

FJ1532M.name: Left levator scapulae
FJ1532M.details: Origin: transverse processes of C1–C4; insertion: medial border of scapula; elevates the scapula and laterally flexes the neck; supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve and C3–C4 branches.
FJ1532M.clinicalCondition: Levator scapulae strain — sustained poor posture produces chronic neck-to-shoulder-blade pain and stiffness.
FJ1532M.clinicalScenario: An office worker has chronic aching from the left neck to the upper medial scapula with a tender trigger point, diagnosed as levator scapulae strain.

FJ1258.name: Left lower central secondary incisor tooth
FJ1258.details: Permanent mandibular left central incisor (FDI 31); the smallest tooth, with a single root and narrow crown; erupts around six to seven years.
FJ1258.clinicalCondition: Incisal fracture — front teeth are most exposed to falls and sports trauma.
FJ1258.clinicalScenario: A child falls from a bicycle and chips her lower left central incisor; the dentist tests the pulp and restores the corner with composite.

FJ1254.name: Left lower first secondary molar tooth
FJ1254.details: Permanent mandibular left first molar; usually the first permanent tooth to erupt, around six years; broad cusped crown for grinding and two roots.
FJ1254.clinicalCondition: Fissure caries — deep occlusal pits make this the most decay-prone permanent tooth in children.
FJ1254.clinicalScenario: A seven-year-old has toothache and a deep cavity in her newly erupted lower left first molar; the tooth is restored and fissure-sealed.

FJ1255.name: Left lower first secondary premolar tooth
FJ1255.details: Permanent mandibular left first premolar; replaces the deciduous first molar around ten to twelve years; single root with a dominant buccal cusp.
FJ1255.clinicalCondition: Orthodontic extraction — first premolars are the teeth most often removed to relieve crowding.
FJ1255.clinicalScenario: A teenager with severe dental crowding has the lower first premolars included in an extraction plan before fixed braces are fitted.

FJ1259.name: Left lower lateral secondary incisor tooth
FJ1259.details: Permanent mandibular left lateral incisor; slightly larger than the central incisor with a single root; erupts around seven to eight years.
FJ1259.clinicalCondition: Traumatic subluxation — a blow loosens the tooth in its socket without displacement.
FJ1259.clinicalScenario: A schoolboy struck by a cricket ball has a tender, slightly mobile lower left lateral incisor; it is splinted and reviewed for pulp vitality.

FJ1256.name: Left lower second secondary molar tooth
FJ1256.details: Permanent mandibular left second molar; erupts around eleven to thirteen years behind the first molar; two roots lie close to the inferior alveolar canal.
FJ1256.clinicalCondition: Pericoronitis of eruption — inflamed gum flap over a partially erupted molar traps food and bacteria.
FJ1256.clinicalScenario: An adolescent has pain and swelling behind the first molar; a partially erupted lower left second molar with an inflamed operculum is found.

FJ1257.name: Left lower second secondary premolar tooth
FJ1257.details: Permanent mandibular left second premolar; erupts around eleven to twelve years replacing the deciduous second molar; single root, rounded crown.
FJ1257.clinicalCondition: Hypodontia — second premolars are among the most commonly congenitally missing teeth.
FJ1257.clinicalScenario: A panoramic radiograph taken for orthodontics shows the left lower second premolar never formed; the retained deciduous molar is kept under review.

FJ1260.name: Left lower secondary canine tooth
FJ1260.details: Permanent mandibular left canine; longest root in the lower arch, forming the cornerstone of the dental arch; erupts around nine to ten years.
FJ1260.clinicalCondition: Ectopic canine eruption — a malpositioned canine can resorb neighboring incisor roots silently.
FJ1260.clinicalScenario: Imaging for a 12-year-old shows the unerupted lower left canine lying against the lateral incisor root, prompting early orthodontic intervention.

FJ3268.name: Left lunate
FJ3268.details: Crescent-shaped proximal carpal bone articulating with the radius; central to wrist stability; its blood supply enters distally, leaving the proximal pole vulnerable.
FJ3268.clinicalCondition: Kienböck disease — avascular necrosis of the lunate causing chronic wrist pain in young adults.
FJ3268.clinicalScenario: A 25-year-old manual worker has months of left wrist pain and stiffness; MRI shows lunate sclerosis and collapse from avascular necrosis.

FJ2555.name: Left major alar cartilage
FJ2555.details: Nasal cartilage whose lateral crus forms the nostril rim and supports the external nasal valve; shapes the nasal tip and ala.
FJ2555.clinicalCondition: External nasal valve collapse — weak alar cartilage is drawn inward on inspiration, obstructing airflow.
FJ2555.clinicalScenario: A man notices his left nostril sucking shut whenever he breathes in deeply; examination confirms alar collapse and he is offered valve repair.

FJ3269.name: Left maxilla
FJ3269.details: Upper jaw bone housing the upper teeth and maxillary sinus; forms the orbital floor, lateral nasal wall, and most of the hard palate.
FJ3269.clinicalCondition: Le Fort fracture — midface fracture lines pass through the maxilla, mobilizing the tooth-bearing segment.
FJ3269.clinicalScenario: After an assault, a patient has a mobile upper jaw and cheek numbness; CT demonstrates a Le Fort I fracture pattern of the maxilla.

FJ3271.name: Left medial cuneiform bone
FJ3271.details: Largest cuneiform, articulating with the navicular behind and first metatarsal base in front; tibialis anterior and posterior tendons relate to its medial side.
FJ3271.clinicalCondition: Medial midfoot arthrosis — degeneration of the first tarsometatarsal joint causes medial arch pain.
FJ3271.clinicalScenario: An older runner reports aching along the inner left midfoot; imaging shows degenerative change at the medial cuneiform–first metatarsal joint.

FJ3272.name: Left nasal bone
FJ3272.details: Small paired bone forming the bridge of the nose, meeting its fellow in the midline; the most frequently fractured bone of the face.
FJ3272.clinicalCondition: Nasal bone fracture — direct blows deviate the bridge; an associated septal hematoma must be excluded.
FJ3272.clinicalScenario: A footballer elbowed in the face has a swollen, deviated nose; septal hematoma is excluded and closed reduction is performed within the week.

FJ3236.name: Left ninth rib
FJ3236.details: A false rib whose cartilage joins the costal margin; on the left it overlies the spleen, which lies deep to ribs nine to eleven.
FJ3236.clinicalCondition: Rib fracture with occult splenic injury — even stable patients need observation for delayed bleeding.
FJ3236.clinicalScenario: A man falls from a ladder fracturing left ribs nine and ten; CT shows a low-grade splenic injury managed conservatively with monitoring.

FJ3273.name: Left palatine bone
FJ3273.details: L-shaped bone forming the posterior hard palate, part of the lateral nasal wall and orbital floor; its greater palatine foramen transmits vessels and nerve to the palate.
FJ3273.clinicalCondition: Cleft palate — failure of fusion involving the palatine processes leaves a posterior palatal cleft.
FJ3273.clinicalScenario: A newborn struggles to feed and milk escapes through the nose; examination reveals a posterior cleft palate involving the palatine bones.

FJ3274.name: Left parietal bone
FJ3274.details: Paired vault bone forming the skull's sides and roof; meets its fellow at the sagittal suture and the frontal bone at the coronal suture; overlies the parietal lobe.
FJ3274.clinicalCondition: Depressed skull fracture — direct impact drives fragments inward, risking dural tear and cortical injury.
FJ3274.clinicalScenario: A man struck by a falling brick has a depressed left parietal fracture; CT shows the dura intact and he is managed in theatre for elevation.

FJ3275.name: Left patella
FJ3275.details: Largest sesamoid bone, embedded in the quadriceps tendon; articulates with the femoral trochlea and increases extensor leverage across the knee.
FJ3275.clinicalCondition: Transverse patellar fracture — violent quadriceps contraction or direct blow disrupts the extensor mechanism.
FJ3275.clinicalScenario: A man falls directly onto his left knee and cannot perform a straight-leg raise; X-ray shows a displaced transverse patellar fracture needing fixation.

FJ3276.name: Left pisiform
FJ3276.details: Pea-shaped sesamoid within the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, articulating with the triquetrum; forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal at the wrist.
FJ3276.clinicalCondition: Ulnar nerve compression at Guyon's canal — prolonged handlebar pressure beside this bone numbs the ulnar hand.
FJ3276.clinicalScenario: A long-distance cyclist develops aching over the pisiform with tingling in the ring and little fingers, diagnosed as Guyon's canal syndrome.

FJ3277.name: Left radius
FJ3277.details: Lateral forearm bone; its head rotates within the annular ligament for pronation and supination, and its distal end transmits most of the wrist's axial load.
FJ3277.clinicalCondition: Colles fracture — fall on the outstretched hand displaces the distal radius dorsally, the "silver fork" deformity.
FJ3277.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman falls on her outstretched left hand; X-ray shows a dorsally displaced, angulated distal radius fracture treated by reduction and casting.

FJ3278.name: Left scaphoid
FJ3278.details: Boat-shaped carpal bridging both carpal rows; its blood supply enters distally and flows retrograde, so waist fractures endanger the proximal pole.
FJ3278.clinicalCondition: Scaphoid fracture — snuffbox tenderness after a fall; missed injuries progress to nonunion and arthritis.
FJ3278.clinicalScenario: A skateboarder with anatomical snuffbox tenderness but normal X-rays is placed in a thumb spica and re-imaged for an occult scaphoid fracture.

FJ3279.name: Left scapula
FJ3279.details: Flat triangular bone overlying ribs two to seven; its spine, acromion, and coracoid anchor many muscles, and the glenoid cavity forms the shoulder joint.
FJ3279.clinicalCondition: Scapular fracture — a high-energy marker injury, frequently accompanied by rib fractures and lung injury.
FJ3279.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist with severe shoulder pain and breathlessness has a comminuted scapular body fracture with multiple rib fractures on CT.

FJ3242.name: Left second costal cartilage
FJ3242.details: Cartilage attaching the second rib to the sternum at the sternal angle of Louis, the key surface landmark for counting intercostal spaces.
FJ3242.clinicalCondition: Landmark for emergency procedures — the second space below it guides needle decompression and ECG lead placement.
FJ3242.clinicalScenario: In a trauma resuscitation, the team palpates the sternal angle at this cartilage to locate the second intercostal space for finger thoracostomy.

FJ3243.name: Left second metacarpal bone
FJ3243.details: Metacarpal of the index finger with the longest base; its rigid carpometacarpal joint makes the index ray a stable post for pinch.
FJ3243.clinicalCondition: Metacarpal shaft fracture — twisting or axial blows fracture the shaft; rotation must be checked.
FJ3243.clinicalScenario: A cricketer struck on the left index knuckle has a second metacarpal shaft fracture; splinting confirms his fingertip points correctly toward the scaphoid.

FJ3244.name: Left second metatarsal bone
FJ3244.details: The longest metatarsal; its recessed base is the keystone of the Lisfranc joint and its neck bears high bending stress in gait.
FJ3244.clinicalCondition: March fracture — stress fracture of the second metatarsal neck in new runners and recruits.
FJ3244.clinicalScenario: A new army recruit develops forefoot pain after route marches; X-ray shows a healing stress fracture of the left second metatarsal neck.

FJ3229.name: Left second rib
FJ3229.details: Rib attached at the sternal angle, bearing the scalene muscle attachments; upper rib fractures signal high-energy transfer to the thorax.
FJ3229.clinicalCondition: Upper rib fractures — associated with great-vessel and brachial plexus injury, warranting vascular imaging.
FJ3229.clinicalScenario: A restrained passenger in a high-speed crash fractures left ribs one and two; CT angiography is performed and excludes great-vessel injury.

FJ3255.name: Left seventh costal cartilage
FJ3255.details: Cartilage of the last true rib, joining the sixth above to form the costal margin; the epigastrium and xiphoid lie medially.
FJ3255.clinicalCondition: Costal margin pain syndrome — tenderness here mimics epigastric visceral pain but is chest-wall in origin.
FJ3255.clinicalScenario: A patient investigated for dyspepsia has pain reproduced exactly by pressing the left seventh costal margin, and is diagnosed with chest-wall pain.

FJ3234.name: Left seventh rib
FJ3234.details: The last true rib, attached to the sternum by its own cartilage; its lower border shelters the diaphragm and, on the left, the spleen.
FJ3234.clinicalCondition: Lower rib fracture — screening for splenic and diaphragmatic injury is required on the left.
FJ3234.clinicalScenario: An assault victim with a fractured left seventh rib undergoes CT, which excludes splenic injury but shows a small diaphragmatic contusion.

FJ3254.name: Left sixth costal cartilage
FJ3254.details: Cartilage linking the sixth rib to the sternum just above the xiphisternal junction; part of the flexible anterior chest wall.
FJ3254.clinicalCondition: Tietze syndrome — painful, swollen costochondral junctions, typically of the upper cartilages.
FJ3254.clinicalScenario: A young adult has a tender, swollen left sixth costochondral junction with a normal ECG and troponin; Tietze syndrome is diagnosed and NSAIDs prescribed.

FJ3233.name: Left sixth rib
FJ3233.details: A true rib of the mid-chest wall; isolated fractures are common in the elderly after minor falls against furniture edges.
FJ3233.clinicalCondition: Simple rib fracture — pain causes splinting and basal atelectasis, risking pneumonia in the elderly.
FJ3233.clinicalScenario: An elderly lady falls against a table edge and fractures the left sixth rib; analgesia and incentive spirometry are arranged to prevent chest infection.

FJ1504M.name: Left subscapularis
FJ1504M.details: Origin: subscapular fossa; insertion: lesser tubercle of humerus; the largest rotator-cuff muscle, internally rotating the arm; supplied by upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5–C7).
FJ1504M.clinicalCondition: Subscapularis tear — follows anterior shoulder dislocation or forced external rotation; weakens the belly-press test.
FJ1504M.clinicalScenario: After a shoulder dislocation, a man cannot press his palm into his abdomen against resistance; MRI confirms a full-thickness subscapularis tear.

FJ3280.name: Left talus
FJ3280.details: Tarsal bone transmitting weight from the tibia to the foot; largely cartilage-covered with no muscle attachments and a retrograde, easily disrupted blood supply.
FJ3280.clinicalCondition: Talar neck fracture — high-energy injury risking avascular necrosis of the talar body.
FJ3280.clinicalScenario: A driver in a head-on crash sustains a displaced left talar neck fracture; urgent reduction is performed to protect the bone's blood supply.

FJ3281.name: Left temporal bone
FJ3281.details: Skull bone housing the ear: mastoid process, petrous part containing the inner ear and facial nerve canal, styloid process, and mandibular fossa.
FJ3281.clinicalCondition: Temporal bone fracture — head injury causing Battle's sign, CSF otorrhea, and facial nerve palsy.
FJ3281.clinicalScenario: A man with bruising behind the left ear and clear fluid leaking from it after a fall has a temporal bone fracture on CT.

FJ3225.name: Left tenth rib
FJ3225.details: A false rib whose cartilage tapers toward the costal margin; posteriorly it relates to the pleura and the upper pole of the kidney.
FJ3225.clinicalCondition: Lower rib fracture with renal contusion — loin trauma here commonly produces hematuria.
FJ3225.clinicalScenario: A footballer kneed in the left loin fractures the tenth rib; his urine is blood-stained and imaging confirms a renal contusion.

FJ3245.name: Left third costal cartilage
FJ3245.details: Cartilage joining the third rib to the sternum; lies within the common two-to-five range affected by costochondral pain syndromes.
FJ3245.clinicalCondition: Costochondritis — benign chest-wall inflammation, diagnosed by reproducible localized tenderness after cardiac exclusion.
FJ3245.clinicalScenario: A 30-year-old with sharp left chest pain is tender over the third costal cartilage with a normal troponin, and is discharged with costochondritis advice.

FJ3246.name: Left third metacarpal bone
FJ3246.details: Metacarpal of the middle finger forming the hand's central axis; articulates firmly with the capitate; alignment reference when assessing fracture rotation.
FJ3246.clinicalCondition: Metacarpal fracture with malrotation — the middle finger scissors over its neighbors during flexion.
FJ3246.clinicalScenario: A boxer with a third metacarpal fracture notices his middle finger crossing the ring finger when making a fist, indicating malrotation needing correction.

FJ3247.name: Left third metatarsal bone
FJ3247.details: Slender forefoot bone of the third ray; its neck and shaft are exposed to repetitive bending loads during walking and running.
FJ3247.clinicalCondition: Stress fracture — gradual forefoot pain in runners, often visible only on MRI early on.
FJ3247.clinicalScenario: A distance runner with six weeks of insidious left forefoot pain has an MRI showing a stress fracture of the third metatarsal shaft.

FJ3230.name: Left third rib
FJ3230.details: A true rib of the upper chest; fractures at this level lie close to the lung apex, so apical pneumothorax is a key association.
FJ3230.clinicalCondition: Rib fracture with apical pneumothorax — pleural breach by a displaced fragment.
FJ3230.clinicalScenario: A scaffolder falls onto protruding tubes and fractures the left third rib; erect chest X-ray shows a small apical pneumothorax.

FJ3282.name: Left tibia
FJ3282.details: Medial weight-bearing bone of the leg; its medial surface is subcutaneous along the shin, the tibial tuberosity receives the patellar ligament, and the medial malleolus forms the ankle mortise.
FJ3282.clinicalCondition: Tibial shaft fracture — the commonest long-bone fracture; its exposed position risks open injury and compartment syndrome.
FJ3282.clinicalScenario: A footballer's left tibia is fractured in a tackle; the limb is splinted and he is monitored closely for escalating pain of compartment syndrome.

FJ1439M.name: Left tibialis anterior
FJ1439M.details: Origin: lateral tibial surface and interosseous membrane; insertion: medial cuneiform and first metatarsal base; dorsiflexes and inverts the foot; supplied by the deep fibular nerve (L4, L5).
FJ1439M.clinicalCondition: Chronic exertional compartment syndrome — this muscle's compartment causes exercise-induced shin pain and transient foot slap.
FJ1439M.clinicalScenario: A soldier develops anterolateral left leg pain and a slapping gait twenty minutes into every run, easing with rest — exertional compartment syndrome is confirmed by pressure testing.

FJ1440M.name: Left tibialis posterior
FJ1440M.details: Deep posterior leg muscle; origin posterior tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane; tendon passes behind medial malleolus to insert on navicular and midfoot bones; inverts and plantarflexes foot, supports medial arch; tibial nerve L4–L5.
FJ1440M.clinicalCondition: Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction — tendon insufficiency collapses the medial arch, causing adult-acquired flatfoot.
FJ1440M.clinicalScenario: A 52-year-old woman reports progressive left medial ankle pain and a flattening arch; she cannot perform a single-leg heel rise on that side.

FJ3283.name: Left trapezium
FJ3283.details: Distal-row carpal bone on the radial side; its saddle surface articulates with the first metacarpal base forming the thumb carpometacarpal joint; palmar surface grooved by the flexor carpi radialis tendon.
FJ3283.clinicalCondition: Thumb-base osteoarthritis — saddle-joint degeneration causes pain and weak pinch in older adults.
FJ3283.clinicalScenario: A 64-year-old woman has aching pain at the base of her left thumb when opening jars, with a positive grind test and squaring of the joint.

FJ3284.name: Left trapezoid
FJ3284.details: Small distal-row carpal wedged between trapezium and capitate; its base firmly binds the second metacarpal, making the index ray the stable unit of the hand; tight ligaments limit its motion.
FJ3284.clinicalCondition: Trapezoid fracture — rare because the bone is tightly bound; usually part of high-energy carpal injury.
FJ3284.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist lands on his left hand; CT for a suspected scaphoid injury incidentally reveals a nondisplaced trapezoid fracture.

FJ3285.name: Left triquetral
FJ3285.details: Proximal-row carpal on the ulnar side; articulates with the hamate and lunate, bears the pisiform on its palmar facet, and meets the triangular fibrocartilage rather than the ulna directly.
FJ3285.clinicalCondition: Dorsal triquetral chip fracture — commonest carpal fracture after scaphoid; an avulsion from forced hyperextension.
FJ3285.clinicalScenario: A student falls onto an outstretched left hand; radiographs show ulnar wrist swelling and a tiny dorsal chip beside the triquetrum on the lateral view.

FJ3227.name: Left twelfth rib
FJ3227.details: Floating rib without a costal cartilage or sternal attachment; single vertebral facet; overlies the left kidney posteriorly, and the pleural costodiaphragmatic recess descends close to its medial end.
FJ3227.clinicalCondition: Twelfth rib fracture with renal injury — the kidney lies directly anterior, so flank fractures risk haematuria.
FJ3227.clinicalScenario: A man struck in the left flank develops loin pain and visible haematuria; imaging shows a fractured twelfth rib overlying a renal contusion.

FJ3286.name: Left ulna
FJ3286.details: Medial forearm bone; olecranon and coronoid form the trochlear notch gripping the humerus at the elbow; subcutaneous posterior border; slender distal head meets the wrist via triangular fibrocartilage.
FJ3286.clinicalCondition: Monteggia fracture-dislocation — proximal ulna fracture with radial head dislocation; easily missed in children.
FJ3286.clinicalScenario: A 7-year-old falls from monkey bars; the radiograph shows a fractured left ulna, and careful review reveals the radial head is dislocated at the elbow.

FJ1265.name: Left upper central secondary incisor tooth
FJ1265.details: Permanent maxillary left central incisor (FDI 21); broadest incisor, single long root in the maxillary alveolus near the nasal floor; erupts around age 7–8 and forms the aesthetic midline.
FJ1265.clinicalCondition: Traumatic avulsion — this prominent tooth is the one most often knocked out in childhood falls.
FJ1265.clinicalScenario: A 9-year-old falls off a bicycle and completely avulses the tooth; it is stored in milk and reimplanted within the hour to preserve the ligament.

FJ1261.name: Left upper first secondary molar tooth
FJ1261.details: Permanent maxillary left first molar (FDI 26); three divergent roots (two buccal, one large palatal) whose apices lie close beneath the floor of the maxillary sinus.
FJ1261.clinicalCondition: Oroantral communication — extraction can open the sinus because the roots nearly touch its floor.
FJ1261.clinicalScenario: After a difficult extraction of this molar, the patient notices air and fluid passing between mouth and nose when drinking; a small oroantral fistula is confirmed.

FJ1262.name: Left upper first secondary premolar tooth
FJ1262.details: Permanent maxillary left first premolar (FDI 24); two cusps, and frequently two roots or two root canals — the most variable root anatomy among premolars.
FJ1262.clinicalCondition: Vertical root fracture — thin, ribbon-shaped roots split under heavy occlusal load or post placement.
FJ1262.clinicalScenario: A root-treated premolar develops a narrow deep periodontal pocket and a J-shaped radiolucency, leading to a diagnosis of vertical root fracture and extraction.

FJ1266.name: Left upper lateral secondary incisor tooth
FJ1266.details: Permanent maxillary left lateral incisor (FDI 22); smaller and narrower than the central incisor, single root; prone to developmental anomalies including peg shape and palatal invagination.
FJ1266.clinicalCondition: Dens invaginatus — infolded enamel traps plaque, causing early pulp necrosis in a young tooth.
FJ1266.clinicalScenario: A 13-year-old presents with a palatal sinus tract beside this incisor; radiographs show an invagination reaching the pulp with a periapical radiolucency.

FJ1263.name: Left upper second secondary molar tooth
FJ1263.details: Permanent maxillary left second molar (FDI 27); three roots, usually more convergent than the first molar; sits just behind the maxillary tuberosity and below the maxillary sinus.
FJ1263.clinicalCondition: Maxillary tuberosity fracture — extraction forces can fracture the tuberosity supporting this tooth.
FJ1263.clinicalScenario: During forceps extraction of a lone-standing second molar, the dentist feels the whole tuberosity move; the fragment is stabilised and the extraction completed surgically.

FJ1264.name: Left upper second secondary premolar tooth
FJ1264.details: Permanent maxillary left second premolar (FDI 25); single root with usually one canal; its apex lies close to the floor of the maxillary sinus.
FJ1264.clinicalCondition: Odontogenic maxillary sinusitis — periapical infection here can spread upward into the adjacent sinus.
FJ1264.clinicalScenario: A patient with a lingering unilateral blocked nose and bad taste is found to have a necrotic second premolar whose apex breaches the sinus floor.

FJ1267.name: Left upper secondary canine tooth
FJ1267.details: Permanent maxillary left canine (FDI 23); longest root of any tooth, producing the canine eminence; guides lateral jaw movements and is usually the last upper front tooth to erupt.
FJ1267.clinicalCondition: Palatal canine impaction — unerupted canines can silently resorb the neighbouring lateral incisor root.
FJ1267.clinicalScenario: A 14-year-old's left canine has not erupted; CBCT shows it impacted palatally, already resorbing the root of the adjacent lateral incisor.

FJ3287.name: Left zygomatic bone
FJ3287.details: Forms the cheek prominence and lateral orbital wall; its temporal process completes the zygomatic arch; articulates with frontal, maxillary, sphenoid and temporal bones; overlies the coronoid process of the mandible.
FJ3287.clinicalCondition: Zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture — displaced fractures flatten the cheek and block jaw opening by impinging the coronoid.
FJ3287.clinicalScenario: An assault victim has a flattened left cheek, numbness below the eye, and cannot open his mouth fully; CT confirms a displaced tripod fracture.

FJ3289.name: Mandible
FJ3289.details: Only mobile skull bone; body carries the lower teeth, ramus ends in condyle and coronoid; inferior alveolar nerve runs within its canal, exiting at the mental foramen; weakest at the angle and condylar neck.
FJ3289.clinicalCondition: Double fracture pattern — blows typically fracture the body and the opposite condylar neck together.
FJ3289.clinicalScenario: A man punched on the chin cannot bite together properly; imaging shows a parasymphysis fracture plus a fractured opposite condyle, the classic guardsman pattern.

FJ3290.name: Manubrium
FJ3290.details: Broad upper sternum bearing the jugular notch and clavicular facets; its junction with the body forms the sternal angle, a surface landmark at the second costal cartilage and T4/T5 level.
FJ3290.clinicalCondition: Manubrial fracture — high-energy steering-wheel injuries; a marker for associated mediastinal and great-vessel trauma.
FJ3290.clinicalScenario: A driver in a head-on collision has severe central chest bruising; CT shows a transverse manubrial fracture and prompts screening for aortic injury.

FJ3295.name: Middle phalanx of left fourth toe
FJ3295.details: Small short bone between the proximal and distal phalanges of the fourth toe, forming its two interphalangeal joints; moved by long flexor and extensor tendons from the leg.
FJ3295.clinicalCondition: Stubbing fracture — lesser-toe phalangeal fractures are common and usually managed with buddy taping.
FJ3295.clinicalScenario: A woman catches her left fourth toe on a table leg; the toe is swollen and bruised, and radiographs show a nondisplaced middle phalanx fracture.

FJ3296.name: Middle phalanx of left index finger
FJ3296.details: Lies between the proximal and distal phalanges of the index finger; the flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on its sides after splitting around the profundus tendon (Camper's chiasm).
FJ3296.clinicalCondition: Flexor tendon-zone injury — fractures and tendon lacerations here threaten the superficialis insertion and finger glide.
FJ3296.clinicalScenario: A carpenter lacerates the palm-side of his left index finger at this level and cannot flex the middle joint independently; a superficialis injury is suspected.

FJ3297.name: Middle phalanx of left little finger
FJ3297.details: Smallest finger's middle segment; its base forms the proximal interphalangeal joint with the proximal phalanx and carries the central slip insertion of the extensor mechanism dorsally.
FJ3297.clinicalCondition: Volar plate fracture-dislocation — hyperextension injuries at this joint can leave it unstable and stiff.
FJ3297.clinicalScenario: A netball player hyperextends her left little finger; after reduction, radiographs show a small volar plate avulsion fragment at the middle phalanx base.

FJ3298.name: Middle phalanx of left little toe
FJ3298.details: Tiny segment of the fifth toe, frequently fused with the distal phalanx in adults (a biphalangeal fifth toe), so the toe often shows only two visible phalanges.
FJ3298.clinicalCondition: Normal fusion variant — fused middle and distal phalanges are commonly mistaken for an old fracture.
FJ3298.clinicalScenario: Radiographs taken after a stubbed left little toe show the middle and distal phalanges fused; the radiologist reports this as a common normal variant.

FJ3299.name: Middle phalanx of left middle finger
FJ3299.details: Middle segment of the longest finger; receives the flexor digitorum superficialis insertion and serves as the pulley-supported track for the profundus tendon passing to the fingertip.
FJ3299.clinicalCondition: Rotational malunion — even small twists after fracture make the finger cross its neighbours on gripping.
FJ3299.clinicalScenario: Six weeks after a splinted fracture, a patient notices his left middle finger overlaps the ring finger whenever he makes a fist.

FJ3291.name: Middle phalanx of left ring finger
FJ3291.details: Its base receives the central slip of the extensor tendon, the key structure extending the proximal interphalangeal joint; flexor digitorum superficialis inserts along its palmar sides.
FJ3291.clinicalCondition: Boutonnière deformity — central slip disruption at this level lets the joint buttonhole into flexion.
FJ3291.clinicalScenario: Weeks after jamming his left ring finger, a man develops a bent middle joint with a hyperextended fingertip — a classic boutonnière deformity.

FJ3293.name: Middle phalanx of left second toe
FJ3293.details: Middle segment of the second toe, the longest toe ray; its joints are acted on by long flexors and extensors and by the intrinsic muscles balancing toe posture.
FJ3293.clinicalCondition: Hammer toe — fixed flexion at this toe's proximal interphalangeal joint causes painful corns over the knuckle.
FJ3293.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman complains of a painful corn over her bent left second toe that rubs inside shoes; examination shows a hammer toe deformity.

FJ3294.name: Middle phalanx of left third toe
FJ3294.details: Middle segment of the third toe between its metatarsophalangeal and distal joints; lesser-toe phalanges are common sites of inflammatory erosions and minor traumatic fractures.
FJ3294.clinicalCondition: Psoriatic and rheumatoid toe involvement — interphalangeal arthritis erodes these small bones and deforms the toe.
