FJ1434M.clinicalCondition: Femoral triangle landmark relevance — its medial border guides palpation and cannulation of the femoral artery and nerve block placement.
FJ1434M.clinicalScenario: In a shocked patient, the femoral pulse is located just below the inguinal ligament medial to sartorius for emergency arterial access.

FJ1570.name: Left scalenus anterior
FJ1570.details: From anterior tubercles of C3–C6 transverse processes to the scalene tubercle of the first rib; the phrenic nerve crosses its anterior surface; subclavian vein passes in front, artery and brachial plexus behind.
FJ1570.clinicalCondition: Thoracic outlet syndrome — compression of plexus and vessels between this muscle and the first rib causes arm pain and paresthesia.
FJ1570.clinicalScenario: A violinist develops aching and tingling along the medial forearm and hand, provoked by carrying loads and elevated-arm postures.

FJ1571.name: Left scalenus medius
FJ1571.details: From posterior tubercles of cervical transverse processes (C2–C7) to the first rib behind the subclavian groove; with scalenus anterior bounds the interscalene triangle transmitting the brachial plexus and subclavian artery.
FJ1571.clinicalCondition: Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome — a tight interscalene triangle between the scalene muscles compresses the lower plexus trunk.
FJ1571.clinicalScenario: A typist has ulnar-sided hand tingling and shoulder fatigue; symptoms reproduce when the arm is abducted and the head turned away.

FJ1572.name: Left scalenus posterior
FJ1572.details: Smallest scalene, from posterior tubercles of C5–C7 transverse processes to the outer surface of the second rib; cervical ventral rami; laterally flexes the neck and elevates the second rib in inspiration.
FJ1572.clinicalCondition: Accessory respiratory muscle overuse — chronic obstructive disease hypertrophies the scalenes, including this muscle, during laboured breathing.
FJ1572.clinicalScenario: A patient with severe emphysema breathes with visibly working neck muscles and prefers sitting upright, leaning forward on his arms.

FJ1435M.name: Left semimembranosus
FJ1435M.details: Medial hamstring from the ischial tuberosity to the posterior medial tibial condyle with expansions to the popliteal fascia; tibial division of sciatic nerve; extends hip and flexes knee.
FJ1435M.clinicalCondition: Semimembranosus bursitis — inflammation at its tibial insertion causes posteromedial knee pain mimicking a medial meniscus tear.
FJ1435M.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged runner has posteromedial knee pain and focal tenderness below the joint line, but McMurray's test and MRI menisci are normal.

FJ1538M.name: Left semispinalis capitis
FJ1538M.details: Broad neck extensor from transverse processes of C7–T6 and articular processes of C4–C7 to between the nuchal lines of the occiput; dorsal rami; the greater occipital nerve pierces it.
FJ1538M.clinicalCondition: Occipital neuralgia — the greater occipital nerve is irritated where it pierces this muscle, causing shooting vertex pain.
FJ1538M.clinicalScenario: A patient describes electric-shock pains from the occiput to the crown, with tenderness where the nerve emerges through the muscle.

FJ1539M.name: Left semispinalis cervicis
FJ1539M.details: From transverse processes of T1–T5 to spinous processes of C2–C5, thickest to the axis; dorsal rami; extends and contralaterally rotates the cervical spine and supports head posture.
FJ1539M.clinicalCondition: Whiplash-associated disorder — acceleration injury strains these deep extensors, producing persistent neck pain and reduced extensor endurance.
FJ1539M.clinicalScenario: Months after a car crash, a woman still has deep neck ache and fatigues quickly when holding her head upright.

FJ1540M.name: Left semispinalis thoracis
FJ1540M.details: From transverse processes of T6–T10 to spinous processes of C6–T4; dorsal rami; extends the thoracic and lower cervical spine and resists forward flexion moments.
FJ1540M.clinicalCondition: Mechanical mid-back pain — postural overload of the deep spinal extensors produces aching between the shoulder blades.
FJ1540M.clinicalScenario: A student develops mid-back aching after long study sessions, relieved by extension exercises and postural breaks.

FJ1436M.name: Left semitendinosus
FJ1436M.details: Medial hamstring from the ischial tuberosity to the upper medial tibia via pes anserinus; tibial division of sciatic nerve; extends hip, flexes knee; its tendon is a common graft source.
FJ1436M.clinicalCondition: Hamstring tendon graft harvest — this tendon (with gracilis) is routinely harvested to reconstruct a torn anterior cruciate ligament.
FJ1436M.clinicalScenario: An athlete with ACL rupture undergoes reconstruction using his semitendinosus-gracilis autograft, accepting minor knee flexion strength loss.

FJ1459M.name: Left serratus anterior
FJ1459M.details: From the outer surfaces of ribs 1–8 to the costal medial border of the scapula; long thoracic nerve (C5–C7) on its surface; protracts the scapula and holds it against the thorax.
FJ1459M.clinicalCondition: Winged scapula — long thoracic nerve palsy lets the medial scapular border lift off the chest wall.
FJ1459M.clinicalScenario: After axillary node clearance, a woman cannot push against a wall without her shoulder blade protruding backward conspicuously.

FJ1541M.name: Left serratus posterior inferior
FJ1541M.details: Thin sheet from spinous processes T11–L2 to the lower borders of ribs 9–12; lower intercostal and subcostal nerves; depresses the lower ribs and fixes them against diaphragmatic pull.
FJ1541M.clinicalCondition: Lower rib and thoracolumbar myofascial pain — strain of this muscle contributes to aching at the costal margin and flank.
FJ1541M.clinicalScenario: A warehouse worker strains his lower back lifting; pain localizes over the lowest ribs and worsens with trunk rotation.

FJ1542M.name: Left serratus posterior superior
FJ1542M.details: Thin sheet from the ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes C7–T3 to ribs 2–5 near their angles; upper intercostal nerves; elevates the upper ribs, assisting inspiration.
FJ1542M.clinicalCondition: Myofascial upper back pain mimic — trigger points here are frequently mistaken for rhomboid or angina-like interscapular pain.
FJ1542M.clinicalScenario: A patient reports deep aching beneath the upper scapula, tender on palpation, with normal cardiac and shoulder investigations.

FJ1437M.name: Left soleus
FJ1437M.details: Broad calf muscle from the soleal line of the tibia and fibular head, joining gastrocnemius in the calcaneal tendon; tibial nerve (S1–S2); plantarflexor and the main venous pump of the leg.
FJ1437M.clinicalCondition: Soleal vein thrombosis — sluggish flow in its intramuscular veins predisposes to deep vein thrombosis after immobility.
FJ1437M.clinicalScenario: After a long-haul flight, a man develops calf ache and swelling; ultrasound shows thrombus in a soleal vein.

FJ1544M.name: Left spinalis thoracis
FJ1544M.details: Medial column of erector spinae in the thorax, blending from spinous processes of upper lumbar/lower thoracic vertebrae to mid-thoracic spinous processes; dorsal rami; extends and stabilizes the spine.
FJ1544M.clinicalCondition: Erector spinae deconditioning — weakness of these extensors in chronic low back pain perpetuates poor load tolerance.
FJ1544M.clinicalScenario: A sedentary man with recurrent back pain improves after a graded program strengthening his spinal extensor muscles.

FJ1545M.name: Left splenius capitis
FJ1545M.details: From the ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes C7–T4 to the mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line under sternocleidomastoid; dorsal rami C3–C6; extends, laterally flexes, and ipsilaterally rotates the head.
FJ1545M.clinicalCondition: Splenius capitis syndrome — strain or trigger points cause pain referred to the vertex, mimicking migraine.
FJ1545M.clinicalScenario: A driver after minor whiplash has neck stiffness and pain shooting to the top of his head when rotating it.

FJ1546M.name: Left splenius cervicis
FJ1546M.details: From spinous processes T3–T6 to the transverse processes of C1–C3, deep to splenius capitis; dorsal rami; extends the neck and rotates it to the same side.
FJ1546M.clinicalCondition: Cervicogenic pain from deep neck extensor strain — whiplash or poor posture overloads it, restricting rotation.
FJ1546M.clinicalScenario: A woman cannot fully turn her head to check the blind spot while driving since a rear-end collision.

FJ1573.name: Left sternocleidomastoid
FJ1573.details: From manubrium and medial clavicle to the mastoid process; spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) with C2–C3; rotates the face to the opposite side, flexes the neck; divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.
FJ1573.clinicalCondition: Congenital muscular torticollis — fibrosis and shortening (fibromatosis colli) tilt the infant's head toward the affected side.
FJ1573.clinicalScenario: A two-month-old holds her head tilted right with the chin turned left; a firm fusiform swelling is felt in the right sternocleidomastoid.

FJ1574.name: Left sternohyoid
FJ1574.details: Infrahyoid strap from the manubrium and medial clavicle to the hyoid body; ansa cervicalis (C1–C3); depresses the hyoid after swallowing; separated in the midline during tracheostomy and thyroid surgery.
FJ1574.clinicalCondition: Midline neck landmark relevance — the gap between the sternohyoid muscles guides safe entry for emergency tracheostomy.
FJ1574.clinicalScenario: During an emergency airway procedure, the midline raphe between the strap muscles is followed down to reach the trachea.

FJ1575.name: Left sternothyroid
FJ1575.details: Infrahyoid muscle deep to sternohyoid, from the manubrium to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage; ansa cervicalis; depresses the larynx; its insertion limits upward expansion of a goiter.
FJ1575.clinicalCondition: Retrosternal goiter mechanics — because the thyroid gland lies deep here, enlargement is forced downward into the thorax.
FJ1575.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman with a large goiter has Pemberton's sign positive; CT shows the gland extending behind the sternum.

FJ1576.name: Left stylohyoid
FJ1576.details: Slender suprahyoid muscle from the styloid process, splitting around the digastric tendon to insert on the hyoid; facial nerve (CN VII); elevates and retracts the hyoid during swallowing.
FJ1576.clinicalCondition: Eagle syndrome — an elongated styloid process or calcified stylohyoid ligament irritates nearby nerves, causing throat and ear pain.
FJ1576.clinicalScenario: A woman has chronic unilateral throat pain radiating to the ear, worse on swallowing; CT shows a calcified stylohyoid ligament.

FJ1460M.name: Left subclavius
FJ1460M.details: Small muscle from the first costal cartilage to the subclavian groove of the clavicle; nerve to subclavius (C5–C6); depresses the clavicle and cushions the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus beneath it.
FJ1460M.clinicalCondition: Protective landmark in clavicle fracture — it shields the underlying vessels and plexus from displaced fracture fragments.
FJ1460M.clinicalScenario: A cyclist fractures his mid-clavicle; despite displacement, neurovascular examination of the arm is normal, partly thanks to this muscular cushion.

FJ1322.name: Left superior oblique
FJ1322.details: Extraocular muscle from the sphenoid above the annulus, turning through the trochlea pulley to insert on the posterolateral sclera; trochlear nerve (CN IV); intorts, depresses (especially in adduction) and abducts the eye.
FJ1322.clinicalCondition: Trochlear nerve palsy — failure of depression in adduction causes vertical diplopia worst on reading and descending stairs.
FJ1322.clinicalScenario: After head injury, a man sees double looking down at his phone and tilts his head to the opposite shoulder for relief.

FJ1323.name: Left superior rectus
FJ1323.details: Extraocular muscle from the common tendinous ring to the superior sclera; superior division of oculomotor nerve (CN III); elevates, adducts, and intorts the eye; intimately related to levator palpebrae superioris.
FJ1323.clinicalCondition: Oculomotor nerve palsy — its paralysis contributes to the 'down and out' eye with ptosis and a dilated pupil.
FJ1323.clinicalScenario: A diabetic woman develops a painful drooping eyelid; the eye sits down and out with a large, unreactive pupil.

FJ1505M.name: Left supinator
FJ1505M.details: Deep posterior forearm muscle wrapping the radial neck from the lateral epicondyle and ulna to the radius; the posterior interosseous nerve passes between its two heads at the arcade of Frohse; supinates the forearm.
FJ1505M.clinicalCondition: Posterior interosseous nerve syndrome — compression at the arcade of Frohse paralyses finger extension while sparing sensation and wrist extension.
FJ1505M.clinicalScenario: A man drops objects because his fingers will not extend, yet wrist extension and dorsal hand sensation remain intact.

FJ1506M.name: Left supraspinatus
FJ1506M.details: Rotator cuff muscle from the supraspinous fossa passing under the acromion to the greater tubercle of the humerus; suprascapular nerve (C5–C6); initiates abduction and centers the humeral head.
FJ1506M.clinicalCondition: Rotator cuff tear and subacromial impingement — its tendon is pinched in the subacromial space and is the cuff tendon most often torn.
FJ1506M.clinicalScenario: A painter has shoulder pain through a painful arc of abduction and cannot sleep on that side; MRI shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear.

FJ2748.name: Left tensor veli palatini
FJ2748.details: From the scaphoid fossa and auditory tube cartilage, hooking around the pterygoid hamulus into the palatine aponeurosis; nerve to medial pterygoid (V3); tenses the soft palate and opens the auditory tube.
FJ2748.clinicalCondition: Eustachian tube dysfunction — failure of this muscle to open the tube causes ear fullness and middle-ear effusion, notably in cleft palate.
FJ2748.clinicalScenario: A child with repaired cleft palate has recurrent glue ear and hearing loss because the tube does not open on swallowing.

FJ1507M.name: Left teres major
FJ1507M.details: From the dorsal inferior angle of the scapula to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus; lower subscapular nerve (C5–C7); adducts, extends, and medially rotates the arm ('lat's little helper').
FJ1507M.clinicalCondition: Teres major strain — sudden eccentric load in swimming or climbing tears fibers near its insertion, causing posterior axillary pain.
FJ1507M.clinicalScenario: A rock climber feels a pop under the armpit during a pull-up and has pain on resisted arm adduction for weeks.

FJ1508M.name: Left teres minor
FJ1508M.details: Rotator cuff muscle from the upper lateral scapular border to the lowest facet of the greater tubercle; axillary nerve branch (C5–C6); laterally rotates the arm; forms the upper boundary of the quadrangular space.
FJ1508M.clinicalCondition: Quadrangular space syndrome — compression of the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery between the teres muscles causes vague posterior shoulder pain.
FJ1508M.clinicalScenario: A volleyball player has aching posterior shoulder pain and weak external rotation; imaging shows teres minor fatty atrophy.

FJ2784.name: Left thyro-arytenoid
FJ2784.details: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle from the inner thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid's muscular and vocal processes; recurrent laryngeal nerve; shortens and relaxes the vocal fold and adducts the glottis.
FJ2784.clinicalCondition: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury — loss of this muscle's tone leaves the fold bowed and the voice breathy and weak.
FJ2784.clinicalScenario: After parathyroid surgery a teacher complains of a husky, easily tired voice; stroboscopy shows a bowed, flaccid vocal fold.

FJ2785.name: Left thyro-arytenoid
FJ2785.details: Forms the body of the vocal fold lateral to the vocal ligament within the larynx; recurrent laryngeal supply; fine-tunes fold tension and closes the rima glottidis for phonation and airway protection.
FJ2785.clinicalCondition: Laryngeal electromyography relevance — its electrical activity is sampled to distinguish recurrent nerve paralysis from mechanical fold fixation.
FJ2785.clinicalScenario: A man with an immobile fold after intubation undergoes laryngeal EMG of this muscle, confirming neuropathy rather than joint fixation.

FJ1577.name: Left thyrohyoid
FJ1577.details: Quadrilateral muscle from the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid body and greater horn; C1 fibers via the hypoglossal nerve; raises the larynx or depresses the hyoid; membrane above it transmits the internal laryngeal nerve.
FJ1577.clinicalCondition: Superior laryngeal nerve block landmark — anesthetic is placed through the thyrohyoid membrane just below the hyoid's greater horn.
FJ1577.clinicalScenario: Before awake fiberoptic intubation, the anesthetist blocks the internal laryngeal nerve through the thyrohyoid membrane on each side.

FJ1461M.name: Left transversus thoracis
FJ1461M.details: Fan-shaped muscle on the inner anterior chest wall from the posterior xiphoid and lower sternum to costal cartilages 2–6; anterior intercostal nerves; depresses the ribs; the internal thoracic artery runs lateral to its slips.
FJ1461M.clinicalCondition: Internal thoracic artery harvest relevance — in coronary bypass, the artery is mobilized just superficial to this muscle and the endothoracic fascia.
FJ1461M.clinicalScenario: During CABG, the surgeon harvests the internal thoracic artery from the chest wall, noting this muscle deep to its lower course.

FJ1441M.name: Left vastus intermedius
FJ1441M.details: Quadriceps head deep to rectus femoris, from the anterior and lateral femoral shaft to the quadriceps tendon and patella; femoral nerve (L2–L4); extends the knee; articularis genu arises from its distal part.
FJ1441M.clinicalCondition: Thigh compartment bleeding risk — femoral shaft fractures bleed into the quadriceps mass around this muscle, silently sequestering large volumes.
FJ1441M.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist with a femoral fracture develops a tense, expanding thigh and falling hemoglobin before fixation.

FJ1442M.name: Left vastus lateralis
FJ1442M.details: Largest quadriceps head, from the greater trochanter and lateral linea aspera to the patella and quadriceps tendon; femoral nerve (L2–L4); extends the knee and stabilizes the patella laterally.
FJ1442M.clinicalCondition: Intramuscular injection site of choice in infants — its bulk and distance from major nerves and vessels make it the safest site.
FJ1442M.clinicalScenario: A nurse vaccinates a four-month-old into the anterolateral thigh, choosing vastus lateralis to avoid the sciatic nerve and femoral vessels.

FJ1443M.name: Left vastus medialis
FJ1443M.details: Quadriceps head from the intertrochanteric line and medial linea aspera to the patella; its oblique distal fibers (VMO) align the patella; femoral nerve (L2–L4); completes terminal knee extension.
FJ1443M.clinicalCondition: Patellofemoral pain syndrome — relative VMO weakness or delayed activation lets the patella track laterally over the femoral groove.
FJ1443M.clinicalScenario: A teenage girl has anterior knee pain climbing stairs and after prolonged sitting; examination shows poor medial patellar control.

FJ2788.name: Left vocalis
FJ2788.details: Medial fibers of thyroarytenoid within the vocal fold itself, attaching along the vocal process and ligament; recurrent laryngeal nerve; makes fine adjustments of fold tension for pitch and voice quality.
FJ2788.clinicalCondition: Muscle tension dysphonia and voice fatigue — disordered fine control of the fold impairs pitch range in professional voice users.
FJ2788.clinicalScenario: A singer notices loss of high notes and rapid voice fatigue late in performances; laryngeal examination shows hyperfunctional fold behavior.

FJ1478M.name: Long head of left biceps brachii
FJ1478M.details: Arises from the supraglenoid tubercle, traverses the shoulder joint and intertubercular groove, joining the short head to insert on the radial tuberosity; musculocutaneous nerve; flexes elbow and supinates forearm.
FJ1478M.clinicalCondition: Long head biceps tendinopathy and SLAP tear — its intra-articular course predisposes to groove pain and labral detachment in throwers.
FJ1478M.clinicalScenario: A baseball pitcher has deep anterior shoulder pain and clicking; arthroscopy confirms a superior labral tear at the biceps anchor.

FJ1395M.name: Long head of left biceps femoris
FJ1395M.details: Hamstring head from the ischial tuberosity (common tendon with semitendinosus) to the fibular head; tibial division of the sciatic nerve; extends the hip and flexes the knee; common fibular nerve winds around the fibular neck nearby.
FJ1395M.clinicalCondition: Proximal hamstring strain — the biceps femoris is the hamstring most often torn during high-speed sprinting.
FJ1395M.clinicalScenario: A sprinter pulls up mid-race clutching the back of his thigh; MRI shows a tear near the biceps femoris musculotendinous junction.

FJ1479M.name: Long head of left triceps brachii
FJ1479M.details: From the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula, descending between teres major and minor to join the other heads on the olecranon; radial nerve (C6–C8); extends the elbow and assists shoulder extension and adduction.
FJ1479M.clinicalCondition: Radial nerve assessment relevance — because its branch leaves proximally, triceps function is spared in mid-shaft humeral spiral groove lesions.
FJ1479M.clinicalScenario: A man with a humeral shaft fracture has wrist drop, but elbow extension is preserved, localizing the nerve lesion below the triceps branches.

FJ1478.name: Long head of right biceps brachii
FJ1478.details: From the supraglenoid tubercle through the intertubercular groove to the radial tuberosity (shared insertion with the short head); musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6); flexes and supinates the forearm, steadies the humeral head.
FJ1478.clinicalCondition: Proximal biceps tendon rupture — sudden failure of the long head produces the 'Popeye' bulge with surprisingly modest functional loss.
FJ1478.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter hears a snap lifting a heavy box; the biceps bunches distally in his arm though elbow flexion remains fairly strong.

FJ1395.name: Long head of right biceps femoris
FJ1395.details: From the ischial tuberosity to the head of the fibula, forming the superolateral boundary of the popliteal fossa; tibial division of sciatic nerve; extends hip, flexes and laterally rotates the flexed knee.
FJ1395.clinicalCondition: Hamstring origin tendinopathy — chronic overload at its ischial origin causes deep buttock pain in runners, aggravated by sitting.
FJ1395.clinicalScenario: A marathoner reports buttock pain on long runs and while driving; tenderness localizes to the ischial tuberosity with pain on resisted knee flexion.

FJ1479.name: Long head of right triceps brachii
FJ1479.details: Two-joint head from the infraglenoid tubercle to the olecranon via the common triceps tendon; radial nerve; extends the elbow, extends and adducts the shoulder; helps bound the triangular interval transmitting the radial nerve and profunda vessels.
FJ1479.clinicalCondition: Triceps tendon rupture — rare avulsion from the olecranon, typically in weightlifters or after falls on the outstretched hand.
FJ1479.clinicalScenario: A powerlifter feels a snap behind the elbow during bench press; he cannot extend the elbow against gravity and a gap is palpable above the olecranon.

FJ1396M.name: Medial head of left flexor hallucis brevis
FJ1396M.details: Plantar intrinsic from the cuboid and lateral cuneiform to the medial side of the great toe's proximal phalanx, its tendon containing the medial sesamoid; medial plantar nerve; flexes the metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux.
FJ1396M.clinicalCondition: Sesamoiditis — inflammation under the first metatarsal head where this head's sesamoid bears load causes forefoot pain in dancers and runners.
FJ1396M.clinicalScenario: A ballet dancer has aching pain beneath her big toe joint in demi-pointe; tenderness localizes to the medial sesamoid.

FJ1397M.name: Medial head of left gastrocnemius
FJ1397M.details: Arises behind the medial femoral condyle, forming the inferomedial boundary of the popliteal fossa, and joins the calcaneal tendon; tibial nerve (S1–S2); plantarflexes the ankle and flexes the knee.
FJ1397M.clinicalCondition: 'Tennis leg' — a tear at the medial head's musculotendinous junction from sudden push-off produces acute calf pain and swelling.
FJ1397M.clinicalScenario: A 45-year-old squash player lunges and feels as if struck in the calf; examination shows medial calf tenderness and a small hematoma.

FJ1480M.name: Medial head of left triceps brachii
FJ1480M.details: Deep head from the posterior humerus below the radial groove to the olecranon; radial nerve; the workhorse of elbow extension, active in all extension regardless of forearm position; forms the floor over which the radial nerve spirals.
FJ1480M.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark relevance — posterior elbow approaches split or reflect this head, taking care of the radial nerve and its branches above.
FJ1480M.clinicalScenario: During posterior plating of a distal humerus fracture, the surgeon protects the radial nerve while working through the triceps.

FJ1396.name: Medial head of right flexor hallucis brevis
FJ1396.details: From the plantar midfoot bones to the medial base of the hallux proximal phalanx with the medial sesamoid in its tendon; medial plantar nerve (S1–S2 contribution); flexes and stabilizes the great toe at push-off.
FJ1396.clinicalCondition: Turf toe contribution — hyperextension injury of the first MTP joint strains this muscle-sesamoid complex and the plantar plate.
FJ1396.clinicalScenario: An American football player jams his big toe into the turf; he cannot push off and has swelling under the first toe joint.

FJ1397.name: Medial head of right gastrocnemius
FJ1397.details: Originates from the popliteal surface and medial femoral condyle, converging into the calcaneal tendon with soleus; tibial nerve; its medial head is the larger, more distal-reaching of the two heads.
FJ1397.clinicalCondition: Medial gastrocnemius strain differentiation — its tear must be distinguished from Achilles rupture and DVT, which it mimics clinically.
FJ1397.clinicalScenario: An older man presents with acute calf pain; Thompson's squeeze test is normal and ultrasound shows a gastrocnemius tear, not thrombosis.

FJ1480.name: Medial head of right triceps brachii
FJ1480.details: Lies deep to the lateral and long heads on the posterior humerus, inserting broadly on the olecranon; radial nerve; provides most of the force of elbow extension and stabilizes the elbow joint.
FJ1480.clinicalCondition: Elbow extension testing relevance — resisted extension isolates triceps function when assessing C7 radiculopathy versus radial neuropathy.
FJ1480.clinicalScenario: A patient with neck pain radiating to the middle finger shows weak elbow extension, pointing to a C7 root lesion.

FJ1548.name: medial lumbar intertransversarius
FJ1548.details: Small slips between the mammillary and accessory processes of adjacent lumbar vertebrae, medial division of the intertransversarii; dorsal and ventral rami contributions; fine segmental stabilization and proprioception of the lumbar spine.
FJ1548.clinicalCondition: Segmental stabilization relevance — these tiny muscles are rich in proprioceptors and are targeted indirectly in chronic low back pain rehabilitation.
FJ1548.clinicalScenario: A physiotherapist prescribes segmental control exercises for a patient with recurrent lumbar strain and poor trunk proprioception.

FJ1548M.name: Medial lumbar intertransversarius
FJ1548M.details: Medial intertransverse slips of the lumbar region connecting adjacent vertebral processes deep to multifidus; supplied by dorsal rami; contribute to lateral stability and fine intervertebral positioning.
FJ1548M.clinicalCondition: Facet-mediated back pain context — segmental muscle dysfunction coexists with painful lumbar facet joints in mechanical back pain.
FJ1548M.clinicalScenario: A man with localized lumbar ache and restricted side-bending improves with segmental mobilization and deep muscle retraining.

FJ1398M.name: Oblique head of left adductor hallucis
FJ1398M.details: Deep plantar muscle from the bases of metatarsals 2–4 and the peroneus longus sheath to the lateral base of the hallux proximal phalanx; deep branch of lateral plantar nerve; supports the transverse arch and adducts the great toe.
FJ1398M.clinicalCondition: Hallux valgus association — imbalance between this adductor and abductor hallucis contributes to lateral deviation of the great toe.
FJ1398M.clinicalScenario: A woman with a progressive bunion has the great toe drifting toward the second toe, crowding her forefoot in shoes.

FJ1481M.name: Oblique head of left adductor pollicis
FJ1481M.details: Deep thenar muscle from the capitate and bases of metacarpals 2–3 to the medial base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; deep branch of the ulnar nerve; powerfully adducts the thumb for pinch grip.
FJ1481M.clinicalCondition: Froment's sign — ulnar palsy weakens this muscle, so the patient flexes the thumb tip (using median-innervated FPL) to hold paper.
FJ1481M.clinicalScenario: A cyclist with handlebar palsy cannot hold a card between thumb and index without the thumb tip bending sharply.

FJ1398.name: Oblique head of right adductor hallucis
FJ1398.details: From the bases of the middle metatarsals across the deep sole to the hallux, deep to the flexor tendons; lateral plantar nerve (deep branch); maintains the transverse arch and resists splaying of the forefoot.
FJ1398.clinicalCondition: Metatarsalgia association — arch-support failure involving this intrinsic layer overloads the lesser metatarsal heads during gait.
FJ1398.clinicalScenario: A shop assistant standing all day develops burning forefoot pain under the second and third metatarsal heads.

FJ1481.name: Oblique head of right adductor pollicis
FJ1481.details: Fans from the capitate and second/third metacarpal bases to the thumb, deep to the flexor pollicis longus tendon; deep branch of ulnar nerve; the deep palmar arch and ulnar nerve's deep branch cross its surface.
FJ1481.clinicalCondition: Ulnar tunnel (Guyon's canal) lesion effect — deep branch compression paralyses this muscle while sparing dorsal sensation.
FJ1481.clinicalScenario: A man pressing on his hypothenar eminence at work develops weak pinch and interosseous wasting with normal sensation over the dorsal ulnar hand.

FJ2781.name: Oblique part of left cricothyroid
FJ2781.details: Fibers running obliquely upward and backward from the cricoid arch to the thyroid lamina and inferior horn; external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve; tilts the thyroid forward to tense the vocal folds and raise pitch.
FJ2781.clinicalCondition: External laryngeal nerve injury in thyroid surgery — paralysis removes fold tensioning, so high notes and voice projection are lost.
FJ2781.clinicalScenario: A professional singer after hemithyroidectomy finds her upper register gone and her speaking voice monotonous and easily tired.

FJ2799.name: Oblique part of right cricothyroid
FJ2799.details: Oblique division of the only intrinsic laryngeal muscle lying outside the larynx, between the cricoid arch and thyroid cartilage; external superior laryngeal nerve; lengthens and tenses the vocal fold.
FJ2799.clinicalCondition: Surgical vulnerability — the external laryngeal nerve runs close to the superior thyroid vessels and this muscle during thyroidectomy ligation.
FJ2799.clinicalScenario: During thyroid lobectomy, the surgeon ligates the superior pole vessels flush with the gland to spare the nerve supplying this muscle.

FJ1399M.name: Opponens digiti minimi of left foot
FJ1399M.details: Small, inconstant plantar muscle from the base of the fifth metatarsal and peroneus longus sheath to the lateral border of the fifth metatarsal; lateral plantar nerve; weakly flexes and adducts the little toe.
FJ1399M.clinicalCondition: Vestigial variation relevance — human opposition of the little toe is negligible; the muscle matters mainly as a variant in foot surgery anatomy.
FJ1399M.clinicalScenario: During fifth-ray surgery for a tailor's bunion, the surgeon notes this inconstant muscle overlying the metatarsal shaft.

FJ1482M.name: Opponens digiti minimi of left hand
FJ1482M.details: Deepest hypothenar muscle, from the hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum to the medial border of the fifth metacarpal; deep branch of ulnar nerve; rotates the fifth metacarpal to cup the palm for grip.
FJ1482M.clinicalCondition: Hypothenar wasting in ulnar neuropathy — loss of this and other hypothenar muscles flattens the ulnar palm and weakens grip cupping.
FJ1482M.clinicalScenario: A patient with cubital tunnel syndrome shows a flattened hypothenar eminence and cannot cup water in the palm.

FJ1399.name: Opponens digiti minimi of right foot
FJ1399.details: Variable fifth-layer plantar slip along the fifth metatarsal, blending with flexor digiti minimi brevis; lateral plantar nerve; assists little-toe flexion and lateral arch support.
FJ1399.clinicalCondition: Lateral plantar pain differential — strain of the lateral intrinsic group can mimic plantar fasciitis on the outer foot.
FJ1399.clinicalScenario: A runner has pain along the outer border of the foot, tender over the fifth metatarsal shaft rather than the heel.

FJ1482.name: Opponens digiti minimi of right hand
FJ1482.details: Triangular hypothenar muscle deep to the flexor and abductor digiti minimi, acting on the fifth metacarpal; deep branch of the ulnar nerve; brings the little finger toward the thumb in opposition.
FJ1482.clinicalCondition: Deep branch ulnar lesion at the pisohamate hiatus — motor loss including this muscle occurs without sensory deficit.
FJ1482.clinicalScenario: A mechanic develops clumsy grip and weak little-finger opposition after a hamate fracture, with intact ulnar sensation.

FJ2430.name: Posterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
FJ2430.details: Conical projection from the posterior right ventricular wall giving chordae tendineae to the posterior and septal cusps of the tricuspid valve; prevents cusp prolapse during systole; right coronary artery territory supply.
FJ2430.clinicalCondition: Tricuspid regurgitation from papillary dysfunction — right ventricular infarction or dilatation impairs cusp coaptation, producing systolic regurgitant flow.
FJ2430.clinicalScenario: After an inferior myocardial infarction, a man develops a new pansystolic murmur, raised JVP with prominent v waves, and hepatic congestion.

FJ1400.name: Right abductor hallucis
FJ1400.details: Medial plantar muscle from the calcaneal tuberosity and flexor retinaculum to the medial base of the hallux proximal phalanx; medial plantar nerve; abducts and flexes the great toe; covers the plantar vessels and nerves entering the sole.
FJ1400.clinicalCondition: Abductor hallucis strain and medial arch pain — overuse in runners causes pain along the inner arch mimicking plantar fasciitis.
FJ1400.clinicalScenario: A distance runner has aching along the medial arch after mileage increases, tender over the muscle belly rather than the heel insertion.

FJ1483.name: Right abductor pollicis brevis
FJ1483.details: Superficial thenar muscle from the scaphoid, trapezium, and flexor retinaculum to the lateral base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; recurrent branch of the median nerve; abducts the thumb perpendicular to the palm.
FJ1483.clinicalCondition: Carpal tunnel syndrome — compression of the recurrent median branch wastes this muscle early, flattening the thenar eminence.
FJ1483.clinicalScenario: A pregnant woman wakes with numb fingers; months later the thenar pad looks hollowed and thumb abduction against resistance is weak.

FJ1484.name: Right abductor pollicis longus
FJ1484.details: Deep posterior forearm muscle from the ulna, radius, and interosseous membrane to the base of the first metacarpal; posterior interosseous nerve; abducts and extends the thumb; with extensor pollicis brevis forms the lateral border of the anatomical snuffbox.
FJ1484.clinicalCondition: De Quervain's tenosynovitis — stenosing inflammation of the shared first dorsal compartment sheath of this tendon and extensor pollicis brevis.
FJ1484.clinicalScenario: A new mother has radial wrist pain when lifting her baby; Finkelstein's test reproduces sharp pain over the snuffbox tendons.

FJ1401.name: Right adductor brevis
FJ1401.details: Medial thigh muscle from the inferior pubic ramus to the upper linea aspera, deep to adductor longus; obturator nerve (anterior division); adducts and flexes the hip; the obturator nerve's divisions pass on either side of it.
FJ1401.clinicalCondition: Adductor (groin) strain — sprinting and kicking overload the medial thigh group, producing groin pain and weak resisted adduction.
FJ1401.clinicalScenario: A soccer player pulls up after a forceful side-foot pass with immediate groin pain and tenderness deep in the medial thigh.

FJ1402.name: Right adductor longus
FJ1402.details: Flat medial thigh muscle from the pubic body to the middle third of the linea aspera; obturator nerve; adducts and medially rotates the thigh; forms the medial border of the femoral triangle.
FJ1402.clinicalCondition: Adductor longus tendinopathy — the commonest chronic groin pain in footballers, centered on its pubic origin.
FJ1402.clinicalScenario: An academy footballer has months of groin ache at the pubic origin, worst when sprinting and striking the ball.

FJ1403.name: Right adductor magnus
FJ1403.details: Largest medial thigh muscle, pubis/ischium to the linea aspera and adductor tubercle; dual supply — obturator nerve (adductor part) and tibial division of sciatic (hamstring part); its adductor hiatus transmits the femoral vessels into the popliteal fossa.
FJ1403.clinicalCondition: Vascular landmark relevance — the femoral artery passes through this muscle's hiatus to become the popliteal artery, a key level in femoropopliteal disease.
FJ1403.clinicalScenario: Angiography in a claudicant shows the superficial femoral artery occluded precisely where it traverses the adductor hiatus.

FJ1404.name: Right adductor minimus
FJ1404.details: Upper, incompletely separated part of adductor magnus, from the inferior pubic ramus to the upper linea aspera and gluteal tuberosity; obturator nerve; assists hip adduction and lateral rotation; perforating arteries pass close to its insertion.
FJ1404.clinicalCondition: Anatomical-variant relevance — it matters chiefly because the perforating branches of profunda femoris pass near it during posterior thigh surgery.
FJ1404.clinicalScenario: During exploration of a deep thigh hematoma, the surgeon identifies bleeding from a perforating artery crossing this muscle's insertion.

FJ1485.name: Right anconeus
FJ1485.details: Small triangular muscle from the lateral epicondyle to the lateral olecranon and upper ulna; radial nerve branch; assists triceps in elbow extension and stabilizes the ulna during pronation; used as a local flap for elbow coverage.
FJ1485.clinicalCondition: Anconeus epitrochlearis variant — an anomalous muscle replacing the cubital tunnel retinaculum can compress the ulnar nerve at the elbow.
FJ1485.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter develops ulnar hand numbness; exploration finds an accessory anconeus muscle roofing and narrowing the cubital tunnel.

FJ2791.name: Right aryepiglotticus
FJ2791.details: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle within the aryepiglottic fold, from the arytenoid apex to the epiglottic margin; recurrent laryngeal nerve; narrows the laryngeal inlet as a sphincter during swallowing.
FJ2791.clinicalCondition: Laryngomalacia — floppy, lax aryepiglottic folds collapse inward on inspiration, the commonest cause of congenital stridor in infants.
FJ2791.clinicalScenario: A six-week-old has noisy inspiratory breathing since birth, worse when supine and feeding; flexible scope shows prolapsing aryepiglottic folds.

FJ1486.name: Right brachialis
FJ1486.details: Deep anterior arm muscle from the distal humerus to the coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity, forming the floor of the cubital fossa; musculocutaneous nerve with a small radial contribution; pure elbow flexor in all forearm positions.
FJ1486.clinicalCondition: Brachialis strain ('climber's elbow' region) — forceful eccentric elbow flexion in climbing tears fibers, causing deep anterior elbow ache.
FJ1486.clinicalScenario: A boulderer develops deep aching in the front of the elbow after dynamic moves, with pain on fully flexing against load.

FJ1487.name: Right brachioradialis
FJ1487.details: From the lateral supracondylar ridge to the distal radius; radial nerve proper (before its bifurcation); flexes the elbow best in the mid-prone position and forms the lateral boundary of the cubital fossa; tested in the C6 brachioradialis reflex.
FJ1487.clinicalCondition: Radial nerve palsy sign — in 'Saturday night palsy' this muscle is weak with wrist drop, since its branch arises near the spiral groove.
FJ1487.clinicalScenario: A man wakes after sleeping with his arm over a chair; he has wrist drop, a weak brachioradialis, and a reduced brachioradialis reflex.

FJ1524.name: Right cervical rotator
FJ1524.details: Rotatores cervicis are minute muscles between adjacent cervical spinous and transverse processes, deep to multifidus; dorsal rami; segmental rotation and proprioceptive monitoring of intervertebral motion.
FJ1524.clinicalCondition: Proprioceptive neck dysfunction context — injury to these deep segmental muscles after whiplash impairs head repositioning sense and balance.
FJ1524.clinicalScenario: A whiplash patient feels 'unsure' of head position and fails joint position error testing despite normal imaging.

FJ2547.name: Right coccygeus
FJ2547.details: Posterior part of the pelvic diaphragm, from the ischial spine to the lateral sacrum and coccyx, overlying the sacrospinous ligament; branches of S4–S5; supports pelvic viscera and flexes the coccyx.
FJ2547.clinicalCondition: Pelvic floor support failure — weakness of the diaphragm including this muscle contributes to pelvic organ prolapse.
FJ2547.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman with chronic straining has a rectocele and pelvic pressure; pelvic floor assessment shows globally weak diaphragm contraction.

FJ1488.name: Right coracobrachialis
FJ1488.details: From the coracoid process (with short head of biceps) to the medial mid-humerus; the musculocutaneous nerve pierces it; flexes and adducts the arm; a guide to the axillary artery in the arm.
FJ1488.clinicalCondition: Musculocutaneous nerve lesion localization — because the nerve pierces this muscle, proximal entrapment here weakens elbow flexion and forearm sensation.
FJ1488.clinicalScenario: After a shoulder dislocation, a patient has weak elbow flexion and numbness along the lateral forearm, implicating the musculocutaneous nerve.

FJ1556.name: Right digastric
FJ1556.details: Two bellies joined by an intermediate tendon slung to the hyoid: anterior belly from the mandible (mylohyoid nerve, V3), posterior belly from the mastoid notch (facial nerve); elevates the hyoid and depresses the mandible; bounds the submandibular triangle.
FJ1556.clinicalCondition: Neck dissection landmark — its posterior belly marks the level of the spinal accessory nerve and the carotid sheath contents in level II dissection.
FJ1556.clinicalScenario: During submandibular gland excision, the surgeon uses the digastric tendon to define the dissection plane and protect the marginal mandibular nerve.

FJ1579.name: Right digastric
FJ1579.details: Suprahyoid muscle whose two embryologically distinct bellies reflect their different nerves (V3 anteriorly, VII posteriorly); the tendon between them perforates stylohyoid and anchors to the hyoid bone.
FJ1579.clinicalCondition: Submental swelling differential — digastric region lymph nodes and the submandibular gland beneath it are assessed in oral cavity infections and tumors.
FJ1579.clinicalScenario: A patient with a dental abscess has tender submandibular swelling; the clinician palpates the region between the digastric bellies for spread of infection.

FJ1489.name: Right extensor carpi radialis brevis
FJ1489.details: From the lateral epicondyle (common extensor origin) to the base of the third metacarpal; posterior interosseous nerve; extends and abducts the wrist and stabilizes it during grip.
FJ1489.clinicalCondition: Lateral epicondylitis ('tennis elbow') — degenerative tendinopathy begins mainly in this tendon's origin at the lateral epicondyle.
FJ1489.clinicalScenario: A 40-year-old decorator has lateral elbow pain shaking hands and lifting a kettle; tenderness sits just distal to the lateral epicondyle.

FJ1490.name: Right extensor carpi radialis longus
FJ1490.details: From the lateral supracondylar ridge to the base of the second metacarpal; radial nerve proper; extends and radially deviates the wrist; spared in posterior interosseous lesions, so wrist extension survives with radial drift.
FJ1490.clinicalCondition: PIN palsy differentiation — preserved action of this muscle produces radially deviated wrist extension, distinguishing PIN from radial nerve trunk lesions.
FJ1490.clinicalScenario: A man cannot extend his fingers, but wrist extension is strong with radial deviation, localizing the lesion to the posterior interosseous nerve.

FJ1472.name: Right extensor carpi ulnaris
FJ1472.details: From the lateral epicondyle and posterior ulna through the sixth dorsal compartment (in its own fibro-osseous tunnel) to the base of the fifth metacarpal; posterior interosseous nerve; extends and adducts the wrist; key dynamic stabilizer of the distal radioulnar joint.
FJ1472.clinicalCondition: ECU tendinitis and subsheath subluxation — repetitive rotation in racquet sports snaps the tendon out of its ulnar groove, causing painful clicking.
FJ1472.clinicalScenario: A tennis player reports ulnar wrist pain with an audible snap on supination; ultrasound shows the ECU tendon subluxing from its groove.

FJ1517.name: Right extensor carpi ulnaris
FJ1517.details: Medial-most wrist extensor whose tendon lies in the groove on the dorsal ulna, stabilized by the triangular fibrocartilage complex nearby; posterior interosseous innervation; balances radial extensors during power grip.
FJ1517.clinicalCondition: Triangular fibrocartilage complex injury association — ulnar-sided wrist pain after a fall often involves both the TFCC and this tendon.
FJ1517.clinicalScenario: After falling on an outstretched hand, a gymnast has ulnar wrist pain on rotation; MRI shows a TFCC tear with ECU tenosynovitis.

FJ1491.name: Right extensor digiti minimi
FJ1491.details: Slender muscle from the lateral epicondyle through the fifth dorsal compartment to the little finger's extensor expansion; posterior interosseous nerve; provides independent extension of the fifth digit.
FJ1491.clinicalCondition: Rheumatoid extensor tendon rupture (Vaughan–Jackson) — attrition over the distal ulna ruptures the little finger extensor first, then spreads radially.
FJ1491.clinicalScenario: A rheumatoid patient notices the little finger will no longer straighten; within months the ring finger follows, indicating sequential tendon rupture.

FJ1492.name: Right extensor digitorum
FJ1492.details: Main finger extensor from the lateral epicondyle through the fourth dorsal compartment, dividing into four tendons joined by juncturae tendinum over the metacarpals; posterior interosseous nerve; extends the metacarpophalangeal joints.
FJ1492.clinicalCondition: Posterior interosseous nerve palsy — loss of this muscle's action produces finger drop at the MCP joints with preserved wrist extension.
FJ1492.clinicalScenario: A man with a radial neck fracture cannot extend his fingers or thumb, though he extends the wrist with radial deviation.

FJ1406.name: Right extensor digitorum longus
FJ1406.details: Anterior leg muscle from the lateral tibial condyle and fibula to the dorsal expansions of toes 2–5; deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5); extends the toes and dorsiflexes the ankle; its tendon forms the lateral part of the ankle extensor mass.
FJ1406.clinicalCondition: Anterior compartment syndrome — swelling after fracture or exertion raises pressure around this muscle and the deep fibular nerve, threatening foot dorsiflexion.
FJ1406.clinicalScenario: A footballer develops severe shin pain and pain on passive toe flexion after a match; the anterior compartment feels tense and woody.

FJ1407.name: Right extensor hallucis brevis
FJ1407.details: Part of extensor digitorum brevis on the dorsum of the foot, from the calcaneus to the base of the great toe's proximal phalanx; deep fibular nerve; extends the hallux at the MTP joint.
FJ1407.clinicalCondition: EMG landmark — this muscle is sampled to distinguish L5 radiculopathy (abnormal) from common fibular neuropathy at the fibular head (spared).
FJ1407.clinicalScenario: In a foot-drop workup, needle EMG of this muscle shows denervation, supporting an L5 root lesion rather than a fibular head compression.

FJ1408.name: Right extensor hallucis longus
FJ1408.details: Anterior leg muscle from the fibula and interosseous membrane to the distal phalanx of the great toe, crossing in front of the dorsalis pedis pulse; deep fibular nerve (L5); extends the hallux and dorsiflexes the ankle.
FJ1408.clinicalCondition: L5 radiculopathy sign — weakness of great toe extension is a sensitive bedside marker of L5 root involvement.
FJ1408.clinicalScenario: A man with back pain radiating to the dorsum of the foot cannot extend his big toe against resistance on the affected side.

FJ1493.name: Right extensor indicis
FJ1493.details: Deep posterior forearm muscle from the ulna and interosseous membrane through the fourth dorsal compartment to join the index extensor expansion; posterior interosseous nerve; gives the index finger independent extension for pointing.
FJ1493.clinicalCondition: Tendon transfer donor — its independent motor makes it the classic transfer to restore thumb extension after extensor pollicis longus rupture (EIP transfer).
FJ1493.clinicalScenario: A rheumatoid patient who lost thumb extension regains it after the extensor indicis tendon is rerouted to the thumb.

FJ1494.name: Right extensor pollicis brevis
FJ1494.details: From the radius and interosseous membrane through the first dorsal compartment to the base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; posterior interosseous nerve; extends the thumb at the MCP joint and forms the lateral snuffbox border with abductor pollicis longus.
FJ1494.clinicalCondition: De Quervain's tenosynovitis — it shares the stenosed first compartment sheath with abductor pollicis longus, causing radial wrist pain.
FJ1494.clinicalScenario: A golfer has pain over the radial styloid when gripping the club; thumb tuck with ulnar deviation sharply reproduces it.

FJ1495.name: Right extensor pollicis longus
FJ1495.details: From the ulna and interosseous membrane, hooking around Lister's tubercle through the third dorsal compartment to the thumb's distal phalanx; posterior interosseous nerve; extends the interphalangeal joint and forms the medial border of the snuffbox.
FJ1495.clinicalCondition: Delayed EPL rupture — attrition at Lister's tubercle ruptures the tendon weeks after a distal radius fracture, even minimally displaced ones.
FJ1495.clinicalScenario: Six weeks after a Colles fracture healed, a woman suddenly cannot extend her thumb tip or lift the thumb off a flat table.

FJ1452.name: Right external oblique
FJ1452.details: Superficial anterolateral abdominal muscle from ribs 5–12 running inferomedially; its aponeurosis forms the anterior rectus sheath, the inguinal ligament, and the superficial inguinal ring; lower intercostal and subcostal nerves; rotates and flexes the trunk.
FJ1452.clinicalCondition: Inguinal hernia anatomy — the superficial ring in its aponeurosis transmits indirect hernias, while direct hernias push through the posterior wall medially.
FJ1452.clinicalScenario: A man has a groin bulge emerging above and medial to the pubic tubercle that enlarges on coughing; the ring is examined through the aponeurosis.

FJ1412.name: Right flexor accessorius
FJ1412.details: Also called quadratus plantae; a second-layer sole muscle from the calcaneus joining the flexor digitorum longus tendon; lateral plantar nerve; straightens the oblique pull of FDL so the toes flex in line with the foot.
FJ1412.clinicalCondition: Master knot of Henry relevance — FDL and flexor hallucis longus cross just medial to this muscle, a site of triggering and surgical confusion in the midfoot.
FJ1412.clinicalScenario: During tendon transfer surgery in the sole, the surgeon identifies the crossing of the long flexor tendons beside this muscle.

FJ1496.name: Right flexor carpi radialis
FJ1496.details: From the medial epicondyle (common flexor origin) through its own compartment in the flexor retinaculum to the bases of metacarpals 2–3; median nerve; flexes and abducts the wrist; the radial artery pulse lies just lateral to its tendon.
FJ1496.clinicalCondition: FCR tendinitis — degeneration within its tight fibro-osseous tunnel, often with scaphotrapezial arthritis, causes radial volar wrist pain.
FJ1496.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman has aching at the thumb base and pain on resisted wrist flexion and radial deviation; imaging shows trapezial arthritis.

FJ1413.name: Right flexor digitorum brevis
FJ1413.details: First/second-layer sole muscle from the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis, splitting into four tendons that divide around flexor digitorum longus (the foot's Camper chiasm) to the middle phalanges; medial plantar nerve; flexes the lesser toes.
FJ1413.clinicalCondition: Intrinsic foot weakness contribution — its failure in diabetic neuropathy shifts load to the long flexors, promoting claw toes and ulcer-prone pressure points.
FJ1413.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man develops clawing of the lesser toes with callus under the metatarsal heads from intrinsic muscle imbalance.

FJ1414.name: Right flexor digitorum longus
FJ1414.details: Deep posterior leg muscle from the tibia, passing behind the medial malleolus (between tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus) to the distal phalanges of toes 2–5; tibial nerve; flexes the toes and supports the arch at push-off.
FJ1414.clinicalCondition: Medial ankle tenosynovitis differential — inflammation of its sheath behind the medial malleolus mimics posterior tibial tendon dysfunction.
FJ1414.clinicalScenario: A runner reports pain and swelling behind the medial malleolus, with pain on resisted toe flexion but a normal single-leg heel raise.

FJ1497.name: Right flexor digitorum profundus
FJ1497.details: Deep anterior forearm muscle from the ulna and interosseous membrane to the distal phalanges; lateral half by the anterior interosseous nerve (median), medial half by the ulnar nerve; the only flexor of the distal interphalangeal joints.
FJ1497.clinicalCondition: Jersey finger — forced extension of a flexed finger avulses this tendon from the distal phalanx, classically the ring finger.
FJ1497.clinicalScenario: A rugby player grabs an opponent's jersey and cannot flex the tip of his ring finger; the tendon has retracted into the palm.

FJ1475.name: Right flexor digitorum superficialis
FJ1475.details: Intermediate anterior forearm muscle from the medial epicondyle, coronoid, and radius to the middle phalanges, its tendons splitting around profundus (Camper's chiasm); median nerve; flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints.
FJ1475.clinicalCondition: Zone II flexor injury complexity — superficialis and profundus share a tight sheath in the fingers ('no man's land'), where repairs readily adhere.
FJ1475.clinicalScenario: After a glass laceration over the proximal phalanx, a patient cannot flex the finger's middle joint; surgical exploration finds both flexor tendons divided.

FJ1499.name: Right flexor digitorum superficialis
FJ1499.details: Two-headed (humeroulnar and radial) flexor whose independent slips allow individual finger PIP flexion; tested by holding the other fingers extended to inactivate profundus via its common belly; median nerve supply.
FJ1499.clinicalCondition: Superficialis function testing — isolated loss of PIP flexion with intact DIP flexion localizes injury to this tendon alone.
FJ1499.clinicalScenario: A chef slices the front of his index finger; with the other fingers held down he cannot bend its middle joint, proving superficialis division.

FJ1415.name: Right flexor hallucis longus
FJ1415.details: Deep posterior leg muscle from the fibula, grooving the talus and sustentaculum tali, passing under the knot of Henry to the distal phalanx of the hallux; tibial nerve; flexes the great toe, vital for push-off and pointe work.
FJ1415.clinicalCondition: Dancer's tendinitis — stenosing tenosynovitis of this tendon at the talar groove causes posterior ankle pain and triggering of the big toe.
FJ1415.clinicalScenario: A ballet dancer has posteromedial ankle pain and the big toe catches on demi-pointe; pain reproduces with thumb pressure behind the ankle.

FJ1469M.name: Right flexor pollicis brevis
FJ1469M.details: Thenar muscle from the flexor retinaculum and trapezium to the lateral base of the thumb's proximal phalanx (sesamoid in tendon); superficial head by the median recurrent branch, deep head by the ulnar deep branch; flexes the MCP joint.
FJ1469M.clinicalCondition: Thenar function in combined nerve lesions — its dual supply means thumb flexion may persist when either the median or ulnar nerve alone is injured.
FJ1469M.clinicalScenario: A patient with carpal tunnel syndrome retains some thumb flexion because the deep, ulnar-supplied head of this muscle still works.

FJ1498.name: Right flexor pollicis longus
FJ1498.details: Deep anterior forearm muscle from the radius and interosseous membrane, through the carpal tunnel in the radial bursa, to the thumb's distal phalanx; anterior interosseous nerve (median); sole flexor of the thumb's interphalangeal joint.
FJ1498.clinicalCondition: Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome — combined paralysis of this muscle and the index profundus abolishes the pinch 'OK' sign, making a flattened circle.
FJ1498.clinicalScenario: A man after a viral illness cannot pinch a sheet of paper; his attempted OK sign is a teardrop because the thumb tip will not flex.

FJ1416.name: Right gemellus inferior
FJ1416.details: Short lateral hip rotator below the obturator internus tendon, from the ischial tuberosity to the medial greater trochanter; nerve to quadratus femoris; part of the 'triceps coxae' complex stabilizing the femoral head posteriorly.
FJ1416.clinicalCondition: Deep gluteal syndrome — the short external rotators beneath piriformis can irritate the adjacent sciatic nerve, mimicking lumbar radiculopathy.
FJ1416.clinicalScenario: A cyclist has deep buttock pain radiating down the thigh with normal spinal imaging and a negative straight-leg raise.

FJ1417.name: Right gemellus superior
FJ1417.details: Small rotator from the ischial spine above the obturator internus tendon to the greater trochanter; nerve to obturator internus (L5–S2); with its twin and obturator internus acts as one functional unit in hip lateral rotation.
FJ1417.clinicalCondition: Posterior hip surgical anatomy relevance — the short rotators including this muscle are detached and repaired in the posterior approach to hip arthroplasty.
FJ1417.clinicalScenario: During total hip replacement via the posterior approach, the surgeon tags and later repairs the short rotators to reduce dislocation risk.

FJ2750.name: Right genioglossus
FJ2750.details: Fan-shaped extrinsic tongue muscle from the mental spine of the mandible radiating into the tongue and hyoid; hypoglossal nerve (CN XII); protrudes the tongue and keeps it forward, guarding the airway.
FJ2750.clinicalCondition: Hypoglossal palsy sign and obstructive sleep apnea — the paralyzed tongue deviates toward the lesion, and loss of this muscle's tone collapses the airway in sleep.
FJ2750.clinicalScenario: After carotid endarterectomy, a man's protruded tongue deviates to the operated side, indicating hypoglossal nerve injury.

FJ1580.name: Right geniohyoid
FJ1580.details: Narrow suprahyoid muscle above mylohyoid, from the inferior mental spine to the hyoid body; C1 fibers traveling with the hypoglossal nerve; draws the hyoid forward and upward during swallowing and helps depress the mandible.
FJ1580.clinicalCondition: Swallowing mechanics relevance — its hyoid excursion is measured in dysphagia studies; hyoid suspension surgery for sleep apnea anchors this complex.
FJ1580.clinicalScenario: Videofluoroscopy in a stroke patient shows reduced hyoid forward movement with residue in the valleculae, prompting swallow therapy.

FJ1418.name: Right gluteus maximus
FJ1418.details: Largest hip extensor, from the ilium, sacrum, and sacrotuberous ligament to the iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity; inferior gluteal nerve (L5–S2); extends and laterally rotates the hip, essential for rising, climbing, and running.
FJ1418.clinicalCondition: Inferior gluteal nerve injury — damage after posterior hip surgery or pelvic fracture weakens rising from a chair and stair climbing, though gait is fairly preserved.
FJ1418.clinicalScenario: After fixation of an acetabular fracture, a patient cannot rise from a low chair without pushing on his thighs.

FJ1419.name: Right gluteus medius
FJ1419.details: Fan-shaped abductor from the external ilium between the gluteal lines to the lateral greater trochanter; superior gluteal nerve (L4–S1); abducts the hip and, critically, prevents pelvic drop on the swing side during walking.
FJ1419.clinicalCondition: Trendelenburg gait — superior gluteal nerve or muscle failure lets the pelvis fall toward the unsupported side with each step.
FJ1419.clinicalScenario: A woman after hip replacement lurches over the operated side; standing on that leg, her pelvis drops on the opposite side.

FJ1420.name: Right gluteus minimus
FJ1420.details: Deepest gluteal muscle, from the external ilium below medius to the anterior greater trochanter; superior gluteal nerve; abducts and medially rotates the hip and stabilizes the femoral head in the socket.
FJ1420.clinicalCondition: Gluteal tendinopathy ('rotator cuff tear of the hip') — degenerative tearing of minimus and medius insertions causes lateral hip pain and abductor weakness in older adults.
FJ1420.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old woman has lateral hip pain lying on that side and weak abduction; MRI shows a gluteus minimus insertional tear.

FJ1421.name: Right gracilis
FJ1421.details: Long medial thigh strap from the pubic ramus to the pes anserinus on the medial tibia; obturator nerve (anterior division); adducts the hip and flexes the knee; expendable, so widely used as a flap and graft.
FJ1421.clinicalCondition: Gracilis free-flap reconstruction — its reliable pedicle and expendability make it a workhorse flap for facial reanimation and perineal reconstruction.
FJ1421.clinicalScenario: A patient with long-standing facial palsy receives a gracilis free muscle transfer, neurotized to power a new smile.

FJ2751.name: Right hyoglossus
FJ2751.details: Flat extrinsic tongue muscle from the greater horn of the hyoid to the side of the tongue; hypoglossal nerve; depresses and retrudes the tongue; the lingual artery passes deep to it while the hypoglossal nerve and lingual vein run on its surface.
FJ2751.clinicalCondition: Lingual artery ligation landmark — the artery is found deep to this muscle in the submandibular triangle when controlling tongue hemorrhage.
FJ2751.clinicalScenario: For uncontrolled bleeding from a tongue tumor, the surgeon exposes the lingual artery on the deep surface of hyoglossus in the neck.

FJ1422.name: Right iliacus
FJ1422.details: From the iliac fossa and ala of the sacrum, joining psoas major under the inguinal ligament to the lesser trochanter; femoral nerve branches (L2–L4); together with psoas forms iliopsoas, the chief hip flexor.
FJ1422.clinicalCondition: Iliacus hematoma causing femoral neuropathy — bleeding into this muscle in anticoagulated patients compresses the femoral nerve within its fascial compartment.
FJ1422.clinicalScenario: A man on warfarin develops groin pain, a flexed hip, and quadriceps weakness; CT shows a large iliacus hematoma compressing the nerve.

FJ2549.name: Right iliococcygeus
FJ2549.details: Posterior sheet of levator ani from the tendinous arch of the obturator fascia to the anococcygeal raphe and coccyx; pudendal and direct sacral branches; forms the shelf supporting the pelvic organs.
FJ2549.clinicalCondition: Pelvic organ prolapse — descent and thinning of the levator plate including this sheet permits uterine and vaginal prolapse.
FJ2549.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman has a visible vaginal bulge and pelvic heaviness at day's end; examination confirms stage III uterovaginal prolapse.

FJ1526.name: Right iliocostalis cervicis
FJ1526.details: Lateral column of erector spinae in the neck, from the angles of ribs 3–6 to the posterior tubercles of C4–C6 transverse processes; dorsal rami; extends and laterally flexes the cervical spine.
FJ1526.clinicalCondition: Mechanical neck pain contribution — overload of the lateral extensor column produces posterolateral neck ache in sustained postures.
FJ1526.clinicalScenario: A hairdresser develops one-sided neck pain after long shifts with her head tilted, tender over the lateral extensor mass.

FJ1527.name: Right iliocostalis lumborum
FJ1527.details: Lateral erector spinae in the loin, from the sacrum and iliac crest (via the erector spinae aponeurosis) to the angles of the lower six ribs; dorsal rami; extends and side-flexes the lumbar spine.
FJ1527.clinicalCondition: Myofascial low back pain — strain of the erector spinae mass including this column is a common source of acute lumbago after lifting.
FJ1527.clinicalScenario: A gardener 'puts his back out' lifting a pot, with spasm and tenderness in the paravertebral muscles and pain on extension.

FJ1528.name: Right iliocostalis thoracis
FJ1528.details: Lateral erector spinae of the thorax, from the angles of the lower six ribs to the angles of the upper six ribs and C7 transverse process; dorsal rami; extends the thoracic spine and resists flexion.
FJ1528.clinicalCondition: Postural thoracic pain — sustained flexed sitting overloads the thoracic extensors, causing aching across the mid-back in adolescents and desk workers.
FJ1528.clinicalScenario: A schoolboy with heavy backpack use complains of thoracic aching; examination shows tender, fatigued extensor muscles and rounded shoulders.

FJ1345.name: Right inferior oblique
FJ1345.details: Extraocular muscle arising from the orbital floor beside the lacrimal fossa — the only extraocular muscle originating anteriorly — inserting on the posterolateral sclera; inferior division of CN III; elevates (especially in adduction), extorts, and abducts the eye.
FJ1345.clinicalCondition: Inferior oblique overaction — common with congenital esotropia, it produces upshoot of the eye in adduction and is treated by weakening surgery.
FJ1345.clinicalScenario: A child with crossed eyes shows each eye shooting upward when looking to the opposite side, prompting strabismus surgery planning.

FJ1346.name: Right inferior rectus
FJ1346.details: From the common tendinous ring to the inferior sclera; inferior division of oculomotor nerve; depresses, adducts, and extorts the eye; its fascial sheath (capsulopalpebral fascia) links it to the lower eyelid retractors.
FJ1346.clinicalCondition: Thyroid eye disease restriction — this muscle is most often thickened and fibrotic in Graves orbitopathy, tethering the eye and causing vertical diplopia.
FJ1346.clinicalScenario: A hyperthyroid woman cannot look up with the right eye and sees double vertically; CT shows a markedly enlarged inferior rectus.

FJ1500.name: Right infraspinatus muscle
FJ1500.details: Rotator cuff muscle filling the infraspinous fossa, inserting on the middle facet of the greater tubercle; suprascapular nerve (C5–C6); chief external rotator of the arm and humeral head depressor.
FJ1500.clinicalCondition: Spinoglenoid notch entrapment — suprascapular nerve compression there denervates only this muscle, causing isolated wasting in overhead athletes.
FJ1500.clinicalScenario: An elite volleyball player develops weak external rotation and visible hollowing below the scapular spine, with normal deltoid and supraspinatus strength.

FJ1551.name: Right interspinalis thoracis
FJ1551.details: Small paired slips between the tips of adjacent thoracic spinous processes, often poorly developed in the mid-thoracic region; dorsal rami; minute extensors rich in proprioceptors that monitor segmental position.
FJ1551.clinicalCondition: Segmental proprioceptive dysfunction context — these deep slips contribute little force but inform the reflex control lost in chronic back pain.
FJ1551.clinicalScenario: A chronic back pain patient shows poor repositioning accuracy of the trunk despite normal strength, reflecting deep segmental muscle dysfunction.

FJ2796.name: Right lateral crico-arytenoid
FJ2796.details: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle from the lateral cricoid arch to the muscular process of the right arytenoid; adducts the vocal fold and closes the rima glottidis. Recurrent laryngeal nerve.
FJ2796.clinicalCondition: Recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy — loss of adduction leaves the cord paramedian with a breathy, weak voice.
FJ2796.clinicalScenario: After thyroidectomy, a woman has a weak, breathy voice; laryngoscopy shows the right vocal fold immobile near the midline.

FJ1355.name: Right lateral rectus
FJ1355.details: Extraocular muscle from the common tendinous ring to the lateral sclera of the right eye; abducts the globe. Innervated by the abducens nerve (CN VI).
FJ1355.clinicalCondition: Sixth nerve palsy — abduction fails, the eye rests adducted, and horizontal diplopia results.
FJ1355.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man cannot move his right eye outward and reports side-by-side double images that worsen when looking right.

FJ1357.name: Right levator palpebrae superioris
FJ1357.details: From the lesser wing of the sphenoid above the optic canal to the right upper eyelid skin and tarsal plate; elevates the eyelid. Oculomotor nerve, superior division (CN III).
FJ1357.clinicalCondition: Ptosis in third nerve palsy — complete lid droop; sympathetic (Müller) loss alone gives only partial ptosis.
FJ1357.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman has a drooping right lid, an eye pointing down-and-out, and a dilated pupil after a sudden headache.

FJ2753.name: Right levator veli palatini
FJ2753.details: Slings from the petrous temporal bone and auditory tube cartilage down into the right soft palate; elevates the palate during swallowing and speech. Pharyngeal plexus (vagus nerve).
FJ2753.clinicalCondition: Palatal palsy in vagal lesions — the uvula deviates away from the weak side and nasal regurgitation occurs.
FJ2753.clinicalScenario: A stroke patient coughs fluids out through his nose when swallowing, and his uvula pulls over to the left.

FJ1533.name: Right longissimus capitis
FJ1533.details: Intermediate erector spinae column ascending from upper thoracic transverse processes to the right mastoid process; extends and ipsilaterally rotates the head. Dorsal rami of spinal nerves.
FJ1533.clinicalCondition: Paraspinal muscle strain — overuse or whiplash injury causes occipital and neck pain with stiffness.
FJ1533.clinicalScenario: After a rear-end collision, a driver has right-sided neck pain radiating to the mastoid and limited head rotation.

FJ1534.name: Right longissimus cervicis
FJ1534.details: Erector spinae segment from the upper thoracic transverse processes to the posterior tubercles of the C2–C6 transverse processes; extends and laterally flexes the neck. Dorsal rami.
FJ1534.clinicalCondition: Cervical strain — spasm of the neck extensors produces stiffness and a torticollis-like posture.
FJ1534.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter develops acute right neck stiffness and pain on extension after a session of heavy shrugs.

FJ1535.name: Right longissimus thoracis
FJ1535.details: Largest erector spinae part, from the sacrum and lumbar fascia to the thoracic transverse processes and lower ribs; extends and laterally flexes the trunk. Dorsal rami.
FJ1535.clinicalCondition: Lumbar strain — lifting injury causes paravertebral pain, spasm, and pain on trunk extension.
FJ1535.clinicalScenario: A warehouse worker lifts a heavy box, feels a tearing right back pain, and stands bent over with palpable spasm.

FJ1582.name: Right longus capitis
FJ1582.details: Prevertebral muscle from the transverse processes of C3–C6 to the basilar part of the occipital bone; flexes the head and upper neck. Ventral rami of C1–C3.
FJ1582.clinicalCondition: Calcific tendinitis of the longus colli group — acute neck pain, stiffness, and low fever mimicking deep neck infection.
FJ1582.clinicalScenario: A woman presents with severe neck pain, painful swallowing, and fever; CT shows prevertebral edema with calcification near C1–C2.

FJ1522.name: Right lumbar rotator
FJ1522.details: Tiny deep segmental muscle linking a lumbar transverse process to the lamina of the vertebra above; fine rotation and proprioceptive stabilization. Medial branch of the dorsal ramus.
FJ1522.clinicalCondition: Segmental stabilizer dysfunction — inhibition of these deep muscles contributes to chronic, recurrent low back pain.
FJ1522.clinicalScenario: A patient with chronic right low back pain and poor core control improves with targeted deep stabilizer retraining exercises.

FJ1359.name: Right medial rectus
FJ1359.details: Extraocular muscle from the common tendinous ring to the medial sclera of the right eye; adducts the globe. Oculomotor nerve, inferior division (CN III).
FJ1359.clinicalCondition: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia — a medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion weakens adduction while the abducting eye shows nystagmus.
FJ1359.clinicalScenario: A young woman with multiple sclerosis cannot adduct her right eye on left gaze, while the left eye beats with nystagmus.

FJ1583.name: Right mylohyoid
FJ1583.details: Flat sheet from the mylohyoid line of the mandible to the hyoid bone and midline raphe, forming the floor of the mouth. Nerve to mylohyoid (CN V3).
FJ1583.clinicalCondition: Ludwig angina — submandibular space infection around this sheet elevates the tongue and threatens the airway.
FJ1583.clinicalScenario: A man with a dental abscess has a swollen floor of mouth, drooling, and a pushed-up tongue needing urgent airway care.

FJ2798.name: Right oblique arytenoid
FJ2798.details: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle crossing from the muscular process of one arytenoid to the apex of the other; narrows the laryngeal inlet and adducts the arytenoids. Recurrent laryngeal nerve.
FJ2798.clinicalCondition: Laryngeal inlet incompetence after vagal injury — weak sphincteric closure of the inlet predisposes to aspiration.
FJ2798.clinicalScenario: After skull-base surgery, a patient silently aspirates liquids; endoscopy shows a gaping, poorly closing laryngeal inlet.

FJ1584.name: Right obliquus capitis inferior
FJ1584.details: Suboccipital muscle from the spinous process of the axis to the transverse process of the right atlas; chief rotator of the head at the atlanto-axial joint. Suboccipital nerve (C1).
FJ1584.clinicalCondition: Suboccipital muscle tension — a recognized contributor to cervicogenic headache and restricted head rotation.
FJ1584.clinicalScenario: A desk worker has occipital headaches and painful right head rotation, with tender suboccipital muscles on palpation.

FJ1585.name: Right obliquus capitis superior
FJ1585.details: Suboccipital muscle from the transverse process of the right atlas to the occipital bone between the nuchal lines; extends and laterally tilts the head. Suboccipital nerve (C1).
FJ1585.clinicalCondition: Occipital neuralgia overlap — suboccipital tightness aggravates pain radiating through greater occipital nerve territory.
FJ1585.clinicalScenario: A patient describes shooting occipital pain up to the vertex, worsened by prolonged neck extension at a computer screen.

FJ1425.name: Right obturator externus
FJ1425.details: Deep lateral rotator from the external obturator membrane and pubic/ischial rami to the trochanteric fossa of the femur; laterally rotates the extended thigh. Obturator nerve (L3, L4).
FJ1425.clinicalCondition: Deep groin strain — injury here mimics adductor tears, causing twisting-related medial groin pain.
FJ1425.clinicalScenario: A soccer player reports deep right groin pain on cutting movements, with normal adductor strength but painful external rotation.

FJ1426.name: Right obturator internus
FJ1426.details: Pelvic wall muscle exiting through the lesser sciatic foramen to the medial greater trochanter; laterally rotates and abducts the flexed thigh. Nerve to obturator internus (L5–S2).
FJ1426.clinicalCondition: Deep gluteal syndrome — tendon and bursa irritation beside the sciatic nerve causes buttock pain mimicking radiculopathy.
FJ1426.clinicalScenario: A cyclist has deep right buttock aching while seated and pain on combined hip flexion with internal rotation.

FJ1586.name: Right omohyoid
FJ1586.details: Two-bellied infrahyoid strap muscle from the scapula to the hyoid, joined by an intermediate tendon bound to the clavicle; depresses the hyoid. Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3). Landmark for neck node levels.
FJ1586.clinicalCondition: Omohyoid syndrome — a lax fascial sling lets the muscle bulge visibly in the lower neck during swallowing.
FJ1586.clinicalScenario: A young man notices a transient right lower-neck swelling whenever he swallows, with no mass found on imaging.

FJ1501.name: Right opponens pollicis
FJ1501.details: Thenar muscle from the trapezium and flexor retinaculum to the lateral border of the first metacarpal; rotates the thumb into opposition. Recurrent branch of the median nerve.
FJ1501.clinicalCondition: Median nerve injury — thenar wasting and lost opposition make pinch grip and buttoning impossible.
FJ1501.clinicalScenario: A patient with advanced carpal tunnel syndrome cannot touch thumb to little finger and drops small objects.

FJ1502.name: Right palmaris longus
FJ1502.details: Slender superficial forearm muscle from the medial epicondyle to the palmar aponeurosis; weak wrist flexion and tenses the aponeurosis. Median nerve. Congenitally absent in about 14% of people.
FJ1502.clinicalCondition: Congenital absence — a benign variation; the tendon is a favored graft donor and median nerve landmark.
FJ1502.clinicalScenario: Before tendon graft surgery, the surgeon's Schaeffer maneuver reveals the patient's right palmaris longus is absent.

FJ1427.name: Right pectineus
FJ1427.details: Flat quadrangular muscle from the pecten pubis to the pectineal line of the femur, forming the floor of the femoral triangle; adducts, flexes, and medially rotates the thigh. Femoral nerve (L2, L3).
FJ1427.clinicalCondition: Groin strain — pectineus injury causes medial groin pain on resisted adduction and hip flexion.
FJ1427.clinicalScenario: A hockey player feels a sharp right groin pull while pushing off, with tenderness just lateral to the pubic tubercle.

FJ1456.name: Right pectoralis minor
FJ1456.details: Triangular muscle from ribs 3–5 to the coracoid process; protracts and depresses the scapula and divides the axillary artery into three parts. Medial pectoral nerve.
