FJ1456.clinicalCondition: Pectoralis minor syndrome — a tight muscle compresses the neurovascular bundle beneath the coracoid in thoracic outlet syndrome.
FJ1456.clinicalScenario: An overhead athlete has right arm aching and paresthesia when pitching, reproduced by pressing over the coracoid.

FJ1428.name: Right piriformis
FJ1428.details: Pelvic muscle from the anterior sacrum exiting the greater sciatic foramen to the greater trochanter; laterally rotates the thigh. Nerve to piriformis (S1, S2). The sciatic nerve passes just below it.
FJ1428.clinicalCondition: Piriformis syndrome — muscle spasm irritates the adjacent sciatic nerve, mimicking disc radiculopathy.
FJ1428.clinicalScenario: A runner has right buttock pain radiating down the leg, worse when sitting, with a normal lumbar MRI.

FJ1429.name: Right plantaris
FJ1429.details: Small muscle from the lateral supracondylar ridge whose long slender tendon descends between gastrocnemius and soleus to the calcaneus; a weak plantar flexor. Tibial nerve.
FJ1429.clinicalCondition: Tennis leg — plantaris or medial gastrocnemius rupture causes a sudden calf pop, pain, and swelling.
FJ1429.clinicalScenario: A squash player feels a snap in the right calf mid-rally; ultrasound shows fluid between gastrocnemius and soleus.

FJ1587.name: Right platysma
FJ1587.details: Thin superficial sheet from the upper chest fascia over the clavicle to the mandible and lower face; tenses the neck skin and depresses the lower lip. Cervical branch of the facial nerve.
FJ1587.clinicalCondition: Facial nerve branch injury — platysma weakness removes neck-skin wrinkling on grimacing; neck wounds gape as it retracts.
FJ1587.clinicalScenario: After parotid surgery, a patient's right neck skin no longer wrinkles on grimacing, showing cervical branch involvement.

FJ1430.name: Right popliteus
FJ1430.details: Deep posterior knee muscle from the lateral femoral condyle to the posterior tibia above the soleal line; unlocks the knee by rotating the femur laterally on the tibia. Tibial nerve.
FJ1430.clinicalCondition: Posterolateral corner injury — popliteus damage causes knee instability and pain when descending slopes.
FJ1430.clinicalScenario: After a skiing fall, a man has right posterolateral knee pain and a feeling of giving way walking downhill.

FJ2800.name: Right posterior crico-arytenoid
FJ2800.details: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle from the posterior cricoid lamina to the muscular process of the right arytenoid; the only abductor of the vocal fold. Recurrent laryngeal nerve.
FJ2800.clinicalCondition: Bilateral abductor palsy — both cords lie near the midline causing stridor; an airway emergency after thyroid surgery.
FJ2800.clinicalScenario: Hours after total thyroidectomy, a patient develops inspiratory stridor and respiratory distress needing urgent airway intervention.

FJ1503.name: Right pronator quadratus
FJ1503.details: Quadrate deep muscle spanning the distal ulna and radius; pronates the forearm and binds the distal radioulnar joint. Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve.
FJ1503.clinicalCondition: Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome — weak pronation and pinch, shown by a flattened, oval OK sign.
FJ1503.clinicalScenario: A man cannot make a round OK sign with his right hand after a forearm injury; the pinch collapses into a line.

FJ1431.name: Right psoas major
FJ1431.details: Chief hip flexor from the T12–L4 vertebral bodies and transverse processes to the lesser trochanter; the lumbar plexus forms within its substance. Ventral rami L1–L3.
FJ1431.clinicalCondition: Psoas abscess — infection tracks within the sheath causing fever, flank pain, and a comfortably flexed hip.
FJ1431.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient has fever, right groin pain, and pain on hip extension; CT shows a right psoas collection.

FJ2550.name: Right pubococcygeus
FJ2550.details: Main levator ani component from the pubis to the coccyx and anococcygeal raphe; supports the pelvic viscera against raised intra-abdominal pressure. Pudendal nerve and direct S3–S4 branches.
FJ2550.clinicalCondition: Pelvic organ prolapse — levator weakness after childbirth allows the bladder, uterus, or rectum to descend.
FJ2550.clinicalScenario: A multiparous woman reports a vaginal bulge and pelvic pressure by evening, worse after lifting her children.

FJ2551.name: Right puborectalis
FJ2551.details: U-shaped levator ani sling from the pubis looping behind the anorectal junction; maintains the anorectal angle and fecal continence. Pudendal nerve and perineal branches of S3–S4.
FJ2551.clinicalCondition: Paradoxical puborectalis syndrome — failure to relax during defecation causes obstructed, excessively strained stools.
FJ2551.clinicalScenario: A woman strains excessively with a sense of blockage; defecography shows the puborectalis failing to relax on straining.

FJ1432.name: Right quadratus femoris
FJ1432.details: Flat muscle from the lateral ischial tuberosity to the quadrate tubercle of the femur; laterally rotates the thigh. Nerve to quadratus femoris (L4–S1).
FJ1432.clinicalCondition: Ischiofemoral impingement — a narrowed ischiofemoral space compresses this muscle, causing deep buttock and groin pain.
FJ1432.clinicalScenario: A woman has chronic right deep buttock pain; MRI shows quadratus femoris edema between the ischium and lesser trochanter.

FJ1588.name: Right rectus capitis anterior
FJ1588.details: Small prevertebral muscle from the lateral mass of the right atlas to the basilar occipital bone; flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint. Ventral rami of C1–C2.
FJ1588.clinicalCondition: Whiplash-associated disorder — injury to these deep flexors causes anterior neck pain and poor craniocervical control.
FJ1588.clinicalScenario: After a car crash, a patient has deep anterior neck pain and fails the craniocervical flexion test.

FJ1591.name: Right rectus capitis lateralis
FJ1591.details: Small muscle from the transverse process of the right atlas to the jugular process of the occipital bone; laterally flexes the head. Ventral rami C1–C2. A landmark beside the jugular foramen.
FJ1591.clinicalCondition: Jugular foramen lesions — palsies of CN IX–XI dominate clinically; the muscle guides surgeons to the foramen.
FJ1591.clinicalScenario: During skull-base surgery for a glomus tumor, the surgeon uses this muscle to locate the jugular foramen contents.

FJ1589.name: Right rectus capitis posterior major
FJ1589.details: Suboccipital muscle from the spinous process of the axis to the lateral inferior nuchal line; extends and rotates the head, bounding the suboccipital triangle. Suboccipital nerve (C1).
FJ1589.clinicalCondition: Cervicogenic headache — suboccipital spasm refers pain through the greater occipital nerve to the occiput and scalp.
FJ1589.clinicalScenario: A patient with chronic occipital headaches has exquisitely tender right suboccipital muscles and restricted head rotation.

FJ1590.name: Right rectus capitis posterior minor
FJ1590.details: Small suboccipital muscle from the posterior tubercle of the right atlas to the medial inferior nuchal line; extends the head and sends a connective bridge to the dura. Suboccipital nerve (C1).
FJ1590.clinicalCondition: Myodural bridge dysfunction — abnormal dural tension from this muscle is proposed to contribute to cervicogenic headaches.
FJ1590.clinicalScenario: A migraineur's attacks consistently begin as right suboccipital tightness after long hours of screen work.

FJ1433.name: Right rectus femoris
FJ1433.details: Central quadriceps muscle from the anterior inferior iliac spine and acetabular groove to the patella and tibial tuberosity; flexes the hip and extends the knee. Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
FJ1433.clinicalCondition: Rectus femoris strain — kicking tears the deep central tendon, producing anterior thigh pain and weakness.
FJ1433.clinicalScenario: A footballer feels a pop in the front of the right thigh while striking the ball and cannot sprint.

FJ1536.name: Right rhomboid major
FJ1536.details: From the spinous processes of T2–T5 to the medial border of the right scapula; retracts, elevates, and downwardly rotates the scapula. Dorsal scapular nerve (C4, C5).
FJ1536.clinicalCondition: Dorsal scapular nerve entrapment — pain along the medial scapular border with weak scapular retraction.
FJ1536.clinicalScenario: A rower reports aching pain between the right shoulder blade and the spine, aggravated by each rowing stroke.

FJ1537.name: Right rhomboid minor
FJ1537.details: Small muscle from the ligamentum nuchae and C7–T1 spinous processes to the medial scapular border at the root of the spine; retracts the scapula. Dorsal scapular nerve.
FJ1537.clinicalCondition: Rhomboid strain — overuse in throwing or rowing causes interscapular ache and local tenderness.
FJ1537.clinicalScenario: A painter develops right interscapular pain after days of overhead work, tender over the upper medial scapula.

FJ1434.name: Right sartorius
FJ1434.details: Longest muscle in the body, running from the anterior superior iliac spine to the upper medial tibia in the pes anserinus; flexes, abducts, and laterally rotates the thigh. Femoral nerve (L2, L3).
FJ1434.clinicalCondition: Pes anserine bursitis — inflammation at its insertion causes medial knee pain mimicking joint pathology.
FJ1434.clinicalScenario: An overweight runner has aching pain just below the right medial knee joint line, tender to palpation.

FJ1592.name: Right scalenus anterior
FJ1592.details: From the cervical transverse processes to the scalene tubercle of the first rib; the phrenic nerve crosses its anterior surface, the subclavian vein passes in front, and the artery behind. Ventral rami C4–C6.
FJ1592.clinicalCondition: Thoracic outlet syndrome — compression in the interscalene triangle affects the brachial plexus and subclavian artery.
FJ1592.clinicalScenario: A violinist develops right arm numbness and heaviness when playing overhead, relieved by resting the arm.

FJ1593.name: Right scalenus medius
FJ1593.details: Largest scalene, from the posterior tubercles of the cervical transverse processes to the first rib behind the subclavian groove; elevates the first rib and laterally flexes the neck. Cervical ventral rami.
FJ1593.clinicalCondition: Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome — the plexus is pinched between scalenus anterior and this muscle.
FJ1593.clinicalScenario: A typist has right ulnar-side hand tingling and neck pain, reproduced by the elevated-arm stress test.

FJ1594.name: Right scalenus posterior
FJ1594.details: Smallest and deepest scalene, from the posterior tubercles of the C4–C6 transverse processes to the outer surface of the second rib; elevates the rib and laterally flexes the neck. Ventral rami C6–C8.
FJ1594.clinicalCondition: Scalene myofascial pain syndrome — trigger points refer pain to the chest, back, and arm, mimicking angina.
FJ1594.clinicalScenario: A patient cleared of cardiac disease keeps having right chest-and-arm ache traced to tender scalene trigger points.

FJ1435.name: Right semimembranosus
FJ1435.details: Medial hamstring from the ischial tuberosity to the posterior medial tibial condyle; extends the thigh and flexes and medially rotates the leg. Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5–S2).
FJ1435.clinicalCondition: Hamstring strain — sprinting tears cause posterior thigh pain, weakness, and delayed ecchymosis.
FJ1435.clinicalScenario: A sprinter pulls up clutching the back of the right thigh; bruising appears along it two days later.

FJ1538.name: Right semispinalis capitis
FJ1538.details: Broad posterior neck muscle from the upper thoracic transverse processes and C7 to the occiput between the nuchal lines; chief extensor of the head. Dorsal rami. The greater occipital nerve pierces it.
FJ1538.clinicalCondition: Occipital neuralgia — the nerve piercing this muscle can be irritated by its tightness, causing shooting occipital pain.
FJ1538.clinicalScenario: A patient has electric pain from the right occiput to the crown, tender where the nerve emerges through the muscle.

FJ1539.name: Right semispinalis cervicis
FJ1539.details: From the transverse processes of T1–T6 to the spinous processes of C2–C5; extends the neck and rotates it to the opposite side. Medial branches of the dorsal rami.
FJ1539.clinicalCondition: Deep cervical extensor strain — whiplash injury to these muscles causes chronic neck ache and pain on extension.
FJ1539.clinicalScenario: Months after a collision, a driver still has right-sided neck pain that worsens when looking upward.

FJ1540.name: Right semispinalis thoracis
FJ1540.details: Thin muscle from the transverse processes of T6–T10 to the spinous processes of C6–T4; extends and contralaterally rotates the thoracic spine. Medial branches of the dorsal rami.
FJ1540.clinicalCondition: Thoracic back strain — segmental extensor injury causes mid-back pain on extension and rotation.
FJ1540.clinicalScenario: A gymnast develops right mid-back pain after repetitive back walkovers, with localized paraspinal tenderness.

FJ1436.name: Right semitendinosus
FJ1436.details: Medial hamstring from the ischial tuberosity to the upper medial tibia within the pes anserinus; extends the thigh and flexes the leg. Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5–S2).
FJ1436.clinicalCondition: ACL graft donor tendon — its harvest for reconstruction leaves mild knee flexion weakness afterward.
FJ1436.clinicalScenario: A footballer's torn ACL is reconstructed using his right semitendinosus and gracilis tendons as the autograft.

FJ1459.name: Right serratus anterior
FJ1459.details: From the outer surfaces of ribs 1–8 to the costal surface of the medial scapular border; protracts and upwardly rotates the scapula and holds it against the thorax. Long thoracic nerve (C5–C7) on its surface.
FJ1459.clinicalCondition: Winged scapula — long thoracic nerve palsy lets the medial scapular border lift off the chest wall.
FJ1459.clinicalScenario: After a viral illness, a man cannot push against a wall without his right shoulder blade winging out.

FJ1541.name: Right serratus posterior inferior
FJ1541.details: Thin sheet from the T11–L2 spinous processes to the lower borders of ribs 9–12; depresses the lower ribs and resists diaphragmatic pull. Ventral rami of T9–T12.
FJ1541.clinicalCondition: Lower rib pain syndrome — irritation around its costal attachments aggravates flank and lower thoracic pain.
FJ1541.clinicalScenario: A patient has right lower rib pain on twisting, with tenderness along the posterolateral lower chest wall.

FJ1542.name: Right serratus posterior superior
FJ1542.details: Thin sheet deep to the rhomboids, from the C7–T3 spinous processes to the upper borders of ribs 2–5; elevates the upper ribs during inspiration. Intercostal nerves T2–T5.
FJ1542.clinicalCondition: Interscapular myofascial pain — a deep ache beneath the rhomboid region is attributed to this muscle layer.
FJ1542.clinicalScenario: A seamstress has chronic right upper back aching beneath the shoulder blade, worse with deep breathing.

FJ1437.name: Right soleus
FJ1437.details: Broad flat calf muscle beneath gastrocnemius, from the soleal line of the tibia and fibular head to the calcaneal tendon; maintains posture and pumps venous blood upward. Tibial nerve (S1, S2).
FJ1437.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis — the soleal venous sinusoids are a common site for calf thrombus after immobility.
FJ1437.clinicalScenario: After a long-haul flight, a woman has right calf ache and swelling; ultrasound shows a soleal vein thrombus.

FJ1544.name: Right spinalis thoracis
FJ1544.details: Medial erector spinae component blending with semispinalis, linking lower thoracic and upper lumbar spinous processes to the upper thoracic spines; extends the thoracic spine. Medial branches of dorsal rami.
FJ1544.clinicalCondition: Paraspinal strain — overload causes localized midline back pain and spasm after heavy lifting.
FJ1544.clinicalScenario: A mover develops central right thoracic back pain and stiffness after lifting one end of a piano.

FJ1545.name: Right splenius capitis
FJ1545.details: Broad strap from the ligamentum nuchae and C7–T4 spinous processes to the mastoid process and lateral occiput; extends the head and rotates it to the same side. Dorsal rami C3–C6.
FJ1545.clinicalCondition: Splenius capitis syndrome — referred pain from this muscle reaches the vertex, mimicking headache and eye pain.
FJ1545.clinicalScenario: A patient complains of right vertex and temple pain triggered by turning the head while reversing a car.

FJ1546.name: Right splenius cervicis
FJ1546.details: From the spinous processes of T3–T6 upward to the transverse processes of C1–C3; extends the neck and rotates it to the same side. Dorsal rami of the lower cervical nerves.
FJ1546.clinicalCondition: Cervical strain — lateral neck pain and painful rotation follow injury to this muscle in whiplash.
FJ1546.clinicalScenario: A passenger in a side-impact crash has right lateral neck pain and cannot rotate fully toward the right.

FJ1595.name: Right sternocleidomastoid
FJ1595.details: From the manubrium and medial clavicle to the mastoid process; rotates the head to the opposite side and flexes the neck, dividing it into anterior and posterior triangles. Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), C2–C3.
FJ1595.clinicalCondition: Congenital muscular torticollis — fibrotic shortening in infants tilts the head toward the affected side.
FJ1595.clinicalScenario: A newborn holds the head tilted right with a firm right sternocleidomastoid lump and limited passive rotation.

FJ1596.name: Right sternohyoid
FJ1596.details: Infrahyoid strap muscle from the manubrium and medial clavicle to the body of the hyoid; depresses the hyoid after it is raised in swallowing. Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3).
FJ1596.clinicalCondition: Post-thyroidectomy strap tethering — scarred strap muscles cause a pulling sensation and visible neck tug when swallowing.
FJ1596.clinicalScenario: After thyroid surgery, a woman feels her scar pull upward painfully each time she swallows.

FJ1597.name: Right sternothyroid
FJ1597.details: Infrahyoid strap deep to sternohyoid, from the manubrium to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage; depresses the larynx and lies directly on the thyroid gland. Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3).
FJ1597.clinicalCondition: Thyroid surgery landmark — this muscle overlies the gland and is separated in the midline during thyroidectomy.
FJ1597.clinicalScenario: During a right hemithyroidectomy, the surgeon splits the strap muscles in the midline to expose the enlarged lobe.

FJ1598.name: Right stylohyoid
FJ1598.details: Slender suprahyoid muscle from the styloid process to the body of the hyoid, split by the intermediate digastric tendon; elevates and retracts the hyoid in swallowing. Facial nerve (CN VII).
FJ1598.clinicalCondition: Eagle syndrome — an elongated styloid process or calcified stylohyoid ligament causes throat pain radiating to the ear.
FJ1598.clinicalScenario: A woman has right throat pain radiating to the ear, worse on turning her head; imaging shows a calcified stylohyoid ligament.

FJ1460.name: Right subclavius
FJ1460.details: Small muscle from the first costal cartilage to the undersurface of the clavicle; anchors and depresses the clavicle and cushions the subclavian vessels beneath it. Nerve to subclavius (C5, C6).
FJ1460.clinicalCondition: Clavicle fracture protection — the muscle helps shield the subclavian artery and vein from displaced fracture fragments.
FJ1460.clinicalScenario: A cyclist fractures the right clavicle midshaft in a fall yet keeps intact pulses and no venous congestion.

FJ1373.name: Right superior oblique
FJ1373.details: Extraocular muscle from the body of the sphenoid, reflected through the trochlea pulley onto the posterolateral sclera of the right eye; intorts, depresses, and abducts the globe. Trochlear nerve (CN IV).
FJ1373.clinicalCondition: Fourth nerve palsy — vertical diplopia with a compensatory head tilt away from the lesion, worse on stairs.
FJ1373.clinicalScenario: A man tilts his head to the left and sees vertically stacked double images when reading after head trauma.

FJ1374.name: Right superior rectus
FJ1374.details: Extraocular muscle from the common tendinous ring to the superior sclera of the right eye; elevates, adducts, and intorts the globe. Oculomotor nerve, superior division (CN III).
FJ1374.clinicalCondition: Third nerve palsy — failed elevation leaves the eye deviated down-and-out, with ptosis and a dilated pupil.
FJ1374.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient presents with a drooping right lid and an eye resting down-and-out, unable to look up.

FJ1505.name: Right supinator
FJ1505.details: Deep elbow muscle wrapping the proximal radius from the lateral epicondyle, supinator crest, and annular ligament; supinates the forearm. The posterior interosseous nerve pierces it at the arcade of Frohse.
FJ1505.clinicalCondition: Radial tunnel syndrome — posterior interosseous nerve compression within the supinator causes lateral elbow and forearm pain.
FJ1505.clinicalScenario: A tennis player has right lateral elbow ache radiating down the forearm, tender a few centimetres distal to the epicondyle.

FJ1506.name: Right supraspinatus
FJ1506.details: Rotator cuff muscle from the supraspinous fossa to the top of the greater tubercle; initiates the first degrees of abduction and stabilizes the humeral head. Suprascapular nerve (C5, C6). Its tendon passes beneath the acromion.
FJ1506.clinicalCondition: Rotator cuff impingement and tear — the tendon rubs under the acromion, causing a painful arc and weak abduction.
FJ1506.clinicalScenario: A painter has right shoulder pain between 60 and 120 degrees of abduction and cannot lift the arm after a fall.

FJ2760.name: Right tensor veli palatini
FJ2760.details: From the scaphoid fossa and auditory tube cartilage, its tendon hooks around the pterygoid hamulus into the palatine aponeurosis; tenses the soft palate and opens the auditory tube. Nerve to medial pterygoid (CN V3).
FJ2760.clinicalCondition: Eustachian tube dysfunction — poor tubal opening causes ear fullness, a retracted drum, and middle-ear effusion.
FJ2760.clinicalScenario: A child with a cleft palate keeps developing glue ear because this muscle cannot open the auditory tube properly.

FJ1507.name: Right teres major
FJ1507.details: From the dorsal surface of the inferior scapular angle to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus; adducts, extends, and medially rotates the arm. Lower subscapular nerve (C5–C7).
FJ1507.clinicalCondition: Teres major strain — an uncommon isolated tear in throwing athletes causing posterior axillary pain and weakness.
FJ1507.clinicalScenario: A baseball pitcher feels a pop at the back of the right armpit during a pitch and loses throwing velocity.

FJ1508.name: Right teres minor
FJ1508.details: Rotator cuff muscle from the upper lateral scapular border to the inferior facet of the greater tubercle; laterally rotates the arm and stabilizes the humeral head. Axillary nerve (C5, C6) via the quadrilateral space.
FJ1508.clinicalCondition: Quadrilateral space syndrome — axillary nerve compression causes posterior shoulder pain, paresthesia, and teres minor atrophy.
FJ1508.clinicalScenario: A volleyball player has vague right posterior shoulder pain and weak external rotation after repeated overhead hitting.

FJ2802.name: Right thyro-arytenoid
FJ2802.details: Broad intrinsic laryngeal muscle from the inner surface of the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid; shortens and relaxes the vocal fold, lowering pitch, and forms the fold's body. Recurrent laryngeal nerve.
FJ2802.clinicalCondition: Vocal fold atrophy in recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy — loss of muscle bulk bows the fold, causing breathy dysphonia.
FJ2802.clinicalScenario: An elderly man after aortic arch surgery has a breathy voice; stroboscopy shows a bowed, flaccid right vocal fold.

FJ2803.name: Right thyro-arytenoid
FJ2803.details: Forms the muscular body of the right vocal fold, running from the thyroid cartilage to the vocal and muscular processes of the arytenoid; adjusts fold tension and mass during phonation. Recurrent laryngeal nerve.
FJ2803.clinicalCondition: Paralyzed vocal fold — medialization thyroplasty or injection repositions the fold this muscle can no longer move.
FJ2803.clinicalScenario: A woman with right vocal fold paralysis after neck surgery undergoes injection medialization to restore a stronger voice.

FJ1599.name: Right thyrohyoid
FJ1599.details: Infrahyoid muscle from the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage to the body and greater horn of the hyoid; depresses the hyoid or elevates the larynx. C1 fibers traveling with the hypoglossal nerve.
FJ1599.clinicalCondition: Impaired hyolaryngeal elevation — weak excursion after stroke or neck surgery reduces airway protection during swallowing.
FJ1599.clinicalScenario: A stroke patient aspirates thin liquids; a swallow study shows reduced hyoid elevation and incomplete laryngeal closure.

FJ1461.name: Right transversus thoracis
FJ1461.details: Fan-shaped muscle on the inner anterior chest wall radiating from the lower sternum and xiphoid to costal cartilages 2–6; depresses the ribs. Intercostal nerves. The internal thoracic vessels run just lateral to it.
FJ1461.clinicalCondition: Internal thoracic artery harvest landmark — this muscle layer marks the dissection plane during coronary bypass grafting.
FJ1461.clinicalScenario: During bypass surgery, the surgeon reflects this muscle to harvest the right internal thoracic artery as a graft.

FJ1441.name: Right vastus intermedius
FJ1441.details: Deep quadriceps component covering the anterior femoral shaft beneath rectus femoris, joining the quadriceps tendon; extends the knee. Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
FJ1441.clinicalCondition: Quadriceps strain — deep fiber injury causes central anterior thigh pain and an extension lag.
FJ1441.clinicalScenario: A sprinter reports deep central right thigh pain and a lag on straight-leg raising after maximal sprint efforts.

FJ1442.name: Right vastus lateralis
FJ1442.details: Largest quadriceps mass on the anterolateral femur, inserting through the quadriceps tendon and lateral patellar retinaculum; extends the knee. Femoral nerve (L2–L4). A preferred intramuscular injection site.
FJ1442.clinicalCondition: Injection-site complications — hematoma or abscess can follow faulty intramuscular injection into this muscle.
FJ1442.clinicalScenario: A toddler receives a vaccine into the right vastus lateralis because the deltoid muscle mass is still too small.

FJ1443.name: Right vastus medialis
FJ1443.details: Quadriceps part from the intertrochanteric line and linea aspera to the medial border of the patella; extends the knee, and its oblique fibers stabilize patellar tracking. Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
FJ1443.clinicalCondition: Patellofemoral pain syndrome — a weak oblique part lets the patella track laterally, causing anterior knee pain.
FJ1443.clinicalScenario: A teenage girl has right anterior knee pain climbing stairs and sitting through films, with visible wasting of the inner quadriceps.

FJ2806.name: Right vocalis
FJ2806.details: Medial deep fibers of the thyro-arytenoid lying along the right vocal fold margin; fine-tunes fold tension segment by segment for pitch control and voice quality. Recurrent laryngeal nerve.
FJ2806.clinicalCondition: Muscle tension dysphonia — disordered fine fold control produces a strained, effortful, easily fatigued voice.
FJ2806.clinicalScenario: A teacher develops a strained, strangled voice by each day's end; laryngoscopy shows structurally normal but hyperfunctional folds.

FJ1385M.name: Second lumbrical of left foot
FJ1385M.details: Small intrinsic foot muscle arising from the flexor digitorum longus tendons and inserting on the second toe's extensor expansion; flexes the MTP joint and extends the IP joints. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1385M.clinicalCondition: Claw toe deformity — intrinsic muscle weakness unbalances the toe, causing deformity and plantar callus formation.
FJ1385M.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient develops clawing of the left second toe with a painful callus under the metatarsal head.

FJ1385.name: Second lumbrical of right foot
FJ1385.details: Small intrinsic foot muscle arising from the flexor digitorum longus tendons and inserting on the second toe's extensor expansion; flexes the MTP joint and extends the IP joints. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1385.clinicalCondition: Hammer and claw toe — intrinsic imbalance deforms the toe, producing painful dorsal corns from shoe pressure.
FJ1385.clinicalScenario: An elderly man has a clawed right second toe rubbing in his shoes, with a painful corn over its top.

FJ1386M.name: Second plantar interosseous of left foot
FJ1386M.details: Plantar interosseous arising from the base and medial shaft of the fourth metatarsal, inserting on the medial proximal phalanx of the fourth toe; adducts the toe toward the foot's second-toe axis. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1386M.clinicalCondition: Intermetatarsal bursitis — deep forefoot pain from inflammation in the web spaces, worsened by squeezing the metatarsals.
FJ1386M.clinicalScenario: A ballet dancer has left forefoot pain during pointe work, with tenderness on transverse squeeze of the metatarsal heads.

FJ1386.name: Second plantar interosseous of right foot
FJ1386.details: Plantar interosseous arising from the base and medial shaft of the fourth metatarsal, inserting on the medial proximal phalanx of the fourth toe; adducts the toe toward the foot's second-toe axis. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1386.clinicalCondition: Metatarsalgia — intrinsic muscle weakness and overload produce aching pain under the forefoot on walking.
FJ1386.clinicalScenario: A hiker develops right forefoot ache after long descents, with pain when the metatarsals are squeezed together.

FJ2437.name: Septal papillary muscle of right ventricle
FJ2437.details: Smallest papillary muscle of the right ventricle, arising from the interventricular septum and sending chordae tendineae to the septal and anterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve, preventing systolic prolapse.
FJ2437.clinicalCondition: Tricuspid regurgitation — papillary or chordal disruption from endocarditis or trauma lets the septal leaflet flail.
FJ2437.clinicalScenario: A man with infective endocarditis develops a new pansystolic murmur and a pulsatile liver from severe tricuspid regurgitation.

FJ1549.name: set of anterior cervical intertransversarii
FJ1549.details: Series of small slips between the anterior tubercles of adjacent cervical transverse processes; assist lateral flexion and segmental stabilization of the neck. Ventral rami of cervical nerves. The vertebral artery runs close by.
FJ1549.clinicalCondition: Cervical foraminal stenosis — spondylotic osteophytes in this region narrow the intervertebral foramina and irritate nerve roots.
FJ1549.clinicalScenario: A patient has neck pain radiating into the arm; MRI shows C5–C6 foraminal narrowing from uncovertebral osteophytes.

FJ1549M.name: Set of anterior cervical intertransversarii
FJ1549M.details: Paired small muscles occupying the intervals between the anterior tubercles of the cervical transverse processes; laterally flex the neck and sense segmental position. Ventral rami of cervical nerves.
FJ1549M.clinicalCondition: Lateral flexion strain — side-impact injuries stretch these slips, causing deep lateral neck pain.
FJ1549M.clinicalScenario: A passenger in a T-bone collision has deep right lateral neck pain and guards against side-bending.

FJ1509M.name: Set of dorsal interossei of left hand
FJ1509M.details: Four bipennate muscles filling the spaces between the metacarpals of the left hand; abduct the fingers from the middle-finger axis and assist MCP flexion. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
FJ1509M.clinicalCondition: Ulnar nerve palsy — interosseous wasting gutters the back of the hand and weakens finger abduction.
FJ1509M.clinicalScenario: A racing cyclist with prolonged handlebar pressure cannot spread the left fingers, and the first web space looks hollowed.

FJ1509.name: Set of dorsal interossei of right hand
FJ1509.details: Four bipennate muscles filling the spaces between the metacarpals of the right hand; abduct the fingers from the middle-finger axis and assist MCP flexion. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
FJ1509.clinicalCondition: Cubital tunnel ulnar neuropathy — interosseous weakness and wasting accompany clawing of the ring and little fingers.
FJ1509.clinicalScenario: A man who fell asleep with his right elbow deeply flexed wakes with weak finger abduction and early clawing.

FJ1552.name: set of interspinales cervicis
FJ1552.details: Paired small muscles between adjacent cervical spinous processes; assist neck extension and provide proprioceptive feedback for segmental control. Dorsal rami of cervical nerves.
FJ1552.clinicalCondition: Chronic post-whiplash neck pain — deep segmental stabilizer dysfunction perpetuates aching and poor head control.
FJ1552.clinicalScenario: A patient with persistent neck pain after whiplash improves once deep neck stabilizer retraining is added to therapy.

FJ1552M.name: Set of interspinales cervicis
FJ1552M.details: Short paired slips bridging the bifid cervical spinous processes segment by segment; extend the neck and stabilize individual motion segments. Dorsal rami of cervical nerves.
FJ1552M.clinicalCondition: Cervical segmental strain — overload after sudden extension causes localized midline neck pain and spasm.
FJ1552M.clinicalScenario: A rugby player develops midline neck pain after a scrum collapse, with tenderness over one interspinous level.

FJ1550.name: set of interspinales lumborum
FJ1550.details: Small paired slips between adjacent lumbar spinous processes; assist extension and fine segmental stabilization of the lumbar spine. Dorsal rami of lumbar nerves.
FJ1550.clinicalCondition: Baastrup disease — closely opposed spinous processes ('kissing spines') cause midline pain on extension.
FJ1550.clinicalScenario: An elderly man has midline lumbar pain when standing extended, relieved by sitting flexed; imaging shows kissing spinous processes.

FJ1550M.name: Set of interspinales lumborum
FJ1550M.details: Short muscles occupying the lumbar interspinous spaces; extend the lumbar spine and contribute proprioceptive segmental control. Dorsal rami of lumbar nerves.
FJ1550M.clinicalCondition: Lumbar interspinous strain — sudden flexion-rotation lifting injuries cause focal midline tenderness and protective spasm.
FJ1550M.clinicalScenario: A gardener twists while lifting a pot and develops focal midline lumbar pain with an exquisitely tender interspinous gap.

FJ1462M.name: Set of left levatores costarum breves
FJ1462M.details: Twelve small muscles, each passing from a transverse process (C7–T11) to the rib immediately below near its angle; elevate the ribs and assist lateral flexion. Dorsal rami of thoracic nerves.
FJ1462M.clinicalCondition: Rib angle dysfunction — spasm of these short elevators produces sharp posterolateral rib pain on deep inspiration.
FJ1462M.clinicalScenario: A patient wakes with sharp left upper back and rib pain on breathing in, localized precisely at one rib angle.

FJ1463M.name: Set of left levatores costarum longi
FJ1463M.details: The lower four levatores costarum, each spanning two segments from a transverse process to the second rib below; elevate the ribs and assist lateral flexion of the trunk. Dorsal rami of thoracic nerves.
FJ1463M.clinicalCondition: Thoracic segmental pain — these deep slips overlie rib angles used as landmarks in manual rib-raising treatment.
FJ1463M.clinicalScenario: A manual therapist treats a patient's left mid-thoracic pain by mobilizing the rib angles where these long elevators attach.

FJ1510M.name: Set of lumbricals of left hand
FJ1510M.details: Four worm-like muscles arising from the flexor digitorum profundus tendons of the left hand; flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints. First two by the median nerve, last two by the deep ulnar branch.
FJ1510M.clinicalCondition: Lumbrical-plus finger — after profundus disruption beyond their origin, attempted flexion paradoxically extends the IP joints.
FJ1510M.clinicalScenario: After a deep left palm laceration, a patient's ring finger extends at the IP joints whenever he tries to make a fist.

FJ1510.name: Set of lumbricals of right hand
FJ1510.details: Four worm-like muscles arising from the flexor digitorum profundus tendons of the right hand; flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints. First two by the median nerve, last two by the deep ulnar branch.
FJ1510.clinicalCondition: Carpal tunnel syndrome — median-innervated lumbrical weakness degrades fine finger coordination before gross power fails.
FJ1510.clinicalScenario: A seamstress with carpal tunnel syndrome fumbles buttons because her right index and middle fingers lose fine control.

FJ1511M.name: Set of palmar interossei of left hand
FJ1511M.details: Three small muscles on the palmar surfaces of the second, fourth, and fifth metacarpals of the left hand; adduct the fingers toward the middle finger and assist MCP flexion. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
FJ1511M.clinicalCondition: Ulnar neuropathy — weak finger adduction reduces grip and key-pinch strength in the affected hand.
FJ1511M.clinicalScenario: A patient cannot keep a sheet of paper gripped between the extended left fingers when the examiner tugs it.

FJ1511.name: Set of palmar interossei of right hand
FJ1511.details: Three small muscles on the palmar surfaces of the second, fourth, and fifth metacarpals of the right hand; adduct the fingers toward the middle finger and assist MCP flexion. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
FJ1511.clinicalCondition: Guyon canal syndrome — ulnar compression at the wrist wastes the interossei while sparing sensation over the dorsal ulnar hand.
FJ1511.clinicalScenario: A long-distance cyclist has right palm numbness and weak finger adduction after weeks of handlebar pressure.

FJ1553.name: set of posterior cervical intertransversarii
FJ1553.details: Small slips between the posterior tubercles of adjacent cervical transverse processes; assist lateral flexion and extension of the neck. Dorsal rami of cervical nerves.
FJ1553.clinicalCondition: Lateral neck strain — forced side-flexion injuries cause pain and tenderness along the transverse process line.
FJ1553.clinicalScenario: A footballer struck from the side has neck pain on side-bending, with a line of tenderness behind the sternocleidomastoid.

FJ1553M.name: Set of posterior cervical intertransversarii
FJ1553M.details: Paired short muscles bridging the posterior tubercles of neighbouring cervical vertebrae; laterally flex the neck and sense segmental position. Dorsal rami of cervical nerves.
FJ1553M.clinicalCondition: Cervicogenic dizziness association — disordered proprioception from deep cervical muscles is implicated in post-whiplash unsteadiness.
FJ1553M.clinicalScenario: A whiplash patient complains of neck pain with unsteadiness turning the head; joint-position error testing is abnormal.

FJ1462.name: Set of right levatores costarum breves
FJ1462.details: Twelve small muscles, each passing from a transverse process (C7–T11) to the rib immediately below near its angle; elevate the ribs and assist lateral flexion. Dorsal rami of thoracic nerves.
FJ1462.clinicalCondition: Acute rib angle pain — spasm mimics pleuritic pain but is localized, tender, and movement-related.
FJ1462.clinicalScenario: A swimmer develops sharp right posterolateral rib pain after a tumble turn, reproduced by trunk rotation.

FJ1463.name: Set of right levatores costarum longi
FJ1463.details: The lower four levatores costarum, each spanning two segments from a transverse process to the second rib below; elevate the ribs and assist lateral flexion of the trunk. Dorsal rami of thoracic nerves.
FJ1463.clinicalCondition: Chronic thoracic ache — dysfunction at these rib-angle attachments sustains mid-back pain in sedentary workers.
FJ1463.clinicalScenario: An office worker has stubborn right mid-back aching that eases with rib-angle mobilization and postural exercise.

FJ1512M.name: Short head of left biceps brachii
FJ1512M.details: Arises with coracobrachialis as the conjoint tendon from the tip of the coracoid process, joining the long head to reach the radial tuberosity; flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm. Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6).
FJ1512M.clinicalCondition: Conjoint tendon overload — anterior shoulder pain in throwers; the tendon is also a key coracoid surgery landmark.
FJ1512M.clinicalScenario: During a Latarjet procedure, the surgeon splits this conjoint tendon while transferring the coracoid to the glenoid neck.

FJ1444M.name: Short head of left biceps femoris
FJ1444M.details: Arises from the linea aspera and lateral supracondylar line, joining the long head tendon on the fibular head; flexes the knee. Uniquely among hamstrings, supplied by the common fibular division of the sciatic nerve (L5–S2).
FJ1444M.clinicalCondition: Biceps femoris tendinopathy — lateral knee pain at the fibular head in runners, close to the vulnerable common fibular nerve.
FJ1444M.clinicalScenario: A runner has left lateral knee pain at the fibular head with intermittent tingling over the dorsum of the foot.

FJ1512.name: Short head of right biceps brachii
FJ1512.details: Arises with coracobrachialis as the conjoint tendon from the tip of the coracoid process, joining the long head to reach the radial tuberosity; flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm. Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6).
FJ1512.clinicalCondition: Biceps tendinopathy — repetitive curling overloads the conjoint origin, causing deep anterior shoulder ache.
FJ1512.clinicalScenario: A bodybuilder feels deep right anterior shoulder pain at the coracoid during heavy preacher curls.

FJ1444.name: Short head of right biceps femoris
FJ1444.details: Arises from the linea aspera and lateral supracondylar line, joining the long head tendon on the fibular head; flexes the knee. Uniquely among hamstrings, supplied by the common fibular division of the sciatic nerve (L5–S2).
FJ1444.clinicalCondition: Distal hamstring strain — sprinting tears near the fibular head cause lateral posterior knee pain.
FJ1444.clinicalScenario: A hurdler pulls up with pain behind the right knee laterally and cannot fully extend the leg when walking.

FJ1513M.name: Spinal part of left deltoid
FJ1513M.details: Posterior fibers of the deltoid arising from the crest of the scapular spine, converging on the deltoid tuberosity; extends and laterally rotates the arm. Axillary nerve (C5, C6).
FJ1513M.clinicalCondition: Axillary nerve injury — posterior deltoid weakness impairs backward arm movement after humeral neck fracture.
FJ1513M.clinicalScenario: After a displaced left surgical neck fracture, a woman cannot extend her arm backward and has a numb patch over the shoulder.

FJ1513.name: Spinal part of right deltoid
FJ1513.details: Posterior fibers of the deltoid arising from the crest of the scapular spine, converging on the deltoid tuberosity; extends and laterally rotates the arm. Axillary nerve (C5, C6).
FJ1513.clinicalCondition: Shoulder dislocation with axillary nerve palsy — the deltoid, including this part, weakens and the shoulder contour flattens.
FJ1513.clinicalScenario: After an anterior right shoulder dislocation, a rugby player cannot abduct against resistance and the deltoid looks wasted.

FJ1543.name: spinalis
FJ1543.details: Most medial column of the erector spinae, linking spinous processes of the upper lumbar and lower thoracic vertebrae to those above; extends the vertebral column. Dorsal rami of spinal nerves.
FJ1543.clinicalCondition: Erector spinae strain — medial column overload produces paravertebral pain on lifting and spinal extension.
FJ1543.clinicalScenario: A deadlifter develops acute midline back pain and palpable spasm when trying to stand fully upright after a heavy set.

FJ1543M.name: Spinalis
FJ1543M.details: Medial erector spinae component whose thoracic fibers blend with semispinalis thoracis and whose cervical fibers reach the axis; maintains upright posture and extends the spine. Medial branches of dorsal rami.
FJ1543M.clinicalCondition: Postural back fatigue — weak medial extensors ache during prolonged standing in deconditioned patients.
FJ1543M.clinicalScenario: A shop assistant has midline back aching by the end of long shifts that eases with sitting and lumbar support.

FJ1464M.name: Sternocostal part of left pectoralis major
FJ1464M.details: Larger part of pectoralis major arising from the sternum and upper six costal cartilages, inserting on the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus; adducts, medially rotates, and flexes the arm. Lateral and medial pectoral nerves.
FJ1464M.clinicalCondition: Pectoralis major rupture — the sternocostal tendon tears during bench press, causing axillary bruising and weak adduction.
FJ1464M.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter hears a pop in his left chest at maximal bench press and develops swelling in the front of the armpit.

FJ1464.name: Sternocostal part of right pectoralis major
FJ1464.details: Larger part of pectoralis major arising from the sternum and upper six costal cartilages, inserting on the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus; adducts, medially rotates, and extends the flexed arm. Lateral and medial pectoral nerves.
FJ1464.clinicalCondition: Pectoralis major tear — eccentric overload in the bench press avulses fibers, deforming the anterior axillary fold.
FJ1464.clinicalScenario: A powerlifter feels a tearing sensation in the right chest lowering a heavy bar and notices the chest fold looks hollow.

FJ2783.name: Straight part of left cricothyroid
FJ2783.details: Vertical pars recta fibers of the cricothyroid running from the cricoid arch up to the thyroid lamina; tilts the thyroid cartilage forward to lengthen and tense the vocal fold. External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.
FJ2783.clinicalCondition: External laryngeal nerve injury — damage near the superior thyroid pole removes pitch-raising power after thyroid surgery.
FJ2783.clinicalScenario: A singer cannot reach her high notes after thyroidectomy and her voice tires quickly, from external laryngeal nerve damage.

FJ2801.name: Straight part of right cricothyroid
FJ2801.details: Vertical pars recta fibers of the cricothyroid running from the cricoid arch up to the thyroid lamina; tilts the thyroid cartilage forward to lengthen and tense the vocal fold. External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.
FJ2801.clinicalCondition: Voice projection loss — superior laryngeal nerve branch injury leaves a monotone, easily fatigued voice.
FJ2801.clinicalScenario: After right thyroid lobectomy, a teacher notices she can no longer project her voice across a classroom by afternoon.

FJ1514M.name: Superficial head of left flexor pollicis brevis
FJ1514M.details: Thenar head arising from the flexor retinaculum and trapezium, inserting on the radial sesamoid and base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; flexes the thumb's MCP joint. Recurrent branch of the median nerve.
FJ1514M.clinicalCondition: Thenar wasting in carpal tunnel syndrome — late median compression flattens the eminence and weakens thumb flexion.
FJ1514M.clinicalScenario: A typist with long-standing carpal tunnel syndrome has a flattened left thenar eminence and keeps dropping coins.

FJ1514.name: Superficial head of right flexor pollicis brevis
FJ1514.details: Thenar head arising from the flexor retinaculum and trapezium, inserting on the radial sesamoid and base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; flexes the thumb's MCP joint. Recurrent branch of the median nerve.
FJ1514.clinicalCondition: Median recurrent branch injury — a thenar-space laceration can selectively paralyze thumb flexion and opposition muscles.
FJ1514.clinicalScenario: A chef slices the base of his right thumb and afterward cannot flex the thumb firmly around a knife handle.

FJ1450.name: superficial perineal muscle
FJ1450.details: Superficial transverse perineal muscle running from the ischial ramus to the central perineal body; steadies the perineal body and supports the pelvic floor outlet. Perineal branch of the pudendal nerve (S2–S4).
FJ1450.clinicalCondition: Perineal trauma and episiotomy scarring — injury here contributes to perineal pain and pelvic floor dysfunction after delivery.
FJ1450.clinicalScenario: After a difficult vaginal delivery with a perineal tear, a woman has perineal aching and pain when sitting.

FJ1600.name: Superior oblique part of left longus colli
FJ1600.details: Upper oblique fibers of longus colli from the anterior tubercles of the C3–C5 transverse processes to the anterior tubercle of the atlas; flexes and rotates the neck. Ventral rami C2–C6. The sympathetic trunk lies on the muscle.
FJ1600.clinicalCondition: Acute calcific tendinitis of longus colli — neck pain, stiffness, and painful swallowing mimicking a retropharyngeal abscess.
FJ1600.clinicalScenario: A man has severe neck pain and painful swallowing; CT shows calcification at C1–C2 with prevertebral fluid but no abscess.

FJ1387M.name: Third lumbrical of left foot
FJ1387M.details: Intrinsic foot muscle arising between the flexor digitorum longus tendons and inserting on the fourth toe's extensor expansion; flexes its MTP joint and extends the IP joints. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1387M.clinicalCondition: Claw toe progression — intrinsic failure unbalances the fourth toe, causing dorsal shoe-pressure lesions.
FJ1387M.clinicalScenario: A diabetic woman has a clawed left fourth toe with a dorsal blister needing offloading footwear.

FJ1387.name: Third lumbrical of right foot
FJ1387.details: Intrinsic foot muscle arising between the flexor digitorum longus tendons and inserting on the fourth toe's extensor expansion; flexes its MTP joint and extends the IP joints. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1387.clinicalCondition: Intrinsic-minus foot in diabetic neuropathy — lumbrical loss drives clawing and raises forefoot ulcer risk.
FJ1387.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man is found to have a clawed right fourth toe and a pre-ulcerative callus at its tip.

FJ1388M.name: Third plantar interosseous of left foot
FJ1388M.details: Plantar interosseous arising from the base and medial shaft of the fifth metatarsal, inserting on the medial proximal phalanx of the little toe; adducts the fifth toe toward the foot's axis. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1388M.clinicalCondition: Forefoot splaying — interosseous weakness contributes to toe drift and metatarsalgia in narrow, high-heeled footwear.
FJ1388M.clinicalScenario: A woman who wears narrow heels daily has left forefoot ache and early splaying of the outer toes.

FJ1388.name: Third plantar interosseous of right foot
FJ1388.details: Plantar interosseous arising from the base and medial shaft of the fifth metatarsal, inserting on the medial proximal phalanx of the little toe; adducts the fifth toe toward the foot's axis. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1388.clinicalCondition: Lateral forefoot overload — weakness here accompanies fifth-ray pain in cavus feet and supinators.
FJ1388.clinicalScenario: A trail runner with high arches has right lateral forefoot pain and callus beneath the fifth metatarsal head.

FJ1525.name: thoracic rotator
FJ1525.details: Deep segmental rotatores muscles linking thoracic transverse processes to the lamina and spinous process above; assist rotation and proprioceptive stabilization. Medial branches of the dorsal rami.
FJ1525.clinicalCondition: Thoracic segmental dysfunction — deep rotator inhibition is linked to recurrent, same-level mid-back pain episodes.
FJ1525.clinicalScenario: A rower keeps straining the same mid-thoracic segment; rehabilitation targets deep rotator and multifidus control.

FJ1525M.name: Thoracic rotator
FJ1525M.details: Rotatores thoracis slips spanning one or two segments between transverse and spinous processes; fine-tune thoracic rotation and posture. Medial branches of the dorsal rami.
FJ1525M.clinicalCondition: Segmental thoracic strain — sudden twisting lifts cause focal pain beside one thoracic spinous process.
FJ1525M.clinicalScenario: An office worker twists to lift a file box and develops one-sided mid-back pain next to a single vertebra.

FJ2809.name: Transverse arytenoid
FJ2809.details: Unpaired intrinsic laryngeal muscle spanning the posterior surfaces of both arytenoid cartilages; draws the arytenoids together to close the posterior glottis. Recurrent laryngeal nerves of both sides.
FJ2809.clinicalCondition: Posterior glottic insufficiency — incomplete interarytenoid closure causes a breathy voice and microaspiration of liquids.
FJ2809.clinicalScenario: A patient with partial bilateral vagal injury has a persistent posterior glottic chink and coughs on thin fluids.

FJ1445M.name: Transverse head of left adductor hallucis
FJ1445M.details: Head of adductor hallucis running across the forefoot from the plantar ligaments of the third to fifth MTP joints to the lateral base of the great toe's proximal phalanx; maintains the transverse arch. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1445M.clinicalCondition: Hallux valgus — imbalance of this lateral pull on the great toe contributes to bunion deformity progression.
FJ1445M.clinicalScenario: A woman has a worsening left bunion, with the great toe drifting toward and under the second toe.

FJ1515M.name: Transverse head of left adductor pollicis
FJ1515M.details: Broad head of adductor pollicis arising from the capitate and the shaft of the third metacarpal, inserting on the medial base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; powers thumb adduction in pinch. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
FJ1515M.clinicalCondition: Ulnar nerve lesion — adductor weakness produces a positive Froment sign during key pinch.
FJ1515M.clinicalScenario: A patient asked to pinch a card instead flexes the left thumb tip strongly, demonstrating Froment sign of ulnar neuropathy.

FJ1445.name: Transverse head of right adductor hallucis
FJ1445.details: Head of adductor hallucis running across the forefoot from the plantar ligaments of the third to fifth MTP joints to the lateral base of the great toe's proximal phalanx; maintains the transverse arch. Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve.
FJ1445.clinicalCondition: Bunionette-toe drift complex — forefoot muscle imbalance accompanies progressive hallux valgus in runners.
FJ1445.clinicalScenario: A distance runner notices her right great toe angling outward with a tender bunion over the first metatarsal head.

FJ1515.name: Transverse head of right adductor pollicis
FJ1515.details: Broad head of adductor pollicis arising from the capitate and the shaft of the third metacarpal, inserting on the medial base of the thumb's proximal phalanx; powers thumb adduction in pinch. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).
FJ1515.clinicalCondition: Deep ulnar branch compression — selective adductor paralysis weakens pinch while finger sensation stays normal.
FJ1515.clinicalScenario: A mechanic cannot hold a spanner firmly in a right key pinch after a deep palm contusion.

FJ1554M.name: Transverse part of left trapezius
FJ1554M.details: Middle horizontal fibers of trapezius from the upper thoracic spinous processes to the scapular spine and acromion; retracts the scapula. Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) with C3–C4 contributions.
FJ1554M.clinicalCondition: Spinal accessory nerve injury — trapezius weakness causes shoulder droop and poor scapular retraction after neck surgery.
FJ1554M.clinicalScenario: After a left posterior triangle node biopsy, a patient's shoulder sits lower and shrugging is weak.

FJ1554.name: Transverse part of right trapezius
FJ1554.details: Middle horizontal fibers of trapezius from the upper thoracic spinous processes to the scapular spine and acromion; retracts the scapula. Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) with C3–C4 contributions.
FJ1554.clinicalCondition: Iatrogenic accessory nerve palsy — lymph node excision in the posterior triangle is the classic cause.
FJ1554.clinicalScenario: After excision of a right neck node, a man cannot retract his shoulder blade and the arm hangs heavily.

FJ1518M.name: Ulnar head of left flexor carpi ulnaris
FJ1518M.details: Head of flexor carpi ulnaris arising from the olecranon and posterior border of the ulna; the ulnar nerve passes between this head and the humeral head to enter the forearm. The muscle itself is supplied by the ulnar nerve (C7–T1).
FJ1518M.clinicalCondition: Cubital tunnel syndrome — the ulnar nerve is compressed between the two heads, numbing the little and ring fingers.
FJ1518M.clinicalScenario: A man who rests his left elbow on his desk has tingling in the ring and little fingers, worse at night.

FJ1516M.name: Ulnar head of left pronator teres
FJ1516M.details: Deep head of pronator teres arising from the coronoid process of the ulna; the median nerve typically passes between this head and the humeral head to enter the forearm. Supplied by median nerve branches (C6, C7).
FJ1516M.clinicalCondition: Pronator teres syndrome — median nerve entrapment between the heads causes aching forearm pain and palmar sensory loss.
FJ1516M.clinicalScenario: A carpenter has left forearm pain and thumb-side hand numbness, but no night symptoms, unlike carpal tunnel syndrome.

FJ1518.name: Ulnar head of right flexor carpi ulnaris
FJ1518.details: Head of flexor carpi ulnaris arising from the olecranon and posterior border of the ulna; the ulnar nerve passes between this head and the humeral head to enter the forearm. The muscle itself is supplied by the ulnar nerve (C7–T1).
FJ1518.clinicalCondition: Cubital tunnel syndrome — prolonged elbow flexion stretches and compresses the nerve behind the medial epicondyle.
FJ1518.clinicalScenario: A truck driver who rests his right elbow on the window frame develops little-finger numbness on long journeys.

FJ1516.name: Ulnar head of right pronator teres
FJ1516.details: Deep head of pronator teres arising from the coronoid process of the ulna; the median nerve typically passes between this head and the humeral head to enter the forearm. Supplied by median nerve branches (C6, C7).
FJ1516.clinicalCondition: Pronator syndrome — repetitive pronation hypertrophies the muscle and entraps the median nerve in the proximal forearm.
FJ1516.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter doing heavy wrist curls develops right proximal forearm ache and a positive pronator compression test.

FJ2762.name: Uvular muscle
FJ2762.details: Midline muscle within the uvula arising from the posterior nasal spine and palatine aponeurosis; shortens and thickens the uvula to help seal the nasopharynx in swallowing. Pharyngeal plexus (vagus nerve).
FJ2762.clinicalCondition: Bifid uvula — a split uvula flags a possible submucous cleft palate with velopharyngeal insufficiency.
FJ2762.clinicalScenario: A child with hypernasal speech is found on examination to have a bifid uvula and a notched hard palate.

FJ1601.name: Vertical intermediate part of left longus colli
FJ1601.details: Central vertical fibers of longus colli linking the bodies of C5–T3 to the C2–C4 vertebrae along the anterior spine; flexes the neck and resists hyperextension forces. Ventral rami C2–C6.
FJ1601.clinicalCondition: Whiplash deep-flexor impairment — delayed activation of this prevertebral flexor group drives chronic post-injury neck pain.
FJ1601.clinicalScenario: After whiplash, a driver cannot perform a pain-free chin-tuck hold, demonstrating deep cervical flexor weakness.

FJ1284.name: Check ligament of left lateral rectus
FJ1284.details: Fascial expansion from the left lateral rectus sheath to the lacrimal gland fascia and orbital wall; checks abduction and supports the globe's fascial sling.
FJ1284.clinicalCondition: Fascial disruption in orbital trauma — contributes to abnormal globe motility.
FJ1284.clinicalScenario: After a left orbital fracture, a patient shows restricted horizontal eye movement and diplopia from fascial scarring around the lateral rectus.

FJ1292.name: Check ligament of left medial rectus
FJ1292.details: Fascial expansion anchoring the left medial rectus sheath toward the lacrimal bone; part of the suspensory fascial system limiting excessive adduction.
FJ1292.clinicalCondition: Medial rectus entrapment in medial orbital wall fracture — tethered fascia restricts abduction.
FJ1292.clinicalScenario: A teenager with a fractured lamina papyracea cannot abduct the left eye and has horizontal diplopia on looking left.

FJ1334.name: Check ligament of right lateral rectus
FJ1334.details: Fascial expansion from the right lateral rectus sheath to the zygomatic bone at the marginal tubercle of the lateral orbital wall; helps suspend the globe and limit excessive abduction.
FJ1334.clinicalCondition: Scarring after orbital surgery — fascial tethering restricts eye movement.
FJ1334.clinicalScenario: Following right lateral orbitotomy, a patient develops restricted abduction and diplopia attributed to check-ligament fascial adhesions.

FJ1335.name: Check ligament of right medial rectus
FJ1335.details: Fascial band from the right medial rectus sheath to the medial orbital wall; with the muscle it is vulnerable where the medial wall is paper-thin.
FJ1335.clinicalCondition: White-eyed blowout fracture — occult entrapment in children despite minimal bruising.
FJ1335.clinicalScenario: A child struck by a ball has little external bruising but cannot move the right eye properly and vomits on attempted gaze.

FJ2771.name: Hyo-epiglottic ligament
FJ2771.details: Connects the anterior epiglottis to the posterior body of the hyoid bone, across the fat-filled pre-epiglottic space; helps tilt the epiglottis during swallowing.
FJ2771.clinicalCondition: Relevant in acute epiglottitis — swelling above this region threatens the airway.
FJ2771.clinicalScenario: A drooling, tripod-sitting child with a thumbprint sign on lateral neck X-ray is rushed to theatre for a controlled airway.

FJ1476M.name: Interosseous membrane of left forearm
FJ1476M.details: Fibrous sheet between radius and ulna; transfers axial load from radius to ulna and stabilises the distal radioulnar joint longitudinally.
FJ1476M.clinicalCondition: Essex-Lopresti injury — membrane rupture with radial head fracture causes forearm instability.
FJ1476M.clinicalScenario: A man falls on his left hand and has both elbow and wrist pain; imaging shows radial head fracture with longitudinal forearm instability.

FJ1392M.name: Interosseous membrane of left leg
FJ1392M.details: Syndesmotic sheet uniting tibia and fibula along their shafts; maintains ankle mortise width and transmits part of the load to the fibula.
FJ1392M.clinicalCondition: High ankle (syndesmotic) sprain — membrane injury heals far slower than lateral sprain.
FJ1392M.clinicalScenario: A rugby player's left foot is forced into external rotation in a tackle; squeeze test is positive for syndesmotic injury.

FJ1476.name: Interosseous membrane of right forearm
FJ1476.details: Oblique collagen fibres between radius and ulna of the right forearm; its central band is the main longitudinal stabiliser after radial head loss.
FJ1476.clinicalCondition: Chronic longitudinal instability after radial head excision — radius migrates proximally.
FJ1476.clinicalScenario: Years after right radial head removal, a patient develops wrist pain and weak grip from proximal radial migration.

FJ1392.name: Interosseous membrane of right leg
FJ1392.details: Tibiofibular syndesmotic sheet of the right leg; force travelling up it from an injured ankle can fracture the proximal fibula.
FJ1392.clinicalCondition: Maisonneuve fracture — ankle syndesmosis tear with proximal fibular fracture.
FJ1392.clinicalScenario: A skier twists his right ankle and also has tenderness below the knee; films confirm a Maisonneuve fracture pattern.

FJ1405M.name: Left calcaneal tendon
FJ1405M.details: Achilles tendon: combined tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus inserting on the calcaneal tuberosity; strongest tendon in body, surrounded by paratenon, plantarflexes the ankle.
FJ1405M.clinicalCondition: Achilles tendon rupture — sudden push-off tears the tendon, Thompson test positive.
FJ1405M.clinicalScenario: A 40-year-old squash player feels as if kicked in the left calf; squeezing the calf produces no plantarflexion.

FJ2777.name: Left conus elasticus
FJ2777.details: Elastic cricovocal membrane forming the subglottic framework; its thickened upper free edge is the vocal ligament, running from thyroid cartilage to cricoid and arytenoids.
FJ2777.clinicalCondition: Post-intubation subglottic stenosis — scarring narrows the airway at cricoid level.
FJ2777.clinicalScenario: After weeks of ICU ventilation, a patient develops progressive inspiratory stridor and is diagnosed with subglottic stenosis.

FJ2779.name: Left lateral thyrohyoid ligament
FJ2779.details: Thickened posterior edge of the thyrohyoid membrane joining the superior horn of thyroid cartilage to the greater horn of hyoid; may contain the triticeous cartilage.
FJ2779.clinicalCondition: Landmark near superior laryngeal nerve block — anaesthesia protects against aspiration during awake intubation.
FJ2779.clinicalScenario: An anaesthetist performs bilateral superior laryngeal nerve blocks before awake fibreoptic intubation in a patient with a difficult airway.

FJ1424M.name: Left long plantar ligament
FJ1424M.details: Strong ligament from plantar calcaneus to cuboid and metatarsal bases; principal support of the lateral longitudinal arch, roofing the fibularis longus groove.
FJ1424M.clinicalCondition: Arch strain in acquired flat foot — ligament overload causes plantar midfoot pain.
FJ1424M.clinicalScenario: A nurse working long shifts develops aching along the sole of her left foot with flattening of the arch.

FJ2744.name: Left pterygomandibular raphe
FJ2744.details: Tendinous junction between buccinator and superior constrictor, from pterygoid hamulus to the mandible behind the last molar; visible fold inside the cheek.
FJ2744.clinicalCondition: Key landmark for inferior alveolar nerve block — needle passes just lateral to it.
FJ2744.clinicalScenario: A dental student landmarks the pterygomandibular raphe and coronoid notch before giving a left inferior alveolar block.

FJ2763.name: Left stylohyoid ligament
FJ2763.details: Cord from the styloid process tip to the lesser horn of the hyoid, a second pharyngeal arch derivative; may partly ossify with age.
FJ2763.clinicalCondition: Eagle syndrome — elongated styloid or ossified ligament irritates adjacent nerves.
FJ2763.clinicalScenario: A woman has chronic left throat and ear pain worsened by swallowing; CT shows an elongated styloid process with ossified ligament.

FJ1438M.name: Left tensor fasciae latae
FJ1438M.details: Muscle of the lateral hip: origin anterior iliac crest and ASIS, insertion via iliotibial band to lateral tibial condyle; abducts and flexes hip; superior gluteal nerve.
FJ1438M.clinicalCondition: Iliotibial band friction syndrome — overuse irritates the band at the lateral knee.
FJ1438M.clinicalScenario: A cyclist develops sharp pain over the outer left knee on long rides, diagnosed as iliotibial band syndrome.

FJ2786.name: Left thyrohyoid membrane
FJ2786.details: Fibroelastic sheet from hyoid to the upper thyroid cartilage; pierced by the internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal vessels, which supply supraglottic sensation.
FJ2786.clinicalCondition: Internal laryngeal nerve injury — loss of supraglottic sensation risks silent aspiration.
FJ2786.clinicalScenario: After neck surgery, a patient coughs on thin fluids; endoscopy shows impaired supraglottic sensation above the left vocal fold.

FJ2787.name: Left vocal ligament
FJ2787.details: Elastic free upper edge of the conus elasticus forming the core of the left vocal fold, stretching from thyroid angle to the arytenoid vocal process.
FJ2787.clinicalCondition: Reinke oedema — swollen vocal fold ligament layer causes chronic hoarseness in smokers.
FJ2787.clinicalScenario: A long-term smoker with a rough, low-pitched voice is found to have gelatinous swelling of both vocal folds.

FJ1448.name: Linea alba
FJ1448.details: Midline aponeurotic raphe from xiphoid to pubic symphysis where the flat abdominal muscle aponeuroses interweave; relatively avascular, used for midline surgical access.
FJ1448.clinicalCondition: Epigastric hernia — preperitoneal fat protrudes through a linea alba defect.
FJ1448.clinicalScenario: A man notices a small tender midline lump above the umbilicus that appears when straining; it is a fat-containing epigastric hernia.

FJ2789.name: Median cricothyroid ligament
FJ2789.details: Thickened midline part of the cricothyroid membrane between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages; the palpable subglottic gateway used for emergency front-of-neck airway access.
FJ2789.clinicalCondition: Site of emergency cricothyrotomy — incised when intubation and oxygenation both fail.
FJ2789.clinicalScenario: In a "can't intubate, can't oxygenate" crisis, the anaesthetist palpates the cricothyroid membrane and performs a scalpel cricothyrotomy.

FJ2790.name: Median thyrohyoid ligament
FJ2790.details: Midline thickening of the thyrohyoid membrane between hyoid body and thyroid notch; lies close to the embryological thyroglossal tract descending from foramen caecum.
FJ2790.clinicalCondition: Thyroglossal duct cyst — midline swelling along this tract moves with tongue protrusion.
FJ2790.clinicalScenario: A child has a painless midline neck lump that rises when she swallows and protrudes her tongue.

FJ2749.name: Pharyngeal raphe
FJ2749.details: Midline fibrous seam on the posterior pharyngeal wall where the constrictor muscles meet, anchored above to the pharyngeal tubercle of the occipital bone.
FJ2749.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark in pharyngeal reconstruction — midline seam guides symmetrical closure.
FJ2749.clinicalScenario: During pharyngoplasty for a cleft patient, the surgeon uses the raphe to align the constrictor muscles in the midline.

FJ1405.name: Right calcaneal tendon
FJ1405.details: Achilles tendon of the right leg: gastrocnemius and soleus converge to insert on the calcaneus; a relatively hypovascular zone 2–6 cm above insertion predisposes to degeneration.
FJ1405.clinicalCondition: Fluoroquinolone-associated tendinopathy — antibiotic exposure weakens the Achilles tendon.
FJ1405.clinicalScenario: A man taking ciprofloxacin for prostatitis develops posterior right ankle pain and swelling, prompting immediate drug review.

FJ2794.name: Right conus elasticus
FJ2794.details: Elastic subglottic membrane of the right larynx whose free upper border forms the vocal ligament; the cricoid ring below it is the narrowest paediatric airway segment.
FJ2794.clinicalCondition: Laryngotracheitis (croup) — subglottic swelling here produces the classic steeple sign.
FJ2794.clinicalScenario: A toddler wakes at night with a barking cough and stridor; neck X-ray shows subglottic narrowing like a church steeple.

FJ1581.name: Right intermediate tendon
FJ1581.details: Central tendon of the digastric joining its posterior belly (facial nerve) and anterior belly (nerve to mylohyoid), anchored to the hyoid by a fibrous sling.
FJ1581.clinicalCondition: Landmark in submandibular gland excision — tendon guides safe dissection of level Ib.
FJ1581.clinicalScenario: During neck dissection, a surgeon identifies the digastric intermediate tendon to protect the marginal mandibular nerve above it.

FJ2797.name: Right lateral thyrohyoid ligament
FJ2797.details: Posterior thickening of the right thyrohyoid membrane linking superior thyroid horn to hyoid greater horn; frequently contains a small triticeous cartilage within its fibres.
FJ2797.clinicalCondition: Triticeous cartilage mimics a foreign body — small opacity misread on neck imaging.
FJ2797.clinicalScenario: A lateral neck radiograph taken for suspected fish bone shows a small calcified dot that proves to be a triticeous cartilage.

FJ1424.name: Right long plantar ligament
FJ1424.details: Strong plantar ligament of the right foot spanning calcaneus to cuboid and metatarsal bases; maintains the longitudinal arch and converts the cuboid groove into a tendon canal.
FJ1424.clinicalCondition: Plantar arch overload in pes planus — ligament strain causes deep midfoot ache.
FJ1424.clinicalScenario: A warehouse worker with flat feet reports deep aching under the right midfoot after standing all day in safety boots.

FJ2756.name: Right pterygomandibular raphe
FJ2756.details: Fibrous band uniting buccinator and superior constrictor on the right, stretching from pterygoid hamulus to the mylohyoid line region of the mandible.
FJ2756.clinicalCondition: Pterygomandibular space infection — spread here after dental injection causes trismus.
FJ2756.clinicalScenario: Two days after a difficult lower molar extraction, a patient develops worsening trismus and fever from a pterygomandibular space abscess.

FJ2764.name: Right stylohyoid ligament
FJ2764.details: Fibrous cord from right styloid process to hyoid lesser horn, lying near the external carotid artery and glossopharyngeal nerve; may ossify into a rigid chain.
FJ2764.clinicalCondition: Vascular Eagle syndrome — elongated styloid compresses the internal carotid artery.
FJ2764.clinicalScenario: A man has transient dizziness and neck pain when turning his head right; imaging shows the styloid impinging on the carotid.

FJ1438.name: Right tensor fasciae latae
FJ1438.details: Right hip muscle arising from the iliac crest near the ASIS and inserting into the iliotibial band; flexes, abducts and medially rotates the hip; superior gluteal nerve (L4–S1).
FJ1438.clinicalCondition: Greater trochanteric pain contribution — tight tensor fasciae latae overloads the lateral hip.
FJ1438.clinicalScenario: A runner reports aching over the outer right hip that disturbs sleep when lying on that side.

FJ2804.name: Right thyrohyoid membrane
FJ2804.details: Fibroelastic membrane spanning hyoid to thyroid cartilage on the right; pierced by the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal artery.
FJ2804.clinicalCondition: External laryngocele — air-filled sac herniates outward through this membrane.
FJ2804.clinicalScenario: A glassblower notices a right neck swelling that visibly enlarges when he blows and empties with gentle pressure.

FJ2805.name: Right vocal ligament
FJ2805.details: Elastic cord forming the skeleton of the right vocal fold, from the thyroid cartilage angle to the vocal process of the arytenoid; vibrates to produce voice.
FJ2805.clinicalCondition: Vocal fold nodules — phonotrauma thickens the fold at its midpoint.
FJ2805.clinicalScenario: A primary-school teacher with months of hoarseness after shouting in class is found to have bilateral vocal fold nodules.

FJ1465.name: tendinous arch of levator ani
FJ1465.details: Arcus tendineus: thickened obturator fascia running from the pubic bone to the ischial spine, giving origin to the levator ani pelvic floor muscles.
FJ1465.clinicalCondition: Paravaginal defect — detachment of vaginal support from this arch causes prolapse.
FJ1465.clinicalScenario: A parous woman presents with a vaginal bulge; examination finds loss of lateral sulci from arcus detachment.

FJ1465M.name: Tendinous arch of levator ani
FJ1465M.details: The mirror-image arcus tendineus on the opposite pelvic sidewall; the pudendal nerve travels in a fascial canal on the obturator fascia just below it.
FJ1465M.clinicalCondition: Pudendal neuralgia — nerve irritation near its fascial canal causes perineal pain.
FJ1465M.clinicalScenario: A long-distance cyclist develops burning perineal pain when sitting, relieved by standing, consistent with pudendal nerve entrapment.

FJ2552.name: Tendinous arch of levator ani
FJ2552.details: Fibrous arch of obturator fascia forming the lateral origin line of iliococcygeus; a key fixed landmark during pelvic floor reconstructive surgery.
FJ2552.clinicalCondition: Landmark in sacrospinous and paravaginal repair — sutures anchor support to this arch.
FJ2552.clinicalScenario: During prolapse surgery, the gynaecologist palpates the ischial spine and arcus tendineus to place paravaginal repair sutures safely.

FJ2553.name: Tendinous arch of levator ani
FJ2553.details: Second-side representation of the arcus tendineus; childbirth trauma near the levator origin along this arch weakens pelvic support decades later.
FJ2553.clinicalCondition: Levator avulsion after vaginal delivery — muscle torn from its origin predisposes to prolapse.
FJ2553.clinicalScenario: A woman who had a forceps delivery years ago now has stage III prolapse; imaging shows levator avulsion from the pelvic sidewall.

FJ1343.name: Tendon of right levator palpebrae superioris
FJ1343.details: Aponeurosis of the levator palpebrae superioris (oculomotor nerve) inserting into the upper tarsal plate and eyelid skin, forming the lid crease; Müller's muscle assists sympathetically.
FJ1343.clinicalCondition: Aponeurotic ptosis — age-related dehiscence of this tendon droops the lid with preserved levator action.
FJ1343.clinicalScenario: An elderly man's right upper lid droops with a high lid crease, but levator excursion measures normal, confirming aponeurotic ptosis.

FJ2807.name: Thyro-epiglottic ligament
FJ2807.details: Short elastic band anchoring the stalk (petiole) of the epiglottis to the inner surface of the thyroid cartilage just below the notch.
FJ2807.clinicalCondition: Assessed in supraglottic tumour spread — petiole involvement changes laryngeal cancer staging and surgery.
FJ2807.clinicalScenario: Laryngoscopy in a hoarse patient shows a supraglottic tumour approaching the epiglottic petiole, prompting cross-sectional imaging before partial laryngectomy.

FJ1329.name: Trochlea of left superior oblique
FJ1329.details: Fibrocartilaginous pulley fixed to the frontal bone at the superomedial orbit; the superior oblique tendon turns sharply within it to insert posterolaterally on the globe.
FJ1329.clinicalCondition: Acquired Brown syndrome — trochlear inflammation restricts tendon glide, limiting elevation in adduction.
FJ1329.clinicalScenario: A child cannot elevate the adducted left eye and compensates with a head posture; trochlear tenderness suggests Brown syndrome.

FJ1380.name: Trochlea of right superior oblique
FJ1380.details: Pulley on the right frontal bone redirecting the superior oblique tendon (trochlear nerve, CN IV) so the muscle intorts, depresses and abducts the eye.
FJ1380.clinicalCondition: Fourth nerve palsy — weak superior oblique action causes vertical diplopia.
FJ1380.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man reports double vision reading and climbing stairs, tilting his head left to fuse images — a right CN IV palsy.

FJ1932.name: Abdominal aorta
FJ1932.details: Continuation of the thoracic aorta below the diaphragm (T12), descending to bifurcate at L4 into the common iliac arteries; gives celiac, superior mesenteric, renal, gonadal and inferior mesenteric branches.
FJ1932.clinicalCondition: Abdominal aortic aneurysm — atherosclerotic dilatation, usually infrarenal; rupture causes life-threatening retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
FJ1932.clinicalScenario: A 68-year-old hypertensive smoker has a pulsatile, expansile epigastric mass; ultrasound confirms a 5.8 cm infrarenal aneurysm requiring surveillance and elective repair planning.

FJ3009.name: Accessory subsuperior branch of right posterior basal segmental artery
FJ3009.details: Small variant pulmonary arterial twig from the right posterior basal segmental artery, accompanying its bronchus to supply an accessory subsuperior part of the right lower lobe.
