FJ3009.clinicalCondition: Hemoptysis source localization — segmental bleeding points are mapped on CT angiography before embolization.
FJ3009.clinicalScenario: A bronchiectasis patient coughs frank blood; CT angiography traces bleeding to a small right basal segmental pulmonary branch, guiding targeted embolization.

FJ3010.name: Accessory subsuperior branch of right posterior basal segmental artery
FJ3010.details: Duplicate mesh of the accessory subsuperior twig of the right posterior basal segmental pulmonary artery; pulmonary segmental arteries follow the segmental bronchi to the bronchopulmonary segment.
FJ3010.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — small basal emboli may lodge in such peripheral branches.
FJ3010.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient develops pleuritic pain and tachycardia; CT pulmonary angiography shows a filling defect in a small right basal segmental branch.

FJ2211.name: Acromial branch of left thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2211.details: Branch of the thoracoacromial artery (from the second part of the axillary artery) piercing the clavipectoral fascia to supply the acromion, deltoid and shoulder joint; joins the acromial anastomosis.
FJ2211.clinicalCondition: Surgical bleeding point — encountered in deltopectoral shoulder approaches and proximal humerus surgery.
FJ2211.clinicalScenario: During left shoulder arthroplasty, brisk bleeding near the coracoacromial region from an acromial branch is controlled before the joint is exposed.

FJ2263.name: Acromial branch of right thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2263.details: Right-sided counterpart of the acromial branch of the thoracoacromial artery; supplies the acromion and overlying deltoid and anastomoses with suprascapular and circumflex humeral arteries.
FJ2263.clinicalCondition: Rotator cuff vascularity — the acromial anastomosis contributes to cuff and humeral head perfusion.
FJ2263.clinicalScenario: A surgeon repairing a right rotator cuff tear notes the acromial arterial network while developing the subacromial space and preserves it during bursectomy.

FJ2982.name: Anterior branch of lateral segmental artery
FJ2982.details: Hepatic arterial branch of the left lateral segmental artery supplying segment III of the left liver, running with the corresponding portal branch and bile ductule.
FJ2982.clinicalCondition: Left lateral sectionectomy planning — segmental arterial anatomy guides resection and living-donor graft harvesting.
FJ2982.clinicalScenario: A living liver donor's CT angiogram maps the segment II–III arterial supply so the left lateral graft can be removed safely.

FJ2985.name: Anterior branch of lateral segmental artery
FJ2985.details: Second mesh of the anterior branch of the left lateral segmental hepatic artery, supplying the anterior part of the left lateral section (segment III territory).
FJ2985.clinicalCondition: Segmental chemoembolization — superselective catheterization treats segment III tumors while sparing healthy liver.
FJ2985.clinicalScenario: A segment III hepatocellular carcinoma is treated by delivering chemoembolic beads through this branch under angiographic guidance.

FJ2975.name: Anterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2975.details: Branch of the right anterior sectoral hepatic artery supplying segment VIII in the superior part of the right lobe, following the right anterior portal pedicle.
FJ2975.clinicalCondition: Segment VIII tumor supply — dome lesions may recruit extrahepatic collaterals, complicating embolization.
FJ2975.clinicalScenario: Preoperative CT angiography shows a segment VIII tumor fed by this branch; an anatomical segmentectomy is planned preserving segments V–VII.

FJ2976.name: Anterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2976.details: Additional mesh of the anterior branch of the right anterior segmental hepatic artery, distributing to the segment VIII territory of the right lobe.
FJ2976.clinicalCondition: Post-embolization segmental infarction — sectoral arterial occlusion produces a predictable wedge of treated liver.
FJ2976.clinicalScenario: Follow-up imaging after chemoembolization of a segment VIII tumor shows the expected wedge-shaped treated zone without injury to adjacent segments.

FJ2977.name: Anterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2977.details: Further mesh of the same right anterior segmental branch; segmental hepatic arteries are effectively end arteries for their segments, matching portal venous segmentation.
FJ2977.clinicalCondition: Iatrogenic segmental ischemia — inadvertent ligation during cholecystectomy variants can infarct segment VIII.
FJ2977.clinicalScenario: A patient develops right upper quadrant pain after difficult gallbladder surgery; CT shows a small segment VIII perfusion defect from an injured arterial branch.

FJ2979.name: Anterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2979.details: Final mesh of the anterior branch of the right anterior segmental hepatic artery supplying the anterior sector (segments V/VIII) distribution, chiefly segment VIII.
FJ2979.clinicalCondition: Hepatic arterial variation — replaced or accessory right hepatic supply changes resection and transplant planning.
FJ2979.clinicalScenario: A donor liver CT reveals variant right anterior sectoral branching, prompting the transplant team to plan an extra arterial anastomosis.

FJ3406.name: Anterior cecal artery
FJ3406.details: Branch of the ileocolic artery (from the superior mesenteric artery) reaching the anterior cecal wall, anastomosing with the posterior cecal artery around the cecum.
FJ3406.clinicalCondition: Cecal bleeding and ischemia — relevant to right hemicolectomy ligation and obscure GI hemorrhage workup.
FJ3406.clinicalScenario: During emergency right hemicolectomy for a bleeding cecal tumor, the ileocolic pedicle including the anterior cecal branch is ligated near its origin.

FJ1655.name: Anterior communicating artery
FJ1655.details: Short vessel joining the two anterior cerebral arteries across the lamina terminalis, completing the anterior part of the circle of Willis; gives small hypothalamic perforators.
FJ1655.clinicalCondition: Berry aneurysm — the commonest circle-of-Willis aneurysm site; rupture causes subarachnoid hemorrhage.
FJ1655.clinicalScenario: A 52-year-old woman collapses with a thunderclap headache and vomiting; CT shows interhemispheric subarachnoid blood from a ruptured anterior communicating aneurysm.

FJ3458.name: Anterior division of left renal artery
FJ3458.details: One of two terminal divisions of the left renal artery at the hilum; gives segmental branches to the apical, upper, middle and lower segments of the left kidney.
FJ3458.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction — renal segmental arteries are end arteries, so emboli cause wedge-shaped necrosis.
FJ3458.clinicalScenario: A man with atrial fibrillation develops acute left flank pain and hematuria; CT shows a wedge-shaped mid-kidney perfusion defect from an embolus.

FJ3459.name: Anterior division of left renal artery
FJ3459.details: Second mesh of the anterior division of the left renal artery; its segmental branches supply most of the left kidney except the posterior segment.
FJ3459.clinicalCondition: Partial nephrectomy planning — segmental anatomy (avascular plane of Brödel) guides tumor excision with minimal bleeding.
FJ3459.clinicalScenario: A small left renal tumor is removed by partial nephrectomy after mapping the anterior division's segmental branches on CT angiography.

FJ3460.name: Anterior division of left renal artery
FJ3460.details: Third mesh of the anterior division of the left renal artery, branching into apical, upper, middle and lower segmental arteries within the renal sinus.
FJ3460.clinicalCondition: Renovascular hypertension — stenosis of a divisional or segmental branch can drive renin-mediated hypertension.
FJ3460.clinicalScenario: A young woman with resistant hypertension has a bruit over the left loin; angiography shows a fibromuscular stenosis of a segmental renal branch.

FJ3461.name: Anterior division of left renal artery
FJ3461.details: Fourth mesh of the anterior division of the left renal artery; multiple renal arteries and early division are common variants relevant to donor nephrectomy.
FJ3461.clinicalCondition: Transplant bench surgery — multiple segmental branches may need separate anastomoses in renal transplantation.
FJ3461.clinicalScenario: A donor kidney shows early division of the renal artery; the transplant surgeon prepares a Carrel patch to implant both divisions safely.

FJ3462.name: Anterior division of left renal artery
FJ3462.details: Fifth mesh of the anterior division of the left renal artery; segmental branches run with the minor calyces and do not anastomose across segment boundaries.
FJ3462.clinicalCondition: Traumatic segmental devascularization — renal lacerations can isolate a segment supplied by one branch.
FJ3462.clinicalScenario: After a road traffic accident, CT shows a shattered left kidney with a devascularized lower segment; selective embolization controls the bleeding.

FJ3463.name: Anterior division of left renal artery
FJ3463.details: Sixth mesh of the anterior division of the left renal artery, completing the pre-hilar branching pattern that determines left renal segmental supply.
FJ3463.clinicalCondition: Segmental aneurysm or arteriovenous fistula — divisional branch lesions cause hematuria or hypertension.
FJ3463.clinicalScenario: A patient with persistent microscopic hematuria after renal biopsy is found to have a small segmental arteriovenous fistula, closed by coil embolization.

FJ3558.name: Anterior division of right renal artery
FJ3558.details: One of two terminal divisions of the right renal artery at the hilum; gives segmental branches to the apical, upper, middle and lower segments of the right kidney.
FJ3558.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction — embolic occlusion of an end-arterial segment causes flank pain and hematuria.
FJ3558.clinicalScenario: An elderly man with untreated atrial fibrillation presents with right flank pain; CT reveals a wedge-shaped upper-pole renal infarct.

FJ3559.name: Anterior division of right renal artery
FJ3559.details: Second mesh of the anterior division of the right renal artery; the right renal artery passes behind the inferior vena cava before dividing.
FJ3559.clinicalCondition: Renal artery stenosis — atherosclerotic ostial disease reduces flow through both divisions, causing hypertension.
FJ3559.clinicalScenario: A 70-year-old smoker with flash pulmonary edema and worsening renal function has bilateral renal artery stenosis confirmed on duplex scanning.

FJ3560.name: Anterior division of right renal artery
FJ3560.details: Third mesh of the anterior division of the right renal artery, whose segmental branches supply most of the right kidney apart from the posterior segment.
FJ3560.clinicalCondition: Partial nephrectomy — divisional anatomy defines the ischemic segment during clamped tumor excision.
FJ3560.clinicalScenario: For a right lower-pole renal mass, selective clamping of one anterior division branch allows tumor excision while the rest of the kidney stays perfused.

FJ3561.name: Anterior division of right renal artery
FJ3561.details: Fourth mesh of the anterior division of the right renal artery; accessory renal arteries occur in about a third of people and alter this pattern.
FJ3561.clinicalCondition: Accessory artery and ureteropelvic obstruction — a lower-pole accessory branch may compress the renal pelvis outlet.
FJ3561.clinicalScenario: A teenager with intermittent right loin pain and hydronephrosis is found to have a crossing lower-pole vessel at the ureteropelvic junction.

FJ3562.name: Anterior division of right renal artery
FJ3562.details: Fifth mesh of the anterior division of the right renal artery, branching within the renal sinus alongside the pelvis and veins of the right kidney.
FJ3562.clinicalCondition: Selective embolization for hemorrhage — divisional branches are catheterized to stop post-biopsy or traumatic bleeding.
FJ3562.clinicalScenario: After a right renal biopsy, falling hemoglobin and a perinephric hematoma lead to embolization of a bleeding lower segmental branch.

FJ3563.name: Anterior division of right renal artery
FJ3563.details: Sixth mesh of the anterior division of the right renal artery, completing its segmental distribution to the anterior-facing segments of the right kidney.
FJ3563.clinicalCondition: Segmental ischemia in vasculitis — medium-vessel disease produces multiple small renal infarcts and microaneurysms.
FJ3563.clinicalScenario: A patient with polyarteritis nodosa and new hypertension shows multiple small segmental renal infarcts and beaded microaneurysms on angiography.

FJ1656.name: anterior inferior cerebellar artery
FJ1656.details: Arises from the lower basilar artery, loops toward the internal acoustic meatus (giving the labyrinthine artery) and supplies the anterior inferior cerebellum, flocculus and lateral pons.
FJ1656.clinicalCondition: AICA (lateral pontine) syndrome — occlusion causes ipsilateral deafness, facial palsy and ataxia with contralateral pain–temperature loss.
FJ1656.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old man suddenly develops vertigo, right hearing loss, right facial weakness and limb ataxia; MRI confirms a lateral pontine AICA-territory infarct.

FJ1656M.name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery
FJ1656M.details: Mirrored mesh of the anterior inferior cerebellar artery, a basilar branch related to the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves at the cerebellopontine angle.
FJ1656M.clinicalCondition: Labyrinthine ischemia — sudden sensorineural hearing loss and vertigo from inner-ear branch occlusion.
FJ1656M.clinicalScenario: A woman presents with abrupt unilateral deafness and severe vertigo but no weakness; MRI shows a tiny infarct in the AICA distribution involving the labyrinthine artery.

FJ3401.name: Anterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FJ3401.details: Branch of the superior mesenteric artery ascending in the groove between the pancreatic head and duodenum, anastomosing with the anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery (celiac route).
FJ3401.clinicalCondition: Pancreaticoduodenal arcade collateral — hypertrophies when the celiac trunk is stenosed, signaling median arcuate compression.
FJ3401.clinicalScenario: Angiography for postprandial pain shows an enlarged pancreaticoduodenal arcade filling celiac branches retrogradely, confirming severe celiac trunk stenosis.

FJ3075.name: Anterior inferior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3075.details: Segmental branch of the right hepatic artery supplying segment V, the anterior inferior segment of the right lobe, following the right anterior sectoral portal pedicle.
FJ3075.clinicalCondition: Segment V tumor feeding vessel — target for selective chemoembolization of right-lobe tumors.
FJ3075.clinicalScenario: Interventional radiology catheterizes this branch superselectively to deliver beads to a segment V hepatocellular carcinoma, sparing the remaining liver.

FJ2978.name: Anterior part of right apical segmental artery
FJ2978.details: Sub-branch of the apical segmental pulmonary artery of the right upper lobe supplying the anterior portion of segment S1, accompanying the apical segmental bronchus.
FJ2978.clinicalCondition: Apical segmentectomy planning — segmental vessels define the resection plane for early apical tumors.
FJ2978.clinicalScenario: For a 1.5 cm ground-glass nodule in the right apex, the surgeon dissects the apical segmental branches to perform an anatomical S1 segmentectomy.

FJ2989.name: Anterior part of right apical segmental artery
FJ2989.details: Second mesh of the anterior part of the right apical segmental pulmonary artery, distributing within the apical segment of the right upper lobe.
FJ2989.clinicalCondition: Apical tuberculosis — the apex's high ventilation–perfusion ratio favors reactivation TB with cavitation.
FJ2989.clinicalScenario: A smoker with night sweats and weight loss has a cavitating right apical lesion; sputum confirms tuberculosis and vessels are mapped before possible resection.

FJ3000.name: Anterior part of right apical segmental artery
FJ3000.details: Third mesh of the anterior part of the right apical segmental pulmonary artery supplying S1 of the right upper lobe.
FJ3000.clinicalCondition: Segmental embolism — apical segment branches are reviewed on CT pulmonary angiography for clot burden.
FJ3000.clinicalScenario: A breathless patient after long-haul travel has CT evidence of embolus extending into right apical segmental branches, confirming pulmonary embolism.

FJ3011.name: Anterior part of right apical segmental artery
FJ3011.details: Fourth mesh of the anterior part of the right apical segmental pulmonary artery; apical pleural blebs nearby are the usual source of spontaneous pneumothorax.
FJ3011.clinicalCondition: Apical bleb disease — tall young patients develop apical bullae that rupture into pneumothorax.
FJ3011.clinicalScenario: A tall, thin 19-year-old presents with sudden breathlessness and a right apical pneumothorax; apical vessels are identified during VATS bleb stapling.

FJ3409.name: Anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FJ3409.details: Terminal branch of the gastroduodenal artery descending on the pancreatic head, supplying the head of the pancreas and duodenum and anastomosing with the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.
FJ3409.clinicalCondition: Bleeding duodenal ulcer — the gastroduodenal axis erodes from a posterior ulcer, causing major hematemesis.
FJ3409.clinicalScenario: A patient with recurrent hematemesis from a posterior duodenal ulcer undergoes embolization of the gastroduodenal axis, including this branch, with success.

FJ3076.name: Anterior superior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3076.details: Segmental branch of the right hepatic artery supplying segment VIII, the anterior superior segment in the dome of the right hepatic lobe.
FJ3076.clinicalCondition: Segment VIII arterial mapping — dome tumors may draw parasitic extrahepatic supply, altering treatment.
FJ3076.clinicalScenario: CT angiography shows a segment VIII tumor supplied by this branch; the surgeon plans an anatomical segmentectomy preserving segments V–VII.

FJ1661M.name: Anterior temporal branch of left lateral occipital artery
FJ1661M.details: Cortical branch of the left posterior cerebral artery (lateral occipital/P4 segment) coursing over the inferior temporal lobe to supply the anterior inferior temporal cortex.
FJ1661M.clinicalCondition: Posterior cerebral artery infarction — inferior temporal ischemia impairs visual recognition and memory processing.
FJ1661M.clinicalScenario: An elderly man cannot recognize familiar objects visually despite normal acuity; imaging shows a left inferior temporal infarct in PCA territory.

FJ1661.name: Anterior temporal branch of right lateral occipital artery
FJ1661.details: Right-sided counterpart: a cortical branch of the right posterior cerebral artery supplying the anterior part of the inferior temporal lobe.
FJ1661.clinicalCondition: PCA-territory stroke — right inferior temporal lesions may cause prosopagnosia, difficulty recognizing faces.
FJ1661.clinicalScenario: After a right occipitotemporal stroke, a woman fails to recognize her husband's face until he speaks, indicating fusiform/inferior temporal involvement.

FJ1662M.name: Anterolateral central branch of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1662M.details: Lenticulostriate perforator arising from the M1 segment of the left middle cerebral artery, ascending to supply the lentiform nucleus, caudate and posterior limb of the internal capsule.
FJ1662M.clinicalCondition: Hypertensive deep hemorrhage — Charcot–Bouchard microaneurysms on these perforators rupture into the basal ganglia.
FJ1662M.clinicalScenario: A hypertensive 65-year-old develops pure motor hemiparesis without cortical signs; CT shows a small hemorrhage centered on the left lentiform nucleus.

FJ1663M.name: Anterolateral central branch of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1663M.details: Second mesh of a left lenticulostriate (anterolateral central) branch of the middle cerebral artery, supplying deep grey matter and the internal capsule.
FJ1663M.clinicalCondition: Lacunar infarction — lipohyalinosis of a single perforator produces a small deep lacune.
FJ1663M.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient notices clumsiness of the right hand; MRI shows a 7 mm lacunar infarct in the left internal capsule region.

FJ1662.name: Anterolateral central branch of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1662.details: Lenticulostriate perforator from the M1 segment of the right middle cerebral artery supplying the right basal ganglia and posterior limb of the internal capsule.
FJ1662.clinicalCondition: Capsular stroke — a small lesion here causes dense contralateral hemiplegia because fibers are tightly packed.
FJ1662.clinicalScenario: A 58-year-old hypertensive woman develops sudden left face, arm and leg weakness equally; imaging confirms a right posterior capsular infarct.

FJ1663.name: Anterolateral central branch of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1663.details: Second mesh of a right anterolateral central (lenticulostriate) branch of the middle cerebral artery, an end artery with no collateral supply.
FJ1663.clinicalCondition: Striatocapsular infarction — larger proximal perforator occlusion causes combined motor and sensory deficits.
FJ1663.clinicalScenario: A man with uncontrolled hypertension presents with left hemiparesis and hemisensory loss; MRI shows a striatocapsular infarct on the right.

FJ2967.name: Apical part of right apical segmental artery
FJ2967.details: Terminal twig of the apical segmental pulmonary artery supplying the apex proper of the right upper lobe segment S1, running with the apical bronchus.
FJ2967.clinicalCondition: Apical cavitary disease — post-primary tuberculosis classically reactivates at the lung apex.
FJ2967.clinicalScenario: A chronic smoker with hemoptysis has an apical cavity on chest radiograph; bronchoscopy excludes a bleeding apical vessel before biopsy.

FJ3015.name: Apical part of right apical segmental artery
FJ3015.details: Second mesh of the apical part of the right apical segmental pulmonary artery, distributing to the extreme apex of the right upper lobe.
FJ3015.clinicalCondition: Rasmussen aneurysm — a pulmonary arterial branch within a TB cavity wall can rupture fatally.
FJ3015.clinicalScenario: A tuberculosis patient with massive hemoptysis undergoes CT angiography revealing a small pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm in the apical cavity wall.

FJ3016.name: Apical part of right apical segmental artery
FJ3016.details: Third mesh of the apical part of the right apical segmental pulmonary artery supplying segment S1.
FJ3016.clinicalCondition: Segmental resection anatomy — stapling across the apical segment requires control of these twigs.
FJ3016.clinicalScenario: During an apical segmentectomy for a small peripheral cancer, the apical arterial twigs are individually clipped to avoid postoperative bleeding.

FJ3017.name: Apical part of right apical segmental artery
FJ3017.details: Fourth mesh of the apical part of the right apical segmental pulmonary artery, completing the apical S1 distribution of the right upper lobe.
FJ3017.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation — apical feeding branches may be the nidus in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
FJ3017.clinicalScenario: A patient with epistaxis, mucosal telangiectasia and hypoxemia has a right apical pulmonary AVM fed by an apical segmental branch, treated by embolization.

FJ2968.name: Apical part of right posterior segmental artery
FJ2968.details: Sub-branch of the posterior segmental pulmonary artery of the right upper lobe supplying the apical portion of the posterior segment (S2), which is dependent when supine.
FJ2968.clinicalCondition: Aspiration pneumonitis — the posterior segment of the upper lobe is a classic site when recumbent.
FJ2968.clinicalScenario: A patient who aspirated while supine develops an infiltrate localized to the right posterior segment, supplied by this branch.

FJ2969.name: Apical part of right posterior segmental artery
FJ2969.details: Second mesh of the apical part of the right posterior segmental pulmonary artery distributing within segment S2 of the right upper lobe.
FJ2969.clinicalCondition: Posterior segment tuberculosis — S2 is the other classic upper-lobe site of reactivation disease.
FJ2969.clinicalScenario: Chest CT in a patient with chronic cough shows tree-in-bud change and early cavitation focused on the right posterior segment.

FJ3018.name: Apical part of right posterior segmental artery
FJ3018.details: Third mesh of the apical part of the right posterior segmental pulmonary artery, accompanying the posterior segmental bronchus of the right upper lobe.
FJ3018.clinicalCondition: Segmental atelectasis — mucus plugging of the S2 bronchus collapses its arterial territory.
FJ3018.clinicalScenario: A ventilated patient develops right upper lobe posterior segment collapse; bronchoscopy removes a mucus plug and the segment re-expands.

FJ3410.name: Appendicular artery
FJ3410.details: Branch of the ileocolic artery (from the superior mesenteric artery) descending behind the terminal ileum within the mesoappendix to supply the vermiform appendix; effectively an end artery.
FJ3410.clinicalCondition: Acute appendicitis — arterial thrombosis in the inflamed mesoappendix promotes gangrene and perforation.
FJ3410.clinicalScenario: During appendectomy for a gangrenous appendix, the surgeon ligates the appendicular artery in the mesoappendix close to the base before dividing it.

FJ3411.name: Arch of aorta
FJ3411.details: Continuation of the ascending aorta at the sternal angle, arching over the left main bronchus; gives the brachiocephalic, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries; the isthmus lies just beyond.
FJ3411.clinicalCondition: Coarctation and arch aneurysm — narrowing or dilatation of the arch threatens cerebral and arm perfusion.
FJ3411.clinicalScenario: A 45-year-old with tearing chest pain radiating to the back has a widened mediastinum; CT angiography shows a dissection flap involving the aortic arch.

FJ1664.name: artery of central sulcus
FJ1664.details: Rolandic cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the central sulcus, supplying the primary motor and sensory cortex around it.
FJ1664.clinicalCondition: Rolandic stroke — occlusion causes contralateral face and arm weakness with cortical sensory loss.
FJ1664.clinicalScenario: A woman suddenly drops objects from her left hand, with left arm weakness and impaired stereognosis; MRI shows an infarct around the right central sulcus.

FJ1664M.name: Artery of central sulcus
FJ1664M.details: Mirrored mesh of the artery of the central sulcus, an MCA cortical branch supplying precentral and postcentral gyri near the sulcus.
FJ1664M.clinicalCondition: Focal motor seizures — rolandic cortex lesions produce Jacksonian march seizures from hyperexcitable motor cortex.
FJ1664M.clinicalScenario: A man describes jerking that begins in his right thumb and marches up the arm; imaging shows a small lesion beside the left central sulcus.

FJ1665.name: artery of central sulcus
FJ1665.details: Additional mesh of the rolandic artery, a middle cerebral branch whose territory covers the trunk and limb representation of the sensorimotor strip.
FJ1665.clinicalCondition: Surgical mapping landmark — the central sulcus artery helps localize motor cortex during tumor resection.
FJ1665.clinicalScenario: Before resecting a glioma near the motor strip, the neurosurgeon uses the central sulcus vessels and stimulation mapping to preserve hand function.

FJ1665M.name: Artery of central sulcus
FJ1665M.details: Further mesh of the artery of the central sulcus; its anastomoses with anterior and posterior cerebral branches form part of the leptomeningeal collateral network.
FJ1665M.clinicalCondition: Watershed vulnerability — borderzone cortex near the sulcus is sensitive to global hypoperfusion.
FJ1665M.clinicalScenario: After prolonged cardiac arrest resuscitation, a patient has bilateral proximal arm and leg weakness ("man-in-the-barrel") from watershed infarction.

FJ1666M.name: Artery of left postcentral sulcus
FJ1666M.details: Cortical branch of the left middle cerebral artery supplying the postcentral gyrus, the primary somatosensory cortex of the dominant parietal lobe.
FJ1666M.clinicalCondition: Cortical sensory loss — lesions impair proprioception, stereognosis and two-point discrimination contralaterally.
FJ1666M.clinicalScenario: After a small left parietal stroke, a man cannot identify coins in his right hand with eyes closed, though power is normal.

FJ1668M.name: Artery of left precentral sulcus
FJ1668M.details: Cortical branch of the left middle cerebral artery running in the precentral sulcus, supplying premotor and primary motor cortex of the frontal lobe.
FJ1668M.clinicalCondition: Motor cortex stroke — occlusion causes contralateral weakness, most marked in the face and hand.
FJ1668M.clinicalScenario: A patient develops isolated right-hand weakness mimicking a radial palsy; diffusion MRI shows a tiny infarct in the left precentral "hand knob."

FJ1669M.name: Artery of left precentral sulcus
FJ1669M.details: Second mesh of the artery of the left precentral sulcus, distributing to the opercular and premotor frontal cortex near Broca's area inferiorly.
FJ1669M.clinicalCondition: Expressive language disturbance — inferior frontal ischemia near Broca's area impairs speech production.
FJ1669M.clinicalScenario: A woman suddenly speaks only in short, effortful phrases while comprehension is intact; imaging shows an infarct in the left inferior frontal region.

FJ1670M.name: Artery of left precentral sulcus
FJ1670M.details: Third mesh of the artery of the left precentral sulcus, supplying the superior premotor cortex involved in planning limb movements.
FJ1670M.clinicalCondition: Limb apraxia — premotor lesions disrupt learned skilled movements despite normal strength.
FJ1670M.clinicalScenario: A stroke patient cannot demonstrate how to brush his teeth on command, although he uses a real toothbrush correctly at the sink.

FJ1666.name: Artery of right postcentral sulcus
FJ1666.details: Cortical branch of the right middle cerebral artery supplying the postcentral gyrus, the primary somatosensory cortex of the non-dominant parietal lobe.
FJ1666.clinicalCondition: Sensory neglect component — right parietal lesions blunt awareness of left-sided stimuli.
FJ1666.clinicalScenario: A man after a right parietal stroke extinguishes left-hand touch when both hands are stimulated together, though single stimuli are felt.

FJ1668.name: Artery of right precentral sulcus
FJ1668.details: Cortical branch of the right middle cerebral artery running in the precentral sulcus, supplying premotor and primary motor cortex.
FJ1668.clinicalCondition: Contralateral hemiparesis — precentral territory infarction weakens the left face, arm and leg in a cortical pattern.
FJ1668.clinicalScenario: A 70-year-old develops sudden left-sided weakness with frontal release signs; MRI localizes the lesion to the right precentral gyrus.

FJ1669.name: Artery of right precentral sulcus
FJ1669.details: Second mesh of the artery of the right precentral sulcus, supplying motor cortex including the leg area extension toward the paracentral region.
FJ1669.clinicalCondition: Focal epilepsy source — motor strip irritation produces contralateral clonic seizures.
FJ1669.clinicalScenario: A teenager has stereotyped seizures beginning with left foot jerking; EEG and imaging implicate the right precentral region near the midline.

FJ1670.name: Artery of right precentral sulcus
FJ1670.details: Third mesh of the artery of the right precentral sulcus, a pial MCA branch anastomosing with neighboring prefrontal and rolandic branches.
FJ1670.clinicalCondition: Tumor resection planning — preserving this branch protects motor function during frontal glioma surgery.
FJ1670.clinicalScenario: A neurosurgeon maps the right precentral vessels before removing a frontal tumor, adjusting the resection margin to spare the motor branch.

FJ3413.name: Ascending aorta
FJ3413.details: Arises from the left ventricle at the aortic valve, giving the right and left coronary arteries from its sinuses, and continues as the aortic arch at the sternal angle.
FJ3413.clinicalCondition: Type A dissection and ascending aneurysm — rupture or dissection risks tamponade and sudden death.
FJ3413.clinicalScenario: A tall young man with Marfan syndrome has a 5.2 cm ascending aortic aneurysm on echo and is referred for prophylactic root replacement.

FJ3414.name: Ascending branch of inferior branch of ileocolic artery
FJ3414.details: Small colic branch from the inferior division of the ileocolic artery ascending along the lower ascending colon, joining the marginal artery anastomosis with the right colic artery.
FJ3414.clinicalCondition: Marginal artery collateral — maintains colonic perfusion when a major colic trunk is narrowed.
FJ3414.clinicalScenario: In chronic superior mesenteric stenosis, angiography shows colonic flow preserved through an enlarged marginal arcade including this ascending ileocolic branch.

FJ3399.name: Ascending branch of left colic artery
FJ3399.details: Branch of the left colic artery (from the inferior mesenteric artery) ascending toward the splenic flexure to anastomose with the middle colic artery in the marginal artery.
FJ3399.clinicalCondition: Ischemic colitis at the splenic flexure — a watershed between superior and inferior mesenteric territories.
FJ3399.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient with atrial fibrillation passes bloody diarrhea after a hypotensive episode; colonoscopy shows ischemia centered on the splenic flexure.

FJ3002.name: Basal branch of right anterior basal segmental artery
FJ3002.details: Sub-branch of the right anterior basal segmental pulmonary artery supplying the basal part of the anterior basal segment (S8) of the right lower lobe.
FJ3002.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — basal branches are dependent sites where emboli commonly lodge.
FJ3002.clinicalScenario: A breathless postoperative patient has CT pulmonary angiography showing a filling defect extending into the right anterior basal segmental branches.

FJ3003.name: Basal branch of right anterior basal segmental artery
FJ3003.details: Second mesh of the basal branch of the right anterior basal segmental pulmonary artery distributing within segment S8 of the right lower lobe.
FJ3003.clinicalCondition: Basal bronchiectasis — dependent basal segments accumulate secretions and recurrent infection.
FJ3003.clinicalScenario: CT in a patient with chronic productive cough shows right basal bronchiectasis; segmental vessels are mapped in case lobectomy is required.

FJ1672.name: Basilar artery
FJ1672.details: Formed by the union of the two vertebral arteries at the pontomedullary junction; runs on the ventral pons giving pontine branches, AICA and the superior cerebellar arteries, ending as the posterior cerebral arteries.
FJ1672.clinicalCondition: Basilar artery occlusion — catastrophic brainstem stroke causing locked-in syndrome, coma or death.
FJ1672.clinicalScenario: A 62-year-old with vertigo and diplopia abruptly becomes quadriplegic and responsive only by vertical eye movements; angiography shows mid-basilar thrombosis.

FJ1844.name: Basilar artery
FJ1844.details: Second mesh of the basilar artery, the midline trunk of the posterior circulation supplying the pons, midbrain and, via its terminal branches, the occipital lobes.
FJ1844.clinicalCondition: Basilar tip syndrome — embolus at the bifurcation causes midbrain and occipital signs including vertical gaze palsy.
FJ1844.clinicalScenario: A patient is found drowsy with upgaze palsy and bilateral visual loss; imaging reveals a "top of the basilar" embolus.

FJ3417.name: Brachiocephalic artery
FJ3417.details: First and largest branch of the aortic arch, dividing behind the right sternoclavicular joint into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.
FJ3417.clinicalCondition: Brachiocephalic stenosis — proximal disease simultaneously threatens the right arm and right cerebral circulation.
FJ3417.clinicalScenario: A man has a weak right radial pulse, right arm claudication and transient right visual dimming; imaging shows severe brachiocephalic trunk stenosis.

FJ1674M.name: Branch of left anterior choroidal artery to posterior limb of left internal capsule
FJ1674M.details: Tiny perforating twig of the left anterior choroidal artery (from the internal carotid artery) supplying the posterior limb of the internal capsule, which carries corticospinal fibers.
FJ1674M.clinicalCondition: Anterior choroidal artery syndrome — capsular infarction produces hemiplegia, hemisensory loss and homonymous hemianopia.
FJ1674M.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient develops dense right hemiplegia and sensory loss; MRI shows a small infarct in the posterior limb of the left internal capsule.

FJ1673M.name: Branch of left middle cerebral artery to left angular gyrus
FJ1673M.details: Cortical branch of the inferior division of the left middle cerebral artery supplying the angular gyrus, a language-association area of the dominant parietal lobe.
FJ1673M.clinicalCondition: Gerstmann syndrome — dominant angular gyrus lesions cause agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia and left–right confusion.
FJ1673M.clinicalScenario: After a left parietal stroke, a teacher cannot calculate, write coherently or name her fingers, though her speech is fluent.

FJ1674.name: Branch of right anterior choroidal artery to posterior limb of right internal capsule
FJ1674.details: Perforating twig of the right anterior choroidal artery supplying the posterior limb of the right internal capsule, including corticospinal and thalamocortical fibers.
FJ1674.clinicalCondition: Capsular hemiplegia — small deep infarcts here cause disproportionately dense contralateral weakness.
FJ1674.clinicalScenario: A hypertensive man presents with sudden left face, arm and leg weakness; MRI shows a lacune in the right posterior internal capsule.

FJ1673.name: Branch of right middle cerebral artery to right angular gyrus
FJ1673.details: Cortical branch of the inferior division of the right middle cerebral artery supplying the angular gyrus of the non-dominant parietal lobe, important for spatial attention.
FJ1673.clinicalCondition: Hemispatial neglect — non-dominant parietal lesions make patients ignore the left side of space.
FJ1673.clinicalScenario: After a right parietal stroke, a man eats only from the right half of his plate and shaves only his right cheek.

FJ1933.name: Bronchial artery
FJ1933.details: Systemic arteries, usually from the descending thoracic aorta at T5–T6 or intercostal trunks, supplying the bronchi, bronchial glands and visceral pleura; they form bronchopulmonary anastomoses.
FJ1933.clinicalCondition: Massive hemoptysis — hypertrophied bronchial arteries in bronchiectasis or cystic fibrosis bleed; treated by embolization.
FJ1933.clinicalScenario: A cystic fibrosis patient coughs up 300 mL of blood; CT shows enlarged tortuous bronchial arteries and embolization is arranged urgently.

FJ3418.name: Bronchial branch of arch of aorta
FJ3418.details: Variant bronchial artery arising directly from the aortic arch rather than the descending aorta, coursing to supply the bronchi and peribronchial tissues.
FJ3418.clinicalCondition: Variant origin complicating embolization — the bleeding vessel must be located during hemoptysis angiography.
FJ3418.clinicalScenario: During hemoptysis angiography no bronchial artery arises at T5–T6; an arch aortogram reveals the culprit vessel originating from the aortic arch.

FJ3419.name: Caudal pancreatic artery
FJ3419.details: Branch of the splenic artery near the pancreatic tail supplying the tail of the pancreas and anastomosing with the great pancreatic artery within the gland.
FJ3419.clinicalCondition: Distal pancreatectomy anatomy — splenic branch preservation matters in spleen-preserving tail resection.
FJ3419.clinicalScenario: During spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy for a tail neuroendocrine tumor, small splenic branches including the caudal pancreatic artery are meticulously preserved.

FJ3077.name: Caudate lobe branch of left hepatic artery
FJ3077.details: Small branch of the left hepatic artery supplying the caudate lobe (segment I), which also receives right-sided branches and drains directly into the inferior vena cava.
FJ3077.clinicalCondition: Caudate hypertrophy in Budd–Chiari syndrome — independent caudate drainage lets segment I enlarge when other segments congest.
FJ3077.clinicalScenario: Imaging in Budd–Chiari syndrome shows a markedly enlarged caudate lobe compressing the IVC, reflecting its separate vascular arrangement.

FJ1916.name: Caudate lobe branch of right hepatic artery
FJ1916.details: Small branch of the right hepatic artery supplying the caudate lobe (segment I) from the right side; caudate supply is typically dual.
FJ1916.clinicalCondition: Hilar cholangiocarcinoma surgery — caudate branches are divided when segment I is resected with the tumor.
FJ1916.clinicalScenario: For a Klatskin tumor, the surgical plan includes caudate lobectomy, requiring control of both right and left caudate arterial branches.

FJ2386.name: Caudate lobe branch of right hepatic artery
FJ2386.details: Second mesh of the caudate lobe branch of the right hepatic artery distributing to the right part of segment I.
FJ2386.clinicalCondition: Caudate arterial embolization anatomy — segment I tumors may need bilateral branch targeting.
FJ2386.clinicalScenario: A caudate lobe tumor blush persists after right-sided embolization because a left caudate branch also feeds it, requiring a second session.

FJ1846.name: Celiac artery
FJ1846.details: First anterior branch of the abdominal aorta at T12/L1, a short trunk dividing into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries to supply the foregut.
FJ1846.clinicalCondition: Median arcuate ligament syndrome — celiac compression causes postprandial pain, food fear and weight loss.
FJ1846.clinicalScenario: A thin young woman has postprandial epigastric pain and weight loss; CT angiography shows hooked compression of the celiac origin.

FJ2013.name: Celiac artery
FJ2013.details: Second mesh of the celiac artery, the foregut trunk whose branches supply the lower esophagus, stomach, liver, spleen, pancreas and proximal duodenum.
FJ2013.clinicalCondition: Chronic mesenteric ischemia — combined celiac and mesenteric stenosis causes intestinal angina.
FJ2013.clinicalScenario: An elderly smoker loses 10 kg with pain after meals; angiography shows severe celiac and superior mesenteric stenoses requiring revascularization.

FJ3421.name: Celiac trunk
FJ3421.details: The celiac trunk is the first unpaired anterior branch of the abdominal aorta, trifurcating into left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries for the foregut.
FJ3421.clinicalCondition: Celiac aneurysm and injury — rare aneurysms and upper abdominal trauma threaten foregut perfusion.
FJ3421.clinicalScenario: Upper GI bleeding angiography begins with a celiac trunk injection, which reveals the bleeding point in a left gastric branch for embolization.

FJ2649.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FJ2649.details: Branch of the left coronary artery coursing in the left atrioventricular groove, giving obtuse marginal branches to the lateral left ventricular wall; gives the posterior descending artery in left-dominant hearts.
FJ2649.clinicalCondition: Circumflex occlusion — lateral wall infarction, often electrocardiographically subtle ("silent" territory).
FJ2649.clinicalScenario: A 55-year-old diabetic has crushing chest pain with a near-normal ECG; troponin is high and angiography shows an occluded circumflex artery.

FJ2650.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FJ2650.details: Second mesh of the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery, running posteriorly in the coronary sulcus toward the crux in left-dominant circulation.
FJ2650.clinicalCondition: Left coronary dominance — in about 10% of people the circumflex supplies the posterior descending artery and AV node region.
FJ2650.clinicalScenario: Angiography in a patient with inferior infarction shows the posterior descending artery arising from a large circumflex, indicating left dominance.

FJ2651.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FJ2651.details: Third mesh of the circumflex branch; its obtuse marginal branches are common bypass graft targets for the lateral ventricular wall.
FJ2651.clinicalCondition: Multivessel coronary disease — circumflex and marginal stenoses are weighed for stenting versus bypass surgery.
FJ2651.clinicalScenario: A heart team chooses bypass grafting for a diabetic patient with severe three-vessel disease including a proximal circumflex lesion.

FJ2652.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FJ2652.details: Fourth mesh of the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery; it also gives atrial branches, including the sinus nodal artery in a substantial minority.
FJ2652.clinicalCondition: Atrial ischemia and arrhythmia — circumflex disease can compromise sinus node supply and provoke atrial fibrillation.
FJ2652.clinicalScenario: A patient with lateral NSTEMI develops new atrial fibrillation; the culprit circumflex lesion involves atrial branches near its origin.

FJ2653.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FJ2653.details: Fifth mesh of the circumflex branch, supplying the posterolateral wall including the anterolateral papillary muscle via marginal branches.
FJ2653.clinicalCondition: Papillary muscle dysfunction — lateral ischemia causes acute mitral regurgitation after infarction.
FJ2653.clinicalScenario: Three days after a lateral infarction, a patient develops pulmonary edema and a new murmur; echo shows papillary muscle dysfunction with severe mitral regurgitation.

FJ2654.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FJ2654.details: Sixth mesh of the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery, completing its course in the atrioventricular groove toward the posterior interventricular region.
FJ2654.clinicalCondition: Silent lateral ischemia — diabetics may show circumflex territory defects only on stress imaging.
FJ2654.clinicalScenario: A diabetic with atypical fatigue has a reversible lateral wall defect on stress imaging, leading to angiography showing a tight circumflex stenosis.

FJ3078.name: Common hepatic artery
FJ3078.details: Branch of the celiac trunk running toward the porta hepatis, giving the gastroduodenal artery and continuing as the hepatic artery proper; contributes supply to liver, gallbladder, stomach and pancreas.
FJ3078.clinicalCondition: Hepatic artery thrombosis after transplantation — the graft bile ducts depend entirely on arterial inflow.
FJ3078.clinicalScenario: After liver transplantation, Doppler shows absent arterial flow; exploration confirms common hepatic artery thrombosis requiring urgent thrombectomy to save the graft.

FJ2643.name: Conus branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2643.details: First small branch of the anterior interventricular (LAD) artery supplying the conus (infundibulum) of the right ventricle; anastomoses with the right coronary conus branch as Vieussens' ring.
FJ2643.clinicalCondition: Collateral pathway — the conus anastomosis can bypass proximal coronary occlusions between LAD and RCA systems.
FJ2643.clinicalScenario: Angiography in chronic total RCA occlusion shows the conus collateral ring filling the distal right coronary artery from the LAD.

FJ2644.name: Conus branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2644.details: Second mesh of the conus branch of the LAD; a conus artery may instead arise independently from the aorta as a common variant.
FJ2644.clinicalCondition: Variant third coronary ostium — a separate conus origin can be injured during aortic valve surgery.
FJ2644.clinicalScenario: During coronary angiography the operator notes a separate small conus ostium in the right sinus and documents it before planned valve surgery.

FJ2230.name: Deltoid branch of left thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2230.details: Branch of the thoracoacromial artery descending with the cephalic vein in the deltopectoral groove, supplying the deltoid and pectoralis major muscles.
FJ2230.clinicalCondition: Deltopectoral approach landmark — the vein and this branch mark the safe surgical interval at the shoulder.
FJ2230.clinicalScenario: In a left deltopectoral approach for shoulder replacement, the cephalic vein is found beside the deltoid branch and retracted laterally to protect it.

FJ2282.name: Deltoid branch of right thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2282.details: Right-sided counterpart of the deltoid branch, accompanying the cephalic vein in the right deltopectoral groove to supply deltoid and pectoralis major.
FJ2282.clinicalCondition: Pectoralis flap planning — thoracoacromial branches perfuse the pectoralis major myocutaneous flap.
FJ2282.clinicalScenario: A head-and-neck surgeon designs a pectoralis major flap for a right-sided defect, preserving the thoracoacromial pedicle including its deltoid branch.

FJ3427.name: Descending aorta
FJ3427.details: Continuation of the aortic arch from T4 through the thorax and diaphragm into the abdomen, giving intercostal, visceral and parietal branches along its course.
FJ3427.clinicalCondition: Stanford type B dissection — a tear distal to the left subclavian artery, usually managed medically unless complicated.
FJ3427.clinicalScenario: A hypertensive man with abrupt interscapular pain has a dissection flap confined to the descending aorta and is managed with strict blood-pressure control.

FJ3428.name: Descending branch of left colic artery
FJ3428.details: Branch of the left colic artery (inferior mesenteric artery) descending to supply the lower descending colon and join the marginal artery anastomosis with the sigmoid branches.
FJ3428.clinicalCondition: Left colectomy ligation level — branch anatomy decides high versus low IMA tie in colon cancer surgery.
FJ3428.clinicalScenario: During laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy, the inferior mesenteric pedicle and its left colic branches are mapped before ligation is performed.

FJ2063.name: Descending branch of left lateral circumflex femoral artery
FJ2063.details: Branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery (from the profunda femoris) descending beneath rectus femoris along vastus lateralis, supplying the quadriceps and the genicular anastomosis.
FJ2063.clinicalCondition: Anterolateral thigh flap pedicle — its perforators supply the workhorse ALT free flap.
FJ2063.clinicalScenario: A reconstructive surgeon raises a left anterolateral thigh flap on perforators of this descending branch to cover a post-traumatic leg defect.

FJ2057.name: Descending branch of right lateral circumflex femoral artery
FJ2057.details: Right-sided counterpart descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery, coursing under rectus femoris with the nerve to vastus lateralis toward the knee.
FJ2057.clinicalCondition: Quadriceps perfusion in femoral disease — this branch sustains the thigh when the superficial femoral artery occludes.
FJ2057.clinicalScenario: Angiography in a claudicant shows the right superficial femoral artery occluded, with quadriceps and knee flow maintained via profunda and circumflex branches.

FJ1931.name: Descending thoracic aorta
FJ1931.details: Thoracic part of the descending aorta extending from T4 to the T12 diaphragmatic hiatus, giving posterior intercostal, subcostal, bronchial and esophageal branches.
FJ1931.clinicalCondition: Spinal cord ischemia risk — intercostal feeders, especially the artery of Adamkiewicz, supply the cord during repair.
FJ1931.clinicalScenario: Before thoracoabdominal aneurysm repair, imaging localizes the artery of Adamkiewicz from a lower intercostal branch to plan spinal protection.

FJ2633.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2633.details: Branch of the anterior interventricular (LAD) artery coursing diagonally across the anterolateral left ventricular wall; branches are numbered D1, D2 from proximal to distal.
FJ2633.clinicalCondition: Bifurcation disease — diagonal ostial lesions complicate LAD stenting and risk side-branch loss.
FJ2633.clinicalScenario: A patient with exertional angina has a tight LAD–first diagonal bifurcation stenosis; a planned two-stent strategy protects both branches.

FJ2634.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2634.details: Second mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD supplying the anterolateral wall of the left ventricle, territory often visible in leads I, aVL and V5–V6.
FJ2634.clinicalCondition: Anterolateral infarction — diagonal occlusion produces ST changes in high lateral leads.
FJ2634.clinicalScenario: An ECG shows ST elevation in I and aVL only; angiography identifies an occluded large first diagonal branch as the culprit.

FJ2635.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2635.details: Third mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD; a large diagonal may equal the LAD in importance for anterolateral perfusion.
FJ2635.clinicalCondition: Bypass graft target — sizeable diagonals receive vein or arterial grafts during coronary bypass surgery.
FJ2635.clinicalScenario: At bypass surgery, the LIMA is grafted to the LAD and a vein graft placed to a large diseased diagonal branch.

FJ2636.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2636.details: Fourth mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD, part of the variable diagonal system crossing the anterolateral ventricular surface.
FJ2636.clinicalCondition: Ramus intermedius variant — a trifurcation branch behaves like a large diagonal and shares its disease patterns.
FJ2636.clinicalScenario: Angiography reveals a ramus intermedius trifurcation; its ostial stenosis is treated like a high diagonal lesion during intervention.

FJ2637.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2637.details: Fifth mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD supplying anterolateral myocardium in parallel with septal perforators from the same parent artery.
FJ2637.clinicalCondition: Diagonal NSTEMI — subtotal diagonal stenosis causes troponin-positive pain with subtle ECG changes.
FJ2637.clinicalScenario: A woman with rest pain and raised troponin has a near-normal ECG; angiography shows a 95% mid-diagonal stenosis, stented successfully.

FJ2638.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2638.details: Sixth mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD; diagonal caliber decreases distally, with the first diagonal usually the largest.
FJ2638.clinicalCondition: Side-branch jail — stenting across a diagonal origin can occlude it and cause periprocedural infarction.
FJ2638.clinicalScenario: After LAD stenting, a jailed diagonal loses flow with chest pain; it is rescued by balloon dilation through the stent struts.

FJ2639.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2639.details: Seventh mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD, supplying the anterolateral wall jointly with obtuse marginal branches of the circumflex.
FJ2639.clinicalCondition: Collateral overlap — anterolateral wall may survive diagonal occlusion via circumflex collaterals, masking severity.
FJ2639.clinicalScenario: A chronic total diagonal occlusion is found incidentally; the territory is viable because marginal branches of the circumflex supply it retrogradely.

FJ2640.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2640.details: Eighth mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD, a surface vessel on the anterolateral ventricle accessible to epicardial mapping and grafting.
FJ2640.clinicalCondition: Diagonal dissection — spontaneous coronary artery dissection can involve diagonal branches, especially in younger women.
FJ2640.clinicalScenario: A postpartum woman presents with anterolateral infarction; angiography shows a long smooth diagonal dissection managed conservatively.

FJ2642.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2642.details: Ninth mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD; diagonal branches also serve as markers separating LAD from circumflex territories on imaging.
FJ2642.clinicalCondition: Stress-imaging correlation — anterolateral defects localize to diagonal or circumflex disease and guide angiography.
FJ2642.clinicalScenario: A reversible anterolateral defect on nuclear imaging prompts angiography, which confirms a proximal diagonal stenosis as the cause.

FJ2648.name: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery
FJ2648.details: Tenth mesh of a diagonal branch of the LAD, completing the diagonal series supplying the anterolateral left ventricular wall.
FJ2648.clinicalCondition: Small-branch disease — distal diagonal narrowing in diabetics contributes to diffuse ischemia despite patent main vessels.
FJ2648.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient has ongoing angina after main-vessel stenting; review shows diffuse distal diagonal disease treated medically.

FJ2058.name: Distal perforating artery
FJ2058.details: Perforating branch of the profunda femoris artery piercing the adductor magnus to reach the posterior thigh, joining the anastomotic network around the femur and knee.
FJ2058.clinicalCondition: Profunda collateral system — perforators reconstitute the popliteal artery when the superficial femoral artery is occluded.
FJ2058.clinicalScenario: A claudicant with an occluded superficial femoral artery keeps a viable leg because profunda perforating collaterals fill the popliteal artery on angiography.

FJ2064.name: Distal perforating artery
FJ2064.details: Second mesh of a distal perforating artery of the profunda femoris, passing through adductor magnus close to the linea aspera to supply the hamstring compartment.
FJ2064.clinicalCondition: Posterior thigh bleeding — perforators can bleed significantly after femoral fracture or intramuscular injection injury.
FJ2064.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a large posterior thigh hematoma after a femur fracture; angiography shows a torn perforating branch, embolized successfully.

FJ2231.name: Dorsal carpal branch of left radial artery
FJ2231.details: Small branch of the left radial artery at the wrist passing deep to the extensor tendons to join the dorsal carpal arch with ulnar and interosseous contributions.
FJ2231.clinicalCondition: Wrist collateral network — the dorsal carpal arch helps sustain hand perfusion after radial injury or harvest.
FJ2231.clinicalScenario: After a left wrist laceration divides the radial artery, the hand stays warm and pink via the dorsal carpal arch and palmar collaterals.

FJ2283.name: Dorsal carpal branch of right radial artery
FJ2283.details: Right-sided counterpart of the dorsal carpal branch of the radial artery, contributing to the dorsal carpal rete at the wrist.
FJ2283.clinicalCondition: Radial artery graft assessment — palmar and dorsal arch completeness is checked before radial harvest for bypass.
FJ2283.clinicalScenario: Before using the right radial artery as a bypass conduit, ultrasound confirms adequate ulnar and dorsal carpal collateral flow to the hand.

FJ2072.name: Dorsal digital artery of foot
FJ2072.details: Tiny arteries on the dorsal aspect of the toes, arising from dorsal metatarsal branches of the dorsalis pedis/arcuate system and anastomosing with plantar digital arteries.
FJ2072.clinicalCondition: Digital perfusion assessment — toe blood flow predicts healing of diabetic foot ulcers and minor amputations.
FJ2072.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a non-healing toe ulcer has digital flow assessed before a planned ray amputation to ensure stump healing.

FJ2141.name: Dorsal digital artery of foot
FJ2141.details: Second mesh of a dorsal digital artery of the foot, part of the small terminal arterial network supplying the toe dorsum and nail bed.
FJ2141.clinicalCondition: Raynaud-type digital ischemia — toe-tip pain and color change reflect small digital artery vasospasm or occlusion.
FJ2141.clinicalScenario: A young woman reports painful blue toes in cold weather; examination and Doppler assessment point to digital artery vasospasm.

FJ3430.name: Dorsal pancreatic artery
FJ3430.details: Branch usually of the splenic artery (origin variable: celiac or common hepatic) descending behind the pancreatic neck and body, dividing to supply the body, neck and uncinate region.
FJ3430.clinicalCondition: Variant anatomy in Whipple surgery — an anomalous dorsal pancreatic origin alters bleeding risk during resection.
FJ3430.clinicalScenario: Preoperative CT for a pancreatic head tumor maps a dorsal pancreatic artery arising from the celiac trunk, alerting the surgeon to variant supply.

FJ1934.name: Esophageal artery
FJ1934.details: Two or more small unpaired esophageal branches arising from the front of the descending thoracic aorta to supply the mid-esophagus, anastomosing with left gastric and inferior thyroid esophageal twigs.
FJ1934.clinicalCondition: Aortoesophageal fistula — erosion between aorta and esophagus causes herald then catastrophic gastrointestinal bleeding.
FJ1934.clinicalScenario: A patient with a thoracic aortic graft develops a small "herald" hematemesis; imaging confirms an aortoesophageal fistula, a surgical emergency.

FJ2671.name: First anterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2671.details: First of several small anterior ventricular (right ventricular) branches of the right coronary artery supplying the anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2671.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction — proximal RCA occlusion involving these branches causes hypotension with clear lung fields.
FJ2671.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient becomes hypotensive with raised JVP and clear lungs; right-sided chest leads confirm right ventricular infarction.

FJ2673.name: First anterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2673.details: Second mesh of the first anterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery distributing over the infundibular and anterior right ventricular surface.
FJ2673.clinicalCondition: RV branch compromise during PCI — stenting across these branches can worsen RV function in inferior infarction.
FJ2673.clinicalScenario: During proximal RCA stenting for inferior STEMI, the team monitors right ventricular function because small RV branches may be covered by the stent.

FJ2677.name: First anterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2677.details: Third mesh of the first anterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery; RV branches are small but functionally important in the low-pressure right ventricle.
FJ2677.clinicalCondition: Isolated RV ischemia — rare branch occlusion causes RV failure without left ventricular involvement.
FJ2677.clinicalScenario: A patient with chest pain and isolated RV dilation on echo is found to have a discrete stenosis of a right ventricular branch.

FJ2714.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2714.details: First posterolateral (posterior ventricular) branch of the right coronary artery, arising beyond the posterior descending artery in right-dominant hearts to supply the posterolateral left ventricular wall.
FJ2714.clinicalCondition: Posterolateral ischemia — occlusion contributes to inferoposterior infarction and papillary muscle dysfunction.
FJ2714.clinicalScenario: A patient with inferoposterior STEMI develops a new pansystolic murmur; echo shows posteromedial papillary muscle dysfunction from posterolateral ischemia.

FJ2715.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2715.details: Second mesh of the first posterior ventricular (posterolateral) branch of the right coronary artery supplying diaphragmatic-surface left ventricular myocardium.
FJ2715.clinicalCondition: Inferior wall hypokinesis — posterolateral branch disease reduces inferior wall motion on imaging.
FJ2715.clinicalScenario: Echocardiography after an inferior infarction shows posterolateral hypokinesis matching a diseased posterolateral branch on angiography.

FJ2716.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2716.details: Third mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery, part of the posterolateral system present in right coronary dominance.
FJ2716.clinicalCondition: Coronary dominance assessment — posterolateral branches define right dominance and influence revascularization strategy.
FJ2716.clinicalScenario: A heart team reviews angiography showing posterolateral branches from the RCA, confirming right dominance before planning grafts.

FJ2717.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2717.details: Fourth mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery distributing over the posterolateral left ventricle.
FJ2717.clinicalCondition: Silent posterolateral ischemia — this territory may infarct without classic ECG changes, especially in diabetics.
FJ2717.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient's routine stress test shows a posterolateral defect; angiography reveals a severe posterolateral branch stenosis.

FJ2718.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2718.details: Fifth mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery, arising distal to the crux in right-dominant circulation.
FJ2718.clinicalCondition: Multivessel disease burden — posterolateral lesions add to the ischemic burden considered in SYNTAX scoring.
FJ2718.clinicalScenario: A patient with left main and posterolateral branch disease is scored and referred for bypass rather than multivessel stenting.

FJ2719.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2719.details: Sixth mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery supplying posterolateral myocardium supplied beyond the posterior descending artery.
FJ2719.clinicalCondition: Posterolateral aneurysm risk — transmural infarction in this territory can thin and remodel the wall.
FJ2719.clinicalScenario: Months after an inferoposterior infarction, imaging shows a small posterolateral wall aneurysm at the site of the occluded branch territory.

FJ2720.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2720.details: Seventh mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery, coursing over the diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle.
FJ2720.clinicalCondition: Collateral recipient — posterolateral branches receive collaterals from the circumflex when the RCA is occluded.
FJ2720.clinicalScenario: In a chronic RCA occlusion, the posterolateral branch fills retrogradely from circumflex collaterals, keeping the territory viable.

FJ2721.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2721.details: Eighth mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery, a terminal posterolateral division of the distal RCA.
FJ2721.clinicalCondition: Distal branch embolization — atheroembolism during catheterization can occlude small posterolateral branches.
FJ2721.clinicalScenario: After complex stenting, a patient has chest pain and a troponin rise attributed to distal embolization into a posterolateral branch.

FJ2722.name: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2722.details: Ninth mesh of the first posterior ventricular branch of the right coronary artery, completing the posterolateral series in right-dominant hearts.
FJ2722.clinicalCondition: Balanced circulation variant — when posterolateral supply is shared, branch anatomy changes infarction patterns.
FJ2722.clinicalScenario: Angiography shows codominant circulation with posterolateral supply split between RCA and circumflex, explaining an atypical infarction pattern.

FJ2632.name: First right anterior branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2632.details: Small branch of the anterior interventricular (LAD) artery crossing the anterior interventricular groove to supply the adjacent anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2632.clinicalCondition: Combined anterior ischemia — LAD disease can simultaneously threaten left ventricular and right ventricular anterior territories.
FJ2632.clinicalScenario: Angiography shows a small right ventricular branch from the mid-LAD, noted while assessing anterior ischemia after LAD stenting.

FJ2645.name: First right anterior branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2645.details: Second mesh of the first right anterior branch of the LAD, a minor right ventricular twig paralleling the conus branch distribution.
FJ2645.clinicalCondition: Angiographic landmark — small RV branches help confirm LAD position and side-branch anatomy during intervention.
FJ2645.clinicalScenario: During rotational atherectomy planning, the operator notes the small right anterior branch origin to avoid compromising it with the burr path.

FJ2735.name: First septal branch of right posterior interventricular artery
FJ2735.details: First septal perforating branch of the posterior interventricular (posterior descending) artery, entering the posterior interventricular septum to supply its posterior third.
FJ2735.clinicalCondition: Conduction disturbance in inferior infarction — septal and nodal ischemia from proximal RCA disease causes heart block.
FJ2735.clinicalScenario: A patient with inferior STEMI develops transient complete heart block from a proximal RCA lesion compromising posterior descending septal branches.

FJ3433.name: Great pancreatic artery
FJ3433.details: The arteria pancreatica magna, the largest pancreatic branch of the splenic artery, entering the body of the pancreas and anastomosing with the caudal pancreatic artery.
FJ3433.clinicalCondition: Pancreatitis pseudoaneurysm — splenic-system branches erode in necrotizing pancreatitis and bleed into pseudocysts.
FJ3433.clinicalScenario: In necrotizing pancreatitis, CT angiography reveals a pseudoaneurysm of a splenic pancreatic branch bleeding into a pseudocyst, treated by coil embolization.

FJ3081.name: Hepatic artery proper
FJ3081.details: Continuation of the common hepatic artery after the gastroduodenal artery arises, running in the hepatoduodenal ligament within the portal triad and dividing into right and left hepatic arteries.
FJ3081.clinicalCondition: Hepatic artery thrombosis after transplantation — bile ducts depend solely on this arterial supply and become ischemic.
FJ3081.clinicalScenario: On day two after liver transplantation, rising transaminases prompt Doppler study showing hepatic artery proper thrombosis; urgent revascularization follows.

FJ1679M.name: Hypothalamic branch of left posterior communicating artery
FJ1679M.details: Small perforating (premamillary) branch of the left posterior communicating artery supplying the posterior hypothalamus and mamillary region of the diencephalon.
FJ1679M.clinicalCondition: Perforator injury during aneurysm surgery — hypothalamic ischemia causes temperature dysregulation and hypersomnolence.
FJ1679M.clinicalScenario: After clipping of a posterior communicating artery aneurysm, a patient develops temperature instability and excessive sleepiness attributed to hypothalamic perforator ischemia.

FJ1679.name: Hypothalamic branch of right posterior communicating artery
FJ1679.details: Tiny perforating twig from the right posterior communicating artery near its origin from the internal carotid; supplies anterior hypothalamus, tuber cinereum and optic tract region.
FJ1679.clinicalCondition: Hypothalamic perforator infarction — small-vessel stroke here disrupts autonomic and endocrine regulation.
FJ1679.clinicalScenario: After posterior communicating aneurysm clipping, a patient develops labile temperature, diabetes insipidus and drowsiness from hypothalamic perforator injury.

FJ3437.name: Ileal artery
FJ3437.details: One of multiple branches from the left side of the superior mesenteric artery; runs in the mesentery, forming arcades and vasa recta supplying the ileum.
FJ3437.clinicalCondition: Acute mesenteric ischaemia — SMA embolus lodges distally and infarcts jejunal/ileal loops.
FJ3437.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation develops severe central abdominal pain out of proportion to signs; CT shows pneumatosis of ileum.

FJ2034.name: Ileal branch of inferior branch of ileocolic artery
FJ2034.details: Terminal division of the ileocolic artery's inferior branch; anastomoses with the last ileal branch of the SMA, supplying terminal ileum and caecal base.
FJ2034.clinicalCondition: Watershed anastomotic insufficiency — hypotension can ischaemically injure the terminal ileum despite this collateral.
FJ2034.clinicalScenario: After prolonged shock, a patient develops right iliac fossa pain and bloody stool; colonoscopy shows ischaemic terminal ileitis.

FJ3439.name: Ileocolic artery
FJ3439.details: Lowest right-sided branch of the SMA; descends rightward giving colic, caecal, appendicular and ileal branches to terminal ileum, caecum, appendix and ascending colon.
FJ3439.clinicalCondition: Appendicular artery thrombosis — occlusion of its appendicular branch predisposes to gangrenous appendicitis.
FJ3439.clinicalScenario: An elderly diabetic with right iliac fossa pain rapidly develops peritonitis; theatre finds a gangrenous appendix with thrombosed appendicular vessels.

FJ2987.name: Inferior branch of medial segmental artery
FJ2987.details: Small pulmonary arterial sub-branch within the medial basal (cardiac) segment of the right lower lobe, arising from the basal trunk of the right pulmonary artery.
FJ2987.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — embolus in basal branches causes pleuritic pain and haemoptysis.
FJ2987.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient develops pleuritic pain and a wedge-shaped basal opacity on CT pulmonary angiography showing a filling defect.

FJ2988.name: Inferior branch of medial segmental artery
FJ2988.details: Companion sub-branch of the medial basal segmental pulmonary artery of the right lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus to supply the cardiac segment.
FJ2988.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — peripheral embolic occlusion produces a Hampton hump opacity.
FJ2988.clinicalScenario: A long-haul traveller presents with pleuritic pain, tachycardia and haemoptysis; CTPA confirms a right lower-lobe segmental embolus.

FJ2896.name: Inferior lingular artery
FJ2896.details: Lower division of the lingular branch of the left pulmonary artery; descends to supply the inferior lingular segment of the left upper lobe.
FJ2896.clinicalCondition: Lingular pneumonia — infection, not the artery itself, classically obscures the left heart border.
FJ2896.clinicalScenario: A patient with fever and cough has a chest radiograph showing loss of the left heart border silhouette from lingular consolidation.

FJ2897.name: Inferior lingular artery
FJ2897.details: Second mesh of the inferior lingular branch of the left pulmonary artery, running with the inferior lingular bronchus to aerated lingular parenchyma.
FJ2897.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — lingular branch occlusion may mimic lingular infection radiologically.
FJ2897.clinicalScenario: An immobile stroke patient becomes breathless; CTPA shows an embolus in a lingular pulmonary branch with peripheral consolidation.

FJ3442.name: Inferior mesenteric artery
FJ3442.details: Arises from the aorta at L3; supplies hindgut via left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal arteries — distal transverse colon to upper anal canal.
FJ3442.clinicalCondition: Ischaemic colitis — low flow at the splenic flexure watershed causes mucosal infarction.
FJ3442.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient after aortic surgery passes bloody diarrhoea; flexible sigmoidoscopy shows segmental ischaemic colitis at the splenic flexure.

FJ3444.name: Inferior pancreatic artery
FJ3444.details: Branch typically of the splenic artery or SMA running along the inferior pancreatic border, anastomosing with pancreatic branches to supply body and tail.
FJ3444.clinicalCondition: Pancreatic ischaemia in necrotising pancreatitis — compromised pancreatic perfusion worsens necrosis.
FJ3444.clinicalScenario: A patient with severe acute pancreatitis deteriorates; contrast CT shows non-enhancing pancreatic body suggesting ischaemic necrosis.

FJ3446.name: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FJ3446.details: First branch of the SMA; divides into anterior/posterior branches forming an arcade with the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery around the pancreatic head and duodenum.
FJ3446.clinicalCondition: Median arcuate ligament syndrome — enlarged pancreaticoduodenal arcades collateralise a compressed coeliac trunk.
FJ3446.clinicalScenario: A young woman with postprandial epigastric pain and weight loss has imaging showing coeliac compression with prominent pancreaticoduodenal collaterals.

FJ2049.name: Inferior segmental branch of left renal artery
FJ2049.details: End-arterial segmental branch of the left renal artery supplying the inferior renal segment; segmental branches have no significant collateral anastomosis.
FJ2049.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction — embolic occlusion produces a wedge-shaped perfusion defect.
FJ2049.clinicalScenario: A patient with endocarditis develops left flank pain and haematuria; CT shows a wedge-shaped non-enhancing inferior renal pole.

FJ2043.name: Inferior segmental branch of right renal artery
FJ2043.details: End-arterial segmental branch of the right renal artery supplying the inferior segment of the right kidney, entering at the hilum in a predictable segmental pattern.
FJ2043.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction — often embolic from atrial fibrillation or endocarditis.
FJ2043.clinicalScenario: A patient with new atrial fibrillation reports right flank pain and microscopic haematuria; imaging reveals an inferior segment renal infarct.

FJ1660M.name: Insular part of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1660M.details: M2 segment of the left MCA, looping over the insula within the lateral sulcus after the genu at the limen insulae; gives insular branches.
FJ1660M.clinicalCondition: M2 occlusion stroke — dominant-side blockage causes aphasia with face/arm weakness.
FJ1660M.clinicalScenario: A patient suddenly cannot speak fluently and has right facial weakness; angiography shows a left M2 insular segment occlusion.

FJ1694M.name: Insular part of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1694M.details: Second mesh of the left MCA insular (M2) segment, coursing over the insular cortex deep within the Sylvian fissure before emerging as opercular branches.
FJ1694M.clinicalCondition: Insular stroke — M2 branch occlusion can add dysphagia and autonomic instability.
FJ1694M.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation develops expressive aphasia and right arm drift; MRI shows infarct centred on the left insula.

FJ1660.name: Insular part of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1660.details: M2 segment of the right MCA, arching over the insula in the lateral sulcus and dividing into superior and inferior trunks.
FJ1660.clinicalCondition: M2 occlusion stroke — non-dominant occlusion causes left neglect and anosognosia.
FJ1660.clinicalScenario: A patient ignores the left side of her plate and denies weakness; imaging shows a right M2 insular occlusion.

FJ1694.name: Insular part of right middle cerebral artery
