FJ1694.details: Second mesh of the right MCA insular segment, running on the insular surface deep to the frontal and temporal opercula.
FJ1694.clinicalCondition: Insular ribbon infarction — early CT sign of MCA territory stroke.
FJ1694.clinicalScenario: A patient presents within the thrombolysis window; CT shows loss of the right insular ribbon, prompting urgent reperfusion therapy.

FJ1681M.name: Intermediomedial branch of left callosomarginal artery
FJ1681M.details: Small cortical branch of the left callosomarginal artery (ACA branch) running in the cingulate sulcus; supplies intermediate medial frontal/paracentral cortex and cingulum.
FJ1681M.clinicalCondition: ACA territory infarction — medial frontal involvement weakens the contralateral leg.
FJ1681M.clinicalScenario: A patient develops isolated right leg weakness and apathy; MRI shows a left medial frontal infarct in callosomarginal territory.

FJ1681.name: Intermediomedial branch of right callosomarginal artery
FJ1681.details: Small cortical branch of the right callosomarginal artery in the cingulate sulcus, supplying medial premotor and paracentral regions of the right hemisphere.
FJ1681.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarction — occlusion causes contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss.
FJ1681.clinicalScenario: A patient with a patent foramen ovale develops sudden left leg monoparesis; imaging localises infarction to the right paracentral lobule.

FJ1684M.name: Lateral branch of left pontine artery
FJ1684M.details: Circumferential pontine branch from the basilar artery, sweeping laterally around the left pons to supply the lateral tegmentum and middle cerebellar peduncle region.
FJ1684M.clinicalCondition: Lateral pontine syndrome — occlusion mimics AICA territory signs with ataxia and facial sensory loss.
FJ1684M.clinicalScenario: A hypertensive patient develops vertigo, left facial numbness and limb ataxia; MRI confirms a lateral pontine infarct.

FJ1683M.name: Lateral branch of left superior cerebellar artery
FJ1683M.details: Lateral (superior) division of the left superior cerebellar artery, coursing along the tentorial surface to supply the superior cerebellar hemisphere and dentate region.
FJ1683M.clinicalCondition: Superior cerebellar artery infarction — causes ipsilateral limb ataxia and dysarthria.
FJ1683M.clinicalScenario: A patient with vertebral dissection develops slurred speech and left-sided clumsiness; MRI shows a superior cerebellar infarct.

FJ3001.name: Lateral branch of right anterior basal segmental artery
FJ3001.details: Sub-branch of the right anterior basal segmental pulmonary artery, supplying the lateral portion of the anterior basal segment of the right lower lobe.
FJ3001.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — small basal emboli cause pleuritic pain and hypoxaemia.
FJ3001.clinicalScenario: A patient on chemotherapy develops pleuritic pain; CTPA reveals an embolus in a right lower-lobe basal segmental branch.

FJ3004.name: Lateral branch of right lateral basal segmental artery
FJ3004.details: Sub-branch of the right lateral basal segmental pulmonary artery following its bronchus to the lateral basal segment of the right lower lobe.
FJ3004.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism — basal segmental occlusion may produce infarction and pleural effusion.
FJ3004.clinicalScenario: A postoperative hip patient becomes tachypnoeic with a small right pleural effusion; CTPA shows a lateral basal embolic occlusion.

FJ3005.name: Lateral branch of right lateral basal segmental artery
FJ3005.details: Second mesh of the lateral branch of the right lateral basal segmental pulmonary artery, ramifying within the lateral basal segment parenchyma.
FJ3005.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary infarction — peripheral occlusion gives a wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity.
FJ3005.clinicalScenario: A patient with malignancy presents with haemoptysis; CT shows a pleural-based wedge opacity fed by an occluded basal branch.

FJ3006.name: Lateral branch of right lateral basal segmental artery
FJ3006.details: Third mesh of this lateral basal sub-branch of the right pulmonary artery, accompanying subsegmental bronchi of the right lower lobe.
FJ3006.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary thromboembolism — CTPA filling defects here confirm segmental-level disease.
FJ3006.clinicalScenario: A pregnant patient with dyspnoea undergoes CTPA after a positive D-dimer workup, showing a right basal segmental embolus.

FJ3007.name: Lateral branch of right lateral basal segmental artery
FJ3007.details: Fourth mesh of the lateral branch of the right lateral basal segmental pulmonary artery, supplying peripheral lateral basal lung tissue.
FJ3007.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction with haemoptysis — peripheral embolic occlusion necroses a small lung wedge.
FJ3007.clinicalScenario: A young smoker on oral contraceptives develops pleuritic pain and blood-streaked sputum; imaging confirms a basal pulmonary infarct.

FJ1684.name: Lateral branch of right pontine artery
FJ1684.details: Long circumferential branch of the basilar artery curving around the right pons, supplying lateral pontine tegmentum near trigeminal root entry.
FJ1684.clinicalCondition: Lateral pontine infarction — produces ipsilateral facial sensory loss and ataxia.
FJ1684.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient develops right facial numbness, vertigo and gait unsteadiness; MRI shows a lateral pontine lesion.

FJ1683.name: Lateral branch of right superior cerebellar artery
FJ1683.details: Lateral (superior) division of the right superior cerebellar artery, running below the tentorium to supply the superior cerebellar hemisphere and vermis laterally.
FJ1683.clinicalCondition: SCA syndrome — ipsilateral ataxia, dysarthria and contralateral pain-temperature loss.
FJ1683.clinicalScenario: A patient with severe vertigo and vomiting cannot walk straight; MRI shows infarction of the right superior cerebellum.

FJ2991.name: Lateral branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2991.details: Sub-branch of the apical (superior) segmental artery of the right upper lobe pulmonary artery, supplying the lateral part of the apical segment.
FJ2991.clinicalCondition: Apical segmental pulmonary embolism — occlusion may accompany upper-lobe infarction.
FJ2991.clinicalScenario: A patient with a central line develops breathlessness; CTPA shows an embolus in the right upper-lobe apical segmental branch.

FJ2992.name: Lateral branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2992.details: Second mesh of the lateral branch of the right upper-lobe superior segmental pulmonary artery, ramifying with apical subsegmental bronchi.
FJ2992.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism — segmental defects are diagnostic on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2992.clinicalScenario: An obese postoperative patient desaturates; CTPA demonstrates a filling defect in the right apical segmental pulmonary artery.

FJ2993.name: Lateral branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2993.details: Third mesh of this apical segmental sub-branch of the right pulmonary artery, supplying peripheral apical parenchyma near the pleura.
FJ2993.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — pleural-based occlusion causes pleuritic pain and a hump-shaped opacity.
FJ2993.clinicalScenario: A patient with a leg DVT develops sharp right upper chest pain; CT shows a peripheral wedge opacity in the apex.

FJ3092.name: Lateral inferior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3092.details: Segmental branch of the left hepatic artery supplying the inferior part of the lateral segment (segments II–III) of the left hepatic lobe.
FJ3092.clinicalCondition: Hepatic ischaemia after embolisation — segmental branch occlusion can infarct lateral segment tissue.
FJ3092.clinicalScenario: After chemoembolisation for a left-lobe tumour, a patient develops fever and pain; CT shows non-enhancing lateral segment liver.

FJ2336.name: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of left little finger
FJ2336.details: Small artery on the radial (lateral) side of the left little finger arising from its common palmar digital artery; runs with the proper palmar digital nerve.
FJ2336.clinicalCondition: Digital artery thrombosis — occlusion causes a cold, painful, cyanosed fingertip.
FJ2336.clinicalScenario: A smoker presents with a dusky, painful left little fingertip; Doppler shows absent flow in its digital arteries.

FJ2334.name: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of left middle finger
FJ2334.details: Radial-side proper palmar digital artery of the left middle finger from the second common palmar digital artery of the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2334.clinicalCondition: Fingertip ischaemia in Raynaud phenomenon — digital vasospasm blanches the digit.
FJ2334.clinicalScenario: A young woman reports her left middle finger turning white then blue in cold weather, with normal pulses between attacks.

FJ2335.name: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of left ring finger
FJ2335.details: Radial-side proper palmar digital artery of the left ring finger, branching from the third common palmar digital artery and accompanying the digital nerve.
FJ2335.clinicalCondition: Laceration bleeding — divided digital arteries bleed briskly and may need ligation.
FJ2335.clinicalScenario: A chef cuts the left ring finger deeply; pulsatile bleeding from the digital artery requires pressure and wound exploration.

FJ2368.name: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of right little finger
FJ2368.details: Radial-side proper palmar digital artery of the right little finger from the superficial palmar arch's digital branches; anastomoses across the fingertip pulp.
FJ2368.clinicalCondition: Hypothenar hammer syndrome — ulnar-sided digital ischaemia follows repeated palmar trauma.
FJ2368.clinicalScenario: A carpenter who uses his palm as a hammer develops a cold, ulcerated right little fingertip from distal ulnar artery thrombosis.

FJ2365.name: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of right middle finger
FJ2365.details: Radial-side proper palmar digital artery of the right middle finger, arising from a common palmar digital artery and running alongside the digital nerve.
FJ2365.clinicalCondition: Digital vasospasm in vibration white finger — occupational vibration damages digital vessels.
FJ2365.clinicalScenario: A road worker notices blanching and numbness of the right middle finger in winter, attributed to vibrating-tool exposure.

FJ2366.name: Lateral proper palmar digital artery of right ring finger
FJ2366.details: Radial-side proper palmar digital artery of the right ring finger from the third common palmar digital artery of the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2366.clinicalCondition: Embolic digital occlusion — cardiac emboli can lodge in small digital arteries.
FJ2366.clinicalScenario: A patient with infective endocarditis develops a painful blue right ring fingertip with splinter haemorrhages in other nails.

FJ3091.name: Lateral superior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3091.details: Segmental branch of the left hepatic artery supplying the superior part of the lateral segment (segment II) of the left liver lobe.
FJ3091.clinicalCondition: Segmental hepatic infarction — rare because of portal venous dual supply, but follows arterial injury.
FJ3091.clinicalScenario: After laparoscopic cholecystectomy with aberrant arterial injury, imaging shows a small segment II perfusion defect in the left lobe.

FJ3093.name: Lateral superior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3093.details: Second mesh of the lateral superior segmental branch from the left hepatic artery, ramifying in segment II near the falciform ligament.
FJ3093.clinicalCondition: Hepatic artery thrombosis after transplant — threatens bile ducts supplied solely by arterial blood.
FJ3093.clinicalScenario: A liver transplant recipient develops rising cholestatic enzymes; Doppler suggests hepatic arterial compromise requiring urgent revascularisation.

FJ3013.name: Laterobasal branch of right posterior basal segmental artery
FJ3013.details: Sub-branch of the right posterior basal segmental pulmonary artery supplying the laterobasal portion of the posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe.
FJ3013.clinicalCondition: Basal pulmonary embolism — occlusion contributes to lower-lobe infarction and effusion.
FJ3013.clinicalScenario: A patient after knee replacement develops pleuritic pain and a right basal opacity; CTPA confirms posterior basal segment emboli.

FJ3014.name: Laterobasal branch of right posterior basal segmental artery
FJ3014.details: Second mesh of the laterobasal sub-branch of the right posterior basal segmental pulmonary artery, following subsegmental bronchi to peripheral lung.
FJ3014.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — peripheral basal occlusion classically causes haemoptysis and pleuritic pain.
FJ3014.clinicalScenario: A long-distance driver presents with blood-streaked sputum and calf swelling; imaging shows DVT with right basal pulmonary infarction.

FJ2883.name: Left anterior basal segmental artery
FJ2883.details: Branch of the basal trunk of the left pulmonary artery accompanying the anterior basal bronchus to supply that segment of the left lower lobe.
FJ2883.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — a target branch in CTPA diagnosis of PE.
FJ2883.clinicalScenario: A patient with cancer develops acute dyspnoea; CTPA shows emboli in left lower-lobe basal segmental arteries.

FJ2886.name: Left anterior basal segmental artery
FJ2886.details: Second mesh of the left anterior basal segmental pulmonary artery, dividing within the anterior basal segment alongside its bronchus.
FJ2886.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — peripheral occlusion produces a pleural-based wedge opacity.
FJ2886.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient has pleuritic left basal pain; CT demonstrates infarction in the anterior basal segment.

FJ2887.name: Left anterior basal segmental artery
FJ2887.details: Third mesh of the left anterior basal segmental artery of the pulmonary circulation, supplying distal anterior basal parenchyma.
FJ2887.clinicalCondition: Chronic thromboembolic disease — unresolved segmental emboli can raise pulmonary pressures.
FJ2887.clinicalScenario: A patient with previous PE reports progressive breathlessness; perfusion scanning shows persistent left basal segmental defects.

FJ1654M.name: Left anterior cerebral artery
FJ1654M.details: Arises from the left internal carotid terminus, runs medially (A1) then up around the corpus callosum (A2) via callosomarginal and pericallosal branches; supplies medial hemisphere.
FJ1654M.clinicalCondition: ACA stroke — causes contralateral leg-predominant weakness, abulia and urinary incontinence.
FJ1654M.clinicalScenario: A patient becomes apathetic with right leg weakness after anterior communicating aneurysm rupture floods the left ACA territory.

FJ1658M.name: Left anterior choroidal artery
FJ1658M.details: Arises from the left internal carotid just distal to the posterior communicating origin; supplies posterior limb of internal capsule, optic tract, lateral geniculate body and choroid plexus.
FJ1658M.clinicalCondition: Anterior choroidal artery syndrome — hemiparesis, hemisensory loss and hemianopia triad.
FJ1658M.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient develops dense right weakness, sensory loss and visual field cut from a small deep left infarct.

FJ2212.name: Left anterior circumflex humeral artery
FJ2212.details: Small branch of the third part of the left axillary artery; winds anteriorly around the surgical neck of the humerus, anastomosing with the posterior circumflex.
FJ2212.clinicalCondition: Quadrilateral space syndrome — compression affects this artery and the axillary nerve.
FJ2212.clinicalScenario: A volleyball player has posterior shoulder pain and deltoid weakness; imaging shows fibrous bands compressing the circumflex vessels.

FJ2214.name: Left anterior interosseous artery
FJ2214.details: Branch of the left common interosseous artery descending on the anterior interosseous membrane with the anterior interosseous nerve, supplying deep forearm flexors.
FJ2214.clinicalCondition: Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome — vascular or neuritic insult weakens pinch grip.
FJ2214.clinicalScenario: A patient cannot make an 'OK' sign with the left hand, unable to flex the thumb tip and index distal phalanx.

FJ1667M.name: Left anterior parietal artery
FJ1667M.details: Cortical branch of the left MCA (angular/posterior division) supplying the anterior parietal lobe including somatosensory association cortex of the dominant hemisphere.
FJ1667M.clinicalCondition: Dominant parietal stroke — causes Gerstmann features and receptive language difficulty.
FJ1667M.clinicalScenario: A patient suddenly cannot calculate or write and confuses left and right after a left parietal branch embolus.

FJ2902.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2902.details: Branch of the left pulmonary artery's upper-lobe division accompanying the anterior segment bronchus (B3) to supply the anterior segment of the left upper lobe.
FJ2902.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — upper-lobe branch occlusion seen on CTPA.
FJ2902.clinicalScenario: A patient with nephrotic syndrome develops dyspnoea; CTPA shows an embolus in the left upper-lobe anterior segmental artery.

FJ2904.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2904.details: Second mesh of the left anterior segmental pulmonary artery, subdividing within the anterior segment of the left upper lobe.
FJ2904.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — peripheral occlusion gives pleuritic pain over the upper chest.
FJ2904.clinicalScenario: A young postpartum patient develops sharp anterior chest pain; imaging confirms a small left upper-lobe pulmonary infarct.

FJ2905.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2905.details: Third mesh of the left anterior segmental pulmonary artery, following subsegmental bronchi toward the anterior segment pleural surface.
FJ2905.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism — a filling defect here confirms segmental embolism in symptomatic patients.
FJ2905.clinicalScenario: A patient with a fractured pelvis becomes hypoxic; CTPA demonstrates emboli including the left anterior segmental branch.

FJ2906.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2906.details: Fourth mesh of the left anterior segmental artery within the left upper lobe's anterior segment, part of the pulmonary arterial tree paired with airways.
FJ2906.clinicalCondition: Septic pulmonary emboli — infected emboli lodge in segmental branches causing cavitating nodules.
FJ2906.clinicalScenario: An intravenous drug user with tricuspid endocarditis develops multiple peripheral cavitating lung lesions from septic emboli.

FJ2907.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2907.details: Fifth mesh of the left anterior segmental pulmonary artery, ramifying in the anterior segment of the left upper lobe beside its bronchus.
FJ2907.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary thromboembolism — segmental occlusion detected as a CTPA filling defect.
FJ2907.clinicalScenario: A patient recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia develops new hypoxia; CTPA shows a left upper-lobe segmental embolus.

FJ2908.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2908.details: Sixth mesh of the left anterior segmental artery of the left pulmonary artery, supplying distal anterior segment parenchyma.
FJ2908.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — small peripheral infarcts present with pleuritic pain and haemoptysis.
FJ2908.clinicalScenario: A patient on hormone therapy presents with pleuritic pain; CT reveals a wedge-shaped left upper-lobe opacity.

FJ2909.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2909.details: Seventh mesh of the left anterior segmental pulmonary artery, a terminal division accompanying subsegmental anterior bronchi.
FJ2909.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — contributes to ventilation-perfusion mismatch and hypoxaemia.
FJ2909.clinicalScenario: An elderly immobile patient desaturates suddenly; CTPA confirms multiple segmental emboli including this anterior segmental branch.

FJ2910.name: Left anterior segmental artery
FJ2910.details: Eighth mesh of the left anterior segmental pulmonary artery within the anterior segment of the left upper lobe.
FJ2910.clinicalCondition: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension — organised unresolved emboli obstruct segmental arteries.
FJ2910.clinicalScenario: A patient with prior PE and worsening exertional dyspnoea has echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension and mismatched perfusion defects.

FJ1657M.name: Left anterior spinal artery
FJ1657M.details: Left contributor (from vertebral artery) to the single midline anterior spinal artery descending in the anterior median fissure, supplying anterior two-thirds of the cord.
FJ1657M.clinicalCondition: Anterior spinal artery syndrome — infarction causes bilateral weakness and pain-temperature loss, sparing proprioception.
FJ1657M.clinicalScenario: After aortic aneurysm repair, a patient wakes with flaccid paraplegia and lost pain sensation but preserved vibration sense.

FJ1659M.name: Left anterior temporal artery
FJ1659M.details: Cortical branch of the left MCA arising from its inferior division, supplying the anterior temporal lobe including temporal pole cortex.
FJ1659M.clinicalCondition: Temporal branch occlusion stroke — dominant-side infarction impairs naming and comprehension.
FJ1659M.clinicalScenario: A patient suddenly cannot name familiar objects after an embolus occludes a left anterior temporal MCA branch.

FJ2065.name: Left anterior tibial artery
FJ2065.details: Smaller terminal branch of the popliteal artery; pierces the interosseous membrane into the anterior leg compartment, accompanies deep fibular nerve, continues as dorsalis pedis.
FJ2065.clinicalCondition: Anterior compartment syndrome — injury or swelling here threatens the artery and nerve.
FJ2065.clinicalScenario: A footballer with a tibial fracture develops pain on passive toe stretch and a tense anterior compartment needing fasciotomy.

FJ2066.name: Left anterior tibial recurrent artery
FJ2066.details: Small branch of the left anterior tibial artery just below the knee, ascending to join the genicular anastomosis around the knee joint.
FJ2066.clinicalCondition: Genicular collateral circulation — these recurrent branches sustain the knee when popliteal flow fails.
FJ2066.clinicalScenario: Angiography in a patient with popliteal occlusion shows the knee supplied by enlarged recurrent collateral branches.

FJ2259.name: Left anterior ulnar recurrent artery
FJ2259.details: Small ascending branch of the left ulnar artery near its origin, running up to anastomose with the inferior ulnar collateral artery around the elbow.
FJ2259.clinicalCondition: Elbow collateral network — preserves forearm flow after brachial artery injury above the elbow.
FJ2259.clinicalScenario: After a supracondylar fracture, the left hand remains perfused via elbow collaterals despite a diminished brachial pulse.

FJ2915.name: Left apical segmental artery
FJ2915.details: Upper division branch of the left pulmonary artery (often a common apicoposterior trunk) supplying the apical segment of the left upper lobe.
FJ2915.clinicalCondition: Apical pulmonary embolism — occlusion may be missed without careful CTPA review.
FJ2915.clinicalScenario: A patient with pleuritic pain has CTPA showing a small embolus in the left apical segmental pulmonary artery.

FJ2916.name: Left apical segmental artery
FJ2916.details: Second mesh of the left apical segmental pulmonary artery, accompanying the apical bronchus toward the lung apex above the clavicle.
FJ2916.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — apical occlusion produces pleural-based opacity near the apex.
FJ2916.clinicalScenario: A smoker with a DVT develops shoulder-tip pleuritic pain; imaging shows an apical wedge-shaped pulmonary infarct.

FJ2917.name: Left apical segmental artery
FJ2917.details: Third mesh of the left apical segmental pulmonary artery, ramifying in apical parenchyma of the left upper lobe.
FJ2917.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — contributes to dead-space ventilation when occluded.
FJ2917.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient becomes tachycardic and hypoxic; CTPA demonstrates emboli in several left upper-lobe segmental branches.

FJ2918.name: Left apical segmental artery
FJ2918.details: Fourth mesh of the left apical segmental artery of the pulmonary trunk's left branch, supplying distal apical lung tissue.
FJ2918.clinicalCondition: Septic emboli — right-sided endocarditis showers segmental pulmonary branches with infected emboli.
FJ2918.clinicalScenario: A patient with a pacemaker infection develops fever and multiple peripheral lung nodules from septic pulmonary emboli.

FJ2067.name: Left arcuate artery
FJ2067.details: Branch of the left dorsalis pedis artery arcing laterally across the metatarsal bases, giving the second to fourth dorsal metatarsal arteries.
FJ2067.clinicalCondition: Forefoot ischaemia in diabetes — small foot artery disease impairs wound healing.
FJ2067.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient has a non-healing forefoot ulcer; Doppler shows poor arcuate and metatarsal artery flow.

FJ2338.name: Left arteria princeps pollicis
FJ2338.details: Main artery of the thumb, arising from the left radial artery in the palm; runs along the first metacarpal and divides into proper palmar digital arteries of the thumb.
FJ2338.clinicalCondition: Thumb ischaemia — injury threatens pinch and grip function disproportionately.
FJ2338.clinicalScenario: A glass injury in the thenar palm bleeds briskly; the thumb is pale until the princeps pollicis injury is repaired.

FJ2339.name: Left arteria princeps pollicis
FJ2339.details: Second mesh of the left princeps pollicis artery, the dominant supply to the thumb pulp and nail bed from the radial artery.
FJ2339.clinicalCondition: Allen test relevance — collateral thumb flow depends on ulnar arch completeness.
FJ2339.clinicalScenario: Before radial artery harvest, an Allen test confirms ulnar collateral flow can sustain the thumb and hand.

FJ2314.name: Left arteria radialis indicis
FJ2314.details: Slender branch of the left radial artery (often shared with princeps pollicis) running along the lateral side of the index finger to its tip.
FJ2314.clinicalCondition: Index finger ischaemia — compromises precision pinch used in fine tasks.
FJ2314.clinicalScenario: A seamstress develops a painful blue left index fingertip; vascular studies show distal radial-side digital occlusion.

FJ2332.name: Left arteria radialis indicis
FJ2332.details: Second mesh of the left radialis indicis artery, coursing on the radial border of the index finger beside the digital nerve.
FJ2332.clinicalCondition: Digital artery injury — lacerations here bleed briskly and risk fingertip necrosis if both sides fail.
FJ2332.clinicalScenario: A carpenter slices the radial side of his left index finger; pulsatile bleeding is controlled and the vessel repaired.

FJ2216.name: Left axillary artery
FJ2216.details: Continuation of the left subclavian artery from the first rib to teres major, in three parts relative to pectoralis minor; becomes the brachial artery.
FJ2216.clinicalCondition: Axillary artery injury in shoulder dislocation — threatens upper-limb perfusion, especially in the elderly.
FJ2216.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman dislocates her left shoulder and has a weak radial pulse; CT angiography confirms axillary artery intimal tear.

FJ2219.name: Left brachial artery
FJ2219.details: Main artery of the left arm from teres major to the cubital fossa, dividing into radial and ulnar arteries; palpated medial to biceps tendon.
FJ2219.clinicalCondition: Brachial artery injury in supracondylar fracture — Volkmann ischaemic contracture may follow untreated occlusion.
FJ2219.clinicalScenario: A child with a displaced left supracondylar fracture has a pink but pulseless hand requiring urgent reduction and vascular review.

FJ1676M.name: Left callosomarginal artery
FJ1676M.details: Major branch of the left pericallosal (ACA) artery running in the cingulate sulcus; supplies medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule.
FJ1676M.clinicalCondition: Callosomarginal infarction — causes contralateral leg weakness and grasp reflex.
FJ1676M.clinicalScenario: A patient develops right foot drag and abulia after an anterior communicating aneurysm bleed affects the left ACA branches.

FJ2221.name: Left circumflex scapular artery
FJ2221.details: Branch of the left subscapular artery passing through the triangular space to the infraspinous fossa, joining the scapular anastomosis.
FJ2221.clinicalCondition: Scapular collateral circulation — maintains shoulder flow when the axillary artery is blocked.
FJ2221.clinicalScenario: Angiography for subclavian stenosis shows a hypertrophied circumflex scapular artery collateralising the arm.

FJ3494.name: Left colic artery
FJ3494.details: First branch of the inferior mesenteric artery; ascending and descending branches supply the distal transverse and descending colon via the marginal artery.
FJ3494.clinicalCondition: Watershed ischaemia at Griffiths point — marginal artery insufficiency ischaemises the splenic flexure.
FJ3494.clinicalScenario: A hypotensive patient develops bloody diarrhoea; colonoscopy shows ischaemic change maximal at the splenic flexure watershed.

FJ3483.name: Left common carotid artery
FJ3483.details: Second branch of the aortic arch; ascends in the carotid sheath and bifurcates at C4 into external and internal carotid arteries.
FJ3483.clinicalCondition: Carotid artery stenosis — bifurcation atheroma causes TIAs and embolic stroke.
FJ3483.clinicalScenario: A patient with recurrent transient right-arm weakness has duplex showing 80% stenosis at the left carotid bifurcation.

FJ3464.name: Left common iliac artery
FJ3464.details: Terminal branch of the aorta at L4, descending to the sacroiliac joint where it divides into external and internal iliac arteries; crossed by the ureter.
FJ3464.clinicalCondition: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche syndrome) — causes buttock claudication and impotence.
FJ3464.clinicalScenario: A heavy smoker reports buttock claudication and absent femoral pulses; CT angiography shows distal aortic and common iliac occlusion.

FJ2223.name: Left common interosseous artery
FJ2223.details: Short branch of the left ulnar artery dividing into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries supplying deep forearm compartments.
FJ2223.clinicalCondition: Forearm compartment syndrome — bleeding from interosseous branches can raise compartment pressure.
FJ2223.clinicalScenario: After a forearm fracture, a patient develops tense compartments and pain on passive stretch requiring emergency fasciotomy.

FJ2224.name: Left costocervical trunk
FJ2224.details: Branch of the second part of the left subclavian artery over the pleural dome; divides into deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries.
FJ2224.clinicalCondition: Subclavian steal physiology — proximal stenosis reverses vertebral flow, with this trunk among collateral pathways.
FJ2224.clinicalScenario: A patient with a weak left radial pulse and dizziness on arm exertion has imaging showing proximal subclavian stenosis.

FJ2225.name: Left deep brachial artery
FJ2225.details: Large branch of the left brachial artery (profunda brachii) accompanying the radial nerve through the spiral groove, supplying triceps and posterior arm.
FJ2225.clinicalCondition: Humeral shaft fracture — threatens this artery and the radial nerve in the groove.
FJ2225.clinicalScenario: A patient with a mid-shaft humeral fracture cannot extend the wrist and has posterior arm bleeding from the profunda branch.

FJ2226.name: Left deep cervical artery
FJ2226.details: Branch of the left costocervical trunk passing between the first rib neck and C7 transverse process to supply deep posterior neck muscles.
FJ2226.clinicalCondition: Cervical collateral supply — enlarges when vertebral or carotid flow is compromised.
FJ2226.clinicalScenario: Imaging in chronic vertebral artery occlusion shows prominent deep cervical collaterals reconstituting distal flow.

FJ2227.name: Left deep palmar arch
FJ2227.details: Formed mainly by the terminal left radial artery with the deep palmar branch of the ulnar; lies on the interossei, giving palmar metacarpal arteries.
FJ2227.clinicalCondition: Deep arch injury in crush wounds — hand perfusion usually survives via the superficial arch.
FJ2227.clinicalScenario: A machine worker crushes his left palm; angiography shows a disrupted deep arch but a viable hand through collaterals.

FJ2068.name: Left deep plantar artery
FJ2068.details: Deep branch of the left dorsalis pedis artery passing between the first two metatarsals into the sole, completing the plantar arch with the lateral plantar artery.
FJ2068.clinicalCondition: Plantar arch insufficiency — diabetic foot disease here worsens forefoot ulcer healing.
FJ2068.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient has a plantar forefoot ulcer; vascular assessment shows a diseased deep plantar contribution to the arch.

FJ2069.name: Left descending genicular artery
FJ2069.details: Branch of the left femoral artery just before the adductor hiatus; divides into saphenous and articular branches joining the knee anastomosis.
FJ2069.clinicalCondition: Knee collateral circulation — this branch helps sustain the leg in superficial femoral occlusion.
FJ2069.clinicalScenario: Angiography in chronic femoral occlusion shows the descending genicular artery reconstituting popliteal flow around the knee.

FJ3496.name: Left dorsal artery of penis
FJ3496.details: Terminal branch of the left internal pudendal artery running on the penile dorsum beneath Buck fascia, beside the dorsal nerve, supplying glans and skin.
FJ3496.clinicalCondition: Vasculogenic erectile dysfunction — pudendal/dorsal arterial insufficiency reduces penile perfusion.
FJ3496.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man with erectile dysfunction has penile Doppler showing reduced dorsal artery peak systolic velocities.

FJ3497.name: Left dorsal artery of penis
FJ3497.details: Second mesh of the left dorsal penile artery, coursing distally on the dorsum to the glans, paired with its fellow under the deep fascia.
FJ3497.clinicalCondition: Penile fracture surgery — dorsal vessels are avoided when repairing torn tunica albuginea.
FJ3497.clinicalScenario: During repair of a penile fracture, the surgeon preserves the dorsal neurovascular bundles while closing the tunica defect.

FJ2236.name: Left dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery
FJ2236.details: Small branch of the left ulnar artery just proximal to the pisiform, passing dorsally beneath flexor carpi ulnaris into the dorsal carpal network.
FJ2236.clinicalCondition: Dorsal carpal rete — collateral route sustaining the hand in radial artery occlusion.
FJ2236.clinicalScenario: After radial artery cannulation thrombosis, the left hand stays perfused through ulnar and dorsal carpal collaterals.

FJ2232.name: Left dorsal scapular artery
FJ2232.details: Arises variably from the left subclavian (second/third part) or transverse cervical artery; pierces the brachial plexus and descends deep to levator scapulae and rhomboids.
FJ2232.clinicalCondition: Nerve entrapment variation — its passage through the plexus is a surgical landmark in neck dissection.
FJ2232.clinicalScenario: During a left neck dissection, the surgeon identifies the dorsal scapular artery passing between brachial plexus trunks.

FJ2073.name: Left dorsalis pedis artery
FJ2073.details: Continuation of the left anterior tibial artery onto the foot dorsum, palpable lateral to extensor hallucis longus; gives lateral tarsal, arcuate and deep plantar branches.
FJ2073.clinicalCondition: Absent dorsalis pedis pulse — a marker of peripheral arterial disease (or a normal variant in ~10%).
FJ2073.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient has an impalpable left dorsalis pedis pulse with a foot ulcer, prompting arterial duplex assessment.

FJ3466.name: Left external iliac artery
FJ3466.details: Larger terminal branch of the left common iliac artery, running along the pelvic brim behind the inguinal ligament to become the femoral artery.
FJ3466.clinicalCondition: External iliac stenosis — causes thigh claudication and reduced femoral pulse.
FJ3466.clinicalScenario: A cyclist develops left thigh claudication; imaging reveals external iliac endofibrosis from repetitive hip flexion.

FJ2074.name: Left femoral artery
FJ2074.details: Main artery of the left lower limb, from the inguinal ligament through the femoral triangle and adductor canal to the hiatus, becoming popliteal.
FJ2074.clinicalCondition: Femoral pseudoaneurysm — a common complication of arterial catheterisation at this access site.
FJ2074.clinicalScenario: Two days after coronary angiography, a patient develops a painful pulsatile groin swelling confirmed as a femoral pseudoaneurysm.

FJ2315.name: Left first common palmar digital artery
FJ2315.details: First branch of the left superficial palmar arch, dividing into proper palmar digital arteries for the adjacent sides of index and middle fingers.
FJ2315.clinicalCondition: Digital ischaemia — small-vessel occlusion here blanches the web-space fingers.
FJ2315.clinicalScenario: A patient with scleroderma develops fingertip ulcers on the left index and middle fingers from digital artery disease.

FJ1973.name: Left first posterior intercostal artery
FJ1973.details: Branch of the supreme intercostal artery (from costocervical trunk) supplying the left first intercostal space, running below the first rib.
FJ1973.clinicalCondition: First-space collateral supply — relevant in coarctation where intercostals enlarge and notch ribs (spares upper spaces).
FJ1973.clinicalScenario: A patient with aortic coarctation shows inferior rib notching of lower ribs on chest radiography from dilated intercostal collaterals.

FJ2337.name: Left fourth common palmar digital artery
FJ2337.details: Medial branch of the left superficial palmar arch dividing into proper palmar digital arteries for the adjacent sides of the ring and little fingers.
FJ2337.clinicalCondition: Ulnar-sided digital ischaemia — often first affected in hypothenar hammer syndrome.
FJ2337.clinicalScenario: A mechanic presents with a cold left little finger and an occluded distal ulnar artery at the wrist.

FJ3499.name: Left gastric artery
FJ3499.details: Smallest branch of the coeliac trunk; runs up to the cardia then along the lesser curvature, anastomosing with the right gastric artery; supplies lower oesophagus and stomach.
FJ3499.clinicalCondition: Gastric ulcer bleeding — lesser-curvature ulcers can erode this artery.
FJ3499.clinicalScenario: A patient on NSAIDs vomits fresh blood; endoscopy finds a lesser-curvature ulcer with a visible gastric artery vessel.

FJ3501.name: Left gastro-epiploic artery
FJ3501.details: Terminal branch of the splenic artery running rightward along the greater curvature within the greater omentum, anastomosing with the right gastro-epiploic artery.
FJ3501.clinicalCondition: Greater curvature bleeding — omental branches are targets in embolisation for gastric haemorrhage.
FJ3501.clinicalScenario: Interventional radiology embolises a bleeding greater-curvature branch in a patient with a Dieulafoy lesion unresponsive to endoscopy.

FJ3511.name: Left inferior epigastric artery
FJ3511.details: Branch of the left external iliac artery just above the inguinal ligament; ascends behind the rectus sheath (lateral to Hesselbach triangle), anastomosing with the superior epigastric.
FJ3511.clinicalCondition: Rectus sheath haematoma — rupture of this artery causes acute abdominal wall pain mimicking peritonitis.
FJ3511.clinicalScenario: A patient on warfarin coughs violently then develops a tender abdominal wall mass; CT shows a rectus sheath haematoma.

FJ2076.name: Left inferior lateral genicular artery
FJ2076.details: Branch of the left popliteal artery passing laterally below the lateral femoral condyle, deep to the lateral collateral ligament, in the knee anastomosis.
FJ2076.clinicalCondition: Knee anastomotic collateral — helps perfuse the leg below popliteal embolism.
FJ2076.clinicalScenario: Angiography after acute popliteal embolus shows genicular collaterals maintaining weak distal runoff to the left foot.

FJ2077.name: Left inferior medial genicular artery
FJ2077.details: Branch of the left popliteal artery winding medially below the medial tibial condyle beneath the medial collateral ligament, joining the genicular anastomosis.
FJ2077.clinicalCondition: Genicular collateral circulation — enlarges in chronic superficial femoral artery occlusion.
FJ2077.clinicalScenario: A claudicant's angiogram shows prominent medial genicular collaterals bypassing a long left femoral occlusion.

FJ3514.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3514.details: First paired branch of the abdominal aorta (or coeliac trunk) ascending to the undersurface of the left diaphragm; gives superior suprarenal branches.
FJ3514.clinicalCondition: Diaphragmatic collateral in liver tumours — this artery may supply hepatocellular carcinoma near the dome.
FJ3514.clinicalScenario: During chemoembolisation planning, angiography shows a segment VII tumour partly supplied by the left inferior phrenic artery.

FJ3515.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3515.details: Second mesh of the left inferior phrenic artery, dividing into medial and lateral branches on the diaphragmatic undersurface.
FJ3515.clinicalCondition: Superior suprarenal supply — its branches contribute to adrenal perfusion assessed in adrenal surgery.
FJ3515.clinicalScenario: A surgeon removing a left adrenal tumour controls the inferior phrenic superior suprarenal branches to avoid bleeding.

FJ3516.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3516.details: Third mesh of the left inferior phrenic artery, running superomedially toward the central tendon and oesophageal opening of the diaphragm.
FJ3516.clinicalCondition: Variant origin — may arise from the left gastric or aorta, relevant in upper abdominal surgery.
FJ3516.clinicalScenario: Preoperative CT for gastric cancer maps a left inferior phrenic artery arising directly from the aorta.

FJ3517.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3517.details: Fourth mesh of the left inferior phrenic artery supplying the left crus and posteromedial diaphragm.
FJ3517.clinicalCondition: Diaphragmatic ischaemia is rare — rich anastomoses with pericardiacophrenic and musculophrenic vessels protect it.
FJ3517.clinicalScenario: Even after aortic branch embolisation, a patient's diaphragm remains viable on imaging thanks to phrenic collateral supply.

FJ3518.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3518.details: Fifth mesh of the left inferior phrenic artery, with branches ramifying over the inferior surface of the left hemidiaphragm.
FJ3518.clinicalCondition: Tumour collateral supply — extrahepatic feeders like this limit complete chemoembolisation of dome tumours.
FJ3518.clinicalScenario: A liver tumour at the dome recurs after embolisation because parasitized inferior phrenic feeders were untreated.

FJ3519.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3519.details: Sixth mesh of the left inferior phrenic artery, contributing twigs toward the spleen's diaphragmatic surface and the gastric fundus region.
FJ3519.clinicalCondition: Referred shoulder-tip pain — diaphragmatic irritation in its territory travels via the phrenic nerve (C3–5).
FJ3519.clinicalScenario: A patient with a subphrenic collection complains of left shoulder-tip pain from diaphragmatic irritation.

FJ3520.name: Left inferior phrenic artery
FJ3520.details: Seventh mesh of the left inferior phrenic artery, terminating in anastomoses with intercostal and musculophrenic branches at the diaphragmatic periphery.
FJ3520.clinicalCondition: Accessory hepatic supply — an aberrant left hepatic artery may travel with phrenic branches, complicating liver surgery.
FJ3520.clinicalScenario: A replaced left hepatic artery is identified on preoperative imaging before a Whipple procedure to prevent inadvertent injury.

FJ3467.name: Left inferior suprarenal artery
FJ3467.details: Branch of the left renal artery ascending to the lower part of the left suprarenal gland, anastomosing with middle and superior suprarenal arteries.
FJ3467.clinicalCondition: Adrenal perfusion redundancy — triple arterial supply protects the gland during renal artery clamping.
FJ3467.clinicalScenario: During left nephrectomy, the adrenal gland survives because its inferior suprarenal supply is preserved with phrenic branches.

FJ2210.name: Left inferior thyroid artery
FJ2210.details: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk looping medially behind the carotid sheath to the posterior thyroid; gives the inferior parathyroid supply and ascending cervical branch; recurrent laryngeal nerve crosses it.
FJ2210.clinicalCondition: Thyroid surgery nerve injury — the nerve's variable relation to this artery risks vocal cord palsy.
FJ2210.clinicalScenario: After total thyroidectomy, a patient has a breathy voice; laryngoscopy shows a left vocal cord palsy from nerve injury near the artery.

FJ2215.name: Left inferior ulnar collateral artery
FJ2215.details: Branch of the left brachial artery about 5 cm above the elbow, descending anterior to the medial epicondyle to join the anterior ulnar recurrent artery.
FJ2215.clinicalCondition: Elbow anastomosis — collateral channel protecting the forearm in brachial artery occlusion.
FJ2215.clinicalScenario: Angiography in a patient with brachial embolus shows the inferior ulnar collateral reconstituting ulnar flow at the elbow.

FJ1682M.name: Left internal carotid artery
FJ1682M.details: Arises at the left common carotid bifurcation (C4), ascends through the carotid canal and cavernous sinus, ending as anterior and middle cerebral arteries; no cervical branches.
FJ1682M.clinicalCondition: Internal carotid occlusion — causes major hemispheric stroke or amaurosis fugax from retinal emboli.
FJ1682M.clinicalScenario: A patient reports transient monocular blindness in the left eye, then develops right hemiparesis from left ICA territory embolism.

FJ3468.name: Left internal iliac artery
FJ3468.details: Smaller terminal branch of the left common iliac artery at the sacroiliac joint; divides into anterior (visceral) and posterior (parietal) divisions supplying pelvis and gluteal region.
FJ3468.clinicalCondition: Pelvic fracture haemorrhage — internal iliac branches are embolised to control life-threatening bleeding.
FJ3468.clinicalScenario: A patient with an unstable pelvic fracture remains hypotensive despite transfusion; angiographic embolisation of internal iliac branches stops the bleeding.

FJ1972.name: Left internal thoracic artery
FJ1972.details: Branch of the first part of the left subclavian artery descending behind the upper six costal cartilages, ending as musculophrenic and superior epigastric arteries.
FJ1972.clinicalCondition: CABG conduit of choice — its use as a graft to the LAD gives superior long-term patency.
FJ1972.clinicalScenario: A patient undergoing bypass surgery receives a left internal thoracic artery graft anastomosed to the left anterior descending artery.

FJ2882.name: Left lateral basal segmental artery
FJ2882.details: Branch of the basal trunk of the left pulmonary artery accompanying the lateral basal bronchus to that segment of the left lower lobe.
FJ2882.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — basal branches are frequent sites of embolic occlusion.
FJ2882.clinicalScenario: A patient with calf DVT develops pleuritic pain; CTPA shows an embolus in the left lateral basal segmental artery.

FJ2921.name: Left lateral basal segmental artery
FJ2921.details: Second mesh of the left lateral basal segmental pulmonary artery, subdividing with lateral basal subsegmental bronchi.
FJ2921.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — occlusion of basal branches causes pleural-based wedge opacities.
FJ2921.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient has haemoptysis and a left basal wedge opacity from segmental embolic infarction.

FJ2922.name: Left lateral basal segmental artery
FJ2922.details: Third mesh of the left lateral basal segmental artery in the basal trunk territory of the left pulmonary artery.
FJ2922.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism — multiple basal defects explain hypoxaemia disproportionate to chest signs.
FJ2922.clinicalScenario: An immobile patient with pneumonia becomes suddenly more breathless; CTPA reveals superimposed left basal segmental emboli.

FJ2923.name: Left lateral basal segmental artery
FJ2923.details: Fourth mesh of the left lateral basal segmental pulmonary artery, reaching peripheral lateral basal parenchyma near the costal pleura.
FJ2923.clinicalCondition: Chronic thromboembolic disease — organised clot in basal branches contributes to pulmonary hypertension.
FJ2923.clinicalScenario: A patient with previous PE has persistent perfusion defects in the left lower lobe on follow-up V/Q scanning.

FJ2078.name: Left lateral circumflex femoral artery
FJ2078.details: Large lateral branch of the left profunda femoris artery; its descending branch runs beneath rectus femoris and anastomoses around the knee, supplying anterolateral thigh.
FJ2078.clinicalCondition: Anterolateral thigh flap pedicle — its descending branch is the standard flap vessel in reconstruction.
FJ2078.clinicalScenario: A reconstructive surgeon raises a left anterolateral thigh flap based on the descending branch of this artery for a scalp defect.

FJ1685M.name: Left lateral frontobasal artery
FJ1685M.details: Cortical branch of the left anterior cerebral artery (orbitofrontal group) supplying the lateral orbital surface and inferior frontal gyrus region.
FJ1685M.clinicalCondition: Orbitofrontal infarction — may cause disinhibition and personality change after ACA stroke.
FJ1685M.clinicalScenario: Following aneurysm surgery, a patient becomes disinhibited and impulsive; imaging shows a left orbitofrontal infarct.

FJ1686M.name: Left lateral frontobasal artery
FJ1686M.details: Second mesh of the left lateral frontobasal (orbitofrontal) branch of the ACA, ramifying over the lateral orbital frontal cortex.
FJ1686M.clinicalCondition: ACA branch stroke — behavioural change can be the only sign of frontal infarction.
FJ1686M.clinicalScenario: A family reports personality change after a small left ACA branch stroke localised to frontobasal cortex on MRI.

FJ1687M.name: Left lateral occipital artery
FJ1687M.details: Branch of the left posterior cerebral artery (temporal group) supplying the lateral and inferior occipital lobe and posterior inferior temporal cortex.
FJ1687M.clinicalCondition: PCA branch infarction — causes visual field defects and object-recognition difficulty.
FJ1687M.clinicalScenario: A patient suddenly cannot recognise familiar faces after an embolus occludes a left lateral occipital branch.

FJ2079.name: Left lateral plantar artery
FJ2079.details: Larger terminal branch of the left posterior tibial artery, running diagonally across the sole and forming the plantar arch, completed by the deep plantar artery.
FJ2079.clinicalCondition: Plantar arch disease in diabetes — impairs forefoot perfusion and ulcer healing.
FJ2079.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a forefoot ulcer has angiography showing lateral plantar artery occlusion at the arch.

FJ2080.name: Left lateral superior genicular artery
FJ2080.details: Branch of the left popliteal artery passing laterally above the lateral femoral condyle, deep to biceps femoris, joining the genicular anastomosis.
FJ2080.clinicalCondition: Genicular collateral network — sustains knee and calf flow when the popliteal artery is injured.
FJ2080.clinicalScenario: After knee dislocation, angiography shows genicular collaterals maintaining left foot perfusion despite popliteal injury.

FJ2081.name: Left lateral tarsal artery
FJ2081.details: Branch of the left dorsalis pedis artery at the ankle passing laterally beneath extensor digitorum brevis, anastomosing with the arcuate artery.
FJ2081.clinicalCondition: Foot collateral circulation — contributes to forefoot supply in anterior tibial disease.
FJ2081.clinicalScenario: In a patient with anterior tibial occlusion, Doppler shows collateral flow across the lateral tarsal–arcuate network.

FJ1976.name: Left lateral thoracic artery
FJ1976.details: Branch of the second part of the left axillary artery descending along the lateral border of pectoralis minor, supplying pectoral muscles, serratus anterior and lateral breast.
FJ1976.clinicalCondition: Breast collateral supply — in women this artery contributes significantly to lateral mammary branches.
FJ1976.clinicalScenario: During a left mastectomy, the surgeon controls lateral thoracic branches along the pectoralis minor border to prevent bleeding.

FJ1874.name: Left lobe branch of left hepatic artery
FJ1874.details: Terminal division of the left hepatic artery entering the left lobe at the porta hepatis, dividing into medial and lateral segmental branches for segments II–IV.
FJ1874.clinicalCondition: Aberrant left hepatic anatomy — a replaced branch from the left gastric artery is common and surgically important.
FJ1874.clinicalScenario: Preoperative imaging before gastrectomy identifies a replaced left hepatic artery arising from the left gastric, altering the dissection plan.

FJ2884.name: Left medial basal segmental artery
FJ2884.details: Branch of the basal trunk of the left pulmonary artery supplying the medial basal (cardiac) segment of the left lower lobe beside the heart border.
FJ2884.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — cardiac segment occlusion is a common CTPA finding.
FJ2884.clinicalScenario: A patient with breathlessness has CTPA showing an embolus in the left medial basal segmental pulmonary artery.

FJ2885.name: Left medial basal segmental artery
FJ2885.details: Second mesh of the left medial basal segmental pulmonary artery, following the cardiac segment bronchus toward the diaphragmatic surface.
FJ2885.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary infarction — medial basal occlusion may silhouette the diaphragm on imaging.
FJ2885.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient develops pleuritic pain; CT shows a wedge opacity in the left cardiac segment from embolism.

FJ1690M.name: Left medial frontobasal artery
FJ1690M.details: Medial orbitofrontal branch of the left anterior cerebral artery supplying the medial orbital surface, gyrus rectus and olfactory region.
FJ1690M.clinicalCondition: Orbitofrontal ACA infarction — associated with anosmia and behavioural disinhibition.
FJ1690M.clinicalScenario: After anterior communicating aneurysm rupture, a patient loses smell and becomes apathetic from medial frontobasal infarction.

FJ1691M.name: Left medial occipital artery
FJ1691M.details: Terminal medial branch of the left posterior cerebral artery supplying the calcarine cortex, cuneus and lingual gyrus — the primary visual area.
FJ1691M.clinicalCondition: Calcarine infarction — produces a contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.
FJ1691M.clinicalScenario: A patient suddenly loses the right half of vision in both eyes; MRI shows a left calcarine region infarct.

FJ2082.name: Left medial plantar artery
FJ2082.details: Smaller terminal branch of the left posterior tibial artery running forward along the medial sole with the medial plantar nerve, supplying medial foot and great toe side.
FJ2082.clinicalCondition: Medial plantar flap territory — its skin paddle is used for heel and midfoot reconstruction.
FJ2082.clinicalScenario: A surgeon plans an instep flap based on the medial plantar artery to cover a heel pressure sore.

FJ2083.name: Left medial superior genicular artery
FJ2083.details: Branch of the left popliteal artery passing medially above the medial femoral condyle, deep to semimembranosus, joining the genicular anastomosis around the knee.
FJ2083.clinicalCondition: Knee collateral circulation — enlarges when the superficial femoral artery occludes chronically.
FJ2083.clinicalScenario: An elderly claudicant's angiogram demonstrates large medial genicular collaterals reconstituting the popliteal artery.

FJ2084.name: Left middle genicular artery
FJ2084.details: Small branch from the front of the left popliteal artery piercing the posterior capsule and oblique popliteal ligament to supply the cruciate ligaments and synovium.
FJ2084.clinicalCondition: Cruciate ligament vascularity — this artery is the principal blood supply to the ACL and PCL.
FJ2084.clinicalScenario: During knee arthroscopy, bleeding from the middle genicular territory is noted while debriding a torn anterior cruciate ligament.

FJ3472.name: Left middle suprarenal artery
FJ3472.details: Small direct branch of the aorta at about L1 running laterally over the left crus to the hilum of the left suprarenal gland.
FJ3472.clinicalCondition: Adrenal arterial redundancy — multiple sources mean adrenal infarction is uncommon even in vasculitis.
FJ3472.clinicalScenario: Imaging in a patient with antiphospholipid syndrome shows a perfused left adrenal despite aortic branch disease, reflecting collateral supply.

FJ1979.name: Left musculophrenic artery
FJ1979.details: Terminal branch of the internal thoracic artery; descends obliquely behind the 7th-9th costal cartilages along the costal margin, giving anterior intercostal branches, then pierces the diaphragm.
FJ1979.clinicalCondition: Collateral pathway in aortic coarctation: enlarged intercostal collaterals bypass the narrowed aorta, increasing flow through this vessel.
FJ1979.clinicalScenario: A 24-year-old with coarctation shows dilated, tortuous anterior intercostal collateral vessels along the costal margin on CT angiography.

FJ1695M.name: Left ophthalmic artery
FJ1695M.details: First major branch of the internal carotid artery after it leaves the cavernous sinus; enters the orbit through the optic canal and supplies the globe, extraocular muscles, and lacrimal gland.
FJ1695M.clinicalCondition: Central retinal artery occlusion: this end-artery branch blocks, causing sudden painless monocular blindness with a cherry-red spot.
FJ1695M.clinicalScenario: A 78-year-old man loses vision in the left eye within minutes; fundoscopy shows a pale retina with a cherry-red spot at the fovea.

FJ2237.name: Left palmar metacarpal artery
FJ2237.details: One of three branches of the deep palmar arch; runs distally on the interosseous muscles and joins a common palmar digital artery from the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2237.clinicalCondition: Completes the palmar collateral network: its anastomosis keeps the fingers perfused if the superficial arch is interrupted.
FJ2237.clinicalScenario: After a palm laceration severs the superficial arch, the fingers stay pink because deep-arch metacarpal branches back-fill the digital arteries.

FJ1699M.name: Left pericallosal artery
FJ1699M.details: Distal continuation of the anterior cerebral artery beyond the callosomarginal branch; curves above the corpus callosum in the callosal sulcus, supplying medial frontal and parietal cortex.
FJ1699M.clinicalCondition: Anterior cerebral artery territory infarct: distal occlusion produces contralateral leg-predominant weakness and sensory loss.
FJ1699M.clinicalScenario: A 70-year-old woman develops weakness and cortical sensory loss confined to the right leg; MRI shows a left pericallosal territory infarct.

FJ2085.name: Left plantar arch
FJ2085.details: Arterial arcade deep in the sole, formed by the lateral plantar artery and completed medially by the deep plantar branch of dorsalis pedis; gives off the plantar metatarsal arteries.
FJ2085.clinicalCondition: Diabetic foot ischemia: arch disease starves the forefoot, driving toe ulceration and gangrene.
FJ2085.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a non-healing great-toe ulcer has a diseased plantar arch and absent forefoot flow on Doppler study.

FJ1712M.name: Left polar temporal artery
FJ1712M.details: Inferior temporal branch of the posterior cerebral artery (P2 segment) supplying the temporal pole and anterior inferior temporal lobe, including parahippocampal cortex.
FJ1712M.clinicalCondition: Temporal pole infarction: usually part of a wider posterior cerebral stroke, contributing memory and naming difficulty.
FJ1712M.clinicalScenario: Following a left PCA occlusion, a patient has impaired visual naming and memory alongside a right homonymous hemianopia.

FJ2086.name: Left popliteal artery
FJ2086.details: Continuation of the femoral artery from the adductor hiatus across the popliteal fossa to the lower border of popliteus, where it divides into anterior tibial and tibioperoneal trunks.
FJ2086.clinicalCondition: Popliteal aneurysm: commonest peripheral aneurysm; mural thrombus embolizes and can suddenly threaten the leg.
FJ2086.clinicalScenario: A 68-year-old man with a pulsatile mass behind the knee presents with a cold, painful foot from aneurysm thrombosis and distal emboli.

FJ2881.name: Left posterior basal segmental artery
FJ2881.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus.
FJ2881.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism: clot lodging here creates a wedge-shaped segmental perfusion defect and pleuritic pain.
FJ2881.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain and tachycardia has a CTPA filling defect in the posterior basal segmental artery.

FJ2892.name: Left posterior basal segmental artery
FJ2892.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus.
FJ2892.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism: clot lodging here creates a wedge-shaped segmental perfusion defect and pleuritic pain.
FJ2892.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain and tachycardia has a CTPA filling defect in the posterior basal segmental artery.

FJ2903.name: Left posterior basal segmental artery
FJ2903.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus.
FJ2903.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism: clot lodging here creates a wedge-shaped segmental perfusion defect and pleuritic pain.
FJ2903.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain and tachycardia has a CTPA filling defect in the posterior basal segmental artery.

FJ2914.name: Left posterior basal segmental artery
FJ2914.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus.
FJ2914.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism: clot lodging here creates a wedge-shaped segmental perfusion defect and pleuritic pain.
FJ2914.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain and tachycardia has a CTPA filling defect in the posterior basal segmental artery.

FJ2919.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus.

FJ2919.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain and tachycardia has a CTPA filling defect in the posterior basal segmental artery.

FJ2920.name: Left posterior basal segmental artery
FJ2920.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe, accompanying the segmental bronchus.

FJ2920.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain and tachycardia has a CTPA filling defect in the posterior basal segmental artery.

FJ2239.name: Left posterior circumflex humeral artery
FJ2239.details: Branch of the third part of the axillary artery; passes backward through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve, winds around the surgical neck of the humerus, supplies deltoid and shoulder joint.
FJ2239.clinicalCondition: Quadrangular space syndrome: fibrous compression of this artery and the axillary nerve causes shoulder pain and deltoid weakness.
FJ2239.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter has posterior shoulder pain, weak abduction, and angiographic compression of this artery in the quadrangular space.

FJ2240.name: Left posterior circumflex humeral artery
FJ2240.details: Branch of the third part of the axillary artery; passes backward through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve, winds around the surgical neck of the humerus, supplies deltoid and shoulder joint.
FJ2240.clinicalCondition: Quadrangular space syndrome: fibrous compression of this artery and the axillary nerve causes shoulder pain and deltoid weakness.
FJ2240.clinicalScenario: A weightlifter has posterior shoulder pain, weak abduction, and angiographic compression of this artery in the quadrangular space.

FJ1713M.name: Left posterior communicating artery
FJ1713M.details: Short vessel joining the internal carotid to the posterior cerebral artery, completing the circle of Willis; the oculomotor nerve passes immediately inferolateral to it.
FJ1713M.clinicalCondition: Posterior communicating artery aneurysm: expansion compresses the oculomotor nerve, causing a painful, pupil-involving third nerve palsy.
FJ1713M.clinicalScenario: A 45-year-old woman develops sudden ptosis, a down-and-out eye, and a dilated pupil; imaging confirms a PCom aneurysm.

FJ1700M.name: Left posterior inferior cerebellar artery
FJ1700M.details: Largest branch of the vertebral artery; winds around the medulla and supplies the lateral medulla, inferior cerebellar vermis and hemisphere, and choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle.
FJ1700M.clinicalCondition: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: occlusion gives vertigo, dysphagia, ipsilateral facial and contralateral body pain-temperature loss.
FJ1700M.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old man has vertigo, hoarseness, left facial numbness, and loss of pain sensation over the right limbs after PICA occlusion.

FJ1701M.name: Left posterior inferior cerebellar artery
FJ1701M.details: Largest branch of the vertebral artery; winds around the medulla and supplies the lateral medulla, inferior cerebellar vermis and hemisphere, and choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle.
FJ1701M.clinicalCondition: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: occlusion gives vertigo, dysphagia, ipsilateral facial and contralateral body pain-temperature loss.
FJ1701M.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old man has vertigo, hoarseness, left facial numbness, and loss of pain sensation over the right limbs after PICA occlusion.

FJ1702M.name: Left posterior inferior cerebellar artery
FJ1702M.details: Largest branch of the vertebral artery; winds around the medulla and supplies the lateral medulla, inferior cerebellar vermis and hemisphere, and choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle.
