FJ1711M.clinicalCondition: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: occlusion gives vertigo, dysphagia, ipsilateral facial and contralateral body pain-temperature loss.
FJ1711M.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old man has vertigo, hoarseness, left facial numbness, and loss of pain sensation over the right limbs after PICA occlusion.

FJ1715M.name: Left posterior inferior cerebellar artery
FJ1715M.details: Largest branch of the vertebral artery; winds around the medulla and supplies the lateral medulla, inferior cerebellar vermis and hemisphere, and choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle.
FJ1715M.clinicalCondition: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: occlusion gives vertigo, dysphagia, ipsilateral facial and contralateral body pain-temperature loss.
FJ1715M.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old man has vertigo, hoarseness, left facial numbness, and loss of pain sensation over the right limbs after PICA occlusion.

FJ1727M.name: Left posterior medial choroidal artery
FJ1727M.details: Branch of the P2 posterior cerebral artery curving around the midbrain to the choroid plexus of the third ventricle; contributes supply to midbrain, pineal region, and medial thalamus.
FJ1727M.clinicalCondition: Deep PCA perforator infarction: involvement adds thalamic and midbrain signs to a posterior cerebral artery stroke.
FJ1727M.clinicalScenario: A patient with a left PCA stroke shows drowsiness and vertical gaze difficulty from medial choroidal territory ischemia.

FJ1716M.name: Left posterior parietal artery
FJ1716M.details: Cortical (M4) branch of the middle cerebral artery ramifying over the posterior parietal lobe, supplying somatosensory association cortex and superior parietal lobule.
FJ1716M.clinicalCondition: Dominant parietal infarct (Gerstmann syndrome): acalculia, agraphia, finger agnosia, and left-right disorientation from angular region damage.
FJ1716M.clinicalScenario: A right-handed teacher suddenly cannot calculate, write, or name her fingers after a left posterior parietal branch infarct.

FJ2911.name: Left posterior segmental artery
FJ2911.details: Segmental branch of the posterior division of the left renal artery supplying the posterior renal segment; segmental arteries are end-arteries with no collateral flow between segments.
FJ2911.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction: embolic occlusion produces a wedge-shaped non-perfused segment, flank pain, and hematuria.
FJ2911.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation develops sudden left flank pain; CT shows a wedge-shaped posterior segment renal infarct.

FJ2912.name: Left posterior segmental artery
FJ2912.details: Segmental branch of the posterior division of the left renal artery supplying the posterior renal segment; segmental arteries are end-arteries with no collateral flow between segments.
FJ2912.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction: embolic occlusion produces a wedge-shaped non-perfused segment, flank pain, and hematuria.
FJ2912.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation develops sudden left flank pain; CT shows a wedge-shaped posterior segment renal infarct.

FJ2913.name: Left posterior segmental artery
FJ2913.details: Segmental branch of the posterior division of the left renal artery supplying the posterior renal segment; segmental arteries are end-arteries with no collateral flow between segments.
FJ2913.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction: embolic occlusion produces a wedge-shaped non-perfused segment, flank pain, and hematuria.
FJ2913.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation develops sudden left flank pain; CT shows a wedge-shaped posterior segment renal infarct.

FJ2087.name: Left posterior tibial artery
FJ2087.details: Terminal branch of the popliteal artery descending in the deep posterior leg compartment, passing behind the medial malleolus (where its pulse is palpated) and dividing into medial and lateral plantar arteries.
FJ2087.clinicalCondition: Peripheral arterial disease: a diminished or absent posterior tibial pulse is a key bedside sign, used in ankle-brachial index measurement.
FJ2087.clinicalScenario: A 65-year-old diabetic smoker with calf claudication has an impalpable left posterior tibial pulse and an ABI of 0.5.

FJ2241.name: Left posterior ulnar recurrent artery
FJ2241.details: Branch of the ulnar artery just distal to the elbow; ascends behind the medial epicondyle and anastomoses with the inferior ulnar collateral artery, forming part of the elbow collateral network.
FJ2241.clinicalCondition: Elbow collateral circulation: this anastomosis helps maintain forearm perfusion when the brachial artery is injured at the elbow.
FJ2241.clinicalScenario: After a supracondylar fracture with brachial artery spasm, the hand remains perfused through the recurrent ulnar collateral pathway.

FJ1724M.name: Left prefrontal artery
FJ1724M.details: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery ascending over the frontal operculum to supply the prefrontal cortex anterior to the premotor area.
FJ1724M.clinicalCondition: Frontal lobe infarct: prefrontal ischemia produces apathy, poor planning, and personality change rather than weakness.
FJ1724M.clinicalScenario: A previously organized manager becomes apathetic and disorganized after a left prefrontal branch infarct on MRI.

FJ2924.name: Left pulmonary artery
FJ2924.details: Branch of the pulmonary trunk passing beneath the aortic arch, tethered to it by the ligamentum arteriosum, then entering the left lung hilum to supply the whole left lung.
FJ2924.clinicalCondition: Cardiovocal (Ortner) syndrome: an enlarged left pulmonary artery or atrium compresses the left recurrent laryngeal nerve, causing hoarseness.
FJ2924.clinicalScenario: A patient with mitral stenosis and a chronically hoarse voice has an enlarged left pulmonary artery compressing the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

FJ2242.name: Left radial artery
FJ2242.details: Terminal branch of the brachial artery at the elbow; descends under brachioradialis, gives the wrist pulse, and ends forming the deep palmar arch; widely used for arterial sampling and grafting.
FJ2242.clinicalCondition: Radial artery occlusion after cannulation: usually silent because ulnar collaterals via the palmar arches protect the hand.
FJ2242.clinicalScenario: Before a radial arterial line is placed, a normal Allen test confirms ulnar flow can supply the hand if the radial occludes.

FJ2243.name: Left radial recurrent artery
FJ2243.details: Branch of the radial artery just below the elbow; ascends between brachioradialis and brachialis to anastomose with the radial collateral branch of the profunda brachii at the elbow.
FJ2243.clinicalCondition: Elbow collateral network: this anastomosis sustains forearm flow around an obstructed brachial artery.
FJ2243.clinicalScenario: During lateral elbow surgery for tennis elbow release, the recurrent radial branch is identified and protected in the surgical field.

FJ2245.name: Left recurrent interosseous artery
FJ2245.details: Branch of the posterior interosseous artery that ascends between supinator and anconeus to the back of the lateral epicondyle, anastomosing with the middle collateral branch of the profunda brachii.
FJ2245.clinicalCondition: Elbow collateral circulation: completes the posterior anastomosis around the lateral epicondyle, supporting flow after brachial injury.
FJ2245.clinicalScenario: In an elbow dislocation with arterial injury, back-filling through the recurrent interosseous anastomosis keeps the forearm viable.

FJ2046.name: Left renal artery
FJ2046.details: Branch of the abdominal aorta at L1, just below the superior mesenteric artery; reaches the renal hilum behind the left renal vein, giving inferior suprarenal and ureteric branches.
FJ2046.clinicalCondition: Renal artery stenosis: atherosclerosis or fibromuscular dysplasia narrows it, causing secondary renovascular hypertension.
FJ2046.clinicalScenario: A 28-year-old woman with resistant hypertension and an abdominal bruit has beaded fibromuscular narrowing of the left renal artery.

FJ2316.name: Left second common palmar digital artery
FJ2316.details: Branch of the superficial palmar arch running distally to the second web space, where it bifurcates into proper palmar digital arteries for the adjacent sides of index and middle fingers.
FJ2316.clinicalCondition: Digital ischemia from palmar injury: laceration here bleeds briskly and can compromise the neighbouring finger margins.
FJ2316.clinicalScenario: A glass cut across the second web space causes pulsatile bleeding controlled by pressure over this artery's course.

FJ1974.name: Left second posterior intercostal artery
FJ1974.details: Arises from the superior intercostal artery (costocervical trunk) rather than the aorta; runs in the costal groove of the second intercostal space below the vein and nerve.
FJ1974.clinicalCondition: Coarctation collateral flow: upper intercostal arteries enlarge as collaterals, though rib notching mainly involves the third to ninth spaces.
FJ1974.clinicalScenario: Imaging in aortic coarctation shows an enlarged superior intercostal and second posterior intercostal artery feeding collateral chest-wall flow.

FJ1677M.name: Left splenial artery
FJ1677M.details: Branch of the posterior cerebral artery (parieto-occipital division) supplying the splenium of the corpus callosum and the precuneus region.
FJ1677M.clinicalCondition: Splenial infarction: combined with left occipital damage it disconnects visual input from language areas, giving alexia without agraphia.
FJ1677M.clinicalScenario: A patient who can write but cannot read his own writing has a left occipital and splenial infarct on MRI.

FJ1678M.name: Left splenial artery
FJ1678M.details: Branch of the posterior cerebral artery (parieto-occipital division) supplying the splenium of the corpus callosum and the precuneus region.
FJ1678M.clinicalCondition: Splenial infarction: combined with left occipital damage it disconnects visual input from language areas, giving alexia without agraphia.
FJ1678M.clinicalScenario: A patient who can write but cannot read his own writing has a left occipital and splenial infarct on MRI.

FJ3479.name: Left subclavian artery
FJ3479.details: Arises directly from the aortic arch (unlike the right), ascends behind the scalenus anterior into three parts, giving vertebral, internal thoracic, and thyrocervical branches before continuing as the axillary artery.
FJ3479.clinicalCondition: Subclavian steal syndrome: proximal stenosis reverses vertebral artery flow, causing arm claudication with dizziness on exertion.
FJ3479.clinicalScenario: A 66-year-old man has a 30 mmHg lower left-arm blood pressure and vertigo when using that arm; Doppler shows reversed vertebral flow.

FJ1977.name: Left subcostal artery
FJ1977.details: Lowest branch of the descending thoracic aorta, running below the 12th rib with the subcostal nerve (T12), supplying the lateral abdominal wall muscles.
FJ1977.clinicalCondition: Flank incision hazard: the vessel and nerve are vulnerable in subcostal and lumbar surgical approaches, risking bleeding and wall weakness.
FJ1977.clinicalScenario: After a flank nephrectomy incision, a hematoma forms along the subcostal neurovascular plane below the 12th rib.

FJ2246.name: Left subscapular artery
FJ2246.details: Largest branch of the third part of the axillary artery; descends along subscapularis, giving the circumflex scapular branch and continuing as the thoracodorsal artery to latissimus dorsi.
FJ2246.clinicalCondition: Scapular anastomosis collateral: its circumflex scapular branch links subclavian and axillary systems around a blocked axillary artery.
FJ2246.clinicalScenario: With a proximal axillary occlusion, shoulder perfusion is maintained through the subscapular and circumflex scapular collateral channels.

FJ2256.name: Left superficial cervical artery
FJ2256.details: Superficial division of the transverse cervical artery (from the thyrocervical trunk), supplying trapezius and neighbouring neck muscles and overlying skin.
FJ2256.clinicalCondition: Trapezius flap pedicle: this vessel's territory supports myocutaneous flaps used in head and neck reconstruction.
FJ2256.clinicalScenario: A trapezius myocutaneous flap for a neck defect is raised on the superficial cervical and transverse cervical pedicle.

FJ3529.name: Left superficial epigastric artery
FJ3529.details: Small branch of the femoral artery just below the inguinal ligament; ascends in the superficial fascia of the lower abdominal wall toward the umbilicus.
FJ3529.clinicalCondition: SIEA flap donor vessel: its calibre determines whether a superficial inferior epigastric artery flap can be used for breast reconstruction.
FJ3529.clinicalScenario: At harvest, a tiny superficial epigastric artery forces the surgeon to convert a planned SIEA flap to a DIEP flap.

FJ2089.name: Left superficial medial plantar artery
FJ2089.details: Small superficial branch of the medial plantar artery supplying skin and superficial structures along the medial border of the sole.
FJ2089.clinicalCondition: Medial sole perfusion: relevant to healing of medial plantar wounds and to instep flap design in foot reconstruction.
FJ2089.clinicalScenario: A medial plantar instep flap for a heel defect is planned around the medial plantar artery and its superficial branch.

FJ2248.name: Left superficial palmar arterial arch
FJ2248.details: Continuation of the ulnar artery across the palm deep to the palmar aponeurosis, completed laterally by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery; gives the common palmar digital arteries.
FJ2248.clinicalCondition: Hypothenar hammer syndrome: repeated palm trauma injures the ulnar artery at the arch origin, embolizing into the fingers.
FJ2248.clinicalScenario: A mechanic who uses his palm as a hammer develops a cold, painful ring and little finger from arch-level ulnar thrombosis.

FJ1726M.name: Left superior cerebellar artery
FJ1726M.details: Final branch of the basilar artery before its bifurcation; winds around the midbrain below the oculomotor nerve and supplies the superior cerebellum, dentate nucleus, and parts of the midbrain and pons.
FJ1726M.clinicalCondition: Superior cerebellar artery infarct: produces ipsilateral cerebellar ataxia with contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation.
FJ1726M.clinicalScenario: A 62-year-old man develops left-sided limb ataxia, nystagmus, and right-sided spinothalamic loss from an SCA territory stroke.

FJ1971.name: Left superior epigastric artery
FJ1971.details: One of two terminal branches of the internal thoracic artery; descends into the rectus sheath, supplies the upper rectus abdominis, and anastomoses with the inferior epigastric artery.
FJ1971.clinicalCondition: Rectus sheath collateral: the superior-inferior epigastric anastomosis becomes an important collateral route in aortoiliac occlusive disease.
FJ1971.clinicalScenario: In severe aortoiliac disease, enlarged epigastric collaterals reconstitute femoral flow, a pathway traced on angiography.

FJ1970.name: Left superior intercostal artery
FJ1970.details: Branch of the costocervical trunk descending in front of the necks of the first and second ribs, giving the first and second posterior intercostal arteries.
FJ1970.clinicalCondition: Apical thoracic surgery landmark: the vessel crosses the neck of the first rib and can bleed during thoracoscopic sympathectomy.
FJ1970.clinicalScenario: During VATS sympathectomy, brisk bleeding from the superior intercostal artery near the first rib neck requires careful clip control.

FJ2888.name: Left superior segmental artery
FJ2888.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2888.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2888.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2889.name: Left superior segmental artery
FJ2889.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2889.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2889.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2890.name: Left superior segmental artery
FJ2890.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2890.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2890.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2891.name: Left superior segmental artery
FJ2891.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2891.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2891.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2893.name: Left superior segmental artery
FJ2893.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2893.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2893.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2894.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2894.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2894.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2895.name: Left superior segmental artery
FJ2895.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior segment (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular branches.
FJ2895.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: a clot here gives a focal S6 perfusion defect visible on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ2895.clinicalScenario: CTPA in a breathless cancer patient shows an embolus isolated to the superior segmental artery of the left lower lobe.

FJ2374.name: Left superior ulnar collateral artery
FJ2374.details: Branch of the brachial artery (or profunda) descending with the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle to join the posterior ulnar recurrent artery in the elbow anastomosis.
FJ2374.clinicalCondition: At risk in ulnar nerve transposition: the vessel travels with the nerve and its injury can compromise nerve perfusion.
FJ2374.clinicalScenario: During cubital tunnel release with transposition, the superior ulnar collateral vessels are preserved alongside the ulnar nerve.

FJ2251.name: Left suprascapular artery
FJ2251.details: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk passing laterally through the suprascapular notch above the superior transverse scapular ligament (the nerve passes below), supplying supraspinatus and infraspinatus.
FJ2251.clinicalCondition: Scapular collateral anastomosis: links thyrocervical and subscapular systems, sustaining the shoulder after subclavian or axillary occlusion.
FJ2251.clinicalScenario: Angiography after axillary artery occlusion shows the suprascapular artery feeding the circumflex scapular anastomosis around the scapula.

FJ3532.name: Left testicular artery
FJ3532.details: Slender branch of the abdominal aorta at L2 descending on psoas major, through the inguinal canal within the spermatic cord, to supply the testis and epididymis.
FJ3532.clinicalCondition: Testicular torsion: twisting of the cord strangles this artery, infarcting the testis unless detorsion occurs within hours.
FJ3532.clinicalScenario: A 15-year-old boy with sudden severe testicular pain has absent arterial flow on Doppler, confirming torsion requiring emergency surgery.

FJ1675M.name: Left thalamogeniculate artery
FJ1675M.details: Group of branches from the P2 posterior cerebral artery supplying the ventrolateral thalamus, including the ventral posterolateral and posteromedial sensory nuclei and geniculate bodies.
FJ1675M.clinicalCondition: Thalamic pain syndrome (Dejerine-Roussy): ventrolateral thalamic infarct later causes burning contralateral hemisensory pain.
FJ1675M.clinicalScenario: Months after a small thalamic stroke, a patient develops severe burning pain over the entire right side of the body.

FJ1720M.name: Left thalamoperforating artery
FJ1720M.details: Perforating branches from the P1 posterior cerebral artery and basilar tip supplying the paramedian thalamus, hypothalamus, and subthalamic region.
FJ1720M.clinicalCondition: Artery of Percheron infarction: a single variant trunk occludes both paramedian thalami, causing coma and vertical gaze palsy.
FJ1720M.clinicalScenario: A drowsy patient with impaired upgaze has bilateral paramedian thalamic infarcts from an artery of Percheron occlusion.

FJ2317.name: Left third common palmar digital artery
FJ2317.details: Branch of the superficial palmar arch running to the third web space, bifurcating into proper palmar digital arteries for the adjacent sides of the middle and ring fingers.
FJ2317.clinicalCondition: Digital perfusion assessment: occlusion here threatens the facing margins of the middle and ring fingers.
FJ2317.clinicalScenario: A crush injury to the palm leaves the ulnar side of the middle finger dusky from third web-space arterial damage.

FJ2253.name: Left thoracodorsal artery
FJ2253.details: Continuation of the subscapular artery descending on serratus anterior with the thoracodorsal nerve to enter latissimus dorsi; gives a serratus anterior branch.
FJ2253.clinicalCondition: Latissimus dorsi flap pedicle: this artery is the flap's lifeline in breast and chest-wall reconstruction.
FJ2253.clinicalScenario: A latissimus dorsi flap for post-mastectomy reconstruction is raised on an intact thoracodorsal artery and nerve pedicle.

FJ2255.name: Left thyrocervical trunk
FJ2255.details: Short branch of the first part of the subclavian artery dividing into inferior thyroid, suprascapular, and transverse cervical arteries, supplying thyroid, neck, and shoulder girdle muscles.
FJ2255.clinicalCondition: Neck surgery landmark: the trunk lies medial to scalenus anterior, near the phrenic nerve, and bleeds briskly if torn.
FJ2255.clinicalScenario: During a difficult central neck dissection, injury to the thyrocervical trunk causes bleeding controlled by ligation.

FJ2257.name: Left transverse cervical artery
FJ2257.details: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk crossing the posterior triangle of the neck superficial to the brachial plexus, supplying trapezius and levator scapulae; its deep branch may be the dorsal scapular artery.
FJ2257.clinicalCondition: Posterior triangle surgery hazard: the vessel crosses near the accessory nerve and can be damaged during lymph node biopsy.
FJ2257.clinicalScenario: A posterior triangle node biopsy is complicated by bleeding from the transverse cervical artery crossing the field.

FJ2258.name: Left ulnar artery
FJ2258.details: Larger terminal branch of the brachial artery; descends on the medial forearm deep to the flexor muscles, passes through Guyon's canal at the wrist, and forms the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2258.clinicalCondition: Ulnar artery occlusion at Guyon's canal: produces hand ischemia with ulnar-distribution sensory symptoms mimicking nerve compression.
FJ2258.clinicalScenario: A cyclist pressing on handlebars develops a cold little finger and hypothenar pain from ulnar artery thrombosis at the wrist.

FJ1725M.name: Left vertebral artery
FJ1725M.details: First branch of the subclavian artery; ascends through the foramina transversaria of C6-C1, winds behind the atlas, pierces the dura, and unites with its fellow to form the basilar artery.
FJ1725M.clinicalCondition: Vertebral artery dissection: intimal tear after neck trauma or manipulation causes posterior circulation stroke in younger patients.
FJ1725M.clinicalScenario: A 38-year-old woman develops neck pain, vertigo, and diplopia two days after vigorous neck manipulation; MRI shows dissection.

FJ3632.name: Lumbar artery
FJ3632.details: Four paired branches of the posterior abdominal aorta passing behind psoas major, supplying the posterior abdominal wall, quadratus lumborum, and (via spinal branches) the cord and cauda equina.
FJ3632.clinicalCondition: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage: lumbar arteries are a recognised bleeding source after pelvic fracture or anticoagulation, treated by embolization.
FJ3632.clinicalScenario: An anticoagulated patient drops her hemoglobin with flank pain; CT angiography shows a bleeding second lumbar artery, embolized successfully.

FJ3636.name: Lumbar artery
FJ3636.details: Four paired branches of the posterior abdominal aorta passing behind psoas major, supplying the posterior abdominal wall, quadratus lumborum, and (via spinal branches) the cord and cauda equina.
FJ3636.clinicalCondition: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage: lumbar arteries are a recognised bleeding source after pelvic fracture or anticoagulation, treated by embolization.
FJ3636.clinicalScenario: An anticoagulated patient drops her hemoglobin with flank pain; CT angiography shows a bleeding second lumbar artery, embolized successfully.

FJ3534.name: Marginal artery of colon
FJ3534.details: Continuous anastomotic arcade (of Drummond) running along the inner border of the colon, linking ileocolic, right, middle, and left colic branches of the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries.
FJ3534.clinicalCondition: Ischemic colitis at the splenic flexure: the Griffiths point here is a watershed with tenuous collateral flow.
FJ3534.clinicalScenario: A hypotensive elderly patient passes bloody stool; colonoscopy shows segmental ischemia at the splenic flexure watershed.

FJ2667.name: Marginal branch of right coronary artery
FJ2667.details: Acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery coursing along the acute margin of the heart, supplying the anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2667.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction: occlusion with proximal RCA block causes hypotension, raised JVP, and clear lung fields.
FJ2667.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient becomes more hypotensive after nitrates; ECG right-sided leads confirm RV infarction from RCA occlusion.

FJ2668.name: Marginal branch of right coronary artery
FJ2668.details: Acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery coursing along the acute margin of the heart, supplying the anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2668.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction: occlusion with proximal RCA block causes hypotension, raised JVP, and clear lung fields.
FJ2668.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient becomes more hypotensive after nitrates; ECG right-sided leads confirm RV infarction from RCA occlusion.

FJ2672.name: Marginal branch of right coronary artery
FJ2672.details: Acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery coursing along the acute margin of the heart, supplying the anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2672.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction: occlusion with proximal RCA block causes hypotension, raised JVP, and clear lung fields.
FJ2672.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient becomes more hypotensive after nitrates; ECG right-sided leads confirm RV infarction from RCA occlusion.

FJ2674.name: Marginal branch of right coronary artery
FJ2674.details: Acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery coursing along the acute margin of the heart, supplying the anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2674.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction: occlusion with proximal RCA block causes hypotension, raised JVP, and clear lung fields.
FJ2674.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient becomes more hypotensive after nitrates; ECG right-sided leads confirm RV infarction from RCA occlusion.

FJ2675.name: Marginal branch of right coronary artery
FJ2675.details: Acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery coursing along the acute margin of the heart, supplying the anterior wall of the right ventricle.
FJ2675.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction: occlusion with proximal RCA block causes hypotension, raised JVP, and clear lung fields.
FJ2675.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient becomes more hypotensive after nitrates; ECG right-sided leads confirm RV infarction from RCA occlusion.

FJ2025.name: Marginal colic artery
FJ2025.details: The colic anastomotic arcade (marginal artery of Drummond) lying a few centimetres from the colon wall, feeding the vasa recta; a key SMA-IMA collateral channel.
FJ2025.clinicalCondition: Post-aortic-surgery colonic ischemia: marginal flow may fail after inferior mesenteric artery ligation during aneurysm repair.
FJ2025.clinicalScenario: Two days after open AAA repair, a patient develops bloody diarrhea from left colon ischemia in the IMA territory.

FJ1689M.name: Medial branch of left pontine artery
FJ1689M.details: Paramedian perforating branch of the basilar artery entering the medial pons, supplying corticospinal fibres, medial lemniscus, and the medial longitudinal fasciculus.
FJ1689M.clinicalCondition: Pontine lacunar infarct: paramedian perforator occlusion causes pure motor hemiparesis or internuclear ophthalmoplegia.
FJ1689M.clinicalScenario: A hypertensive man develops right-sided pure motor weakness and left eye adduction failure from a medial pontine infarct.

FJ1688M.name: Medial branch of left superior cerebellar artery
FJ1688M.details: Medial (superior vermian) branch of the superior cerebellar artery supplying the superior vermis and paravermian cerebellar hemisphere.
FJ1688M.clinicalCondition: Vermian infarction: produces truncal and gait ataxia out of proportion to limb incoordination.
FJ1688M.clinicalScenario: A patient who cannot sit unsupported and walks with a wide-based gait has a superior vermis infarct on MRI.

FJ1689.name: Medial branch of right pontine artery
FJ1689.details: Paramedian perforating branch of the basilar artery entering the medial pons on the right, supplying corticospinal fibres, medial lemniscus, and the medial longitudinal fasciculus.
FJ1689.clinicalCondition: Pontine lacunar infarct: perforator occlusion causes pure motor hemiparesis or internuclear ophthalmoplegia on the affected side.
FJ1689.clinicalScenario: A diabetic woman develops left pure motor hemiparesis and right internuclear ophthalmoplegia from a right medial pontine lacune.

FJ1688.name: Medial branch of right superior cerebellar artery
FJ1688.details: Medial (superior vermian) branch of the right superior cerebellar artery supplying the superior vermis and paravermian cerebellar hemisphere.
FJ1688.clinicalCondition: Vermian infarction: produces truncal ataxia and falls with relatively preserved limb coordination.
FJ1688.clinicalScenario: An elderly man repeatedly falls sideways and cannot sit steadily after an infarct of the right superior vermian branch.

FJ2994.name: Medial branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2994.details: Medial subdivision of the superior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the medial part of the superior (apical) renal segment; a functional end-artery.
FJ2994.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct: embolic occlusion leaves a wedge-shaped apical perfusion defect with flank pain.
FJ2994.clinicalScenario: A man with mitral stenosis develops right flank pain; imaging shows a wedge infarct in the superior renal segment.

FJ2995.name: Medial branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2995.details: Medial subdivision of the superior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the medial part of the superior (apical) renal segment; a functional end-artery.
FJ2995.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct: embolic occlusion leaves a wedge-shaped apical perfusion defect with flank pain.
FJ2995.clinicalScenario: A man with mitral stenosis develops right flank pain; imaging shows a wedge infarct in the superior renal segment.

FJ2996.name: Medial branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2996.details: Medial subdivision of the superior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the medial part of the superior (apical) renal segment; a functional end-artery.
FJ2996.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct: embolic occlusion leaves a wedge-shaped apical perfusion defect with flank pain.
FJ2996.clinicalScenario: A man with mitral stenosis develops right flank pain; imaging shows a wedge infarct in the superior renal segment.

FJ3106.name: Medial inferior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3106.details: Segmental hepatic arterial branch supplying the inferior part of the medial segment (segment IV) of the liver, usually arising from the left or middle hepatic arterial system.
FJ3106.clinicalCondition: Segment IV ischemia after embolization: usually silent because of intrahepatic collaterals, but mapped before chemoembolization.
FJ3106.clinicalScenario: Pre-TACE angiography maps a medial inferior segmental branch feeding segment IV so the tumour supply can be selectively catheterized.

FJ2333.name: Medial proper palmar digital artery of left index finger
FJ2333.details: Small artery running with the digital nerve along the medial (ulnar) side of the left index finger, from the second common palmar digital bifurcation; supplies pulp and skin.
FJ2333.clinicalCondition: Digital artery laceration: a cut here bleeds briskly and threatens pulp viability if both digital arteries are divided.
FJ2333.clinicalScenario: A knife slips while cooking, dividing the medial digital artery of the left index finger, repaired under the microscope.

FJ2364.name: Medial proper palmar digital artery of right index finger
FJ2364.details: Small artery running along the medial (ulnar) side of the right index finger with the digital nerve, from the second common palmar digital bifurcation; supplies pulp and skin of that border.
FJ2364.clinicalCondition: Digital revascularization: divided digital arteries are the vessels repaired in finger replantation and revascularization surgery.
FJ2364.clinicalScenario: After a saw injury, the right index finger is revascularized by repairing its medial proper palmar digital artery.

FJ2367.name: Medial proper palmar digital artery of right middle finger
FJ2367.details: Small artery along the medial (radial) side of the right middle finger, arising from the third common palmar digital artery bifurcation; supplies the radial border and pulp.
FJ2367.clinicalCondition: Allen digital test assessment: occlusion of one digital artery is detected by delayed refill of that side of the finger.
FJ2367.clinicalScenario: A crush injury leaves the radial side of the right middle finger pale, with delayed refill on the digital Allen test.

FJ2369.name: Medial proper palmar digital artery of right ring finger
FJ2369.details: Small artery along the medial (ulnar) side of the right ring finger from the third common palmar digital bifurcation, running with the digital nerve to supply pulp and skin.
FJ2369.clinicalCondition: Fingertip ischemia in vasculitis: small digital arteries like this occlude in systemic sclerosis and Buerger disease.
FJ2369.clinicalScenario: A smoker with Buerger disease develops a painful, non-healing ulcer at the ulnar border of the right ring fingertip.

FJ3107.name: Medial superior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3107.details: Segmental hepatic arterial branch supplying the superior part of the medial segment (segment IV) of the liver, part of the segmental anatomy used in resection planning.
FJ3107.clinicalCondition: Living donor hepatectomy planning: segment IV arterial variants must be mapped to protect the graft and remnant liver.
FJ3107.clinicalScenario: A donor CT angiogram identifies the medial superior segmental branch so segment IV perfusion is preserved at hepatectomy.

FJ3008.name: Mediobasal branch of right posterior basal segmental artery
FJ3008.details: Branch of the right pulmonary artery supplying the mediobasal (cardiac) segment, S7, of the right lower lobe, arising medially near the heart border.
FJ3008.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: clot in this small medial branch is easily overlooked on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ3008.clinicalScenario: A breathless patient after long-haul travel has an isolated filling defect in the mediobasal segmental branch on CTPA.

FJ3012.name: Mediobasal branch of right posterior basal segmental artery
FJ3012.details: Branch of the right pulmonary artery supplying the mediobasal (cardiac) segment, S7, of the right lower lobe, arising medially near the heart border.
FJ3012.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism: clot in this small medial branch is easily overlooked on CT pulmonary angiography.
FJ3012.clinicalScenario: A breathless patient after long-haul travel has an isolated filling defect in the mediobasal segmental branch on CTPA.

FJ3542.name: Middle colic artery
FJ3542.details: Branch of the superior mesenteric artery just below the pancreas; runs within the transverse mesocolon and divides into right and left branches supplying the transverse colon via the marginal artery.
FJ3542.clinicalCondition: SMA embolism: sudden occlusion threatens the midgut including this artery's transverse colon territory.
FJ3542.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation presents with severe central abdominal pain out of proportion to examination from SMA embolism.

FJ2331.name: Middle collateral branch of left deep brachial artery
FJ2331.details: Branch of the profunda brachii (deep brachial) artery descending behind the humerus to the posterior elbow, anastomosing with the recurrent interosseous artery behind the lateral epicondyle.
FJ2331.clinicalCondition: Elbow collateral network: this anastomosis preserves forearm perfusion when the brachial artery is blocked or ligated.
FJ2331.clinicalScenario: After brachial artery ligation for trauma, the left forearm stays viable through profunda collateral channels including this branch.

FJ2362.name: Middle collateral branch of right deep brachial artery
FJ2362.details: Branch of the profunda brachii (deep brachial) artery descending behind the humerus to the posterior elbow, anastomosing with the recurrent interosseous artery behind the lateral epicondyle.
FJ2362.clinicalCondition: Elbow collateral network: sustains distal flow around brachial artery obstruction, part of the periarticular anastomosis.
FJ2362.clinicalScenario: In a humeral fracture with brachial artery injury, collateral flow through the middle collateral branch keeps the right hand perfused.

FJ1680M.name: Middle temporal branch of left lateral occipital artery
FJ1680M.details: Cortical branch of the posterior cerebral artery's lateral occipital (inferior temporal) division supplying the middle part of the inferior temporal cortex.
FJ1680M.clinicalCondition: PCA cortical branch infarct: inferior temporal ischemia can impair visual recognition and colour naming.
FJ1680M.clinicalScenario: Following a left PCA stroke, a patient cannot name colours although he can see and read normally.

FJ1693M.name: Middle temporal branch of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1693M.details: Cortical (M4) branch of the middle cerebral artery supplying the middle temporal gyrus, part of the posterior perisylvian language network in the dominant hemisphere.
FJ1693M.clinicalCondition: Wernicke aphasia contribution: dominant posterior temporal ischemia produces fluent aphasia with poor comprehension.
FJ1693M.clinicalScenario: A retired teacher speaks fluently but nonsensically and cannot follow commands after a left middle temporal branch infarct.

FJ1680.name: Middle temporal branch of right lateral occipital artery
FJ1680.details: Cortical branch of the posterior cerebral artery's lateral occipital (inferior temporal) division supplying the middle inferior temporal cortex on the right.
FJ1680.clinicalCondition: Inferior temporal infarct: right-sided lesions can cause prosopagnosia, difficulty recognising familiar faces.
FJ1680.clinicalScenario: After a right PCA stroke, a man fails to recognise his wife's face although his vision and memory are otherwise intact.

FJ1693.name: Middle temporal branch of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1693.details: Cortical (M4) branch of the right middle cerebral artery supplying the middle temporal gyrus, involved in auditory processing and semantic memory on the non-dominant side.
FJ1693.clinicalCondition: Non-dominant temporal infarct: may cause impaired melody and environmental sound recognition without aphasia.
FJ1693.clinicalScenario: A musician loses the ability to recognise familiar tunes after a right middle temporal branch infarct.

FJ1696M.name: Paracentral branch of left callosomarginal artery
FJ1696M.details: Branch of the callosomarginal artery (anterior cerebral system) supplying the paracentral lobule, which houses motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and bladder control centres.
FJ1696M.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarct: causes contralateral leg weakness with urinary incontinence, mimicking a spinal lesion.
FJ1696M.clinicalScenario: A woman with right leg weakness and new incontinence has a left paracentral lobule infarct rather than cord compression.

FJ1697M.name: Paracentral branch of left callosomarginal artery
FJ1697M.details: Branch of the callosomarginal artery (anterior cerebral system) supplying the paracentral lobule, which houses motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and bladder control centres.
FJ1697M.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarct: causes contralateral leg weakness with urinary incontinence, mimicking a spinal lesion.
FJ1697M.clinicalScenario: A woman with right leg weakness and new incontinence has a left paracentral lobule infarct rather than cord compression.

FJ1698M.name: Paracentral branch of left callosomarginal artery
FJ1698M.details: Branch of the callosomarginal artery (anterior cerebral system) supplying the paracentral lobule, which houses motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and bladder control centres.
FJ1698M.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarct: causes contralateral leg weakness with urinary incontinence, mimicking a spinal lesion.
FJ1698M.clinicalScenario: A woman with right leg weakness and new incontinence has a left paracentral lobule infarct rather than cord compression.

FJ1696.name: Paracentral branch of right callosomarginal artery
FJ1696.details: Branch of the callosomarginal artery (anterior cerebral system) supplying the paracentral lobule: motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and cortical bladder control.
FJ1696.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarct: contralateral leg-predominant weakness and cortical sensory loss with possible incontinence.
FJ1696.clinicalScenario: A man develops isolated left leg weakness after cardiac surgery; MRI shows a right paracentral branch territory infarct.

FJ1697.name: Paracentral branch of right callosomarginal artery
FJ1697.details: Branch of the callosomarginal artery (anterior cerebral system) supplying the paracentral lobule: motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and cortical bladder control.
FJ1697.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarct: contralateral leg-predominant weakness and cortical sensory loss with possible incontinence.
FJ1697.clinicalScenario: A man develops isolated left leg weakness after cardiac surgery; MRI shows a right paracentral branch territory infarct.

FJ1698.name: Paracentral branch of right callosomarginal artery
FJ1698.details: Branch of the callosomarginal artery (anterior cerebral system) supplying the paracentral lobule: motor and sensory cortex for the opposite leg and cortical bladder control.
FJ1698.clinicalCondition: Paracentral lobule infarct: contralateral leg-predominant weakness and cortical sensory loss with possible incontinence.
FJ1698.clinicalScenario: A man develops isolated left leg weakness after cardiac surgery; MRI shows a right paracentral branch territory infarct.

FJ2330.name: Pectoral branch of left thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2330.details: Branch of the thoraco-acromial artery piercing the clavipectoral fascia with the lateral pectoral nerve to supply pectoralis major and minor; the named pedicle of the pectoralis major flap.
FJ2330.clinicalCondition: Pectoralis major flap pedicle: flap survival in head and neck reconstruction depends on preserving this branch.
FJ2330.clinicalScenario: A pectoralis major myocutaneous flap for a floor-of-mouth defect is raised on the pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial artery.

FJ2361.name: Pectoral branch of right thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2361.details: Branch of the thoraco-acromial artery piercing the clavipectoral fascia with the lateral pectoral nerve to supply both pectoral muscles; vascular pedicle of the pectoralis major flap.
FJ2361.clinicalCondition: Deltopectoral region bleeding: the branch may be injured during subclavian vein cannulation through the infraclavicular approach.
FJ2361.clinicalScenario: Infraclavicular subclavian line insertion is followed by an expanding hematoma from a torn pectoral branch.

FJ2096.name: Plantar metatarsal artery
FJ2096.details: One of four branches of the plantar arch running distally in an intermetatarsal space, joining common plantar digital arteries to supply the toes and forefoot webs.
FJ2096.clinicalCondition: Forefoot ischemia: arch and metatarsal artery disease in diabetes underlies toe gangrene and poor healing.
FJ2096.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with gangrene of the second toe has occluded plantar metatarsal flow to that ray on angiography.

FJ2206.name: Plantar metatarsal artery
FJ2206.details: One of four branches of the plantar arch running distally in an intermetatarsal space, joining common plantar digital arteries to supply the toes and forefoot webs.
FJ2206.clinicalCondition: Forefoot ischemia: arch and metatarsal artery disease in diabetes underlies toe gangrene and poor healing.
FJ2206.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with gangrene of the second toe has occluded plantar metatarsal flow to that ray on angiography.

FJ1714M.name: Postcommunicating part of left posterior cerebral artery
FJ1714M.details: Segment of the posterior cerebral artery distal to the posterior communicating artery junction (P2-P3), supplying the occipital lobe visual cortex and inferior temporal lobe.
FJ1714M.clinicalCondition: Homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing: occipital infarction from this segment's occlusion is the classic cause.
FJ1714M.clinicalScenario: A patient keeps bumping into objects on the right; perimetry shows a right homonymous hemianopia sparing central vision.

FJ1714.name: Postcommunicating part of right posterior cerebral artery
FJ1714.details: Segment of the posterior cerebral artery distal to the posterior communicating artery junction (P2-P3), supplying the right occipital visual cortex and inferior temporal lobe.
FJ1714.clinicalCondition: Homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing: distal PCA occlusion infarcts the visual cortex while collateral flow spares the macula.
FJ1714.clinicalScenario: After a right PCA occlusion, a driver fails to see cars approaching from the left despite normal central acuity.

FJ2983.name: Posterior branch of lateral segmental artery
FJ2983.details: Posterior subdivision of the lateral segmental branch of the renal artery, supplying the posterior part of the lateral renal segment; segmental branches are end-arteries.
FJ2983.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction: occlusion produces a wedge-shaped lateral segment defect, seen on contrast CT.
FJ2983.clinicalScenario: A patient with endocarditis develops flank pain and a wedge-shaped lateral renal perfusion defect from a septic embolus.

FJ2984.name: Posterior branch of lateral segmental artery
FJ2984.details: Posterior subdivision of the lateral segmental branch of the renal artery, supplying the posterior part of the lateral renal segment; segmental branches are end-arteries.
FJ2984.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction: occlusion produces a wedge-shaped lateral segment defect, seen on contrast CT.
FJ2984.clinicalScenario: A patient with endocarditis develops flank pain and a wedge-shaped lateral renal perfusion defect from a septic embolus.

FJ2974.name: Posterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2974.details: Posterior subdivision of the anterior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the posterior portion of the anterior renal segment.
FJ2974.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct: embolic occlusion here gives a focal wedge defect without affecting overall renal function much.
FJ2974.clinicalScenario: After cardiac catheterization, cholesterol embolization leaves a small wedge infarct in the right anterior renal segment.

FJ2980.name: Posterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2980.details: Posterior subdivision of the anterior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the posterior portion of the anterior renal segment.
FJ2980.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct: embolic occlusion here gives a focal wedge defect without affecting overall renal function much.
FJ2980.clinicalScenario: After cardiac catheterization, cholesterol embolization leaves a small wedge infarct in the right anterior renal segment.

FJ2981.name: Posterior branch of right anterior segmental artery
FJ2981.details: Posterior subdivision of the anterior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the posterior portion of the anterior renal segment.
FJ2981.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct: embolic occlusion here gives a focal wedge defect without affecting overall renal function much.
FJ2981.clinicalScenario: After cardiac catheterization, cholesterol embolization leaves a small wedge infarct in the right anterior renal segment.

FJ3553.name: Posterior cecal artery
FJ3553.details: Branch of the ileocolic artery supplying the posterior aspect of the cecum; the appendicular artery usually arises from the ileocolic system nearby.
FJ3553.clinicalCondition: Cecal ischemia is rare: rich ileocolic collaterals protect the cecum, but this territory is ligated in right hemicolectomy.
FJ3553.clinicalScenario: During right hemicolectomy for a cecal tumour, the ileocolic pedicle including the posterior cecal branch is ligated at its origin.

FJ3473.name: Posterior division of left renal artery
FJ3473.details: Posterior division of the left renal artery passing behind the renal pelvis, continuing mainly as the posterior segmental artery; the junction between divisions marks the relatively avascular Brödel line.
FJ3473.clinicalCondition: Anatrophic nephrolithotomy plane: the Brödel line between divisions is incised to remove staghorn calculi with minimal bleeding.
FJ3473.clinicalScenario: A staghorn calculus is removed through a nephrotomy placed along the avascular plane between the renal artery divisions.

FJ3474.name: Posterior division of left renal artery
FJ3474.details: Posterior division of the left renal artery passing behind the renal pelvis, continuing mainly as the posterior segmental artery; the junction between divisions marks the relatively avascular Brödel line.
FJ3474.clinicalCondition: Anatrophic nephrolithotomy plane: the Brödel line between divisions is incised to remove staghorn calculi with minimal bleeding.
FJ3474.clinicalScenario: A staghorn calculus is removed through a nephrotomy placed along the avascular plane between the renal artery divisions.

FJ3475.name: Posterior division of left renal artery
FJ3475.details: Posterior division of the left renal artery passing behind the renal pelvis, continuing mainly as the posterior segmental artery; the junction between divisions marks the relatively avascular Brödel line.
FJ3475.clinicalCondition: Anatrophic nephrolithotomy plane: the Brödel line between divisions is incised to remove staghorn calculi with minimal bleeding.
FJ3475.clinicalScenario: A staghorn calculus is removed through a nephrotomy placed along the avascular plane between the renal artery divisions.

FJ3573.name: Posterior division of right renal artery
FJ3573.details: Posterior division of the right renal artery passing behind the renal pelvis, supplying the posterior segment; its border with the anterior division defines the Brödel avascular line.
FJ3573.clinicalCondition: Anatrophic nephrolithotomy plane: incision along the division boundary limits blood loss during complex stone surgery.
FJ3573.clinicalScenario: Imaging for a large right staghorn calculus maps the posterior division so the nephrotomy avoids major segmental vessels.

FJ3574.name: Posterior division of right renal artery
FJ3574.details: Posterior division of the right renal artery passing behind the renal pelvis, supplying the posterior segment; its border with the anterior division defines the Brödel avascular line.
FJ3574.clinicalCondition: Anatrophic nephrolithotomy plane: incision along the division boundary limits blood loss during complex stone surgery.
FJ3574.clinicalScenario: Imaging for a large right staghorn calculus maps the posterior division so the nephrotomy avoids major segmental vessels.

FJ3575.name: Posterior division of right renal artery
FJ3575.details: Posterior division of the right renal artery passing behind the renal pelvis, supplying the posterior segment; its border with the anterior division defines the Brödel avascular line.
FJ3575.clinicalCondition: Anatrophic nephrolithotomy plane: incision along the division boundary limits blood loss during complex stone surgery.
FJ3575.clinicalScenario: Imaging for a large right staghorn calculus maps the posterior division so the nephrotomy avoids major segmental vessels.

FJ3546.name: Posterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FJ3546.details: Branch of the superior mesenteric artery supplying the posterior pancreatic head and duodenum, anastomosing with the posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery from the gastroduodenal artery.
FJ3546.clinicalCondition: Pancreaticoduodenal arcade aneurysm: enlarged collateral arcades in celiac stenosis can form aneurysms that rupture catastrophically.
FJ3546.clinicalScenario: A patient with median arcuate ligament compression presents with a ruptured inferior pancreaticoduodenal arcade aneurysm and hemoperitoneum.

FJ3114.name: Posterior inferior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3114.details: Segmental hepatic arterial branch supplying the posterior inferior segment (segment VI) of the right lobe of the liver.
FJ3114.clinicalCondition: Segment VI tumour supply: this branch is catheterized selectively for chemoembolization of posterior right-lobe tumours.
FJ3114.clinicalScenario: Angiography before treating a segment VI hepatocellular carcinoma identifies its posterior inferior segmental feeding artery.

FJ1961.name: Posterior intercostal arteries
FJ1961.details: Nine paired arteries (3rd-11th) from the descending thoracic aorta running in the costal grooves, ordered vein-artery-nerve from above, supplying intercostal muscles, skin, and spinal branches to the cord.
FJ1961.clinicalCondition: Intercostal artery bleeding: fracture or thoracentesis injury causes hemothorax; drains are inserted just above a rib to avoid the bundle.
FJ1961.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a large hemothorax after posterior rib fractures tear an intercostal artery in its costal groove.

FJ1975.name: Posterior intercostal arteries
FJ1975.details: Nine paired arteries (3rd-11th) from the descending thoracic aorta running in the costal grooves, ordered vein-artery-nerve from above, supplying intercostal muscles, skin, and spinal branches to the cord.
FJ1975.clinicalCondition: Intercostal artery bleeding: fracture or thoracentesis injury causes hemothorax; drains are inserted just above a rib to avoid the bundle.
FJ1975.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a large hemothorax after posterior rib fractures tear an intercostal artery in its costal groove.

FJ2692.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2692.details: Posterior descending artery running in the posterior interventricular sulcus, usually from the right coronary artery (right dominance ~85%), supplying the posterior third of the interventricular septum and inferior ventricular walls.
FJ2692.clinicalCondition: Inferior myocardial infarction with heart block: occlusion here, near AV nodal supply, can cause complete heart block.
FJ2692.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient develops bradycardia and complete heart block from an occluded posterior descending artery.

FJ2693.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2693.details: Posterior descending artery running in the posterior interventricular sulcus, usually from the right coronary artery (right dominance ~85%), supplying the posterior third of the interventricular septum and inferior ventricular walls.
FJ2693.clinicalCondition: Inferior myocardial infarction with heart block: occlusion here, near AV nodal supply, can cause complete heart block.
FJ2693.clinicalScenario: An inferior STEMI patient develops bradycardia and complete heart block from an occluded posterior descending artery.

FJ2694.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2694.details: Continuation of the right coronary artery at the crux; descends in the posterior interventricular sulcus toward the apex, supplying the posterior third of the interventricular septum and adjacent ventricular walls.
FJ2694.clinicalCondition: Inferior myocardial infarction — occlusion here, usually with the parent RCA, infarcts the inferior wall and posterior septum.
FJ2694.clinicalScenario: A 58-year-old man develops crushing central chest pain with nausea; ECG shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF, confirming inferior STEMI from RCA territory occlusion.

FJ2695.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2695.details: Runs from the crux of the heart down the posterior interventricular groove, giving septal perforators to the posterior septum and branches to both ventricles; anastomoses with the anterior interventricular branch at the apex.
FJ2695.clinicalCondition: Posterior septal ischemia — reduced flow threatens the posterior septum and the AV nodal conduction tissue nearby.
FJ2695.clinicalScenario: A diabetic woman with silent inferior ischemia presents with new complete heart block; angiography shows a tight stenosis at the origin of the posterior interventricular branch.

FJ2696.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2696.details: In a right-dominant circulation (about 85% of people) this branch arises from the right coronary artery; it supplies the posterior septum and gives the AV nodal branch near its origin.
FJ2696.clinicalCondition: AV block in inferior infarction — the AV nodal branch shares this origin, so proximal occlusion often causes transient heart block.
FJ2696.clinicalScenario: An elderly man with inferior MI develops a heart rate of 38 with hypotension; atropine fails and temporary pacing is arranged while awaiting reperfusion.

FJ2697.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2697.details: Accompanied by the middle cardiac vein in the posterior interventricular sulcus; its septal branches penetrate the posterior third of the septum, complementing anterior septal supply from the LAD.
FJ2697.clinicalCondition: Ventricular septal rupture — post-infarction necrosis of the posterior septum supplied here can rupture, causing acute left-to-right shunt.
FJ2697.clinicalScenario: Five days after an inferior MI, a patient suddenly becomes breathless with a new harsh pansystolic murmur; echocardiography confirms a posterior ventricular septal defect.

FJ2698.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2698.details: Terminal segment near the apex anastomoses with the anterior interventricular (LAD) branch, forming an important collateral pathway between right and left coronary territories.
FJ2698.clinicalCondition: Balanced ischemia — chronic LAD disease may be masked because this vessel collaterally perfuses the apex, delaying symptoms.
FJ2698.clinicalScenario: A patient with exertional angina has a near-normal resting ECG; stress imaging reveals apical ischemia supplied through collaterals from a dominant right coronary system.

FJ2699.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2699.details: Gives small branches to the posterior papillary muscle of the left ventricle and the posteromedial papillary muscle group, structures critical for mitral valve competence.
FJ2699.clinicalCondition: Papillary muscle dysfunction — ischemia here causes acute mitral regurgitation through failure of the posteromedial papillary muscle.
FJ2699.clinicalScenario: A woman recovering from inferior MI develops sudden pulmonary edema and a soft apical murmur; echo shows flail posterior mitral leaflet from papillary muscle rupture.

FJ2700.name: Posterior interventricular branch of right coronary artery
FJ2700.details: Its dominance pattern defines coronary dominance: right dominance when this branch and the posterolateral branches both arise from the right coronary artery at the crux.
FJ2700.clinicalCondition: Prognostic marker in CAD — left-dominant variants change revascularization planning when this branch instead arises from the circumflex.
FJ2700.clinicalScenario: During pre-bypass angiography review, the surgeon notes a left-dominant system; grafting strategy is adjusted because the posterior descending vessel comes from the circumflex.

FJ2970.name: Posterior part of right posterior segmental artery
FJ2970.details: Subdivision of the posterior segmental branch of the right renal artery, supplying the posterior renal segment behind the renal pelvis; renal segmental arteries are functional end arteries.
FJ2970.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction — embolus lodging here infarcts a wedge of posterior renal parenchyma with no collateral rescue.
FJ2970.clinicalScenario: A man with atrial fibrillation presents with right flank pain and microscopic hematuria; CT shows a wedge-shaped non-enhancing defect in the posterior right kidney.

FJ2971.name: Posterior part of right posterior segmental artery
FJ2971.details: Courses posterior to the renal pelvis within the renal sinus, making the posterior segment relatively avascular along the line used for surgical approaches to the kidney.
FJ2971.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark — the posterior segmental plane guides nephrolithotomy incisions minimizing hemorrhage during stone surgery.
FJ2971.clinicalScenario: A urologist plans percutaneous access for a staghorn calculus, choosing a posterior calyceal puncture to avoid this vessel and reduce bleeding risk.

FJ2972.name: Posterior part of right posterior segmental artery
FJ2972.details: Terminal twigs supply the posterior segment parenchyma and contribute small branches toward the renal capsule and perinephric tissues.
FJ2972.clinicalCondition: Segmental ischemia in vasculitis — small-vessel disease can silently scar this segment, reducing renal reserve over time.
FJ2972.clinicalScenario: Imaging for hypertension workup incidentally shows a scarred, shrunken posterior segment of the right kidney in a patient with long-standing polyarteritis nodosa.

FJ2053.name: Posterior segmental branch of left renal artery
FJ2053.details: One of five segmental branches of the left renal artery, arising from its posterior division and passing behind the renal pelvis to supply the posterior segment of the left kidney.
FJ2053.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarct — occlusion produces a posterior wedge infarct presenting as flank pain mimicking pyelonephritis.
FJ2053.clinicalScenario: A young woman on oral contraceptives develops left flank pain and low-grade fever; CT angiography reveals an embolus in the posterior segmental branch.

FJ2054.name: Posterior segmental branch of left renal artery
FJ2054.details: Lies posterior to the left renal pelvis and upper ureter junction region, a relation exploited in reconstructive surgery of the pelviureteric junction.
FJ2054.clinicalCondition: Iatrogenic injury risk — this vessel can be damaged during pyeloplasty, causing segmental ischemia or postoperative bleeding.
FJ2054.clinicalScenario: After laparoscopic pyeloplasty, a patient's drain output turns bloody; angiography identifies a bleeding pseudoaneurysm of the posterior segmental branch treated by embolization.

FJ2045.name: Posterior segmental branch of right renal artery
FJ2045.details: Posterior division branch of the right renal artery, passing behind the renal pelvis to supply the posterior segment; typically the first and most posterior segmental branch.
FJ2045.clinicalCondition: Renal artery aneurysm — segmental branch aneurysms may rupture into the collecting system causing gross hematuria.
FJ2045.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged woman presents with sudden right flank pain and frank hematuria; CT shows a small aneurysm of the posterior segmental branch of the right renal artery.

FJ3557.name: Posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FJ3557.details: Branch of the gastroduodenal artery descending behind the pancreatic head, supplying the posterior duodenum and pancreatic head; anastomoses with the posterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal branch of the SMA.
FJ3557.clinicalCondition: Collateral pathway in celiac stenosis — it enlarges to carry SMA blood retrogradely into the hepatic circulation, sometimes forming aneurysms.
FJ3557.clinicalScenario: CT for abdominal pain shows median arcuate ligament compression of the celiac trunk with a dilated pancreaticoduodenal arcade and a small aneurysm under surveillance.

FJ3115.name: Posterior superior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3115.details: Segmental branch of the right hepatic arterial system supplying the posterior superior segment (segment VII) of the liver within the right lobe.
FJ3115.clinicalCondition: Segmental hepatic ischemia — inadvertent ligation during cholecystectomy or transplant surgery can infarct segment VII silently.
FJ3115.clinicalScenario: After a difficult laparoscopic cholecystectomy, follow-up imaging shows a small perfusion defect in segment VII attributed to an aberrant segmental branch injury.

FJ3116.name: Posterior superior segmental hepatic artery
FJ3116.details: Follows portal triad distribution into segment VII, accompanying the posterior superior segmental portal vein and bile duct within Glissonian sheaths.
FJ3116.clinicalCondition: Target for chemoembolization — selective catheterization delivers TACE beads to segment VII tumors while sparing healthy liver.
FJ3116.clinicalScenario: An interventional radiologist superselectively catheterizes this branch to embolize a hepatocellular carcinoma confined to segment VII in a patient with cirrhosis.

FJ1717M.name: Posterior temporal branch of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1717M.details: Terminal cortical branch of the left MCA (M4 segment) supplying the posterior superior and middle temporal gyri, including Wernicke's sensory speech area in the dominant hemisphere.
FJ1717M.clinicalCondition: Wernicke's aphasia — dominant-hemisphere occlusion causes fluent but meaningless speech with poor comprehension.
FJ1717M.clinicalScenario: A right-handed woman suddenly speaks fluently in jumbled sentences and cannot follow commands; MRI confirms an infarct in the left posterior temporal MCA territory.

FJ1717.name: Posterior temporal branch of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1717.details: Cortical branch of the right MCA supplying the posterior temporal lobe cortex, involved in auditory processing and, on the non-dominant side, prosody and visuospatial aspects of language.
FJ1717.clinicalCondition: Posterior temporal stroke — non-dominant occlusion may cause aprosodia and auditory agnosia rather than classic aphasia.
FJ1717.clinicalScenario: A man after stroke speaks with flat, monotone intonation and misreads others' emotions; imaging shows a right posterior temporal infarct.

FJ1722M.name: Posteromedial branch of left callosomarginal artery
FJ1722M.details: Small pericallosal-system branch of the left anterior cerebral artery complex supplying the posteromedial parietal cortex and paracentral region near the marginal sulcus.
FJ1722M.clinicalCondition: Medial parietal ischemia — occlusion contributes to contralateral leg sensory loss in ACA territory strokes.
FJ1722M.clinicalScenario: A patient with a left ACA infarct complains of numbness and cortical sensory loss confined to the right foot and leg.

FJ1722.name: Posteromedial branch of right callosomarginal artery
FJ1722.details: Terminal twig of the right callosomarginal artery running toward the posteromedial parietal lobe, supplying medial cortex near the precuneus margin.
FJ1722.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark — its territory borders the paracentral lobule approached in interhemispheric surgery for midline lesions.
FJ1722.clinicalScenario: During interhemispheric removal of a falx meningioma, the surgeon carefully preserves these medial branches to avoid postoperative leg weakness.

FJ1721M.name: Posteromedial central branch of left posterior cerebral artery
FJ1721M.details: Thalamoperforating branch from the P1 segment of the left PCA, piercing the posterior perforated substance to supply the medial thalamus and midbrain.
FJ1721M.clinicalCondition: Thalamic stroke — occlusion causes sensory disturbance and, if bilateral from a shared trunk (artery of Percheron), coma.
FJ1721M.clinicalScenario: A patient is found drowsy with vertical gaze palsy; MRI shows bilateral paramedian thalamic infarcts from a single perforating trunk variant.

FJ1721.name: Posteromedial central branch of right posterior cerebral artery
FJ1721.details: Perforating branch of the right P1 segment supplying the posteromedial thalamus, subthalamus and rostral midbrain tegmentum.
FJ1721.clinicalCondition: Midbrain syndrome — occlusion can produce ipsilateral third-nerve palsy with contralateral tremor or ataxia (Benedikt/Claude syndromes).
FJ1721.clinicalScenario: An elderly man develops a right eye that sits down-and-out with a left-sided intention tremor after a small perforator territory stroke.

FJ1723M.name: Precommunicating part of left posterior cerebral artery
FJ1723M.details: The P1 segment of the left PCA, extending from the basilar bifurcation to the posterior communicating artery junction; gives posteromedial central (thalamoperforating) branches.
FJ1723M.clinicalCondition: Top-of-basilar syndrome — embolus at the basilar tip occludes both P1 segments causing bilateral thalamic and occipital infarction.
FJ1723M.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation becomes comatose with small reactive pupils; imaging shows basilar tip occlusion with bilateral P1 territory infarcts.

FJ1723.name: Precommunicating part of right posterior cerebral artery
FJ1723.details: The P1 segment of the right PCA between the basilar bifurcation and the posterior communicating artery; a hypoplastic P1 with dominant PCom defines a fetal-type posterior circulation variant.
FJ1723.clinicalCondition: Fetal PCA variant — carotid disease can then cause occipital infarction, confusing stroke localization during assessment.
FJ1723.clinicalScenario: A woman with severe right carotid stenosis suffers an occipital stroke; angiography reveals a fetal-type right PCA supplied entirely from the carotid system.

FJ1671M.name: Precuneal branch of left pericallosal artery
FJ1671M.details: Branch of the distal left ACA (pericallosal) ascending to supply the precuneus on the medial parietal surface, part of the default mode network.
FJ1671M.clinicalCondition: Rare isolated infarct — small ACA branch occlusion may cause subtle visuospatial and self-referential cognitive deficits.
FJ1671M.clinicalScenario: After an ACA aneurysm coiling, a patient reports difficulty with mental imagery tasks; imaging shows a small left precuneus infarct.

FJ1671.name: Precuneal branch of right pericallosal artery
FJ1671.details: Distal ACA branch supplying the right precuneus and adjacent medial parietal cortex, anastomosing with posterior cerebral branches at the parieto-occipital watershed.
FJ1671.clinicalCondition: Watershed vulnerability — borderzone ischemia here occurs in severe hypotension between ACA and PCA territories.
FJ1671.clinicalScenario: Following prolonged cardiac arrest resuscitation, MRI shows bilateral medial parieto-occipital watershed infarcts including both precuneal territories.

FJ2966.name: Pulmonary trunk
FJ2966.details: Arises from the right ventricular outflow tract at the pulmonary valve, ascends within the pericardium and bifurcates into right and left pulmonary arteries beneath the aortic arch at T5 level.
FJ2966.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism — a saddle embolus straddling this bifurcation obstructs both pulmonary arteries causing acute right heart strain.
FJ2966.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient develops sudden dyspnea, tachycardia and hypotension; CT pulmonary angiography shows a saddle embolus at the pulmonary trunk bifurcation.

FJ2261.name: Radial collateral branch of left deep brachial artery
FJ2261.details: Anterior branch of the profunda brachii bifurcation, descending in the lateral intermuscular septum with the radial nerve to anastomose around the elbow with the radial recurrent artery.
FJ2261.clinicalCondition: Collateral circulation at elbow — maintains forearm perfusion if the brachial artery is injured above the elbow.
FJ2261.clinicalScenario: After a supracondylar humeral fracture with brachial artery spasm, the child's hand stays perfused through this collateral; pulses return after fracture reduction.

FJ2262.name: Radial collateral branch of right deep brachial artery
FJ2262.details: Descends anterior to the lateral intermuscular septum alongside the radial nerve in the spiral groove region, contributing to the periarticular elbow anastomosis.
FJ2262.clinicalCondition: At risk in humeral shaft fracture — accompanies the radial nerve, so fracture hematoma and palsy often occur together.
FJ2262.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist with a mid-shaft humerus fracture has wrist drop and a tense arm; exploration reveals the radial nerve and collateral vessels bruised in the fracture line.

FJ1654.name: Right anterior cerebral artery
FJ1654.details: Arises from the internal carotid bifurcation, passes anteromedially above the optic nerve, joins its fellow via the anterior communicating artery, then curves around the corpus callosum supplying the medial hemisphere.
FJ1654.clinicalCondition: ACA stroke — occlusion causes contralateral leg-predominant weakness and sensory loss, abulia and urinary incontinence.
FJ1654.clinicalScenario: A hypertensive man notices his left leg dragging and becomes apathetic; MRI shows a right medial frontal infarct in ACA territory.

FJ1658.name: Right anterior choroidal artery
FJ1658.details: Small branch of the internal carotid artery (occasionally MCA) coursing posteromedially to supply the posterior limb of the internal capsule, optic tract, lateral geniculate body and choroid plexus of the inferior horn.
FJ1658.clinicalCondition: Anterior choroidal syndrome — occlusion classically causes hemiplegia, hemisensory loss and homonymous hemianopia.
FJ1658.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient develops dense left hemiparesis with visual field loss; diffusion MRI shows a small infarct in the posterior limb of the right internal capsule.

FJ2264.name: Right anterior circumflex humeral artery
FJ2264.details: Small branch of the third part of the axillary artery passing anterior to the surgical neck of the humerus, supplying the shoulder joint and anastomosing with the posterior circumflex humeral artery.
FJ2264.clinicalCondition: At risk in proximal humerus fractures — bleeding from this vessel contributes to hematoma around surgical neck fractures.
FJ2264.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman falls onto her shoulder; X-ray shows a surgical neck fracture with a large axillary hematoma but intact distal pulses.

FJ2266.name: Right anterior interosseous artery
FJ2266.details: Branch of the common interosseous artery descending on the anterior surface of the forearm interosseous membrane with the anterior interosseous nerve, supplying deep flexor compartment muscles.
FJ2266.clinicalCondition: Anterior interosseous syndrome — its companion nerve palsy prevents thumb-index pinch while the artery marks the surgical plane.
FJ2266.clinicalScenario: A patient cannot make the 'OK' sign after forearm trauma; examination shows weak flexor pollicis longus and index FDP with normal sensation.

FJ1667.name: Right anterior parietal artery
FJ1667.details: Cortical branch of the right MCA arising near the insula, supplying the anterior parietal lobe including the postcentral gyrus (primary somatosensory cortex).
FJ1667.clinicalCondition: Cortical sensory loss — occlusion causes contralateral impaired proprioception, stereognosis and two-point discrimination.
FJ1667.clinicalScenario: A stroke patient can move her left hand but cannot identify a key placed in it with eyes closed; imaging localizes infarction to the right anterior parietal cortex.

FJ2041.name: Right anterior segmental artery
FJ2041.details: Segmental branch of the right renal artery supplying the anterior segment of the kidney; one of five end-arterial segments defined by the renal arterial tree.
FJ2041.clinicalCondition: Segmental infarction — embolic occlusion scars the anterior segment, often presenting as flank pain with hematuria.
FJ2041.clinicalScenario: A man with endocarditis develops right flank pain; CT demonstrates a wedge-shaped anterior segment defect consistent with septic embolus.

FJ2044.name: Right anterior segmental artery
FJ2044.details: Courses within the renal sinus to reach the anterior segment parenchyma, lying close to the anterior major calyces used in percutaneous renal access planning.
FJ2044.clinicalCondition: Bleeding risk in PCNL — puncture through its territory can cause significant hemorrhage requiring embolization.
FJ2044.clinicalScenario: After percutaneous nephrolithotomy, a patient bleeds persistently; angiography shows a pseudoaneurysm of an anterior segmental branch, successfully coiled.

FJ1657.name: Right anterior spinal artery
FJ1657.details: Contributor from the right vertebral artery joining its fellow to form the single midline anterior spinal artery, which descends in the anterior median fissure supplying the anterior two-thirds of the cord.
FJ1657.clinicalCondition: Anterior spinal artery syndrome — occlusion causes paraplegia with loss of pain and temperature but preserved proprioception.
FJ1657.clinicalScenario: After aortic aneurysm repair, a patient wakes unable to move both legs yet can still feel vibration; MRI confirms anterior cord infarction.

FJ1659.name: Right anterior temporal artery
FJ1659.details: Early cortical branch of the right MCA (from the M1/M2 region) supplying the anterior temporal pole and anterior superior temporal gyrus.
