FJ2318.details: Dorsal digital branches arising from the dorsal carpal/metacarpal network, running distally on the backs of the fingers toward the nail beds.
FJ2318.clinicalCondition: Frostbite and cold injury — terminal dorsal digital flow is among the first compromised in freezing injury.
FJ2318.clinicalScenario: A mountaineer with frostbitten fingertips is assessed serially; return of dorsal digital Doppler signals guides conservative management over early amputation.

FJ2346.name: Set of dorsal digital arteries
FJ2346.details: Fine dorsal arteries of the digits anastomosing around the distal phalanx with the proper palmar digital arteries, completing the digital arterial arcade.
FJ2346.clinicalCondition: Crush injury prognosis — intact distal dorsal–palmar anastomoses improve fingertip salvage after crush or degloving injuries.
FJ2346.clinicalScenario: After a fingertip crush injury, brisk capillary refill via the distal digital arcade supports replantation assessment of the amputated tip.

FJ2347.name: Set of dorsal metacarpal arteries
FJ2347.details: Three arteries from the dorsal carpal arch running distally within the interosseous spaces of the hand, dividing into dorsal digital arteries and linked to the palmar system by perforating branches.
FJ2347.clinicalCondition: Flap planning — the first dorsal metacarpal artery flap resurfaces thumb and index defects using this system.
FJ2347.clinicalScenario: After a hand dorsum crush injury, dorsal metacarpal flow is checked before raising a first dorsal metacarpal artery flap for thumb resurfacing.

FJ2348.name: Set of dorsal metacarpal arteries
FJ2348.details: Dorsal metacarpal arteries lying on the interossei beneath the extensor tendons, fed proximally by the dorsal carpal arch and perforating branches from the deep palmar arch.
FJ2348.clinicalCondition: Hand trauma bleeding — divided dorsal metacarpal arteries bleed freely in dorsal hand wounds and need ligation.
FJ2348.clinicalScenario: A patient with a deep dorsal hand laceration has pulsatile bleeding from a dorsal metacarpal artery controlled under tourniquet during exploration.

FJ3431.name: Set of oesophageal branches of thoracic aorta
FJ3431.details: Four to five unpaired anterior branches of the descending thoracic aorta passing to the oesophagus, anastomosing with oesophageal branches of the inferior thyroid, left gastric and left inferior phrenic arteries.
FJ3431.clinicalCondition: Aorto-oesophageal fistula — aneurysm erosion into these branches causes a herald bleed then catastrophic haemorrhage.
FJ3431.clinicalScenario: A patient with a thoracic aortic aneurysm vomits a small herald bleed then collapses; an aorto-oesophageal fistula is feared and emergency surgery arranged.

FJ2090.name: Set of perforating arteries
FJ2090.details: Short connecting arteries passing between the metatarsals, linking the dorsal metatarsal/dorsalis pedis system with the plantar arch and reinforcing forefoot circulation.
FJ2090.clinicalCondition: Forefoot collateral flow — these links can sustain toes when either the dorsal or plantar system is diseased.
FJ2090.clinicalScenario: In a patient with plantar arch occlusion, patent perforating arteries keep the forefoot perfused from the dorsalis pedis, shown on angiography.

FJ2094.name: Set of perforating arteries
FJ2094.details: Perforating branches traversing the intermetatarsal spaces from the plantar arch to join dorsal metatarsal arteries, equalising pressure between the two foot circulations.
FJ2094.clinicalCondition: Amputation level planning — perforator patency influences healing of transmetatarsal amputation flaps.
FJ2094.clinicalScenario: A vascular surgeon reviews forefoot perforating runoff before a transmetatarsal amputation to predict whether the stump will heal.

FJ2127.name: Set of perforating arteries
FJ2127.details: Perforating arteries of the hand passing between the metacarpals, connecting the deep palmar arch with the dorsal carpal and dorsal metacarpal arteries.
FJ2127.clinicalCondition: Deep space infection spread — these channels let infection track between palmar and dorsal compartments of the hand.
FJ2127.clinicalScenario: A patient with a midpalmar space abscess develops dorsal hand swelling as infection tracks along a perforating channel.

FJ2203.name: Set of perforating arteries
FJ2203.details: Small arteries piercing the interosseous spaces to unite dorsal and plantar (or palmar) arterial networks, providing cross-flow at each ray of the foot or hand.
FJ2203.clinicalCondition: Traumatic bleeding — perforators retract between metatarsals and can cause persistent deep bleeding in crush injuries.
FJ2203.clinicalScenario: After a forklift crush injury to the foot, persistent intermetatarsal bleeding from a perforating artery requires operative control.

FJ2095.name: Set of plantar digital arteries proper
FJ2095.details: Terminal divisions of the common plantar digital arteries running along the plantar sides of the toes, supplying the toe pulp, nail bed and plantar skin, anastomosing at the tips.
FJ2095.clinicalCondition: Blue toe syndrome — microemboli occluding these arteries cause painful, cyanosed toes with palpable pedal pulses.
FJ2095.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient develops a painful blue great toe after cardiac catheterisation; cholesterol emboli in the proper plantar digital arteries are blamed.

FJ2204.name: Set of plantar digital arteries proper
FJ2204.details: Paired arteries flanking each toe on its plantar aspect, continuations of the common plantar digital arteries at the webspaces, ending in tuft anastomoses at the toe tips.
FJ2204.clinicalCondition: Diabetic toe gangrene — distal occlusion of these vessels is the final pathway to toe necrosis.
FJ2204.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with blackened second-toe tips from occluded proper plantar digital arteries is planned for ray amputation.

FJ2205.name: Set of plantar digital arteries proper
FJ2205.details: Proper plantar digital arteries supplying the plantar skin and pulp of the toes, reinforced by dorsal digital twigs around the distal phalanx.
FJ2205.clinicalCondition: Vasculitic digital ischaemia — small-vessel inflammation narrows these arteries causing toe-tip ulcers.
FJ2205.clinicalScenario: A patient with systemic vasculitis develops painful toe-tip ulceration; angiography shows tapered, narrowed proper plantar digital arteries.

FJ1719.name: set of posterior temporal branches of lateral occipital artery
FJ1719.details: Cortical branches of the lateral occipital (posterior temporal) division of the posterior cerebral artery spreading over the inferior and posterior temporal lobe, including the fusiform gyrus.
FJ1719.clinicalCondition: Prosopagnosia — fusiform territory infarction impairs face recognition despite intact vision.
FJ1719.clinicalScenario: A patient cannot recognise familiar faces after a stroke involving posterior temporal branches of the PCA, indicating fusiform gyrus damage.

FJ1719M.name: Set of posterior temporal branches of lateral occipital artery
FJ1719M.details: Posterior temporal cortical branches of the posterior cerebral artery supplying the posterior inferior temporal cortex and contributing to the ventral visual stream.
FJ1719M.clinicalCondition: Visual agnosia — ventral-stream infarction leaves patients unable to recognise objects by sight.
FJ1719M.clinicalScenario: After a posterior cerebral artery stroke, a man sees objects clearly but cannot name them until he touches them, indicating visual agnosia.

FJ3638.name: Sigmoid artery
FJ3638.details: Usually two or three branches of the inferior mesenteric artery descending in the sigmoid mesocolon, anastomosing with the left colic artery above and the superior rectal artery below.
FJ3638.clinicalCondition: Ischaemic colitis — the sigmoid colon is a watershed zone vulnerable when sigmoid flow falls.
FJ3638.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient with atrial fibrillation passes bloody diarrhoea with left iliac fossa pain; colonoscopy shows an ischaemic sigmoid colon.

FJ1692M.name: Sphenoid part of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1692M.details: The M1 (sphenoid/horizontal) segment of the left middle cerebral artery, running from the internal carotid bifurcation laterally in the stem of the lateral sulcus, giving lenticulostriate branches to the internal capsule.
FJ1692M.clinicalCondition: M1 occlusion — dominant-hemisphere catastrophe causing right hemiplegia, global aphasia and gaze deviation.
FJ1692M.clinicalScenario: A 72-year-old suddenly cannot speak and has right face-and-arm weakness; CT angiography shows a left M1 occlusion and she proceeds to thrombectomy.

FJ1692.name: Sphenoid part of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1692.details: The M1 segment of the right middle cerebral artery coursing laterally deep to the lateral sulcus toward the insula, giving medial and lateral lenticulostriate perforators.
FJ1692.clinicalCondition: M1 occlusion — causes left hemiplegia with hemispatial neglect in right-hemisphere lesions.
FJ1692.clinicalScenario: A man with sudden left-sided paralysis and neglect has a right M1 cut-off on angiography and is treated with emergency clot retrieval.

FJ2562.name: Splenic artery
FJ2562.details: Largest branch of the coeliac trunk; follows a tortuous course along the superior border of the pancreas, posterior to the stomach, entering the splenorenal ligament to reach the splenic hilum.
FJ2562.clinicalCondition: Splenic artery aneurysm — the commonest visceral artery aneurysm, with rupture risk greatest in pregnancy.
FJ2562.clinicalScenario: A pregnant woman collapses with left upper quadrant pain and shock; a ruptured splenic artery aneurysm is found at emergency laparotomy.

FJ3420.name: Splenic artery
FJ3420.details: Coeliac branch giving dorsal and great pancreatic arteries along the pancreas, then short gastric and left gastroepiploic branches before dividing at the splenic hilum.
FJ3420.clinicalCondition: Pancreatic pseudocyst erosion — enzymes erode the artery into a pseudocyst, causing pseudoaneurysm and gastrointestinal bleeding.
FJ3420.clinicalScenario: A chronic pancreatitis patient with a pseudocyst vomits blood; CT shows a splenic artery pseudoaneurysm bleeding into the cyst, treated by embolisation.

FJ3544.name: Splenic artery
FJ3544.details: Tortuous artery running behind the stomach and along the pancreas to the spleen; its calcified, coiled appearance in the left upper quadrant is a common radiographic finding in the elderly.
FJ3544.clinicalCondition: Incidental aneurysm surveillance — small asymptomatic aneurysms are monitored; enlarging ones are embolised or resected.
FJ3544.clinicalScenario: An abdominal CT for another problem reveals a 2.5 cm calcified splenic artery aneurysm in an asymptomatic woman; vascular review arranges embolisation.

FJ3640.name: Splenic artery
FJ3640.details: Terminal coeliac branch entering the splenorenal ligament and dividing into superior and inferior terminal branches that segmentally supply the spleen.
FJ3640.clinicalCondition: Splenic infarction — emboli through this artery produce wedge-shaped splenic infarcts with left upper quadrant pain.
FJ3640.clinicalScenario: A patient with endocarditis develops pleuritic left upper quadrant pain; CT shows wedge-shaped splenic infarcts from septic emboli.

FJ2986.name: Superior branch of medial segmental artery
FJ2986.details: Superior branch of the medial segmental artery of the right middle lobe, arising from the middle-lobe division of the right pulmonary artery and accompanying the medial segment bronchus.
FJ2986.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — small emboli lodge in such segmental branches causing localised infarction and haemoptysis.
FJ2986.clinicalScenario: CT pulmonary angiography localises a small embolus to the superior branch of the medial segmental artery in a patient with pleuritic pain and haemoptysis.

FJ2990.name: Superior branch of medial segmental artery
FJ2990.details: Bronchopulmonary segmental branch supplying the upper part of the medial segment of the right middle lobe, running with its segmental bronchus and vein tributaries.
FJ2990.clinicalCondition: Right middle lobe syndrome — recurrent collapse and infection centre on this segment's bronchovascular unit.
FJ2990.clinicalScenario: A woman with chronic cough and recurrent infections has medial segment bronchiectasis of the middle lobe on CT, under investigation for middle lobe syndrome.

FJ2997.name: Superior branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2997.details: Branch of the superior segmental artery of the right lower lobe, arising from the posterior aspect of the interlobar pulmonary artery and ascending with the superior segment bronchus (B6).
FJ2997.clinicalCondition: Aspiration territory — the superior lower-lobe segment is the classic dependent site for aspiration when supine.
FJ2997.clinicalScenario: An unconscious alcoholic patient aspirates; imaging shows consolidation in the superior segment of the right lower lobe, the dependent segment when lying flat.

FJ2998.name: Superior branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2998.details: Segmental pulmonary arterial branch distributing to the superior segment of the right lower lobe, following the segmental bronchus to the alveolar capillary bed.
FJ2998.clinicalCondition: Segmental embolism — occlusion produces a peripheral wedge opacity (Hampton hump) on imaging.
FJ2998.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with pleuritic pain has a peripheral wedge-shaped opacity at the right base from embolism in this segmental branch.

FJ2999.name: Superior branch of right superior segmental artery
FJ2999.details: Upper division of the right lower lobe's superior segmental artery, entering the segment from its hilum alongside the B6 bronchus and segmental vein.
FJ2999.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy planning — precise mapping of this branch is essential for anatomical lung segment resection.
FJ2999.clinicalScenario: Before a video-assisted segmentectomy for a small lower-lobe tumour, the thoracic surgeon studies 3D CT reconstruction of the superior segmental arterial branches.

FJ2898.name: Superior lingular artery
FJ2898.details: Segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplying the superior lingular segment (S4) of the left upper lobe, accompanying the superior lingular bronchus.
FJ2898.clinicalCondition: Lingular pneumonia — consolidation here silhouettes the left heart border on chest radiography.
FJ2898.clinicalScenario: A patient with community-acquired pneumonia has lingular consolidation obscuring the left heart border on the chest film.

FJ2899.name: Superior lingular artery
FJ2899.details: Lingular division branch of the left pulmonary artery descending into the superior lingular segment, paired with its segmental bronchus and vein.
FJ2899.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary embolism — lingular branch emboli cause localised perfusion defects and pleuritic pain.
FJ2899.clinicalScenario: A breathless patient has a filling defect in the superior lingular artery on CT pulmonary angiography, confirming segmental embolism.

FJ2900.name: Superior lingular artery
FJ2900.details: Arterial supply to the superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe, arising from the anterior aspect of the left pulmonary artery's lingular part.
FJ2900.clinicalCondition: Haemoptysis localisation — bleeding from this segment is traced to its bronchial/pulmonary supply before embolisation.
FJ2900.clinicalScenario: A patient with bronchiectasis coughs blood; CT angiography localises the bleeding source to the lingular segment for targeted management.

FJ2901.name: Superior lingular artery
FJ2901.details: Superior division of the lingular arterial supply to the left upper lobe, travelling with the S4 bronchopulmonary segment's airway and venous drainage.
FJ2901.clinicalCondition: Lingular bronchiectasis — chronic infection damages this segment, sometimes requiring lingular resection.
FJ2901.clinicalScenario: A woman with recurrent lingular infections and localised bronchiectasis is considered for lingulectomy after failed medical therapy.

FJ1928.name: Superior mesenteric artery
FJ1928.details: Anterior branch of the abdominal aorta at L1 behind the pancreas; descends through the small-bowel mesentery giving inferior pancreaticoduodenal, jejunal, ileal, ileocolic, right colic and middle colic branches to the midgut.
FJ1928.clinicalCondition: Acute mesenteric ischaemia — SMA embolus causes severe pain out of proportion to examination findings.
FJ1928.clinicalScenario: An elderly man with atrial fibrillation develops severe central abdominal pain with a soft abdomen; CT shows an SMA embolus and he undergoes emergency embolectomy.

FJ2011.name: Superior mesenteric artery
FJ2011.details: Principal artery of the midgut, from the duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon; its branches form arcades within the mesentery.
FJ2011.clinicalCondition: SMA (Wilkie) syndrome — the third part of the duodenum is compressed between the SMA and aorta after major weight loss.
FJ2011.clinicalScenario: A teenager who lost much weight after scoliosis surgery vomits after meals; imaging shows duodenal compression between the superior mesenteric artery and aorta.

FJ3656.name: Superior rectal artery
FJ3656.details: Continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery into the pelvis after the sigmoid branches; descends between the rectal layers, dividing to supply the upper two-thirds of the rectum.
FJ3656.clinicalCondition: Internal haemorrhoids — its terminal branches supply the haemorrhoidal cushions at the classic 3, 7 and 11 o'clock positions.
FJ3656.clinicalScenario: A patient with painless bright-red rectal bleeding has internal haemorrhoids at the classic positions, supplied by superior rectal branches, treated by band ligation.

FJ2052.name: Superior segmental branch of left renal artery
FJ2052.details: One of five segmental end-arteries of the left kidney, arising from the anterior division of the renal artery to supply the superior (apical) renal segment; segments have no collateral supply.
FJ2052.clinicalCondition: Segmental renal infarction — embolus produces a wedge-shaped infarct with flank pain and haematuria.
FJ2052.clinicalScenario: A patient with atrial fibrillation presents with left flank pain and microscopic haematuria; CT shows a wedge-shaped perfusion defect in the superior renal segment.

FJ2042.name: Superior segmental branch of right renal artery
FJ2042.details: Segmental end-artery of the right kidney supplying its superior segment, branching from the renal artery's anterior division before or within the renal hilum.
FJ2042.clinicalCondition: Segmental artery injury — damage during partial nephrectomy infarcts the dependent segment because there is no cross-flow.
FJ2042.clinicalScenario: During tumour excision from the upper pole, the superior segmental branch is clamped selectively so only the tumour-bearing segment becomes ischaemic.

FJ1728M.name: Superior vermian branch of medial branch of left superior cerebellar artery
FJ1728M.details: Branch of the medial division of the left superior cerebellar artery ascending over the cerebellar hemisphere to supply the superior vermis and adjacent fastigial region.
FJ1728M.clinicalCondition: Vermian infarction — midline cerebellar damage causes truncal ataxia and gait instability disproportionate to limb signs.
FJ1728M.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient cannot sit unsupported and veers broadly when walking after a small left superior vermian infarct shown on MRI.

FJ1728.name: Superior vermian branch of medial branch of right superior cerebellar artery
FJ1728.details: Medial-branch twig of the right superior cerebellar artery ramifying over the superior vermis, supplying midline cerebellar cortex involved in axial and gait control.
FJ1728.clinicalCondition: Superior cerebellar stroke — vermian involvement produces severe imbalance and vomiting mimicking labyrinthitis.
FJ1728.clinicalScenario: A man presents with vomiting and inability to stand; examination shows truncal ataxia and MRI confirms a right superior vermian branch territory infarct.

FJ1729M.name: Temporo-occipital branch of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1729M.details: Cortical branch of the left middle cerebral artery supplying the posterior temporal and lateral occipital cortex, part of the posterior perisylvian language and visual association region.
FJ1729M.clinicalCondition: Wernicke-type aphasia — dominant posterior temporal infarction impairs comprehension with fluent, empty speech.
FJ1729M.clinicalScenario: A patient speaks fluently but comprehends nothing after a left temporo-occipital branch stroke affecting posterior language cortex.

FJ1729.name: Temporo-occipital branch of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1729.details: Cortical branch of the right middle cerebral artery distributing to the posterior temporal and lateral occipital cortex, serving visual association areas.
FJ1729.clinicalCondition: Quadrantanopia — right-sided lesions damage optic radiations/cortex, causing a left superior visual field defect.
FJ1729.clinicalScenario: After a right temporo-occipital branch infarct, a patient has a left superior quadrantanopia and difficulty recognising objects by sight.

FJ2641.name: Third right anterior branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2641.details: Third diagonal branch of the anterior interventricular (LAD) artery crossing the anterolateral left ventricular wall; its size is variable and it may be small or absent.
FJ2641.clinicalCondition: Diagonal territory ischaemia — disease here produces anterolateral changes in leads I, aVL, V5–V6.
FJ2641.clinicalScenario: Exercise testing reproduces angina with ST depression in I, aVL and V5–V6; angiography shows disease in a large third diagonal branch.

FJ2647.name: Third right anterior branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2647.details: A further diagonal branch of the LAD supplying the lateral left ventricular wall, running between the main diagonal branches toward the obtuse margin.
FJ2647.clinicalCondition: Bifurcation disease — diagonal ostia are frequent sites of plaque complicating LAD stenting.
FJ2647.clinicalScenario: During PCI to the LAD, a plaque shift compromises the third diagonal ostium, causing lateral chest pain treated with a kissing-balloon technique.

FJ2631.name: Trunk of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery
FJ2631.details: Main stem of the LAD from the left coronary bifurcation, running the length of the anterior interventricular groove to the apex, giving diagonal and septal perforator branches.
FJ2631.clinicalCondition: Proximal LAD occlusion — the 'widowmaker' lesion causing large anterior STEMI and cardiogenic shock risk.
FJ2631.clinicalScenario: A 55-year-old smoker with crushing chest pain has tombstone ST elevation in V2–V5; primary PCI opens a proximally occluded LAD trunk.

FJ3432.name: Trunk of gastroduodenal artery
FJ3432.details: Main stem of the gastroduodenal artery from the common hepatic artery, descending behind the first part of the duodenum before dividing into right gastroepiploic and superior pancreaticoduodenal branches.
FJ3432.clinicalCondition: Bleeding posterior duodenal ulcer — ulcer erosion into this artery causes massive haematemesis and melaena.
FJ3432.clinicalScenario: A patient with a posterior duodenal ulcer presents with melaena and shock; endoscopy fails, so the gastroduodenal artery is embolised to stop bleeding.

FJ1718M.name: Trunk of inferior terminal branch of left middle cerebral artery
FJ1718M.details: Lower (inferior) division trunk of the left middle cerebral artery emerging from the lateral sulcus to supply the temporal lobe cortex via temporal and temporo-occipital branches.
FJ1718M.clinicalCondition: Inferior division stroke — dominant-hemisphere lesions cause receptive aphasia and a superior quadrantanopia.
FJ1718M.clinicalScenario: A woman develops fluent, meaningless speech with poor comprehension; imaging shows infarction in the left MCA inferior division territory.

FJ1718.name: Trunk of inferior terminal branch of right middle cerebral artery
FJ1718.details: Inferior division trunk of the right middle cerebral artery supplying the lateral temporal lobe and contributing branches toward the parietal and occipital cortex.
FJ1718.clinicalCondition: 'Pie in the sky' defect — temporal (Meyer loop) involvement produces a contralateral superior quadrantanopia.
FJ1718.clinicalScenario: A man develops a left superior quadrantanopia after occlusion of a right inferior MCA division branch shown on CT perfusion.

FJ2737.name: Trunk of left coronary artery
FJ2737.details: Short main stem, about 1–2 cm, arising from the left aortic sinus and passing between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle before bifurcating into the LAD and circumflex arteries.
FJ2737.clinicalCondition: Left main stenosis — a critical lesion jeopardising most of the left ventricle, usually treated by bypass surgery.
FJ2737.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with exertional dyspnoea has 80 percent left main coronary stenosis on angiography and is referred urgently for bypass surgery.

FJ3095.name: Trunk of left hepatic artery
FJ3095.details: Main stem of the left hepatic artery from the proper hepatic artery, ascending at the porta hepatis within the fissure for the ligamentum venosum to supply the left lobe of the liver.
FJ3095.clinicalCondition: Variant origin — a replaced left hepatic artery from the left gastric is common and must be preserved in gastric surgery.
FJ3095.clinicalScenario: During gastrectomy, the surgeon identifies a replaced left hepatic artery in the lesser omentum and preserves it to protect the left liver lobe.

FJ3476.name: Trunk of left renal artery
FJ3476.details: Main stem of the left renal artery from the aorta at L1, passing laterally behind the left renal vein region to the hilum, where it divides into anterior and posterior divisions and segmental branches.
FJ3476.clinicalCondition: Ostial atherosclerotic stenosis — narrowing at this trunk's origin is the commonest cause of renovascular hypertension in older patients.
FJ3476.clinicalScenario: A 62-year-old with flash pulmonary oedema and worsening renal function has tight left renal artery ostial stenosis confirmed on angiography.

FJ2252.name: Trunk of left thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2252.details: Short branch of the second part of the axillary artery piercing the clavipectoral fascia and dividing into pectoral, deltoid, acromial and clavicular branches.
FJ2252.clinicalCondition: Deltopectoral approach landmark — its deltoid branch accompanies the cephalic vein in shoulder surgery.
FJ2252.clinicalScenario: During a deltopectoral approach for shoulder arthroplasty, the deltoid branch of the left thoraco-acromial trunk beside the cephalic vein is ligated.

FJ2723.name: Trunk of right coronary artery
FJ2723.details: Main stem of the right coronary artery arising from the right aortic sinus, running in the right atrioventricular groove and giving the SA nodal, right marginal and usually posterior interventricular branches.
FJ2723.clinicalCondition: Inferior myocardial infarction — proximal occlusion also starves the SA and AV nodes, causing bradyarrhythmias.
FJ2723.clinicalScenario: A patient with inferior ST elevation becomes bradycardic with AV block; angiography shows a proximally occluded right coronary artery trunk.

FJ3117.name: Trunk of right hepatic artery
FJ3117.details: Main stem of the right hepatic artery from the proper hepatic artery, ascending at the porta hepatis posterior to the common hepatic duct to supply the right lobe of the liver.
FJ3117.clinicalCondition: Iatrogenic injury at cholecystectomy — the artery crosses near the cystic artery and can be mistaken for it.
FJ3117.clinicalScenario: At laparoscopic cholecystectomy, the critical view of safety is obtained so the right hepatic artery is not mistaken for the cystic artery.

FJ3576.name: Trunk of right renal artery
FJ3576.details: Main stem of the right renal artery from the aorta at L1 — the longer renal artery, passing posterior to the IVC and the head of the pancreas to reach the right hilum.
FJ3576.clinicalCondition: Fibromuscular dysplasia — mid-distal 'string of beads' narrowing classically affecting younger women and causing hypertension.
FJ3576.clinicalScenario: A 34-year-old woman with new severe hypertension has a string-of-beads appearance of the right renal artery, confirming fibromuscular dysplasia.

FJ2304.name: Trunk of right thoraco-acromial artery
FJ2304.details: Brief trunk from the second part of the right axillary artery that pierces the clavipectoral fascia, dividing into branches for the pectoral muscles, deltoid, acromion and clavicle.
FJ2304.clinicalCondition: Pectoral flap pedicle — its pectoral branch supplies the pectoralis major flap used in head and neck reconstruction.
FJ2304.clinicalScenario: A surgeon raises a pectoralis major flap for a post-laryngectomy defect, preserving the pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial trunk as its pedicle.

FJ3644.name: Trunk of superior mesenteric artery
FJ3644.details: Proximal stem of the SMA leaving the aorta at L1, passing between the splenic vein and pancreas above and crossing the left renal vein and third part of the duodenum.
FJ3644.clinicalCondition: Nutcracker phenomenon — the left renal vein is compressed between this trunk and the aorta, causing haematuria.
FJ3644.clinicalScenario: A thin young woman with intermittent left flank pain and haematuria has left renal vein compression between the aorta and SMA trunk on CT.

FJ3481.name: Ureteric segment of left renal artery
FJ3481.details: Portion of the left renal artery trunk at the hilum lying anterior to the renal pelvis, giving a ureteric branch that descends to supply the upper ureter.
FJ3481.clinicalCondition: Crossing-vessel obstruction — an arterial segment crossing the ureteropelvic junction can compress it and cause hydronephrosis.
FJ3481.clinicalScenario: A young adult with flank pain after drinking fluids has ureteropelvic junction obstruction; imaging shows a crossing renal arterial branch at the junction.

FJ3581.name: Ureteric segment of right renal artery
FJ3581.details: Segment of the right renal artery at the renal hilum related anteriorly to the pelvis of the ureter, contributing a ureteric branch to the upper ureteric blood supply.
FJ3581.clinicalCondition: Ureteric devascularisation risk — injuring this supply during pyeloplasty can stricture the upper ureter.
FJ3581.clinicalScenario: During pyeloplasty for a child with hydronephrosis, the surgeon preserves the ureteric branch of the renal artery to protect ureteric healing.

FJ3582.name: Ureteric segment of right renal artery
FJ3582.details: Hilum segment of the right renal artery crossing in front of the renal pelvis, from which small ureteric twigs pass to the ureteropelvic junction and upper ureter.
FJ3582.clinicalCondition: Intermittent obstruction (Dietl crisis) — a crossing arterial segment at the junction can worsen drainage when the pelvis fills.
FJ3582.clinicalScenario: A teenager has episodic severe flank pain with vomiting after large fluid intake; imaging shows a full renal pelvis with a crossing arterial segment.

FJ1981.name: Accessory hemiazygos vein
FJ1981.details: Descends on the left side of the T5–T8 vertebral bodies, receives the 4th–8th left posterior intercostal veins, and crosses the midline at about T7–T8 to join the azygos vein.
FJ1981.clinicalCondition: Dilated collateral in SVC obstruction — provides an alternative pathway returning upper-body blood to the heart.
FJ1981.clinicalScenario: A 58-year-old smoker with facial swelling and distended chest veins has a lung mass compressing the SVC; CT shows prominent azygos-system collaterals.

FJ2725.name: Anterior cardiac vein
FJ2725.details: Two or three small veins draining the anterior surface of the right ventricle; they cross the atrioventricular groove and open directly into the right atrium, bypassing the coronary sinus.
FJ2725.clinicalCondition: Relevant to retrograde cardioplegia — blood escaping through these veins reduces cardioplegia delivery to the right ventricle during cardiac surgery.
FJ2725.clinicalScenario: During bypass surgery the perfusionist notes poor right ventricular cooling despite retrograde cardioplegia; direct atrial drainage via the anterior cardiac veins explains the washout.

FJ2730.name: Anterior cardiac vein
FJ2730.details: Small veins on the front of the right ventricle and along the right coronary margin; they terminate in tiny openings in the wall of the right atrium.
FJ2730.clinicalCondition: A prominent anterior cardiac vein may appear as an incidental tubular structure on echocardiography and mimic a mass or dissection flap.
FJ2730.clinicalScenario: A 45-year-old's routine echocardiogram shows a vessel-like structure at the right atrioventricular groove; Doppler confirms a benign prominent anterior cardiac vein needing no treatment.

FJ3074.name: Anterior inferior segmental branch of right portal vein
FJ3074.details: Intrahepatic branch of the right portal vein supplying segment VI and the anterior-inferior part of segment V, following the Couinaud segmental portal pedicles.
FJ3074.clinicalCondition: Segmental portal branch thrombosis or tumor invasion — alters perfusion of segments V and VI and changes liver resection planning.
FJ3074.clinicalScenario: A 40-year-old with hepatocellular carcinoma is assessed for right hepatectomy; CT portography maps this branch to confirm adequate perfusion of the future liver remnant.

FJ3083.name: Anterior inferior segmental tributary of middle hepatic vein
FJ3083.details: Hepatic venous tributary draining the anterior-inferior territory, chiefly segment V, into the middle hepatic vein, which joins the left hepatic vein or enters the inferior vena cava directly.
FJ3083.clinicalCondition: Tributary injury during liver resection causes dark, brisk hepatic venous bleeding that can be difficult to control laparoscopically.
FJ3083.clinicalScenario: During laparoscopic segmentectomy, heavy bleeding from the cut surface is traced to a torn middle hepatic vein tributary and controlled with clips and suturing.

FJ3086.name: Anterior inferior segmental tributary of middle hepatic vein
FJ3086.details: Small vein conveying blood from the segment V region into the trunk of the middle hepatic vein close to its confluence with the inferior vena cava.
FJ3086.clinicalCondition: Segment V congestion after right hepatectomy if the middle hepatic vein is taken without reconstructing this tributary's drainage.
FJ3086.clinicalScenario: After an extended right hepatectomy the remnant liver looks dusky over segment V; the surgical team attributes it to the sacrificed middle hepatic tributary.

FJ2657.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2657.details: Runs with the left anterior descending artery in the anterior interventricular sulcus, drains the anterior left ventricle and cardiac apex, and continues as the great cardiac vein.
FJ2657.clinicalCondition: Its territory mirrors LAD occlusion — the vein drains the wall infarcted in an anterior myocardial infarction.
FJ2657.clinicalScenario: A 62-year-old man has crushing central chest pain with ST elevation in V1–V4; angiography shows an occluded LAD, the artery this vein accompanies.

FJ2658.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2658.details: Ascends the anterior interventricular sulcus beside the LAD, receiving tributaries from both ventricles and the apex before turning into the left atrioventricular groove.
FJ2658.clinicalCondition: Key landmark in cardiac resynchronization therapy — leads traverse the coronary sinus and great cardiac vein toward its tributaries for left ventricular pacing.
FJ2658.clinicalScenario: A heart failure patient undergoing CRT implant has the LV lead advanced through the coronary sinus into a lateral vein branching near this vessel.

FJ2659.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2659.details: Accompanies the LAD from the cardiac apex upward, collecting diagonal tributaries from the anterolateral wall of the left ventricle along its course.
FJ2659.clinicalCondition: Enlarged and tortuous in chronic coronary disease, where it may be mistaken for an additional artery on angiographic images.
FJ2659.clinicalScenario: Reviewing a coronary angiogram, the cardiologist distinguishes this vein running parallel to a diffusely diseased LAD, avoiding misinterpretation of the vessel anatomy.

FJ2660.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2660.details: Begins near the apex of the heart and the anterior interventricular notch, runs upward in the sulcus with the LAD, and drains toward the great cardiac vein.
FJ2660.clinicalCondition: Its apical origin marks the territory at risk of apical infarction and thrombus formation after LAD occlusion.
FJ2660.clinicalScenario: After an anterior MI, echocardiography shows an akinetic apex with mural thrombus in exactly the region drained by this vein's distal course.

FJ2661.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2661.details: Lies superficially in the anterior interventricular sulcus beside the LAD, covered only by epicardium and fat, making it vulnerable during epicardial procedures.
FJ2661.clinicalCondition: At risk of injury during epicardial ventricular tachycardia ablation, causing hemopericardium and tamponade.
FJ2661.clinicalScenario: During epicardial ablation for refractory VT, sudden hypotension develops; pericardiocentesis yields blood from a punctured anterior interventricular vein, requiring surgical repair.

FJ2662.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2662.details: The principal venous channel of the anterior ventricular wall, running the full length of the anterior interventricular sulcus from apex to base.
FJ2662.clinicalCondition: Assessed on CT coronary venography before CRT implantation to predict whether suitable target veins exist for lead placement.
FJ2662.clinicalScenario: A patient with dyssynchrony has CT venography showing a well-developed anterior interventricular and lateral vein system, confirming feasibility of biventricular pacing.

FJ2663.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2663.details: Courses with the LAD and gives the surgeon a surface guide to the artery, especially when the artery is buried in fat or myocardium.
FJ2663.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark in off-pump bypass — the vein helps locate an intramyocardial LAD for graft anastomosis.
FJ2663.clinicalScenario: During off-pump CABG the surgeon follows this vein in the sulcus to find a deeply intramyocardial LAD segment suitable for the graft.

FJ2664.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2664.details: Receives septal and anterior wall tributaries as it ascends beside the LAD; its blood ultimately reaches the right atrium via the coronary sinus.
FJ2664.clinicalCondition: Rare post-infarction thrombophlebitis of cardiac veins can extend pain and fever after the acute event has settled.
FJ2664.clinicalScenario: Five days after an anterior MI, a patient develops recurrent pleuritic pain and low-grade fever; imaging excludes pericarditis and suggests thrombosed anterior cardiac veins.

FJ2665.name: Anterior interventricular vein
FJ2665.details: The distal continuation of the cardiac venous system at the apex; it winds around the apical notch region before ascending the anterior sulcus.
FJ2665.clinicalCondition: Apical tributaries are used for retrograde venous ethanol ablation of summit ventricular arrhythmias in selected patients.
FJ2665.clinicalScenario: A patient with incessant outflow-tract VT refractory to drugs undergoes mapping; ethanol ablation via a tributary of this vein abolishes the arrhythmia.

FJ3034.name: Anterior part of lateral segmental vein
FJ3034.details: Tributary draining the anterior portion of the lateral segment (S4) of the right middle lobe, joining the medial segmental vein to form the middle lobe vein entering the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3034.clinicalCondition: Must be identified and divided in right middle lobectomy; unrecognized variation risks postoperative venous congestion of the remaining segment.
FJ3034.clinicalScenario: Before a VATS middle lobectomy for a carcinoid tumor, CT bronchovascular mapping shows this vein's course so the surgeon can divide it safely.

FJ3035.name: Anterior part of lateral segmental vein
FJ3035.details: Small pulmonary vein branch collecting blood from the front of the lateral segment of the right middle lobe toward the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3035.clinicalCondition: Middle lobe syndrome — chronic collapse of the right middle lobe impairs this vein's drainage and perpetuates recurrent infection.
FJ3035.clinicalScenario: A woman with recurrent right middle lobe pneumonias has bronchiectasis and collapse on CT; lobectomy of the congested middle lobe is performed.

FJ3036.name: Anterior part of lateral segmental vein
FJ3036.details: Part of the segmental venous drainage of the right middle lobe; segmental veins run between segments and serve as intersegmental landmarks for anatomical resection.
FJ3036.clinicalCondition: Serves as the intersegmental plane marker in segmentectomy — following it keeps the resection anatomical and spares healthy lung.
FJ3036.clinicalScenario: During an S4 segmentectomy for a small ground-glass lesion, the surgeon follows this vein to define the plane between lateral and medial segments.

FJ3042.name: Anterior part of right apical segmental vein
FJ3042.details: Tributary draining the anterior portion of the apical segment (S1) of the right upper lobe into the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3042.clinicalCondition: Venous variation at the right hilum is a common cause of unexpected bleeding during upper lobectomy if not mapped preoperatively.
FJ3042.clinicalScenario: A preoperative 3D CT reconstruction for right upper lobectomy shows this vein crossing anterior to the bronchus, changing the order of hilar division.

FJ3053.name: Anterior part of right apical segmental vein
FJ3053.details: Collects blood from the front of the right lung apex and joins other apical tributaries forming the upper division of the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3053.clinicalCondition: Preserved when possible in apical segmentectomy to prevent venous congestion and prolonged air leak in the remaining segments.
FJ3053.clinicalScenario: In an S1 segmentectomy for early adenocarcinoma, the surgeon preserves this tributary's drainage of adjacent segments to avoid postoperative congestion.

FJ3073.name: Anterior superior segmental branch of right portal vein
FJ3073.details: Branch of the right portal vein supplying segment VIII and the superior part of segment V within the right anterior sector of the liver.
FJ3073.clinicalCondition: Tumor thrombus extending into this branch upstages hepatocellular carcinoma and may rule out curative resection.
FJ3073.clinicalScenario: MRI in a hepatitis B patient shows HCC in segment VIII with enhancing thrombus in this portal branch, shifting management to systemic therapy.

FJ3121.name: Anterior superior segmental tributary of right hepatic vein
FJ3121.details: Hepatic venous tributary draining the anterior-superior territory, mainly segment VIII, into the right hepatic vein before it enters the inferior vena cava.
FJ3121.clinicalCondition: Segment VIII congestion in Budd–Chiari syndrome when the right hepatic vein ostium is obstructed.
FJ3121.clinicalScenario: A young woman on oral contraceptives presents with ascites and hepatomegaly; imaging shows right hepatic vein thrombosis with a congested segment VIII.

FJ3064.name: Apical part of right apical segmental vein
FJ3064.details: Small tributary draining the very apex of the right upper lobe, joining the apical segmental vein within the right superior pulmonary vein system.
FJ3064.clinicalCondition: Apical venous branches may be injured during pleural adhesiolysis for spontaneous pneumothorax surgery, causing troublesome hilar bleeding.
FJ3064.clinicalScenario: During VATS bullectomy for recurrent pneumothorax, dense apical adhesions tear a small apical vein, controlled with an energy device and pressure.

FJ3067.name: Apical part of right apical segmental vein
FJ3067.details: Drains the cupola of the right lung into the apical segmental tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein, running close to the apical pleura.
FJ3067.clinicalCondition: Its proximity to the apex means it can bleed into a ruptured apical bulla, contributing to hemopneumothorax.
FJ3067.clinicalScenario: A tall thin teenager presents with sudden dyspnea and chest pain; imaging shows right pneumothorax with a small apical hemothorax.

FJ3068.name: Apical part of right apical segmental vein
FJ3068.details: Terminal pulmonary venous radicle of the right lung apex, part of the segmental venous map used in anatomical lung resection.
FJ3068.clinicalCondition: Mapping this radicle prevents accidental ligation during apical segmentectomy, which would congest the preserved lung.
FJ3068.clinicalScenario: The thoracic team reviews 3D reconstructions showing this apical radicle before resecting a tuberculoma confined to the right apex.

FJ3658.name: Ascending lumbar vein
FJ3658.details: Connects the common iliac and lumbar veins below with the azygos vein on the right and hemiazygos on the left; links the caval and vertebral venous systems.
FJ3658.clinicalCondition: Important collateral in inferior vena cava occlusion, and a route by which pelvic tumors or infection reach the vertebral plexus.
FJ3658.clinicalScenario: A patient with an obstructed IVC from retroperitoneal fibrosis shows dilated ascending lumbar collaterals carrying blood toward the azygos system on CT.

FJ3416.name: Azygos vein
FJ3416.details: Formed by the right ascending lumbar and subcostal veins, it ascends on the right of the thoracic vertebrae and arches over the right lung root at T4 to enter the SVC.
FJ3416.clinicalCondition: Azygos enlargement signals SVC obstruction or portal hypertension; an azygos lobe is a common incidental variant.
FJ3416.clinicalScenario: A man with lung cancer develops face and arm swelling; chest imaging shows a markedly dilated azygos arch from SVC compression.

FJ3124.name: Caudate lobe branch of left portal vein
FJ3124.details: Small portal branch from the left portal vein supplying the caudate lobe (segment I), which also drains directly into the IVC through emissary veins.
FJ3124.clinicalCondition: Caudate hypertrophy in Budd–Chiari syndrome — its independent IVC drainage spares segment I while other segments congest.
FJ3124.clinicalScenario: CT of a patient with Budd–Chiari shows a strikingly enlarged caudate lobe compressing the IVC, a classic diagnostic clue.

FJ1914.name: Caudate lobe branch of right portal vein
FJ1914.details: Portal branch arising from the right portal vein or bifurcation supplying part of the caudate lobe and caudate process of segment I.
FJ1914.clinicalCondition: Must be accounted for in segment I resection for hilar cholangiocarcinoma, where caudate branches are routinely involved.
FJ1914.clinicalScenario: Planning surgery for a Klatskin tumor, the hepatobiliary team maps this branch because caudate lobectomy is required for clear margins.

FJ2322.name: Common palmar digital vein
FJ2322.details: Short veins in the palm formed by proper palmar digital veins; they join the superficial palmar venous arch, draining toward the ulnar and basilic veins.
FJ2322.clinicalCondition: Superficial thrombophlebitis of palmar veins after hand cannulation causes tender cords and swelling in the palm.
FJ2322.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a painful, cord-like swelling in the palm two days after a hand IV line; ultrasound confirms thrombophlebitis of a palmar vein.

FJ2352.name: Common palmar digital vein
FJ2352.details: Palmar venous channels collecting blood from adjacent sides of neighboring fingers and emptying into the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2352.clinicalCondition: In finger replantation, repairing these palmar and dorsal veins is critical — venous congestion is the commonest cause of replant failure.
FJ2352.clinicalScenario: After replantation of an amputated index finger, the digit becomes purple and swollen; exploration finds a thrombosed repaired vein needing revision.

FJ2655.name: Coronary sinus
FJ2655.details: The heart's main venous trunk, lying in the posterior atrioventricular groove; it receives the cardiac veins and opens into the right atrium guarded by the Thebesian valve.
FJ2655.clinicalCondition: Cannulated for CRT leads and retrograde cardioplegia; a dilated coronary sinus suggests persistent left SVC or raised right atrial pressure.
FJ2655.clinicalScenario: Echocardiography in a child shows a dilated coronary sinus; further imaging confirms a persistent left superior vena cava draining into it.

FJ2056.name: Deep dorsal vein of penis
FJ2056.details: Single midline vein deep to Buck's fascia draining the glans and corpora cavernosa; it passes below the pubic symphysis into the prostatic venous plexus.
FJ2056.clinicalCondition: Its prostatic plexus connects with the vertebral venous plexus — a valveless route for prostate cancer spread to the spine.
FJ2056.clinicalScenario: A man with prostate cancer develops back pain; MRI shows vertebral metastases, explained by spread through the prostatic and vertebral venous plexuses.

FJ2186.name: Dorsal metacarpal vein
FJ2186.details: Veins running between the metacarpals on the dorsum of the hand, draining the fingers into the dorsal venous network; a favorite site for intravenous cannulation.
FJ2186.clinicalCondition: Cannula-related thrombophlebitis — prolonged siting in these small veins causes pain, redness and a palpable cord.
FJ2186.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient complains of a red, tender track over the back of the hand at the cannula site; the line is removed for phlebitis.

FJ2199.name: Dorsal metacarpal vein
FJ2199.details: Dorsal hand veins between the metacarpal heads that receive digital veins and converge into the dorsal venous network, origin of the cephalic and basilic veins.
FJ2199.clinicalCondition: Chemotherapy extravasation risk — these veins are used for infusions, and leakage causes tissue injury over the hand dorsum.
FJ2199.clinicalScenario: During chemotherapy infusion through a dorsal hand vein, the patient reports burning and swelling; extravasation is recognized and the infusion stopped immediately.

FJ2059.name: Dorsal venous arch of left foot
FJ2059.details: Transverse venous arch across the dorsum of the left foot formed by dorsal metatarsal veins; its medial end continues as the great saphenous vein, the lateral end as the small saphenous vein.
FJ2059.clinicalCondition: Convenient site for venous access and blood sampling in infants when scalp and arm veins are unsuitable.
FJ2059.clinicalScenario: In a dehydrated infant with collapsed arm veins, the team successfully samples blood from the dorsal venous arch of the foot.

FJ2060.name: Dorsal venous arch of left foot
FJ2060.details: Superficial arch on the left foot dorsum collecting the dorsal digital veins of the toes through metatarsal veins, lying just deep to the skin.
FJ2060.clinicalCondition: Prominent, tortuous dorsal foot veins are an early visible sign of chronic venous insufficiency of the leg.
FJ2060.clinicalScenario: A shop assistant who stands all day shows bulging veins over the left foot dorsum with ankle edema, consistent with developing venous insufficiency.

FJ2061.name: Dorsal venous arch of right foot
FJ2061.details: Venous arch across the dorsum of the right foot; medially it gives origin to the great saphenous vein in front of the medial malleolus.
FJ2061.clinicalCondition: The great saphenous origin here is a cutdown site for emergency venous access when peripheral cannulation fails.
FJ2061.clinicalScenario: In a shocked trauma patient with no arm access, a cutdown over the right ankle exposes the great saphenous vein at this arch for rapid infusion.

FJ2062.name: Dorsal venous arch of right foot
FJ2062.details: Subcutaneous arch uniting the dorsal metatarsal veins of the right foot, an important surface landmark at the ankle for the great saphenous vein.
FJ2062.clinicalCondition: In diabetics, congested dorsal foot veins with edema worsen foot ulcer healing and signal coexisting venous disease.
FJ2062.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a non-healing forefoot ulcer has marked dorsal venous congestion; compression is started only after arterial insufficiency is excluded.

FJ2228.name: Dorsal venous network of left hand
FJ2228.details: Subcutaneous venous network over the dorsum of the left hand formed by dorsal metacarpal veins; drains laterally into the cephalic vein and medially into the basilic vein.
FJ2228.clinicalCondition: First-choice site for peripheral IV cannulation — visible, accessible and distant from arteries and nerves.
FJ2228.clinicalScenario: Before elective surgery, the anesthetist cannulates a prominent vein of this left dorsal network for induction and maintenance fluids.

FJ2280.name: Dorsal venous network of right hand
FJ2280.details: Reticular subcutaneous veins on the dorsum of the right hand draining the fingers, converging toward the basilic vein medially and cephalic vein laterally.
FJ2280.clinicalCondition: Repeated cannulation here causes bruising and sclerosis of veins, a problem for patients needing chronic IV therapy.
FJ2280.clinicalScenario: A cystic fibrosis patient on frequent IV antibiotics has scarred dorsal hand veins, prompting placement of a long-term PICC line instead.

FJ2656.name: Great cardiac vein
FJ2656.details: Continuation of the anterior interventricular vein; it turns into the left atrioventricular groove alongside the circumflex artery and ends in the coronary sinus at the valve of Vieussens.
FJ2656.clinicalCondition: A target and route for CRT lead placement; its valve at the coronary sinus junction can obstruct catheter advancement.
FJ2656.clinicalScenario: During CRT implantation the lead repeatedly catches at a prominent Vieussens valve where this vein meets the coronary sinus, requiring a different branch.

FJ3434.name: Hemiazygos vein
FJ3434.details: Ascends on the left side of the lower thoracic vertebrae receiving the 9th–11th left posterior intercostal veins, then crosses at about T8–T9 behind the aorta to join the azygos vein.
FJ3434.clinicalCondition: Enlarges as a collateral when the IVC is obstructed, and in azygos continuation of the IVC it carries lower-body blood upward.
FJ3434.clinicalScenario: CT in a patient with congenital IVC interruption shows a prominent hemiazygos and azygos system draining the lower body to the SVC.

FJ1853.name: Hepatic portal vein
FJ1853.details: Formed behind the neck of the pancreas at L2 by union of the splenic and superior mesenteric veins; carries nutrient-rich, oxygen-poor blood from the gut and spleen to the liver.
FJ1853.clinicalCondition: Portal hypertension — raised pressure produces esophageal varices, ascites, splenomegaly and caput medusae; thrombosis causes acute abdominal pain.
FJ1853.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic man vomits blood; endoscopy shows bleeding esophageal varices fed by portal hypertension, treated with banding and vasoactive drugs.

FJ2818.name: Hepatovenous segment II
FJ2818.details: The superior part of the left lateral section of the liver, above the left portal fissure, drained by tributaries of the left hepatic vein.
FJ2818.clinicalCondition: Segment II lesions are accessible to laparoscopic resection; its veins guide anatomical left lateral sectionectomy.
FJ2818.clinicalScenario: A patient with a solitary colorectal metastasis in segment II undergoes laparoscopic resection with the left hepatic vein tributaries as landmarks.

FJ2819.name: Hepatovenous segment III
FJ2819.details: The inferior part of the left lateral section, lying below the left portal fissure beside the falciform ligament, drained toward the left hepatic vein.
FJ2819.clinicalCondition: Segment III (with II) forms the left lateral section graft used in pediatric and split-liver transplantation.
FJ2819.clinicalScenario: A father donates his left lateral liver section, segments II and III, to his infant daughter with biliary atresia.

FJ2820.name: Hepatovenous segment IV
FJ2820.details: The left medial segment between the umbilical fissure and the middle hepatic vein, above and below the porta hepatis (IVa and IVb), drained by middle and left hepatic tributaries.
FJ2820.clinicalCondition: Segment IV congestion may follow middle hepatic vein sacrifice in extended right hepatectomy, threatening the remnant liver.
FJ2820.clinicalScenario: After extended right hepatectomy for cholangiocarcinoma, imaging shows segment IV congestion because its middle hepatic drainage was divided.

FJ1858.name: Hepatovenous segment IX
FJ1858.details: The dorsal (caudate) segment of the liver, segment I, which uniquely drains through small emissary veins directly into the inferior vena cava rather than the main hepatic veins.
FJ1858.clinicalCondition: Spared in Budd–Chiari syndrome — direct IVC drainage protects this segment, producing characteristic caudate hypertrophy.
FJ1858.clinicalScenario: Imaging of a patient with hepatic vein thrombosis shows an enlarged caudate segment with atrophied peripheral liver, classic for Budd–Chiari.

FJ2821.name: Hepatovenous segment V
FJ2821.details: The inferior part of the right anterior sector, below the right portal fissure, drained by tributaries of the middle and right hepatic veins.
FJ2821.clinicalCondition: Segment V drains near the gallbladder fossa; its veins are encountered and may bleed during cholecystectomy and central hepatectomy.
FJ2821.clinicalScenario: During a difficult cholecystectomy for gangrenous gallbladder, oozing from the liver bed is traced to a segment V venous tributary.

FJ2822.name: Hepatovenous segment VI
FJ2822.details: The inferior part of the right posterior sector of the liver, below the right portal pedicle, drained by the right hepatic vein and sometimes an inferior right hepatic vein.
FJ2822.clinicalCondition: An accessory inferior right hepatic vein draining segment VI is common and must be preserved in right donor hepatectomy.
FJ2822.clinicalScenario: Living-donor assessment CT shows a large inferior right hepatic vein draining segment VI, altering the planned transection plane.

FJ2409.name: Hepatovenous segment VII
FJ2409.details: The superior part of the right posterior sector, above the right portal fissure and beneath the diaphragm, drained by the right hepatic vein.
FJ2409.clinicalCondition: Segment VII tumors are technically demanding to resect because of their high, posterior position against the diaphragm and IVC.
FJ2409.clinicalScenario: A patient with a segment VII hepatocellular carcinoma undergoes posterior sectionectomy, with careful control of the right hepatic vein.

FJ2823.name: Hepatovenous segment VIII
FJ2823.details: The superior part of the right anterior sector, forming much of the liver dome, drained by tributaries of the middle and right hepatic veins.
FJ2823.clinicalCondition: Segment VIII is the commonest site assessed on imaging for hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhotic livers.
FJ2823.clinicalScenario: Surveillance ultrasound in a hepatitis C patient detects a new segment VIII nodule; MRI confirms hepatocellular carcinoma for ablation.

FJ2824.name: Hepatovenous segment VIII
FJ2824.details: Dome segment of the right lobe whose venous outflow crosses both middle and right hepatic vein territories, making its resection planes vascularly complex.
FJ2824.clinicalCondition: Isolated segment VIII resection requires mapping both hepatic vein systems to avoid outflow congestion of neighboring segments.
FJ2824.clinicalScenario: For a deeply placed segment VIII metastasis, the surgeon uses intraoperative ultrasound to map its dual venous drainage before parenchyma transection.

FJ3438.name: Ileal vein
FJ3438.details: Tributaries from the ileum that accompany ileal branches of the superior mesenteric artery and drain into the superior mesenteric vein within the mesentery.
FJ3438.clinicalCondition: Mesenteric venous thrombosis involving ileal veins causes segmental small-bowel ischemia with pain out of proportion to signs.
FJ3438.clinicalScenario: A woman on oral contraceptives presents with severe central abdominal pain and minimal tenderness; CT shows SMV and ileal vein thrombosis with bowel wall thickening.

FJ3415.name: Ileocolic vein
FJ3415.details: Accompanies the ileocolic artery, draining the terminal ileum, cecum and appendix region into the superior mesenteric vein.
FJ3415.clinicalCondition: Divided near its origin in right hemicolectomy; careless dissection risks SMV injury and major hemorrhage.
FJ3415.clinicalScenario: During laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for cecal cancer, the surgeon clips this vein at the ileocolic pedicle while protecting the adjacent SMV.

FJ3440.name: Ileocolic vein
FJ3440.details: Venous companion of the ileocolic artery crossing the right iliac fossa, receiving appendicular and cecal tributaries before joining the superior mesenteric vein.
FJ3440.clinicalCondition: Appendicular vein thrombosis (pylephlebitis) can follow appendicitis, seeding infection into the portal venous system.
FJ3440.clinicalScenario: A patient recovering from perforated appendicitis develops rigors and jaundice; imaging shows infective thrombophlebitis ascending toward the portal vein.

FJ2934.name: Inferior lingular vein
FJ2934.details: Tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein draining the inferior lingular segment (S5) of the left upper lobe, running below the lingular bronchus.
FJ2934.clinicalCondition: Identified and divided in lingulectomy; injury at the hilum is a source of bleeding in left upper lobe surgery.
FJ2934.clinicalScenario: A patient with localized lingular bronchiectasis undergoes lingulectomy, where this vein is isolated and stapled at the left hilum.

FJ2935.name: Inferior lingular vein
FJ2935.details: Small pulmonary vein collecting blood from the lower lingula and joining the superior and inferior lingular veins' common trunk into the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2935.clinicalCondition: Anomalous or shared lingular venous drainage must be recognized in left upper lobectomy to avoid congesting retained segments.
FJ2935.clinicalScenario: Preoperative CT for left upper lobe cancer shows lingular drainage partly into the inferior pulmonary vein, changing the lobectomy dissection plan.

FJ3443.name: Inferior mesenteric vein
FJ3443.details: Drains the hindgut — descending and sigmoid colon and upper rectum — ascending in the retroperitoneum to join the splenic vein behind the pancreas.
FJ3443.clinicalCondition: IMV thrombosis produces left-sided ischemic colitis; in portal hypertension it feeds descending colic collaterals and rectal varices.
FJ3443.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient with atrial fibrillation passes bloody diarrhea; colonoscopy and CT show ischemic descending colon with inferior mesenteric vein thrombosis.

FJ3032.name: Inferior part of medial segmental vein
FJ3032.details: Tributary draining the inferior portion of the medial segment (S5) of the right middle lobe into the middle lobe vein and right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3032.clinicalCondition: Venous mapping of the middle lobe prevents accidental division of this branch during lateral segmentectomy.
FJ3032.clinicalScenario: Before an S5-sparing resection, 3D imaging clarifies this inferior tributary so the preserved medial segment keeps its venous outflow.

FJ3033.name: Inferior part of medial segmental vein
FJ3033.details: Lower radicle of the medial segmental vein of the right middle lobe, running between segments as an intersegmental landmark.
FJ3033.clinicalCondition: Following it defines the intersegmental plane in anatomical middle lobe segmentectomy, minimizing loss of healthy lung.
FJ3033.clinicalScenario: During an anatomical S5 segmentectomy for a benign nodule, the surgeon uses this vein's plane to separate medial from lateral segments.

FJ3021.name: Inferior part of right anterior segmental vein
FJ3021.details: Tributary draining the inferior portion of the anterior segment (S3) of the right upper lobe into the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3021.clinicalCondition: Must be distinguished from the middle lobe vein at the hilum during right upper lobectomy to avoid wrong-vessel ligation.
FJ3021.clinicalScenario: In a right upper lobectomy, careful hilar dissection confirms this S3 tributary before division, protecting the middle lobe vein nearby.

FJ3447.name: Inferior phrenic vein
FJ3447.details: Veins draining the undersurface of the diaphragm; the right typically opens into the inferior vena cava, the left into the left renal vein, suprarenal vein or IVC.
FJ3447.clinicalCondition: They enlarge as portosystemic collaterals in portal hypertension, shunting blood between the portal territory and systemic veins.
FJ3447.clinicalScenario: CT in a cirrhotic patient shows a dilated left inferior phrenic vein forming a spontaneous splenorenal-type shunt around the diaphragm.

FJ3448.name: Inferior phrenic vein
FJ3448.details: Accompanies the inferior phrenic artery across the diaphragmatic crura, collecting tributaries from the diaphragm and the superior suprarenal gland region.
FJ3448.clinicalCondition: Right inferior phrenic vein injury during hepatectomy or IVC surgery causes bleeding close to the caval opening.
FJ3448.clinicalScenario: During mobilization of the right liver lobe, a torn inferior phrenic vein near the IVC bleeds briskly and is sutured under direct vision.

FJ3449.name: Inferior phrenic vein
FJ3449.details: Diaphragmatic veins that mirror the inferior phrenic arteries; the left vein frequently has two trunks joining the left renal and suprarenal veins.
FJ3449.clinicalCondition: Left inferior phrenic vein is a recognized collateral route for gastric variceal outflow and a target in shunt embolization.
FJ3449.clinicalScenario: An interventional radiologist embolizes a gastric varix whose outflow runs through the left inferior phrenic vein to the renal vein.

FJ3450.name: Inferior phrenic vein
FJ3450.details: Small veins leaving the inferior surface of the diaphragm near the central tendon and esophageal opening, draining into caval or renal venous systems.
FJ3450.clinicalCondition: Diaphragmatic rupture with herniation can tear these veins, adding concealed hemorrhage to thoracic or abdominal trauma.
FJ3450.clinicalScenario: After a road traffic accident, a patient with a ruptured left hemidiaphragm has bleeding traced partly to torn inferior phrenic veins at laparotomy.

FJ3451.name: Inferior phrenic vein
FJ3451.details: Venous drainage of the diaphragm that also receives the superior suprarenal veins, linking adrenal drainage with the caval and renal systems.
FJ3451.clinicalCondition: Its suprarenal tributaries bleed during adrenalectomy if the gland is mobilized before the central vein is controlled.
FJ3451.clinicalScenario: In a left adrenalectomy for an aldosteronoma, careful dissection around the inferior phrenic confluence prevents troublesome venous bleeding.

FJ3452.name: Inferior phrenic vein
FJ3452.details: Paired diaphragmatic veins whose openings lie close to the IVC's diaphragmatic passage at T8, within the surgical field of liver transplantation.
FJ3452.clinicalCondition: In Budd–Chiari syndrome these veins hypertrophy as collateral outflow channels around the obstructed hepatic veins.
FJ3452.clinicalScenario: Venography in Budd–Chiari shows a network of enlarged inferior phrenic collaterals bypassing the occluded hepatic venous outflow.

FJ3441.name: Inferior vena cava
FJ3441.details: Formed at L5 by the union of the common iliac veins, it ascends right of the aorta, receives the hepatic veins, pierces the diaphragm at T8 and enters the right atrium.
FJ3441.clinicalCondition: IVC thrombosis causes bilateral leg swelling; filters placed here prevent pulmonary embolism when anticoagulation fails or is contraindicated.
FJ3441.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with recurrent pulmonary emboli despite anticoagulation receives an IVC filter through the right femoral vein.

FJ3659.name: Inferior vena cava
FJ3659.details: The body's largest vein, returning all infradiaphragmatic blood to the heart; in pregnancy the gravid uterus compresses it when the mother lies supine.
FJ3659.clinicalCondition: Supine hypotensive syndrome of pregnancy — caval compression reduces venous return until the uterus is displaced leftward.
FJ3659.clinicalScenario: A woman at 34 weeks becomes pale and hypotensive lying flat for a scan; turning her to the left lateral position restores her blood pressure.

FJ3125.name: Lateral inferior segmental branch of left portal vein
FJ3125.details: Branch of the left portal vein supplying the inferior part of the left lateral section, chiefly segment III, entering through the umbilical fissure region.
FJ3125.clinicalCondition: Its distribution defines the resection territory in anatomical segment III resection and left lateral sectionectomy.
FJ3125.clinicalScenario: A patient with a segment III metastasis undergoes resection planned around this branch to preserve the rest of the left lobe.

FJ3097.name: Lateral inferior segmental tributary of left hepatic vein
FJ3097.details: Hepatic venous tributary draining the inferior left lateral territory, mainly segment III, into the left hepatic vein before its junction with the IVC.
FJ3097.clinicalCondition: If the left hepatic vein is ligated without preserving this tributary, segment III becomes congested and may necrose.
FJ3097.clinicalScenario: During left hepatectomy the surgeon checks this tributary's drainage so the retained segment III keeps adequate venous outflow.

FJ3099.name: Lateral inferior segmental tributary of left hepatic vein
FJ3099.details: Lower radicle of the left hepatic vein system collecting blood from the lower lateral left lobe near the falciform ligament.
FJ3099.clinicalCondition: Injury during laparoscopic left lateral sectionectomy causes venous bleeding along the transection plane left of the falciform.
FJ3099.clinicalScenario: In a laparoscopic left lateral sectionectomy, oozing from this tributary is controlled with a vascular stapler along the transection line.

FJ3100.name: Lateral inferior segmental tributary of left hepatic vein
FJ3100.details: Small hepatic vein branch conveying segment III blood to the left hepatic vein trunk; tributaries like this vary in number between individuals.
FJ3100.clinicalCondition: Variant tributaries entering the middle hepatic vein instead can cause unexpected congestion after left-sided resections.
FJ3100.clinicalScenario: Preoperative imaging reveals this tributary drains into the middle hepatic vein, so the resection plan is adjusted to preserve outflow.

FJ3126.name: Lateral superior segmental branch of left portal vein
FJ3126.details: Branch of the left portal vein curving upward to supply segment II, the superior part of the left lateral section above the left portal fissure.
FJ3126.clinicalCondition: Portal branch embolization planning uses this branch to define how much left lobe will hypertrophy before major hepatectomy.
FJ3126.clinicalScenario: Before right portal vein embolization, volumetry confirms segment II, supplied by this branch, will form an adequate future remnant.

FJ3098.name: Lateral superior segmental tributary of left hepatic vein
FJ3098.details: Tributary draining segment II into the left hepatic vein, running in the left segmental fissure close to the diaphragm.
FJ3098.clinicalCondition: Preserved during segment II graft harvest in living-donor transplantation to guarantee graft venous outflow.
FJ3098.clinicalScenario: In a left lateral graft procurement, this tributary is carefully retained with the left hepatic vein cuff for implantation.

FJ2956.name: Left anterior basal segmental vein
FJ2956.details: Pulmonary vein tributary draining the anterior basal segment (S8) of the left lower lobe into the left inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2956.clinicalCondition: Mapped before basal segmentectomy; wrong division can congest the remaining basal segments of the lower lobe.
FJ2956.clinicalScenario: A patient with an S8 ground-glass nodule has this vein charted on 3D CT before anatomical basal segmentectomy.

FJ2957.name: Left anterior basal segmental vein
FJ2957.details: Collects blood from the front of the left lower lobe base and joins the common basal vein that forms the left inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2957.clinicalCondition: Intralobar pulmonary sequestration in the basal segments usually drains through basal pulmonary veins like this one to the left atrium.
FJ2957.clinicalScenario: CT in a young adult with recurrent basal pneumonia shows a sequestered segment whose venous drainage enters this pulmonary vein system.

FJ2959.name: Left anterior basal segmental vein
FJ2959.details: Basal tributary of the left inferior pulmonary vein serving segment S8, lying between the anterior basal bronchus and neighboring segmental veins.
FJ2959.clinicalCondition: Serves as an intersegmental landmark separating S8 from the lateral and posterior basal segments during resection.
FJ2959.clinicalScenario: During a left S8 segmentectomy, the surgeon follows this vein to keep the dissection in the correct intersegmental plane.

FJ2960.name: Left anterior basal segmental vein
FJ2960.details: Small venous radicle of the anterior basal segment of the left lower lobe, part of the basal venous trunk entering the left atrium.
FJ2960.clinicalCondition: Its ostial region can develop stenosis after atrial fibrillation ablation around the inferior pulmonary vein, causing segmental congestion.
FJ2960.clinicalScenario: Months after AF ablation, a patient has cough and a dense S8 opacity; imaging shows inferior pulmonary vein narrowing affecting this drainage.

FJ2213.name: Left anterior circumflex humeral vein
FJ2213.details: Vena comitans of the left anterior circumflex humeral artery, winding around the surgical neck of the humerus and draining into the axillary vein.
FJ2213.clinicalCondition: Torn in displaced surgical-neck humerus fractures and during shoulder arthroplasty, adding to fracture hematoma.
FJ2213.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman with a fractured surgical neck of humerus has extensive shoulder bruising partly from torn circumflex vessels.

FJ2930.name: Left anterior segmental vein
FJ2930.details: Tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein draining the anterior segment (S3) of the left upper lobe, running below the anterior segmental bronchus.
FJ2930.clinicalCondition: Must be identified in left upper lobectomy to avoid injuring the apicoposterior venous trunk while dividing it.
FJ2930.clinicalScenario: During VATS left upper lobectomy, the surgeon isolates this S3 tributary before stapling the upper division vein.

FJ2931.name: Left anterior segmental vein
FJ2931.details: Venous channel collecting blood from the front of the left upper lobe and joining the superior pulmonary vein near the lingular tributaries.
FJ2931.clinicalCondition: Shared drainage with the lingula is a common variant; dividing the wrong trunk in lobectomy congests the retained lingula.
FJ2931.clinicalScenario: Preoperative imaging shows this vein sharing a trunk with the lingular vein, so the lobectomy plan preserves lingular outflow.

FJ2932.name: Left anterior segmental vein
FJ2932.details: Segmental pulmonary vein of the left S3 segment, forming part of the venous map used for anatomical segmentectomy of the upper lobe.
FJ2932.clinicalCondition: Following this vein defines the plane between S3 and the lingular segments in anterior segmentectomy.
FJ2932.clinicalScenario: For a small S3 adenocarcinoma, the surgeon uses this vein as the guide for an anatomical anterior segmentectomy.

FJ2097.name: Left anterior tibial vein
FJ2097.details: Paired venae comitantes of the left anterior tibial artery, draining the anterior compartment of the leg and joining the posterior tibial veins to form the popliteal vein.
FJ2097.clinicalCondition: Anterior tibial vein thrombosis is an uncommon calf DVT site, often missed unless the whole calf is scanned.
FJ2097.clinicalScenario: A runner with persistent shin pain after a long flight has duplex evidence of thrombus in the left anterior tibial veins.

FJ2183.name: Left anterior tibial vein
FJ2183.details: Deep veins of the front of the left leg lying on the interosseous membrane with the anterior tibial artery and deep fibular nerve.
FJ2183.clinicalCondition: In anterior compartment syndrome these veins are compressed, worsening congestion and swelling within the tight fascial space.
FJ2183.clinicalScenario: After a tibial fracture, a patient develops a tense, painful anterior compartment; fasciotomy relieves pressure on muscles, nerve and these veins.

FJ2936.name: Left apical segmental vein
FJ2936.details: Tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein draining the apical segment (S1) of the left upper lobe, usually joining the apicoposterior trunk.
FJ2936.clinicalCondition: Variations of the left apical venous trunk are a leading cause of unexpected bleeding in left upper lobectomy.
FJ2936.clinicalScenario: Thorough preoperative CT mapping of this vein prevents a difficult hilar bleed during a left upper lobectomy for cancer.

FJ2947.name: Left apical segmental vein
FJ2947.details: Collects blood from the left lung apex and descends medially to enter the upper division of the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2947.clinicalCondition: Apical segment drainage must be preserved in apicoposterior segmentectomy to avoid congestion of the retained anterior segment.
FJ2947.clinicalScenario: In an S1+2 segmentectomy, the team preserves the anterior segment's outflow while dividing the apical tributaries.

FJ2958.name: Left apical segmental vein
FJ2958.details: Small pulmonary vein radicle of the left apex, part of the apicoposterior venous system above the left main bronchus.
FJ2958.clinicalCondition: Left apical veins lie close to apical pleural tumors; invasion can produce hemoptysis in superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumors.
FJ2958.clinicalScenario: A smoker with shoulder pain and Horner syndrome has an apical mass involving the pleura and apical vessels on MRI.

FJ2961.name: Left apical segmental vein
FJ2961.details: Venous drainage channel of the left apical segment running with the apical segmental bronchus toward the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2961.clinicalCondition: Apical tuberculosis cavities sit near these veins; erosion of adjacent vessels underlies Rasmussen-type bleeding in chronic TB.
FJ2961.clinicalScenario: A patient with old apical TB presents with hemoptysis; CT angiography localizes bleeding vessels around the scarred apex.

FJ2962.name: Left apical segmental vein
FJ2962.details: Upper-lobe tributary conveying apical blood to the left superior pulmonary vein, crossing near the aortic arch and left main bronchus.
FJ2962.clinicalCondition: Its relation to the aortic arch makes it vulnerable during mediastinal lymph node dissection in lung cancer surgery.
FJ2962.clinicalScenario: During systematic nodal dissection for left lung cancer, care is taken around the arch where this vein crosses.

FJ2963.name: Left apical segmental vein
FJ2963.details: One of several radicles forming the apicoposterior vein of the left upper lobe; segmental veins mark the borders between bronchopulmonary segments.
FJ2963.clinicalCondition: Used as the intersegmental boundary in apical segmentectomy, keeping the resection anatomical.
FJ2963.clinicalScenario: The surgeon follows this vein's course to separate the apical segment from the anterior segment during a left S1 resection.

FJ2964.name: Left apical segmental vein
