FJ2964.details: Drains the highest part of the left upper lobe into the superior pulmonary vein system; radicles converge behind the left subclavian vessels.
FJ2964.clinicalCondition: Central line or apical chest drain placement near the apex risks injuring these veins and causing hemothorax.
FJ2964.clinicalScenario: After a difficult apical drain insertion, a patient develops a hemothorax attributed to injury of an apical pulmonary vein radicle.

FJ3493.name: Left ascending lumbar vein
FJ3493.details: Vertical vein on the left connecting the common iliac and lumbar veins with the root of the hemiazygos vein; part of the vertebral venous pathway.
FJ3493.clinicalCondition: Dilates as a collateral in May–Thurner syndrome, where the right common iliac artery compresses the left common iliac vein.
FJ3493.clinicalScenario: A young woman with a swollen left leg has CT showing left iliac vein compression with prominent ascending lumbar collaterals.

FJ2217.name: Left axillary vein
FJ2217.details: Continuation of the basilic vein at the lower border of teres major; it runs through the axilla medial to the axillary artery and becomes the subclavian vein at the first rib.
FJ2217.clinicalCondition: Site for PICC and central access and pacemaker leads; thrombosis follows indwelling lines and produces arm swelling.
FJ2217.clinicalScenario: A patient with a left-sided pacemaker develops a swollen, aching arm; duplex confirms axillary vein thrombosis around the leads.

FJ2218.name: Left basilic vein
FJ2218.details: Superficial vein ascending the medial forearm and arm, piercing the deep fascia at mid-arm to join the brachial veins and form the axillary vein.
FJ2218.clinicalCondition: Preferred vein for PICC insertion because of its size and straight course into the axillary vein.
FJ2218.clinicalScenario: A patient needing six weeks of IV antibiotics has a PICC line placed through the left basilic vein under ultrasound guidance.

FJ3482.name: Left brachiocephalic vein
FJ3482.details: Formed behind the left sternoclavicular joint by the internal jugular and subclavian veins; it crosses the midline obliquely behind the manubrium to join the right brachiocephalic vein forming the SVC.
FJ3482.clinicalCondition: Its long transverse course makes left-sided central lines longer; compression by aortic aneurysm or tumor causes left arm and face swelling.
FJ3482.clinicalScenario: A dialysis patient's left internal jugular catheter functions poorly; imaging shows stenosis where the line traversed the left brachiocephalic vein.

FJ2220.name: Left cephalic vein
FJ2220.details: Superficial vein ascending the lateral forearm and arm, running in the deltopectoral groove and piercing the clavipectoral fascia to end in the axillary vein.
FJ2220.clinicalCondition: Used for pacemaker lead insertion by cephalic cutdown and for radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula creation in dialysis patients.
FJ2220.clinicalScenario: During pacemaker implantation, the cephalic vein in the deltopectoral groove proves too small, so the subclavian route is used instead.

FJ2222.name: Left circumflex scapular vein
FJ2222.details: Vena comitans of the circumflex scapular artery passing through the triangular space at the lateral scapular border to join the subscapular vein.
FJ2222.clinicalCondition: A landmark for the triangular space in posterior shoulder surgery; torn branches add to bleeding in scapular fractures.
FJ2222.clinicalScenario: In a posterior approach to a scapular neck fracture, the circumflex scapular vessels are identified and protected in the triangular space.

FJ3400.name: Left colic vein
FJ3400.details: Accompanies the left colic artery, draining the descending colon across the retroperitoneum into the inferior mesenteric vein.
FJ3400.clinicalCondition: Divided during left colectomy and splenic flexure mobilization; bleeding here can be troublesome near the pancreas and duodenojejunal flexure.
FJ3400.clinicalScenario: During laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy with flexure takedown, the left colic vessels are clipped close to the inferior mesenteric vein.

FJ3429.name: Left colic vein
FJ3429.details: Venous drainage of the descending colon that follows the marginal artery arcade before joining the inferior mesenteric vein.
FJ3429.clinicalCondition: Watershed ischemia at the splenic flexure (Griffiths point) involves this vein's territory when mesenteric flow fails.
FJ3429.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient in atrial fibrillation develops bloody stools; colonoscopy shows ischemic changes centered on the splenic flexure watershed.

FJ3495.name: Left colic vein
FJ3495.details: Hindgut tributary conveying blood from the descending colon to the inferior mesenteric vein and onward to the splenic and portal veins.
FJ3495.clinicalCondition: In portal hypertension this pathway can develop colonic varices, a rare cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
FJ3495.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic patient with recurrent hematochezia has colonoscopy showing descending colon varices fed through the inferior mesenteric and left colic veins.

FJ3465.name: Left common iliac vein
FJ3465.details: Formed at the left sacroiliac joint by the external and internal iliac veins; it ascends obliquely and passes beneath the right common iliac artery to join its fellow forming the IVC.
FJ3465.clinicalCondition: May–Thurner syndrome — compression under the right common iliac artery causes left iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis, often in young women.
FJ3465.clinicalScenario: A 28-year-old woman on contraceptive pills presents with a massively swollen left leg; venography confirms iliac compression with extensive thrombosis.

FJ2099.name: Left deep femoral vein
FJ2099.details: The vena comitans of the profunda femoris artery, draining the deep structures of the thigh and joining the femoral vein below the inguinal ligament.
FJ2099.clinicalCondition: Profunda vein thrombosis can be the sole site of proximal DVT and a source of pulmonary embolism.
FJ2099.clinicalScenario: A postoperative hip patient with thigh pain has duplex showing isolated thrombus in the deep femoral vein, prompting full anticoagulation.

FJ2229.name: Left deep palmar venous arch
FJ2229.details: Venous arch accompanying the deep palmar arterial arch in the left hand, draining into the radial and ulnar veins of the forearm.
FJ2229.clinicalCondition: Deep palmar space infections and crush injuries disrupt this arch; venous repair matters in major hand replantation.
FJ2229.clinicalScenario: After a crush injury to the left hand, surgeons restore deep venous outflow alongside the arterial repair to prevent congestion.

FJ3484.name: Left external iliac vein
FJ3484.details: Continuation of the femoral vein behind the inguinal ligament, running medial to the external iliac artery to the sacroiliac joint, where it joins the internal iliac vein.
FJ3484.clinicalCondition: Renal transplant grafts are anastomosed to this vein; injury or thrombosis here threatens graft drainage.
FJ3484.clinicalScenario: A transplant recipient develops graft dysfunction and leg swelling; imaging shows external iliac vein stenosis at the anastomosis.

FJ3522.name: Left external iliac vein
FJ3522.details: The main venous trunk of the left lower limb within the pelvis, receiving the inferior epigastric, deep circumflex iliac and pubic tributaries.
FJ3522.clinicalCondition: Iliofemoral DVT centered here produces severe whole-leg swelling and risks post-thrombotic syndrome.
FJ3522.clinicalScenario: A patient after pelvic surgery presents with a tense, painful, swollen left leg; CT venography shows external iliac vein thrombosis.

FJ3523.name: Left external iliac vein
FJ3523.details: Lies medial and slightly posterior to its artery behind the inguinal ligament, a relationship used in vascular and hernia surgery of the groin.
FJ3523.clinicalCondition: At risk during laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair and pelvic lymphadenectomy, where injury causes major venous hemorrhage.
FJ3523.clinicalScenario: During pelvic node dissection for prostate cancer, a tear in the external iliac vein is repaired with a vascular suture.

FJ3524.name: Left external iliac vein
FJ3524.details: Continuation of the limb's deep venous axis into the pelvis; its valves and caliber make it a conduit segment in venous bypass and patch repair.
FJ3524.clinicalCondition: External iliac vein compression by pelvic masses or lymphadenopathy causes unilateral leg edema mimicking DVT.
FJ3524.clinicalScenario: A woman with bulky lymphoma nodes has left leg swelling but no thrombus; compression of this vein explains the edema.

FJ2102.name: Left femoral vein
FJ2102.details: Continuation of the popliteal vein at the adductor hiatus; in the femoral triangle it lies medial to the femoral artery (nerve, artery, vein from lateral to medial) and ends behind the inguinal ligament.
FJ2102.clinicalCondition: Commonest site of lower-limb DVT and a standard route for emergency central access; catheterization risks thrombosis and pseudoaneurysm confusion.
FJ2102.clinicalScenario: In a shocked patient with no peripheral access, a femoral line is placed by palpating the artery and entering the vein just medial to it.

FJ2184.name: Left fibular vein
FJ2184.details: Paired venae comitantes of the fibular (peroneal) artery in the deep posterior compartment of the leg, joining the posterior tibial veins to form the tibioperoneal trunk.
FJ2184.clinicalCondition: Fibular vein thrombosis is a frequent calf DVT detected on whole-leg duplex scanning after surgery or immobility.
FJ2184.clinicalScenario: A patient with calf pain ten days after knee surgery has duplex evidence of thrombus confined to the left fibular veins.

FJ2187.name: Left fibular vein
FJ2187.details: Deep calf veins running with the fibular artery against the fibula beneath soleus, draining the lateral deep compartment of the leg.
FJ2187.clinicalCondition: These veins are divided with the fibular vessels in free fibula flap harvest, which must preserve leg perfusion through remaining vessels.
FJ2187.clinicalScenario: Reconstructive surgeons harvesting a fibula flap first confirm three-vessel leg runoff so division of the fibular vein and artery is safe.

FJ3500.name: Left gastric vein
FJ3500.details: The coronary vein of the stomach, running along the lesser curvature between the layers of the lesser omentum and draining into the portal vein.
FJ3500.clinicalCondition: In portal hypertension it reverses flow into esophageal veins, forming the esophageal varices that bleed catastrophically.
FJ3500.clinicalScenario: Endoscopy in a cirrhotic patient shows large varices supplied by the left gastric vein; they are treated with band ligation.

FJ3502.name: Left gastroepiploic vein
FJ3502.details: Runs along the greater curvature of the stomach in the greater omentum with the left gastroepiploic artery, draining the stomach and omentum into the splenic vein.
FJ3502.clinicalCondition: Divided during distal gastrectomy and omental resection; in portal hypertension it contributes to fundal gastric varices.
FJ3502.clinicalScenario: During a D2 distal gastrectomy for antral cancer, this vein is ligated at the greater curvature as the omentum is mobilized.

FJ2107.name: Left genicular vein
FJ2107.details: Small veins accompanying the genicular arteries around the left knee, draining the joint capsule and periarticular tissues into the popliteal vein.
FJ2107.clinicalCondition: Genicular venous bleeding contributes to hemarthrosis after knee arthroscopy and arthroplasty if small branches are not coagulated.
FJ2107.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a tense, painful knee swelling hours after arthroscopy; aspiration yields blood from periarticular venous bleeding.

FJ2108.name: Left genicular vein
FJ2108.details: Periarticular veins forming part of the venous plexus around the knee, which provides collateral drainage if the popliteal vein is obstructed.
FJ2108.clinicalCondition: This collateral plexus explains why popliteal vein ligation or thrombosis sometimes causes surprisingly little leg swelling.
FJ2108.clinicalScenario: A trauma patient with a ligated popliteal vein has only mild swelling because the genicular plexus provides collateral outflow.

FJ2124.name: Left genicular vein
FJ2124.details: Tributaries from the knee region that follow the superior and inferior genicular arteries and empty into the popliteal vein behind the knee.
FJ2124.clinicalCondition: Varicosities of the genicular plexus can mimic meniscal or joint pathology with aching around the knee.
FJ2124.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged woman with aching behind the knee and normal joint examination has duplex showing incompetent periarticular genicular veins.

FJ2125.name: Left genicular vein
FJ2125.details: Small deep veins of the left knee region connecting superficial periarticular networks with the popliteal vein.
FJ2125.clinicalCondition: Thrombus from calf veins can propagate through these tributaries into the popliteal vein, converting distal to proximal DVT.
FJ2125.clinicalScenario: Serial duplex scans show a calf thrombus extending via genicular tributaries into the popliteal vein, so anticoagulation is escalated.

FJ2103.name: Left great saphenous vein
FJ2103.details: The body's longest vein; it begins at the medial dorsal foot arch, passes in front of the medial malleolus, ascends the medial leg and thigh, and joins the femoral vein at the saphenofemoral junction.
FJ2103.clinicalCondition: Varicose veins from saphenofemoral incompetence; also the classic conduit harvested for coronary artery bypass grafting.
FJ2103.clinicalScenario: A patient with aching, tortuous medial leg varicosities has reflux demonstrated at the left saphenofemoral junction on duplex scanning.

FJ2415.name: Left hepatic vein
FJ2415.details: Drains the left lobe of the liver — segments II, III and part of IV — running in the left segmental fissure and entering the IVC just below the diaphragm, often with a common trunk with the middle hepatic vein.
FJ2415.clinicalCondition: Obstruction in Budd–Chiari produces left lobe congestion; its ostium is cannulated for hepatic venous pressure studies and TIPS planning.
FJ2415.clinicalScenario: During workup of unexplained ascites, hepatic venography through the left hepatic vein helps confirm Budd–Chiari physiology.

FJ3510.name: Left iliolumbar vein
FJ3510.details: Tributary accompanying the iliolumbar artery, draining the iliac fossa and lower lumbar region into the common iliac or internal iliac vein.
FJ3510.clinicalCondition: Notorious for bleeding during anterior L5–S1 spine exposure and sacroiliac surgery, where it tethers the common iliac vein.
FJ3510.clinicalScenario: In an anterior lumbar interbody fusion, the iliolumbar vein is ligated to mobilize the common iliac vein safely off the disc space.

FJ3512.name: Left inferior epigastric vein
FJ3512.details: Vena comitans of the inferior epigastric artery, ascending on the posterior surface of the rectus abdominis and draining into the external iliac vein.
FJ3512.clinicalCondition: Injured by lateral laparoscopic ports and hernia tacks, causing rectus sheath hematoma and abdominal wall bleeding.
FJ3512.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a painful abdominal wall swelling after laparoscopy; CT shows a rectus sheath hematoma from an inferior epigastric vessel injury.

FJ3513.name: Left inferior gluteal vein
FJ3513.details: Vena comitans of the inferior gluteal artery leaving the pelvis below piriformis, draining the gluteal region into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3513.clinicalCondition: Torn in pelvic and sacral fractures, contributing to concealed retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
FJ3513.clinicalScenario: A patient with an unstable pelvic fracture has ongoing transfusion needs partly from inferior gluteal and iliac venous bleeding.

FJ2944.name: Left inferior pulmonary vein
FJ2944.details: Short trunk draining the entire left lower lobe through the common basal and superior lower-lobe veins, entering the left atrium below the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2944.clinicalCondition: Must be divided in left lower lobectomy; accidental injury to its atrial junction causes major hemorrhage.
FJ2944.clinicalScenario: During left lower lobectomy the surgeon staples this vein at the pericardial reflection after confirming the superior vein is separate.

FJ2950.name: Left inferior pulmonary vein
FJ2950.details: Collects oxygenated blood from the left lower lobe segments and opens into the posteroinferior aspect of the left atrium.
FJ2950.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein stenosis after atrial fibrillation ablation narrows this ostium, causing dyspnea, cough and lobar congestion.
FJ2950.clinicalScenario: Six months after AF ablation, a patient has exertional dyspnea and left lower lobe opacities; CT shows severe inferior pulmonary vein stenosis.

FJ2955.name: Left inferior pulmonary vein
FJ2955.details: Its ostium lies close to the esophagus and descending aorta, a relationship exploited and endangered during posterior left atrial ablation.
FJ2955.clinicalCondition: Atrio-esophageal fistula is a rare, lethal ablation complication near this vein, presenting with fever and sepsis weeks later.
FJ2955.clinicalScenario: Three weeks after ablation, a patient presents with fever and chest pain; CT reveals an atrio-esophageal fistula requiring emergency surgery.

FJ3469.name: Left internal iliac vein
FJ3469.details: Formed by the union of pelvic visceral and parietal veins behind the internal iliac artery; it joins the external iliac vein at the sacroiliac joint to form the common iliac vein.
FJ3469.clinicalCondition: A major source of hemorrhage in pelvic fractures and radical pelvic surgery because of its thin wall and fixed tributaries.
FJ3469.clinicalScenario: During radical cystectomy, a torn internal iliac vein branch bleeds heavily and is controlled with clips and packing.

FJ3470.name: Left internal iliac vein
FJ3470.details: Drains the bladder, rectum and reproductive organ plexuses of the left pelvis through gluteal, pudendal and visceral tributaries.
FJ3470.clinicalCondition: Pelvic congestion syndrome — incompetent, dilated internal iliac tributaries cause chronic pelvic pain, worse on standing.
FJ3470.clinicalScenario: A multiparous woman with years of dull pelvic pain has imaging showing dilated left internal iliac and ovarian venous plexuses.

FJ3471.name: Left internal iliac vein
FJ3471.details: Lies medial to the internal iliac artery within the pelvis, receiving veins corresponding to the artery's branches.
FJ3471.clinicalCondition: Internal iliac vein ligation or embolization is used to control intractable pelvic bleeding when arterial methods fail.
FJ3471.clinicalScenario: After failed arterial embolization for post-hysterectomy bleeding, venous-phase intervention targets the internal iliac tributaries.

FJ3485.name: Left internal jugular vein
FJ3485.details: Continuation of the sigmoid sinus, descending in the carotid sheath lateral to the internal carotid artery and vagus nerve, joining the subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint.
FJ3485.clinicalCondition: Standard site for central venous and dialysis catheters; line infection and thrombosis are its chief complications, and Lemierre syndrome follows oropharyngeal sepsis.
FJ3485.clinicalScenario: A teenager recovering from severe tonsillitis develops neck pain, rigors and lung infiltrates — Lemierre syndrome with internal jugular thrombophlebitis.

FJ3525.name: Left internal pudendal vein
FJ3525.details: Vena comitans of the internal pudendal artery, leaving the perineum through the pudendal (Alcock) canal and draining into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3525.clinicalCondition: Perineal trauma can injure it, producing perineal hematoma; its tributaries dilate in pelvic congestion.
FJ3525.clinicalScenario: A cyclist with a straddle injury develops a spreading perineal hematoma from torn pudendal venous branches.

FJ2951.name: Left lateral basal segmental vein
FJ2951.details: Tributary draining the lateral basal segment (S9) of the left lower lobe into the common basal vein of the left inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2951.clinicalCondition: Mapped in basal segmentectomy to preserve drainage of neighboring anterior and posterior basal segments.
FJ2951.clinicalScenario: Before a left S9 segmentectomy for a benign nodule, 3D imaging charts this vein's junction with the basal trunk.

FJ2952.name: Left lateral basal segmental vein
FJ2952.details: Collects blood from the lateral basal segment of the left lower lobe, running with the lateral basal bronchus toward the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2952.clinicalCondition: Serves as the intersegmental landmark between S9 and the anterior and posterior basal segments during anatomical resection.
FJ2952.clinicalScenario: The surgeon follows this vein to develop the correct plane in a left lateral basal segmentectomy.

FJ2953.name: Left lateral basal segmental vein
FJ2953.details: Basal pulmonary vein radicle of segment S9 on the left, part of the venous drainage entering the left atrium via the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2953.clinicalCondition: Congestion of S9 follows if this radicle is mistakenly divided during posterior basal segmentectomy.
FJ2953.clinicalScenario: Imaging after an S10 resection shows a congested S9 because its lateral basal vein was inadvertently sacrificed.

FJ2954.name: Left lateral basal segmental vein
FJ2954.details: Small vein draining the left lateral basal segment, joining the common basal vein close to its entry into the left inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2954.clinicalCondition: Variant drainage directly into the superior basal vein alters segmentectomy planning and must be recognized on preoperative imaging.
FJ2954.clinicalScenario: A preoperative 3D reconstruction shows this vein joining the superior basal trunk, and the basal segmentectomy plan is modified accordingly.

FJ2188.name: Left lateral circumflex femoral vein
FJ2188.details: Vena comitans of the lateral circumflex femoral artery; drains the lateral thigh and hip region into the femoral or profunda femoris vein near the saphenofemoral junction.
FJ2188.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis — may propagate clot into the femoral vein causing iliofemoral DVT.
FJ2188.clinicalScenario: A 68-year-old man develops left thigh swelling after hip replacement; duplex ultrasound shows thrombus extending from this vein into the common femoral vein.

FJ3526.name: Left lateral sacral vein
FJ3526.details: Runs with the lateral sacral artery on the posterolateral pelvic wall, draining the sacral canal region into the internal iliac vein; communicates with the sacral venous plexus.
FJ3526.clinicalCondition: Presacral venous hemorrhage — thin-walled pelvic veins bleed torrentially and resist ligature during rectal surgery.
FJ3526.clinicalScenario: During a low anterior resection, a surgeon injuring presacral veins faces rapid blood loss and packs the pelvis to control bleeding.

FJ2233.name: Left lateral thoracic vein
FJ2233.details: Descends on the lateral chest wall with the long thoracic nerve on serratus anterior, draining intercostal spaces into the axillary vein.
FJ2233.clinicalCondition: Axillary vein thrombosis — obstruction produces lateral chest wall collateral veins and arm swelling.
FJ2233.clinicalScenario: A woman after axillary node clearance notices prominent veins over her left lateral chest wall, signaling collateral flow around a blocked axillary vein.

FJ2703.name: Left marginal vein
FJ2703.details: Cardiac vein running along the left (obtuse) margin of the heart with the marginal branch of the left circumflex artery, draining the left ventricular wall into the coronary sinus.
FJ2703.clinicalCondition: Coronary sinus thrombosis — rare occlusion may impair left ventricular venous drainage after device leads.
FJ2703.clinicalScenario: An electrophysiologist advancing a left ventricular pacing lead through the coronary sinus uses this vein's ostium as the target branch for cardiac resynchronization.

FJ2704.name: Left marginal vein
FJ2704.details: Courses over the obtuse border of the heart beside the left circumflex marginal artery branch, emptying into the coronary sinus or great cardiac vein.
FJ2704.clinicalCondition: Myocardial ischemia territory marker — its course identifies the lateral wall segment at risk in circumflex occlusion.
FJ2704.clinicalScenario: A cardiologist correlates a patient's lateral-wall ST elevation with the circumflex territory drained by this vein when planning angioplasty.

FJ2705.name: Left marginal vein
FJ2705.details: Small cardiac vein on the left border of the heart, accompanying the obtuse marginal artery, draining into the coronary sinus system.
FJ2705.clinicalCondition: Cardiac vein injury — may bleed during epicardial ablation or lead placement near the obtuse margin.
FJ2705.clinicalScenario: During epicardial ablation for ventricular tachycardia, a patient develops a small pericardial effusion after catheter trauma near this vein.

FJ2313.name: Left medial brachial vein
FJ2313.details: Deep vein of the medial arm accompanying the brachial artery (vena comitans), draining the arm's deep structures into the axillary vein.
FJ2313.clinicalCondition: Upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis — brachial vein clots can embolize, especially with indwelling catheters.
FJ2313.clinicalScenario: A patient with a PICC line in the left arm develops arm ache and swelling; ultrasound confirms brachial vein thrombosis around the catheter.

FJ2189.name: Left medial circumflex femoral vein
FJ2189.details: Vena comitans of the medial circumflex femoral artery; drains the medial thigh and hip adductor region into the profunda femoris or femoral vein.
FJ2189.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis — medial thigh vein clot may extend into the profunda and femoral veins.
FJ2189.clinicalScenario: A postpartum woman reports left groin and medial thigh pain; imaging shows thrombus in this vein extending toward the femoral confluence.

FJ2234.name: Left median antebrachial vein
FJ2234.details: Superficial vein ascending the midline front of the forearm from the palmar venous plexus, dividing near the elbow into median cephalic and median basilic branches.
FJ2234.clinicalCondition: Superficial thrombophlebitis — cannulation of this forearm vein can cause painful cord-like inflammation.
FJ2234.clinicalScenario: After a forearm IV infusion, a patient develops a tender red cord along the mid-forearm following the course of this vein.

FJ2235.name: Left median cubital vein
FJ2235.details: Large superficial vein crossing the cubital fossa obliquely, connecting cephalic to basilic vein; separated from the brachial artery and median nerve by the bicipital aponeurosis.
FJ2235.clinicalCondition: Venipuncture complications — hematoma or inadvertent arterial puncture if the bicipital aponeurosis protection is misjudged.
FJ2235.clinicalScenario: A phlebotomist chooses this vein for blood donation because it is large, well anchored, and overlies the protective bicipital aponeurosis.

FJ1988.name: Left musculophrenic vein
FJ1988.details: Accompanies the musculophrenic artery along the costal margin inside the thoracic cage, draining lower intercostal spaces and diaphragm into the internal thoracic vein.
FJ1988.clinicalCondition: Internal thoracic vein injury — bleeding may occur during costal margin or diaphragmatic surgery.
FJ1988.clinicalScenario: A trauma surgeon repairing a diaphragmatic rupture notes bleeding from veins along the costal margin requiring careful ligation.

FJ3527.name: Left obturator vein
FJ3527.details: Leaves the pelvis through the obturator canal with the obturator nerve and artery, draining the medial thigh and pelvic wall into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3527.clinicalCondition: Pelvic venous congestion — varicosities here contribute to chronic pelvic pain in multiparous women.
FJ3527.clinicalScenario: A woman with chronic dull pelvic pain worsened by standing has pelvic venography showing reflux through the obturator and internal iliac tributaries.

FJ2238.name: Left palmar metacarpal vein
FJ2238.details: Small deep vein in the palm accompanying the palmar metacarpal arteries, draining the deep palm into the deep palmar venous arch.
FJ2238.clinicalCondition: Hand compartment venous congestion — deep palmar swelling after crush injury may compromise these veins.
FJ2238.clinicalScenario: A factory worker with a crushed hand develops a tense, swollen palm; surgeons monitor for deep palmar compartment syndrome.

FJ2320.name: Left palmar metacarpal vein
FJ2320.details: Vena comitans within the palm running with palmar metacarpal vessels, linking the deep palmar arch to digital venous drainage.
FJ2320.clinicalCondition: Palmar hematoma — lacerations may injure these veins causing deep palm bleeding.
FJ2320.clinicalScenario: A glass laceration to the palm produces brisk deep bleeding controlled by pressure and later exploration of the palmar vessels.

FJ2323.name: Left palmar metacarpal vein
FJ2323.details: Deep palmar vein accompanying the metacarpal arteries between the interossei, contributing to the deep palmar venous arch drainage.
FJ2323.clinicalCondition: Deep hand infection spread — venous channels can carry infection between palmar spaces.
FJ2323.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a neglected palmar puncture wound develops a deep midpalmar space abscess requiring surgical drainage.

FJ2117.name: Left popliteal vein
FJ2117.details: Formed behind the knee by anterior and posterior tibial veins; lies between the popliteal artery (deep) and tibial nerve (superficial), becoming the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.
FJ2117.clinicalCondition: Popliteal deep vein thrombosis — classic source of pulmonary embolism and post-thrombotic syndrome.
FJ2117.clinicalScenario: A long-haul traveler presents with left calf pain and swelling; duplex confirms popliteal vein thrombosis, and anticoagulation is started immediately.

FJ1893.name: Left portal vein
FJ1893.details: Intrahepatic branch of the portal vein running leftward in the porta hepatis, supplying segments II, III and IV via lateral and medial segmental branches.
FJ1893.clinicalCondition: Left portal vein thrombosis — may cause segmental atrophy and complicate liver resection or transplant.
FJ1893.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic patient's CT shows thrombus in the left portal vein with atrophy of the left lobe and compensatory right lobe hypertrophy.

FJ2404.name: Left portal vein
FJ2404.details: Horizontal then vertical (pars transversa and umbilical part) division of the portal vein; the umbilical part gives branches to segments III and IV near the ligamentum teres.
FJ2404.clinicalCondition: Umbilical vein recanalization — in portal hypertension, paraumbilical collaterals reopen producing caput medusae.
FJ2404.clinicalScenario: A patient with advanced cirrhosis shows a recanalized paraumbilical vein on Doppler arising from the umbilical part of this vessel.

FJ2945.name: Left posterior basal segmental vein
FJ2945.details: Pulmonary vein tributary draining the posterior basal segment (S10) of the left lower lobe into the left inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2945.clinicalCondition: Segmental venous congestion — misidentification during segmentectomy can cause postoperative hemoptysis and congestion.
FJ2945.clinicalScenario: During a video-assisted left lower lobe segmentectomy, the surgeon carefully preserves this vein to avoid congesting the retained basal segments.

FJ2946.name: Left posterior basal segmental vein
FJ2946.details: Branch of the inferior pulmonary venous tree draining the posterior basal bronchopulmonary segment of the left lung toward the left atrium.
FJ2946.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein stenosis — narrowing after atrial fibrillation ablation can cause dyspnea and hemoptysis.
FJ2946.clinicalScenario: Months after pulmonary vein isolation, a patient develops breathlessness; CT shows stenosis of the left inferior pulmonary vein near this tributary's junction.

FJ2948.name: Left posterior basal segmental vein
FJ2948.details: Small tributary of the left inferior pulmonary vein collecting blood from the posterior basal segment, running below the lower lobe bronchus.
FJ2948.clinicalCondition: Hemoptysis localization — segmental bleeding may be traced to this segment's venous congestion.
FJ2948.clinicalScenario: A patient coughing blood has CT angiography localizing the abnormality to the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe.

FJ2949.name: Left posterior basal segmental vein
FJ2949.details: Venous radicle of the left lower lobe's posterior basal segment, joining sister tributaries to form part of the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2949.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark in basal segmentectomy — dividing the wrong tributary risks venous infarction of spared segments.
FJ2949.clinicalScenario: A thoracic surgeon uses preoperative 3D reconstruction to map this tributary before resecting a small nodule in the posterior basal segment.

FJ2926.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2926.details: Tributary draining the posterior segment (S2) of the left upper lobe, joining the left superior pulmonary vein via the common upper lobe venous trunk.
FJ2926.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein stenosis after ablation — upper lobe vein narrowing causes cough and pleuritic pain.
FJ2926.clinicalScenario: A patient post-ablation for atrial fibrillation develops a persistent cough; imaging shows narrowing of the left superior pulmonary vein near this tributary.

FJ2927.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2927.details: Vein accompanying the posterior segmental bronchus of the left upper lobe, draining oxygenated blood to the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2927.clinicalCondition: Lobar venous infarction — rare, follows torsion or mistaken ligation during lobectomy.
FJ2927.clinicalScenario: After left upper lobectomy a patient's retained lingula appears congested because a shared venous trunk was inadvertently ligated.

FJ2928.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2928.details: Upper-lobe pulmonary venous branch running with the posterior segmental artery and bronchus toward the hilum, entering the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2928.clinicalCondition: Preoperative mapping relevance — variant drainage patterns alter segmentectomy planes and margins.
FJ2928.clinicalScenario: A radiologist's 3D chest reconstruction maps this vein's course so the surgeon can plan an oncologically safe posterior segmentectomy.

FJ2929.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2929.details: Drains the posterior segment of the left upper lobe; joins the apicoposterior venous trunk before reaching the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2929.clinicalCondition: Segmental pulmonary edema — focal venous obstruction produces localized congestion mimicking pneumonia on imaging.
FJ2929.clinicalScenario: A patient's chest film shows a persistent posterior upper-lobe opacity later explained by venous congestion rather than infection.

FJ2939.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2939.details: Posterior segmental tributary of the left upper lobe venous system, coursing medially through the hilum alongside its segmental bronchus.
FJ2939.clinicalCondition: Hemoptysis workup landmark — segmental source identification guides bronchial artery embolization planning.
FJ2939.clinicalScenario: Bronchoscopy localizes bleeding to the posterior segment of the left upper lobe, and interventional radiology plans targeted embolization.

FJ2940.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2940.details: Small pulmonary vein branch from the posterior segment of the left upper lobe, tributary to the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2940.clinicalCondition: Anomalous venous drainage variation — occasionally drains separately, altering ablation lesion sets.
FJ2940.clinicalScenario: Pre-ablation CT reveals an extra venous ostium for this segment, so the electrophysiologist widens the encircling lesions accordingly.

FJ2941.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2941.details: Venous channel accompanying the posterior segmental bronchus and artery of the left upper lobe toward the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2941.clinicalCondition: Post-lobectomy venous congestion — accidental ligation can infarct remaining upper lobe tissue.
FJ2941.clinicalScenario: A surgeon double-checks the venous anatomy at the hilum before stapling to protect the lingular drainage during upper lobectomy.

FJ2942.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2942.details: Tributary within the left upper lobe collecting the posterior segment (S2), merging with apical and anterior segmental veins.
FJ2942.clinicalCondition: Segmental resection planning — its intersegmental course defines the plane between posterior and anterior segments.
FJ2942.clinicalScenario: During segmentectomy, the surgeon follows the intersegmental vein to separate the posterior segment from its neighbors accurately.

FJ2943.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2943.details: Pulmonary venous radicle of the left upper lobe posterior segment, running to the superior pulmonary vein ostium in the left atrium.
FJ2943.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein ostial stenosis — may present with exercise intolerance after catheter ablation.
FJ2943.clinicalScenario: A patient reports new exertional dyspnea after ablation; echocardiography suggests left superior pulmonary vein flow acceleration.

FJ2965.name: Left posterior segmental vein
FJ2965.details: One of the tributaries of the left superior pulmonary vein, draining the posterior segment of the upper lobe along its bronchovascular bundle.
FJ2965.clinicalCondition: Imaging pitfall — a prominent segmental vein can mimic a pulmonary nodule on axial CT slices.
FJ2965.clinicalScenario: A radiologist traces a suspected small nodule through consecutive slices and confirms it is this vein, avoiding an unnecessary biopsy.

FJ2118.name: Left posterior tibial vein
FJ2118.details: Paired venae comitantes of the posterior tibial artery in the deep calf, uniting with anterior tibial and peroneal veins to form the popliteal vein.
FJ2118.clinicalCondition: Calf deep vein thrombosis — isolated tibial vein clots may propagate proximally and embolize.
FJ2118.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient with calf tenderness has duplex showing thrombus in the paired posterior tibial veins, prompting anticoagulation.

FJ2244.name: Left radial vein
FJ2244.details: Paired venae comitantes of the radial artery in the lateral forearm, draining into the brachial veins near the elbow.
FJ2244.clinicalCondition: Deep forearm vein thrombosis — may follow radial artery cannulation or repetitive trauma.
FJ2244.clinicalScenario: After radial arterial line removal, a patient develops forearm swelling; ultrasound shows thrombosed radial venae comitantes.

FJ3477.name: Left renal vein
FJ3477.details: Long vein crossing between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery to reach the inferior vena cava; receives the left suprarenal and left testicular/ovarian veins.
FJ3477.clinicalCondition: Nutcracker syndrome — compression between aorta and SMA causes hematuria and flank pain.
FJ3477.clinicalScenario: A thin young woman with intermittent gross hematuria and left flank pain has CT showing a compressed left renal vein with hilar varices.

FJ3478.name: Left renal vein
FJ3478.details: Drains the left kidney, passing anterior to the aorta below the superior mesenteric artery origin; longer than the right renal vein.
FJ3478.clinicalCondition: Renal vein thrombosis — presents with flank pain, hematuria and worsening renal function, typically in nephrotic syndrome.
FJ3478.clinicalScenario: A patient with membranous nephropathy develops sudden left flank pain and rising creatinine; imaging confirms left renal vein thrombosis.

FJ2121.name: Left small saphenous vein
FJ2121.details: Superficial vein ascending the posterior calf from the lateral foot, piercing the deep fascia to join the popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa.
FJ2121.clinicalCondition: Varicose veins — saphenopopliteal junction incompetence causes posterior calf varicosities.
FJ2121.clinicalScenario: A hairdresser standing all day has aching posterior calf varicosities; duplex maps reflux at the saphenopopliteal junction for surgical planning.

FJ3486.name: Left subclavian vein
FJ3486.details: Continuation of the axillary vein from the first rib's outer border, passing anterior to scalenus anterior to join the internal jugular forming the brachiocephalic vein.
FJ3486.clinicalCondition: Effort thrombosis (Paget–Schroetter) — thoracic outlet compression clots the vein in young athletes.
FJ3486.clinicalScenario: A 22-year-old swimmer develops a swollen, dusky left arm after training; venography confirms subclavian vein thrombosis at the thoracic outlet.

FJ1987.name: Left subcostal vein
FJ1987.details: Runs below the twelfth rib with the subcostal nerve and artery, draining the upper abdominal wall into the ascending lumbar vein system.
FJ1987.clinicalCondition: Collateral pathway in IVC obstruction — enlarges as part of abdominal wall collateral drainage.
FJ1987.clinicalScenario: A patient with chronic inferior vena cava occlusion shows dilated subcostal and lumbar collateral veins on cross-sectional imaging.

FJ2247.name: Left subscapular vein
FJ2247.details: Formed by thoracodorsal and circumflex scapular veins, draining the posterior axilla and latissimus dorsi region into the axillary vein.
FJ2247.clinicalCondition: Axillary web syndrome association — venous and lymphatic disruption after axillary surgery causes cording.
FJ2247.clinicalScenario: After mastectomy with node clearance, a woman develops painful axillary cording and limited shoulder abduction treated with physiotherapy.

FJ3426.name: Left superficial dorsal vein of penis
FJ3426.details: Superficial penile vein in the dartos layer draining the skin and prepuce, typically toward the superficial external pudendal vein and saphenous system.
FJ3426.clinicalCondition: Penile Mondor disease — thrombophlebitis of the superficial dorsal vein causes a painful cord on the dorsum.
FJ3426.clinicalScenario: A man notices a firm, cord-like, tender ridge on the dorsal penis after vigorous intercourse; reassurance and NSAIDs resolve it.

FJ2122.name: Left superficial epigastric vein
FJ2122.details: Superficial vein of the lower anterior abdominal wall ascending from the groin to drain into the great saphenous vein near the saphenous opening.
FJ2122.clinicalCondition: Caput medusae collateral — enlarges in portal hypertension and IVC obstruction as a bypass channel.
FJ2122.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic patient shows dilated superficial epigastric veins radiating from the umbilicus as part of portosystemic collateral flow.

FJ2249.name: Left superficial palmar venous arch
FJ2249.details: Venous network in the superficial palm accompanying the superficial palmar arterial arch, draining digital veins toward the ulnar and radial veins.
FJ2249.clinicalCondition: Palmar venous thrombosis — rare, causes palmar pain and swelling after repetitive palmar trauma.
FJ2249.clinicalScenario: A carpenter striking tools against his palm develops palmar tenderness and swelling attributed to superficial palmar venous thrombosis.

FJ3530.name: Left superior epigastric vein
FJ3530.details: Descends within the rectus sheath accompanying the superior epigastric artery, draining the upper anterior abdominal wall into the internal thoracic vein.
FJ3530.clinicalCondition: Surgical bleeding risk — injured during rectus sheath or paramedian incisions and flap harvest.
FJ3530.clinicalScenario: During harvest of a rectus abdominis flap, the surgeon ligates the superior epigastric pedicle carefully to prevent rectus sheath hematoma.

FJ3531.name: Left superior gluteal vein
FJ3531.details: Vena comitans of the superior gluteal artery leaving the pelvis above piriformis through the greater sciatic foramen, draining into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3531.clinicalCondition: Pelvic fracture hemorrhage — gluteal veins contribute to life-threatening retroperitoneal bleeding.
FJ3531.clinicalScenario: A patient with an unstable pelvic fracture remains hypotensive; angiography identifies bleeding from superior gluteal vessels requiring embolization.

FJ1986.name: Left superior intercostal vein
FJ1986.details: Formed by the second, third and fourth left posterior intercostal veins, arching over the aortic arch to drain into the left brachiocephalic vein.
FJ1986.clinicalCondition: Radiographic landmark — its shadow forms the 'aortic nipple' beside the aortic knuckle on chest films.
FJ1986.clinicalScenario: A radiologist reassures that a small round density beside the aortic arch on a chest X-ray is this vein, not a lymph node.

FJ2925.name: Left superior pulmonary vein
FJ2925.details: Carries oxygenated blood from the left upper lobe and lingula to the left atrium, passing anterior and inferior to the left main bronchus.
FJ2925.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein stenosis — post-ablation narrowing causes dyspnea, cough and recurrent 'pneumonia'.
FJ2925.clinicalScenario: Six months after atrial fibrillation ablation, a patient has repeated left upper lobe infiltrates traced to superior pulmonary vein stenosis.

FJ2933.name: Left superior pulmonary vein
FJ2933.details: One of four pulmonary veins entering the left atrium; drains the apicoposterior, anterior and lingular segments of the left lung.
FJ2933.clinicalCondition: Anomalous ostium variation — common ostia alter catheter ablation strategy for atrial fibrillation.
FJ2933.clinicalScenario: Pre-procedure CT shows a common left pulmonary venous trunk, so the electrophysiologist plans a single wide encirclement lesion.

FJ3480.name: Left suprarenal vein
FJ3480.details: Short vein emerging from the left adrenal gland hilum, usually joined by the inferior phrenic vein, draining into the left renal vein.
FJ3480.clinicalCondition: Adrenal vein sampling landmark — catheterization lateralizes aldosterone in primary hyperaldosteronism workup.
FJ3480.clinicalScenario: An endocrinologist arranges adrenal vein sampling to decide whether a patient's primary aldosteronism comes from a unilateral adenoma.

FJ2250.name: Left suprascapular vein
FJ2250.details: Vena comitans of the suprascapular artery crossing the posterior triangle of the neck to drain into the external jugular or subclavian vein.
FJ2250.clinicalCondition: Neck surgery landmark — encountered during posterior triangle dissection and supraclavicular node biopsy.
FJ2250.clinicalScenario: During excision of a supraclavicular lymph node, the surgeon identifies and preserves the suprascapular vessels crossing the operative field.

FJ3533.name: Left testicular vein
FJ3533.details: Arises from the pampiniform plexus, ascends through the inguinal canal and retroperitoneum, draining at a right angle into the left renal vein.
FJ3533.clinicalCondition: Varicocele — left-sided predominance from the right-angle drainage and higher venous pressure.
FJ3533.clinicalScenario: A 17-year-old has a left scrotal 'bag of worms' swelling that disappears lying down, diagnosed as a varicocele.

FJ2254.name: Left thoracodorsal vein
FJ2254.details: Accompanies the thoracodorsal artery and nerve down the latissimus dorsi, draining the muscle and overlying skin into the subscapular vein.
FJ2254.clinicalCondition: Flap pedicle vein — its patency is critical when the latissimus dorsi flap reconstructs the breast.
FJ2254.clinicalScenario: A plastic surgeon confirms thoracodorsal pedicle flow before rotating a latissimus dorsi flap for post-mastectomy reconstruction.

FJ2260.name: Left ulnar vein
FJ2260.details: Paired venae comitantes of the ulnar artery in the medial forearm and hand, draining the deep palm and forearm into the brachial veins.
FJ2260.clinicalCondition: Hypothenar hammer syndrome association — ulnar artery and venae comitantes injured by repetitive palmar trauma.
FJ2260.clinicalScenario: A mechanic using his palm as a hammer develops ulnar-sided hand ischemia and pain from vascular injury at Guyon's canal.

FJ3631.name: Lumbar vein
FJ3631.details: Segmental veins accompanying the lumbar arteries, draining the posterior abdominal wall and vertebral plexuses into the inferior vena cava or ascending lumbar vein.
FJ3631.clinicalCondition: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage — lumbar veins may bleed after trauma or during posterior spinal surgery.
FJ3631.clinicalScenario: A patient becomes hypotensive after lumbar spine surgery; CT angiography reveals a lumbar vein injury with retroperitoneal hematoma.

FJ3635.name: Lumbar vein
FJ3635.details: Four paired veins running with the lumbar arteries below the corresponding transverse processes, linking the external vertebral plexus to the inferior vena cava.
FJ3635.clinicalCondition: Collateral in IVC occlusion — lumbar and ascending lumbar channels bypass caval obstruction via the azygos system.
FJ3635.clinicalScenario: Imaging in a patient with an IVC filter and chronic occlusion shows enlarged lumbar collateral veins draining upward.

FJ3128.name: Medial inferior segmental branch of left portal vein
FJ3128.details: Branch of the umbilical part of the left portal vein supplying the inferior portion of segment IV of the liver.
FJ3128.clinicalCondition: Segment IV hypoperfusion — tumor thrombus in this branch alters resection planning for hilar cholangiocarcinoma.
FJ3128.clinicalScenario: A hepatobiliary surgeon maps portal branches on CT before deciding whether a left hepatectomy can spare segment IV.

FJ3084.name: Medial inferior segmental tributary of middle hepatic vein
FJ3084.details: Small hepatic venous tributary from the medial/inferior parenchyma near the gallbladder fossa draining into the middle hepatic vein trunk.
FJ3084.clinicalCondition: Outflow congestion in liver grafts — middle hepatic tributary obstruction congests segment IV and V.
FJ3084.clinicalScenario: After living-donor liver transplant, Doppler shows poor flow in middle hepatic tributaries, and the team monitors for segmental congestion.

FJ3085.name: Medial inferior segmental tributary of middle hepatic vein
FJ3085.details: Hepatic vein radicle draining medial inferior liver tissue into the middle hepatic vein, part of the central venous outflow of the liver.
FJ3085.clinicalCondition: Budd–Chiari spectrum — hepatic venous outflow obstruction causes hepatomegaly, ascites and pain.
FJ3085.clinicalScenario: A young woman on oral contraceptives presents with painful hepatomegaly and ascites; imaging shows hepatic venous outflow thrombosis.

FJ3127.name: Medial superior segmental branch of left portal vein
FJ3127.details: Branch arising from the umbilical segment of the left portal vein to supply the superior part of segment IV (quadrate lobe region).
FJ3127.clinicalCondition: Portal vein embolization planning — branch anatomy decides which segments hypertrophy before major hepatectomy.
FJ3127.clinicalScenario: Before an extended right hepatectomy, interventional radiology reviews segment IV portal branches to predict remnant liver growth.

FJ3101.name: Medial superior segmental tributary of left hepatic vein
FJ3101.details: Tributary draining the medial superior liver parenchyma (segment IV/II border region) into the left hepatic vein before it joins the inferior vena cava.
FJ3101.clinicalCondition: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction — left hepatic vein involvement impairs left lobe drainage.
FJ3101.clinicalScenario: A patient's ultrasound in suspected Budd–Chiari syndrome focuses on left hepatic vein patency and collateral formation.

FJ3541.name: Median sacral vein
FJ3541.details: Midline vein accompanying the median sacral artery on the anterior sacrum, draining into the common iliac confluence or left common iliac vein.
FJ3541.clinicalCondition: Presacral bleeding — midline sacral veins are injured during rectal mobilization and sacral surgery.
FJ3541.clinicalScenario: During abdominoperineal resection, brisk presacral bleeding from the median sacral region is controlled with packing and bone wax techniques.

FJ2678.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2678.details: Runs in the posterior interventricular sulcus with the posterior descending artery, draining the posterior septum and both ventricles into the coronary sinus near its atrial opening.
FJ2678.clinicalCondition: Coronary sinus ostial landmark — its opening guides cannulation for retrograde cardioplegia delivery.
FJ2678.clinicalScenario: A cardiac surgeon places a retrograde cardioplegia catheter in the coronary sinus, confirming position just beyond this vein's opening.

FJ2679.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2679.details: Posterior interventricular vein ascending from the cardiac apex beside the posterior descending artery to empty into the coronary sinus.
FJ2679.clinicalCondition: Myocardial territory marker — drains the inferior wall supplied by the posterior descending artery.
FJ2679.clinicalScenario: An inferior myocardial infarction patient has angiography correlating the posterior descending territory with this vein's drainage field.

FJ2680.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2680.details: Cardiac vein in the posterior interventricular groove collecting blood from the posterior third of the interventricular septum and adjacent ventricular walls.
FJ2680.clinicalCondition: Lead placement route — occasionally used for left ventricular pacing lead delivery via the coronary sinus.
FJ2680.clinicalScenario: When the lateral branch is unsuitable, an implanter advances a pacing lead into this vein to achieve resynchronization.

FJ2681.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2681.details: Accompanies the posterior interventricular artery on the diaphragmatic surface of the heart, terminating in the coronary sinus close to the right atrium.
FJ2681.clinicalCondition: Coronary venous injury — trauma or catheter manipulation may cause venous perforation and effusion.
FJ2681.clinicalScenario: A patient develops a small pericardial effusion after difficult coronary sinus catheterization near this vein's ostium.

FJ2682.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2682.details: Posterior cardiac vein whose valve may guard its junction with the coronary sinus; drains the inferior surfaces of both ventricles.
FJ2682.clinicalCondition: Arrhythmia ablation access — used to reach epicardial substrates near the posterior septum.
FJ2682.clinicalScenario: An electrophysiologist maps a ventricular arrhythmia focus through this vein when endocardial ablation fails.

FJ2683.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2683.details: Runs from the apex in the posterior interventricular sulcus, parallel to the posterior descending artery, into the coronary sinus.
FJ2683.clinicalCondition: Venous drainage compromise — occlusion may worsen inferior wall congestion in right ventricular infarction.
FJ2683.clinicalScenario: In a right ventricular infarct, the team avoids excessive fluids partly to limit venous congestion of the inferior myocardium.

FJ2684.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2684.details: Diaphragmatic-surface cardiac vein collecting tributaries from the posterior septum and inferior left ventricular wall before joining the coronary sinus.
FJ2684.clinicalCondition: Imaging landmark — identifies the posterior interventricular sulcus on CT coronary venography.
FJ2684.clinicalScenario: A radiologist uses this vein's course to orient the posterior descending artery territory on a cardiac CT report.

FJ2685.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2685.details: Cardiac vein accompanying the posterior descending artery; part of the coronary sinus system returning myocardial blood to the right atrium.
FJ2685.clinicalCondition: Coronary sinus thrombosis — extension into this vein may follow indwelling coronary sinus catheters.
FJ2685.clinicalScenario: After prolonged coronary sinus instrumentation, a patient has imaging showing thrombus extending from the sinus into this vein.

FJ2686.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2686.details: Posterior interventricular vein lying beside the posterior descending branch, usually of the right coronary artery, draining to the coronary sinus.
FJ2686.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark in CABG — its parallel artery is a frequent bypass graft target.
FJ2686.clinicalScenario: A surgeon grafts the posterior descending artery, identifying it by its position beside this vein in the posterior sulcus.

FJ2687.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2687.details: Vein of the diaphragmatic cardiac surface ascending in the posterior interventricular groove, tributary to the coronary sinus near the crux.
FJ2687.clinicalCondition: Crux region procedures — proximity matters during ablation near the coronary sinus ostium.
FJ2687.clinicalScenario: During ablation for atrial flutter, catheter positions near the cavotricuspid isthmus are checked against coronary venous anatomy.

FJ2688.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2688.details: Collects blood from the posterior interventricular septum and both ventricles, running with the posterior descending artery to the coronary sinus.
FJ2688.clinicalCondition: Myocardial venous congestion — may accompany severe right heart failure with hepatic and cardiac congestion.
FJ2688.clinicalScenario: A patient with decompensated right heart failure shows dilated cardiac veins, including this one, on echocardiographic imaging.

FJ2689.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2689.details: Posterior cardiac vein beginning at the apex, following the posterior interventricular sulcus upward to drain into the coronary sinus.
FJ2689.clinicalCondition: Variant drainage — occasionally opens directly into the right atrium, altering catheter courses.
FJ2689.clinicalScenario: A venogram during device implantation shows this vein draining directly to the atrium, so the operator adjusts the approach.

FJ2690.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2690.details: Tributary of the coronary sinus running with the posterior interventricular artery, draining inferior myocardium of both ventricles.
FJ2690.clinicalCondition: Alcohol septal ablation planning — venous anatomy is mapped alongside septal arterial branches.
FJ2690.clinicalScenario: Before treating hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the team maps septal vessels and adjacent venous drainage to avoid complications.

FJ2691.name: Middle cardiac vein
FJ2691.details: Cardiac vein in the posterior interventricular sulcus, the principal drainage of the posterior septum, ending in the coronary sinus.
FJ2691.clinicalCondition: Posterior septal accessory pathway ablation — this vein helps localize epicardial pathways.
FJ2691.clinicalScenario: A patient with Wolff–Parkinson–White syndrome has a pathway localized near this vein's ostium and ablated successfully.

FJ3543.name: Middle colic vein
FJ3543.details: Follows the middle colic artery in the transverse mesocolon, draining the transverse colon into the superior mesenteric vein.
FJ3543.clinicalCondition: Mesenteric venous thrombosis — clot here causes transverse colon ischemia and abdominal pain.
FJ3543.clinicalScenario: A patient with a clotting disorder and severe central abdominal pain has CT showing superior mesenteric and middle colic vein thrombosis.

FJ2414.name: Middle hepatic vein
FJ2414.details: Runs in the main lobar fissure between right and left lobes, draining segments IV, V and VIII into the inferior vena cava; shared trunk with left hepatic vein is common.
FJ2414.clinicalCondition: Budd–Chiari syndrome — middle hepatic vein thrombosis causes painful hepatomegaly and ascites.
FJ2414.clinicalScenario: A transplant surgeon preserves this vein's tributaries during right-lobe living donation to prevent graft segment congestion.

FJ3545.name: Pancreaticoduodenal vein
FJ3545.details: Veins accompanying the pancreaticoduodenal arcades around the pancreatic head and duodenum, draining into the portal and superior mesenteric veins.
FJ3545.clinicalCondition: Portal hypertension collaterals — these veins enlarge and may bleed during pancreatic surgery.
FJ3545.clinicalScenario: During a Whipple procedure in a patient with chronic pancreatitis, enlarged pancreaticoduodenal collateral veins complicate dissection around the portal vein.

FJ3646.name: Pancreaticoduodenal vein
FJ3646.details: Anterior and posterior arcades drain the head of pancreas and second part of duodenum toward the portal venous system.
FJ3646.clinicalCondition: Duodenal varices — ectopic varices may form here in extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
FJ3646.clinicalScenario: A patient with portal vein thrombosis presents with melena from bleeding duodenal varices supplied by these collateral veins.

FJ3655.name: Pancreaticoduodenal vein
FJ3655.details: Small veins following the pancreaticoduodenal arteries between the superior mesenteric and gastroduodenal systems, linking mesenteric and portal drainage.
FJ3655.clinicalCondition: Pancreatic head tumor involvement — venous encasement signals unresectability in pancreatic cancer staging.
FJ3655.clinicalScenario: A staging CT shows tumor abutting the portal confluence near these veins, and the tumor board deems the cancer borderline resectable.

FJ2191.name: Plantar metatarsal vein
FJ2191.details: Deep veins of the sole accompanying the plantar metatarsal arteries, draining the forefoot into the plantar venous arch.
FJ2191.clinicalCondition: Foot venous pump failure — impaired plantar drainage contributes to dependent edema and venous ulceration.
FJ2191.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with chronic foot swelling is advised on elevation and compression to support the plantar venous pump.

FJ2207.name: Plantar metatarsal vein
FJ2207.details: Venae comitantes in the sole running between the metatarsals with the plantar metatarsal arteries, connecting digital veins to the plantar arch.
FJ2207.clinicalCondition: Plantar vein thrombosis — rare cause of acute sole pain mimicking plantar fasciitis.
FJ2207.clinicalScenario: A runner with sudden sharp arch pain has MRI showing thrombosis of a plantar vein rather than fascial injury.

FJ2128.name: Plantar venous arch of left foot
FJ2128.details: Deep venous arch in the sole accompanying the lateral plantar artery's arch, receiving metatarsal veins and draining into the posterior tibial venae comitantes.
FJ2128.clinicalCondition: Venous pump reservoir — weight-bearing empties this arch, driving calf muscle pump return.
FJ2128.clinicalScenario: A physiotherapist teaches ankle-pump exercises after ankle surgery to empty the plantar arch and reduce thromboembolism risk.

FJ2129.name: Plantar venous arch of right foot
FJ2129.details: Deep plantar venous arch of the right sole, accompanying the plantar arterial arch and emptying through medial and lateral plantar veins.
FJ2129.clinicalCondition: Plantar vein thrombosis — presents with sole pain and forefoot swelling after long standing or travel.
FJ2129.clinicalScenario: After a long flight, a man develops right sole pain; ultrasound demonstrates thrombus in the plantar venous system.

FJ3111.name: Posterior inferior segmental branch of right portal vein
FJ3111.details: Branch of the right posterior sectoral portal pedicle supplying segment VI of the liver, arising near the right portal bifurcation.
FJ3111.clinicalCondition: Segment VI tumor supply — branch anatomy guides anatomical segmentectomy and ablation targeting.
FJ3111.clinicalScenario: A surgeon uses intraoperative ultrasound to identify this branch before performing an anatomical segment VI resection for metastasis.

FJ3118.name: Posterior inferior segmental tributary of right hepatic vein
FJ3118.details: Tributary draining the posterior inferior right lobe (segment VI region) into the right hepatic vein outflow.
FJ3118.clinicalCondition: Segmental outflow block — obstruction congests segment VI, seen in hepatic venous outflow obstruction.
FJ3118.clinicalScenario: Cross-sectional imaging in suspected Budd–Chiari syndrome shows a congested, poorly enhancing segment VI of the liver.

FJ3120.name: Posterior inferior segmental tributary of right hepatic vein
FJ3120.details: Hepatic venous radicle from the right posteroinferior parenchyma joining the right hepatic vein before the inferior vena cava.
FJ3120.clinicalCondition: Living-donor graft outflow — right hepatic vein tributaries must be reconstructed to avoid graft congestion.
FJ3120.clinicalScenario: A transplant team plans reconstruction of a large segment VI tributary to secure outflow in a right-lobe graft.

FJ3037.name: Posterior part of lateral segmental vein
FJ3037.details: Pulmonary venous component draining part of the lateral (lingular/lateral segmental) territory toward the superior pulmonary vein system.
FJ3037.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy landmark — venous branches mark intersegmental planes in the left upper lobe.
FJ3037.clinicalScenario: A thoracic surgeon preserves the intersegmental vein while resecting a lingular nodule to keep a clear anatomical plane.

FJ3038.name: Posterior part of lateral segmental vein
FJ3038.details: Tributary of the left pulmonary venous tree collecting the posterior division of the lateral segmental region near the hilum.
FJ3038.clinicalCondition: Variant drainage — unusual patterns are mapped preoperatively to avoid accidental venous ligation.
FJ3038.clinicalScenario: Preoperative CT venography reveals this tributary's variant course, and the segmentectomy plan is adjusted accordingly.

FJ3039.name: Posterior part of lateral segmental vein
FJ3039.details: Small pulmonary vein branch accompanying segmental bronchi, contributing oxygenated return to the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3039.clinicalCondition: Focal venous stenosis — post-ablation narrowing may cause segmental congestion and cough.
FJ3039.clinicalScenario: A patient with post-ablation cough has CT showing a narrowed left superior pulmonary vein branch with segmental congestion.

FJ3112.name: Posterior superior segmental branch of right portal vein
FJ3112.details: Portal branch supplying segment VII, arising from the right posterior sectoral branch and coursing posterosuperiorly in the right lobe.
FJ3112.clinicalCondition: Posterior sector portal vein tumor thrombus — spread here affects resectability of hepatocellular carcinoma.
FJ3112.clinicalScenario: MRI in a hepatitis B patient shows enhancing tumor thrombus extending into the segment VII portal branch.

FJ3113.name: Posterior superior segmental branch of right portal vein
FJ3113.details: Segment VII portal venous branch from the posterior division of the right portal vein, paired with its segmental bile duct and artery.
FJ3113.clinicalCondition: Transarterial therapy targeting — branch mapping guides selective embolization of segment VII tumors.
FJ3113.clinicalScenario: An interventional radiologist catheterizes this branch's arterial counterpart region to deliver chemoembolization to a segment VII tumor.

FJ3119.name: Posterior superior segmental tributary of right hepatic vein
FJ3119.details: Hepatic venous tributary draining segment VII into the right hepatic vein, part of the right lobe's superior outflow.
FJ3119.clinicalCondition: Outflow obstruction signs — segment VII congestion appears as heterogeneous enhancement on imaging.
FJ3119.clinicalScenario: A radiologist notes a congested segment VII pattern while reporting imaging for suspected hepatic venous outflow obstruction.

FJ2701.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2701.details: Cardiac vein ascending on the posterior (diaphragmatic) surface of the left ventricle, draining into the coronary sinus, sometimes joining the middle cardiac vein region.
FJ2701.clinicalCondition: CRT lead target — this branch is used for left ventricular pacing when lateral branches are unsuitable.
FJ2701.clinicalScenario: An implanter places a left ventricular lead in this posterior branch after phrenic nerve stimulation rules out the lateral vein.

FJ2702.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2702.details: Tributary of the coronary sinus draining the posterior wall of the left ventricle, running parallel to posterolateral arterial branches.
FJ2702.clinicalCondition: Venous branch stenosis — may limit lead advancement during cardiac resynchronization therapy.
FJ2702.clinicalScenario: During CRT implantation, contrast venography shows a tight bend in this vein, prompting selection of an alternative branch.

FJ2706.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2706.details: Posterior left ventricular vein collecting blood from the diaphragmatic surface of the ventricle into the coronary sinus system.
FJ2706.clinicalCondition: Epicardial mapping access — catheter position here overlies posterobasal arrhythmia substrates.
FJ2706.clinicalScenario: An electrophysiologist maps early activation for a ventricular tachycardia from within this vein overlying the posterior left ventricle.

FJ2707.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2707.details: Cardiac vein on the posterior left ventricular surface, draining toward the coronary sinus near the crux of the heart.
FJ2707.clinicalCondition: Coronary venous dissection — forceful contrast injection during venography can dissect this branch.
FJ2707.clinicalScenario: A device implant is complicated by a small venous dissection in this branch, managed conservatively without effusion.

FJ2708.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2708.details: One of several coronary sinus tributaries serving the posterior left ventricle, accompanying posterolateral branches of the circumflex or right coronary artery.
FJ2708.clinicalCondition: Myocardial venous drainage assessment — relevant when planning retrograde perfusion strategies in surgery.
FJ2708.clinicalScenario: A surgical team reviews coronary venous anatomy before using retrograde cardioplegia in a patient with severe left main disease.

FJ2709.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2709.details: Posterior ventricular venous branch running upward on the diaphragmatic surface to enter the coronary sinus.
FJ2709.clinicalCondition: Phrenic nerve capture check — pacing near posterior branches requires threshold testing for diaphragmatic stimulation.
FJ2709.clinicalScenario: After lead placement in this vein, diaphragmatic twitching at high output leads the operator to reposition the lead.

FJ2710.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2710.details: Coronary sinus tributary draining the posterobasal left ventricle, lying in the fat of the posterior atrioventricular groove region.
FJ2710.clinicalCondition: Accessory pathway localization — posteroseptal pathways are mapped near its ostium.
FJ2710.clinicalScenario: A supraventricular tachycardia is localized to a posteroseptal pathway adjacent to the coronary sinus tributaries and ablated.

FJ2711.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2711.details: Vein coursing over the posterior left ventricular wall, returning myocardial blood to the coronary sinus and right atrium.
FJ2711.clinicalCondition: Venous varix mimic — a prominent branch can be mistaken for a coronary artery aneurysm on angiography.
FJ2711.clinicalScenario: A cardiologist confirms by delayed-phase imaging that a rounded vascular blush is this vein rather than an arterial lesion.

FJ2712.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2712.details: Posterior surface cardiac vein, frequently multiple, draining the left ventricle's diaphragmatic wall into the coronary sinus.
FJ2712.clinicalCondition: Lead stability site — its caliber and angle determine suitability for chronic pacing leads.
FJ2712.clinicalScenario: Pre-implant venography shows this vein is too small, so the operator chooses the lateral marginal branch instead.

FJ2713.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
FJ2713.details: Tributary accompanying posterolateral arterial twigs on the back of the left ventricle, emptying into the coronary sinus.
FJ2713.clinicalCondition: Perforation risk — thin-walled cardiac veins may perforate during aggressive lead manipulation.
FJ2713.clinicalScenario: A patient develops chest pain after CRT implant; imaging excludes perforation of this vein and shows only a trivial effusion.

FJ3082.name: Pre-hepatic portal vein
FJ3082.details: Extrahepatic segment of the portal vein formed behind the pancreatic neck by splenic and superior mesenteric vein union, carrying gut blood to the liver.
FJ3082.clinicalCondition: Extrahepatic portal vein obstruction — causes portal hypertension with splenomegaly and varices, often in children.
FJ3082.clinicalScenario: A child with massive splenomegaly and variceal bleeding has Doppler showing cavernous transformation at the blocked portal vein.

FJ2324.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left index finger
FJ2324.details: Small vein running along the palmar side of the left index finger beside the proper palmar digital artery and nerve, draining into palmar metacarpal veins.
FJ2324.clinicalCondition: Digital vein thrombosis — rare painful blue nodule on the finger's palmar aspect.
FJ2324.clinicalScenario: A woman finds a tender bluish lump on her index finger; ultrasound shows a thrombosed palmar digital vein, managed conservatively.

FJ2325.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left index finger
FJ2325.details: Paired venae comitantes flanking the digital neurovascular bundle of the left index finger within the fibrous flexor sheath region.
FJ2325.clinicalCondition: Finger laceration bleeding — digital veins bleed steadily and aid assessment of digital perfusion.
FJ2325.clinicalScenario: A deep knife cut to the index finger is assessed; good venous bleeding and capillary refill reassure the team about viability.

FJ2319.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left little finger
FJ2319.details: Palmar digital vein of the left fifth digit, accompanying the ulnar-sided digital artery and nerve to the palmar venous arches.
FJ2319.clinicalCondition: Ring avulsion injury — venous congestion is the earliest sign of a compromised digit.
FJ2319.clinicalScenario: After a ring avulsion, the little finger looks dusky and swollen; surgeons prioritize restoring venous outflow during repair.

FJ2321.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left little finger
FJ2321.details: Small vein on the palmar aspect of the left little finger, draining toward the superficial palmar venous arch.
FJ2321.clinicalCondition: Digital replantation — venous anastomosis of such veins is essential to prevent congestion failure.
FJ2321.clinicalScenario: In a replanted little finger, the microsurgeon anastomoses two digital veins to secure drainage and graft survival.

FJ2329.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left little finger
FJ2329.details: Vena comitans within the left fifth finger's neurovascular bundle, protected by the palmar skin and fibrous septa.
FJ2329.clinicalCondition: Flexor sheath infection spread — venous channels accompany infection tracking into the ulnar bursa.
FJ2329.clinicalScenario: A puncture wound of the little finger leads to infection spreading along the sheath into the ulnar bursa (horseshoe abscess risk).

FJ2326.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left middle finger
FJ2326.details: Palmar digital vein of the left third digit running with its digital artery and nerve, draining into the palmar metacarpal system.
FJ2326.clinicalCondition: Digital vein thrombosis — spontaneous painful nodule, classically on the palmar middle finger of women.
FJ2326.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged woman presents with a sudden painful blue spot on her middle finger diagnosed as palmar digital vein thrombosis.

FJ2340.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left middle finger
FJ2340.details: One of paired venae comitantes in the left middle finger, lying palmar to the phalanges within Cleland and Grayson ligament framework.
FJ2340.clinicalCondition: Crush injury assessment — venous outflow determines whether a crushed fingertip remains viable.
FJ2340.clinicalScenario: A door-crush injury to a child's middle finger is monitored; pink color and brisk refill indicate intact venous drainage.

FJ2327.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left ring finger
FJ2327.details: Palmar digital vein of the left fourth digit accompanying the digital neurovascular bundle toward the palmar arches.
FJ2327.clinicalCondition: Ring constriction injury — a tight ring obstructs these veins first, causing distal swelling.
FJ2327.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman with a swollen ring finger has the ring cut off urgently to relieve venous congestion before arterial compromise.

FJ2328.name: Proper palmar digital vein of left ring finger
FJ2328.details: Small vein along the palmar left ring finger beside the proper palmar digital artery, part of the finger's venous return.
FJ2328.clinicalCondition: Digital laceration repair — venous integrity checked after tendon and nerve repair in zone injuries.
FJ2328.clinicalScenario: After flexor tendon repair in the ring finger, the surgeon confirms the digit is pink with good venous return.

FJ2354.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right index finger
FJ2354.details: Palmar digital vein of the right index finger running with the digital artery and nerve, draining into palmar metacarpal veins.
FJ2354.clinicalCondition: Digital vein thrombosis — tender blue nodule on the palmar finger, benign and self-limiting.
FJ2354.clinicalScenario: A typist notices a sore bluish pea-sized lump on her right index finger, reassured after diagnosis of digital vein thrombosis.

FJ2355.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right index finger
FJ2355.details: Vena comitans of the right index finger's neurovascular bundle, returning blood from the fingertip pulp to the palm.
FJ2355.clinicalCondition: Fingertip pulp infection (felon) — venous congestion worsens pressure pain in the closed pulp space.
FJ2355.clinicalScenario: A man with a throbbing fingertip felon undergoes drainage; venous congestion had intensified the tense pulp swelling.

FJ2349.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right little finger
FJ2349.details: Palmar digital vein of the right fifth digit accompanying the ulnar digital vessels, draining to the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2349.clinicalCondition: Venous congestion after replantation — the commonest early complication threatening the replanted digit.
FJ2349.clinicalScenario: A replanted right little finger turns purple overnight; leech therapy relieves venous congestion while outflow matures.

FJ2351.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right little finger
FJ2351.details: Small vein within the right little finger's palmar neurovascular bundle, protected beneath the palmar aponeurotic septa.
FJ2351.clinicalCondition: Digital artery/vein injury — associated with nerve injury in penetrating little finger wounds.
FJ2351.clinicalScenario: A glass injury to the right little finger causes numbness and bleeding; exploration repairs the nerve and digital vessels.

FJ2360.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right little finger
FJ2360.details: Palmar venous channel of the right fifth digit joining sister digital veins at the web space toward the palmar arches.
FJ2360.clinicalCondition: Web space infection — may spread along venous and fascial planes between digits.
FJ2360.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a neglected web-space wound develops spreading hand infection requiring drainage and antibiotics.

FJ2356.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right middle finger
FJ2356.details: Palmar digital vein of the right middle finger running beside its digital artery and nerve into the palmar metacarpal veins.
FJ2356.clinicalCondition: Digital vein thrombosis — classic spontaneous palmar nodule of the middle finger.
FJ2356.clinicalScenario: A woman reports a sudden painful blue nodule on her right middle finger; examination confirms palmar digital vein thrombosis.

FJ2357.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right middle finger
FJ2357.details: Paired vena comitans in the right middle finger, lying within the fibrous flexor sheath's lateral gutters.
FJ2357.clinicalCondition: Trigger finger surgery caution — digital veins lie close to the A1 pulley release field.
FJ2357.clinicalScenario: During trigger finger release, the surgeon protects the neurovascular bundles lying just radial and ulnar to the sheath.
