FJ2358.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right ring finger
FJ2358.details: Palmar digital vein of the right fourth digit accompanying the digital neurovascular bundle toward the superficial palmar arch.
FJ2358.clinicalCondition: Ring avulsion (Urbaniak class) — venous-only injury can still salvage the digit if repaired promptly.
FJ2358.clinicalScenario: A worker's ring finger is avulsed by machinery; microsurgical venous repair restores outflow and saves the finger.

FJ2359.name: Proper palmar digital vein of right ring finger
FJ2359.details: Small palmar vein of the right ring finger, one of the venae comitantes of the proper palmar digital artery.
FJ2359.clinicalCondition: Post-traumatic venous congestion — monitored clinically by color, turgor and capillary refill.
FJ2359.clinicalScenario: After repairing a ring finger laceration, nurses chart hourly color and refill checks to catch venous compromise early.

FJ3049.name: Right anterior basal segmental vein
FJ3049.details: Pulmonary vein tributary draining the anterior basal segment (S8) of the right lower lobe into the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3049.clinicalCondition: Basal segmentectomy landmark — its course separates anterior from lateral basal segments.
FJ3049.clinicalScenario: A surgeon follows this vein's intersegmental plane while resecting an anterior basal segment tumor in the right lower lobe.

FJ3056.name: Right anterior basal segmental vein
FJ3056.details: Venous branch accompanying the anterior basal segmental bronchus of the right lung, returning blood to the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3056.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein stenosis risk — right inferior pulmonary vein narrowing after ablation affects this tributary's drainage.
FJ3056.clinicalScenario: Post-ablation imaging shows right inferior pulmonary vein narrowing, and the patient is monitored for cough and dyspnea.

FJ2265.name: Right anterior circumflex humeral vein
FJ2265.details: Small vena comitans of the anterior circumflex humeral artery, running below the shoulder joint to drain into the axillary vein.
FJ2265.clinicalCondition: Surgical bleeding in shoulder arthroplasty — anterior humeral circumflex vessels are ligated during the deltopectoral approach.
FJ2265.clinicalScenario: During shoulder replacement, the surgeon secures the anterior circumflex humeral vessels before proceeding with humeral preparation.

FJ3028.name: Right anterior segmental vein
FJ3028.details: Pulmonary vein tributary draining the anterior segment (S3) of the right upper lobe into the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3028.clinicalCondition: Upper lobectomy landmark — the vein is identified early to avoid tearing at the hilum.
FJ3028.clinicalScenario: In a right upper lobectomy, the surgeon dissects this vein first because anterior segmental branches tear easily during fissure work.

FJ3029.name: Right anterior segmental vein
FJ3029.details: Vein accompanying the anterior segmental bronchus and artery of the right upper lobe toward the superior pulmonary vein ostium.
FJ3029.clinicalCondition: Segmental venous variation — drainage variants change anterior segmentectomy technique.
FJ3029.clinicalScenario: A 3D reconstruction shows this vein joining the middle lobe vein, so the segmentectomy plan is modified to protect middle lobe drainage.

FJ2132.name: Right anterior tibial vein
FJ2132.details: Paired venae comitantes of the anterior tibial artery in the anterior leg compartment, piercing the interosseous membrane to join the popliteal vein.
FJ2132.clinicalCondition: Anterior compartment DVT — uncommon, may accompany compartment syndrome after trauma.
FJ2132.clinicalScenario: A footballer with a tibial fracture and tense anterior compartment has ultrasound showing thrombosed anterior tibial veins alongside compartment syndrome.

FJ2193.name: Right anterior tibial vein
FJ2193.details: Deep veins of the anterior leg running with the anterior tibial artery and deep fibular nerve, draining the dorsum of the foot upward.
FJ2193.clinicalCondition: Calf DVT screening — tibial vein clots are detected on whole-leg duplex protocols.
FJ2193.clinicalScenario: A patient with calf pain after knee arthroscopy has whole-leg ultrasound demonstrating thrombus in the anterior tibial veins.

FJ3589.name: Right ascending lumbar vein
FJ3589.details: Vertical vein on the right side of the lumbar vertebral bodies connecting lumbar veins, becoming the azygos vein root at the diaphragm.
FJ3589.clinicalCondition: Azygos continuation of IVC — congenital interruption drains lower body blood through this channel.
FJ3589.clinicalScenario: Imaging for an unrelated problem reveals an absent intrahepatic IVC with a dilated azygos system fed by the ascending lumbar veins.

FJ2269.name: Right axillary vein
FJ2269.details: Continuation of the basilic vein at the lower border of teres major, running through the axilla medial to the axillary artery to the first rib.
FJ2269.clinicalCondition: Central line access site — ultrasound-guided axillary puncture avoids pneumothorax of subclavian sticks.
FJ2269.clinicalScenario: An intensivist places an ultrasound-guided axillary vein catheter for a patient needing long-term central access.

FJ2270.name: Right basilic vein
FJ2270.details: Large superficial vein ascending the medial forearm and arm from the dorsal venous network, piercing deep fascia mid-arm to join the brachial veins forming the axillary vein.
FJ2270.clinicalCondition: PICC access vein — its size and straight course make it the preferred PICC insertion route.
FJ2270.clinicalScenario: A nurse inserts a PICC through the right basilic vein above the elbow for a patient starting chemotherapy.

FJ3583.name: Right brachiocephalic vein
FJ3583.details: Short wide vein formed behind the right sternoclavicular joint by subclavian and internal jugular union, joining its left counterpart to form the superior vena cava.
FJ3583.clinicalCondition: Central venous stenosis — prior catheters cause stenosis producing arm and face swelling.
FJ3583.clinicalScenario: A dialysis patient with right arm swelling has venography showing right brachiocephalic stenosis from previous catheter placements.

FJ2272.name: Right cephalic vein
FJ2272.details: Superficial vein ascending the lateral forearm and arm, crossing the deltopectoral groove and piercing the clavipectoral fascia to join the axillary vein.
FJ2272.clinicalCondition: Arteriovenous fistula site — cephalic vein is the first-choice conduit for hemodialysis access.
FJ2272.clinicalScenario: A vascular surgeon creates a radiocephalic fistula at the wrist for a patient approaching dialysis dependence.

FJ2274.name: Right circumflex scapular vein
FJ2274.details: Vena comitans of the circumflex scapular artery passing through the triangular space, draining the posterior scapular region into the subscapular vein.
FJ2274.clinicalCondition: Triangular space landmark — vessels here are encountered in posterior shoulder and scapular flap surgery.
FJ2274.clinicalScenario: While raising a scapular flap, the surgeon identifies the circumflex scapular pedicle passing through the triangular space.

FJ3591.name: Right colic vein
FJ3591.details: Drains the ascending colon and hepatic flexure; ascends in the mesocolon beside the right colic artery and empties into the superior mesenteric vein, sometimes via the gastrocolic trunk.
FJ3591.clinicalCondition: Hemorrhage during right hemicolectomy — the vein is thin-walled and easily torn when the mesocolon is mobilized.
FJ3591.clinicalScenario: During laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for colon cancer, traction on the mesocolon avulses this vein; brisk venous bleeding forces prompt clipping and conversion of the dissection plane.

FJ3566.name: Right common iliac vein
FJ3566.details: Formed behind the right sacroiliac joint by the external and internal iliac veins; ascends lateral to its artery and joins its fellow at L5 to form the inferior vena cava.
FJ3566.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis — sluggish flow and pelvic compression make it a common site of iliofemoral clot.
FJ3566.clinicalScenario: Five days after pelvic surgery, a woman develops gross right leg swelling and pain; duplex ultrasonography shows thrombus extending into the right common iliac vein.

FJ2135.name: Right deep femoral vein
FJ2135.details: Vena comitans of the profunda femoris artery; drains the deep thigh muscles and hip region and joins the femoral vein a few centimetres below the inguinal ligament.
FJ2135.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis — profunda thrombus may persist even when the femoral vein appears patent on scanning.
FJ2135.clinicalScenario: A man with a fractured femoral shaft develops thigh swelling; imaging reveals thrombus in the deep femoral vein, requiring anticoagulation before orthopedic fixation.

FJ2281.name: Right deep palmar venous arch
FJ2281.details: Network of venae comitantes accompanying the deep palmar arterial arch in the palm; drains the deep palm and fingers into the radial and ulnar veins.
FJ2281.clinicalCondition: Deep palmar space infection — puncture wounds can seed infection that tracks along these veins into the midpalmar space.
FJ2281.clinicalScenario: A gardener punctures his palm on a thorn; two days later the palm is swollen and painful with loss of its normal concavity, indicating a deep palmar abscess.

FJ3568.name: Right external iliac vein
FJ3568.details: Continuation of the femoral vein above the inguinal ligament; runs medial to the external iliac artery on the pelvic brim and joins the internal iliac vein.
FJ3568.clinicalCondition: Venous compression by pelvic masses — tumors or lymphadenopathy narrow the vein and cause unilateral leg edema.
FJ3568.clinicalScenario: A woman with bulky pelvic lymphadenopathy from cervical cancer presents with progressive right leg swelling; CT shows compression of the right external iliac vein.

FJ2144.name: Right femoral vein
FJ2144.details: Continuation of the popliteal vein at the adductor hiatus; in the femoral triangle it lies medial to the femoral artery within the femoral sheath.
FJ2144.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis and catheter-related infection — also a common access route for emergency central venous cannulation.
FJ2144.clinicalScenario: A shocked trauma patient needs urgent venous access; the right femoral vein is cannulated below the inguinal ligament using the artery's pulse as the medial-lateral landmark.

FJ2190.name: Right fibular vein
FJ2190.details: One of the paired venae comitantes of the fibular (peroneal) artery; drains the lateral and posterior compartments of the leg and joins the posterior tibial vein below the knee.
FJ2190.clinicalCondition: Calf deep vein thrombosis — fibular vein clot is a frequent finding after surgery or prolonged immobility.
FJ2190.clinicalScenario: A plaster cast is removed after six weeks for an ankle fracture; the patient reports new calf ache, and duplex scanning shows thrombus in the right fibular vein.

FJ2194.name: Right fibular vein
FJ2194.details: Paired deep vein accompanying the fibular artery deep to soleus; receives tributaries from the soleal and peroneal muscles and drains toward the popliteal vein.
FJ2194.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism source — calf vein thrombi, including fibular, can propagate proximally and embolize to the lungs.
FJ2194.clinicalScenario: After a long-haul flight, a traveler develops calf discomfort; a week later he presents with pleuritic chest pain, and imaging links a fibular vein thrombosis to pulmonary emboli.

FJ2200.name: Right fibular vein
FJ2200.details: Deep calf vein running with the fibular vessels on the interosseous membrane; part of the soleal venous pump that returns blood from the dependent leg.
FJ2200.clinicalCondition: Post-thrombotic syndrome — valve damage after fibular vein thrombosis contributes to chronic calf pain and swelling.
FJ2200.clinicalScenario: Two years after a treated calf DVT, a nurse who stands all day complains of evening ankle swelling and aching, worse after shifts, consistent with post-thrombotic syndrome.

FJ3595.name: Right gastric vein
FJ3595.details: Runs along the lesser curvature of the stomach with the right gastric artery and drains directly into the portal vein at the level of the pylorus.
FJ3595.clinicalCondition: Gastric varices in portal hypertension — the vein enlarges as a collateral when portal pressure rises.
FJ3595.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic patient vomits blood; endoscopy shows bleeding fundal and lesser-curvature varices fed by dilated gastric veins from portal hypertension.

FJ3597.name: Right gastroepiploic vein
FJ3597.details: Follows the greater curvature of the stomach with the right gastroepiploic artery, draining the stomach and greater omentum into the superior mesenteric vein.
FJ3597.clinicalCondition: Intraoperative hemorrhage during gastrectomy — the vein tears easily when the omentum is stripped from the stomach.
FJ3597.clinicalScenario: During a distal gastrectomy for gastric ulcer, mobilizing the greater omentum avulses this vein, causing troublesome bleeding controlled by ligation along the greater curvature.

FJ2151.name: Right genicular vein
FJ2151.details: One of several small venae comitantes of the genicular arteries forming a venous plexus around the knee joint; drains into the popliteal vein.
FJ2151.clinicalCondition: Hemarthrosis-associated bleeding — torn genicular vessels bleed into the joint after knee trauma.
FJ2151.clinicalScenario: A footballer twists his knee and develops a tense, painful swelling within hours; aspiration yields blood, with genicular vessel injury accompanying a cruciate ligament tear.

FJ2153.name: Right genicular vein
FJ2153.details: Small deep vein accompanying a genicular branch around the femoral condyles; part of the periarticular venous network anastomosing above and below the knee.
FJ2153.clinicalCondition: Postoperative hematoma after knee arthroplasty — genicular vessels are divided during bone cuts and releases.
FJ2153.clinicalScenario: After total knee replacement, a patient's dressing is soaked and a thigh hematoma expands; a bleeding genicular vessel is suspected and the wound is re-explored.

FJ2181.name: Right genicular vein
FJ2181.details: Vena comitans of an inferior genicular artery below the joint line; connects the periarticular plexus to the popliteal and anterior tibial veins.
FJ2181.clinicalCondition: Arthroscopy portal bleeding — inferior genicular vessels lie close to standard arthroscopic approaches.
FJ2181.clinicalScenario: Following knee arthroscopy for a meniscal tear, a patient develops a pulsatile swelling near the medial portal from injury to a genicular vessel, forming a small pseudoaneurysm.

FJ2182.name: Right genicular vein
FJ2182.details: Contributes to the collateral venous network around the knee that bypasses the popliteal vein when it is obstructed; accompanies the superior genicular arteries.
FJ2182.clinicalCondition: Collateral enlargement in popliteal vein obstruction — genicular veins dilate to carry blood past a blocked segment.
FJ2182.clinicalScenario: A patient with chronic popliteal vein occlusion after old DVT shows prominent veins around the knee on CT venography, representing enlarged genicular collaterals.

FJ2145.name: Right great saphenous vein
FJ2145.details: Longest vein in the body; begins at the medial dorsal foot, passes before the medial malleolus, ascends the medial leg and thigh, and joins the femoral vein at the saphenofemoral junction.
FJ2145.clinicalCondition: Varicose veins and venous ulceration — valve incompetence causes varicosities, lipodermatosclerosis and medial ankle ulcers.
FJ2145.clinicalScenario: A shopkeeper with long-standing varicose veins develops a non-healing ulcer above the medial malleolus; duplex confirms great saphenous reflux, and she also donates vein for bypass grafting discussions.

FJ2416.name: Right hepatic vein
FJ2416.details: Drains the right lobe of the liver; runs in the right lobar fissure between anterior and posterior sectors and enters the inferior vena cava just below the diaphragm.
FJ2416.clinicalCondition: Budd–Chiari syndrome — hepatic vein thrombosis causes painful hepatomegaly, ascites and hepatic dysfunction.
FJ2416.clinicalScenario: A young woman on oral contraceptives presents with right upper quadrant pain, tender hepatomegaly and new ascites; Doppler shows absent flow in the right hepatic vein.

FJ3603.name: Right iliolumbar vein
FJ3603.details: Accompanies the iliolumbar artery in the iliac fossa, draining iliacus and the iliac crest region into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3603.clinicalCondition: Operative bleeding in pelvic surgery — the vein is at risk during pelvic lymph node dissection and sacroiliac procedures.
FJ3603.clinicalScenario: During pelvic lymphadenectomy for prostate cancer, dissection near the sacroiliac joint tears the iliolumbar vein, producing deep pelvic oozing that is difficult to expose.

FJ3605.name: Right inferior epigastric vein
FJ3605.details: Vena comitans of the inferior epigastric artery; ascends in the rectus sheath and drains into the external iliac vein, anastomosing above with the superior epigastric vein.
FJ3605.clinicalCondition: Laparoscopic port-site hemorrhage — lateral trocars can pierce the inferior epigastric vessels in the abdominal wall.
FJ3605.clinicalScenario: After laparoscopic appendicectomy, a patient's hemoglobin falls and the abdominal wall bruises; CT shows a rectus sheath hematoma from a trocar-injured inferior epigastric vein.

FJ3606.name: Right inferior gluteal vein
FJ3606.details: Vena comitans of the inferior gluteal artery; leaves the pelvis below piriformis through the greater sciatic foramen and drains into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3606.clinicalCondition: Gluteal hematoma — bleeding from gluteal veins after falls or injections, especially in anticoagulated patients.
FJ3606.clinicalScenario: An elderly man on warfarin falls onto his buttock and develops a large, tense gluteal swelling; imaging shows a hematoma fed by the inferior gluteal vessels.

FJ3040.name: Right inferior pulmonary vein
FJ3040.details: Formed by the common basal vein within the right lung; drains the lower lobe, crosses below the root and opens into the posterior left atrium.
FJ3040.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein stenosis after atrial fibrillation ablation — scarring narrows the ostium, causing dyspnea and hemoptysis.
FJ3040.clinicalScenario: Months after radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation, a man develops breathlessness and coughs blood; CT shows tight narrowing of the right inferior pulmonary vein ostium.

FJ3570.name: Right internal iliac vein
FJ3570.details: Formed by the gluteal, internal pudendal, obturator and visceral veins of the pelvis; lies behind the internal iliac artery and joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac.
FJ3570.clinicalCondition: Pelvic venous thrombosis — a hidden source of pulmonary embolism after pelvic surgery or childbirth.
FJ3570.clinicalScenario: A week after radical hysterectomy, a woman becomes suddenly breathless; CT pulmonary angiography shows emboli arising from thrombus in the right internal iliac vein.

FJ3571.name: Right internal iliac vein
FJ3571.details: Short, wide trunk on the pelvic sidewall receiving tributaries from the bladder, rectum and reproductive organs via the pelvic venous plexuses.
FJ3571.clinicalCondition: Hemorrhage in pelvic fractures — torn internal iliac tributaries cause major retroperitoneal bleeding.
FJ3571.clinicalScenario: A motorcyclist with an unstable pelvic fracture is hypotensive despite transfusion; angiography identifies bleeding from branches of the right internal iliac vein for embolization.

FJ3572.name: Right internal iliac vein
FJ3572.details: Lies medial and posterior to the internal iliac artery; its tributaries correspond to the artery's branches, except the iliolumbar vein pattern, draining the pelvic viscera.
FJ3572.clinicalCondition: Pelvic congestion syndrome — dilated, refluxing pelvic veins cause chronic pelvic pain worsened by standing.
FJ3572.clinicalScenario: A multiparous woman reports dull pelvic ache worse at day's end; venography shows varicosities around the uterus draining into a dilated right internal iliac vein.

FJ3607.name: Right internal iliac vein
FJ3607.details: Begins at the upper greater sciatic foramen where its gluteal and pudendal tributaries converge; ascends to the pelvic brim behind the ureter's crossing point.
FJ3607.clinicalCondition: Operative injury during radical prostatectomy or cystectomy — the vein's thin wall tears during deep pelvic dissection.
FJ3607.clinicalScenario: During radical cystectomy, dissection behind the bladder injures the right internal iliac vein; controlled packing and suture repair are needed to stem the bleeding.

FJ3608.name: Right internal iliac vein
FJ3608.details: Receives the superior and inferior gluteal, lateral sacral, middle rectal and vesical veins; communicates freely with the vertebral venous plexus through sacral tributaries.
FJ3608.clinicalCondition: Tumor spread via pelvic–vertebral communications — prostatic cancer cells can reach the spine through these valveless channels.
FJ3608.clinicalScenario: A man with prostate cancer develops back pain; MRI shows vertebral metastases without lung deposits, explained by spread through pelvic veins into the vertebral venous plexus.

FJ3609.name: Right internal iliac vein
FJ3609.details: Valveless pelvic trunk; because it lies directly behind its artery, arterial pulsation can compress it against the pelvic wall, slowing flow.
FJ3609.clinicalCondition: May–Thurner-type compression variants — iliac vein compression predisposes to iliofemoral thrombosis.
FJ3609.clinicalScenario: A young woman with unexplained right iliofemoral DVT undergoes venography showing extrinsic narrowing of the iliac vein junction, managed with stenting after thrombolysis.

FJ3585.name: Right internal jugular vein
FJ3585.details: Continuation of the sigmoid dural sinus; leaves the skull through the jugular foramen, descends within the carotid sheath lateral to the carotid artery, and joins the subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint.
FJ3585.clinicalCondition: Lemierre syndrome — septic thrombophlebitis of this vein following oropharyngeal infection, seeding septic pulmonary emboli.
FJ3585.clinicalScenario: A teenager recovering from a sore throat develops spiking fevers, neck tenderness and breathlessness; blood cultures grow Fusobacterium and CT shows thrombosis of the right internal jugular vein.

FJ3610.name: Right internal pudendal vein
FJ3610.details: Accompanies the internal pudendal artery through the pudendal canal on the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa; drains the perineum and external genitalia into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3610.clinicalCondition: Perineal hematoma after straddle injury — pudendal tributaries rupture when the perineum strikes a hard object.
FJ3610.clinicalScenario: A cyclist falls astride the bicycle crossbar and develops a painful, bruised perineal swelling; examination shows a hematoma from injured internal pudendal tributaries.

FJ1993.name: Right internal thoracic vein
FJ1993.details: Vena comitans of the internal thoracic artery, running on the inner chest wall lateral to the sternum; unites above to drain into the brachiocephalic vein.
FJ1993.clinicalCondition: Injury during internal thoracic artery harvest for coronary bypass — venous bleeding complicates graft dissection.
FJ1993.clinicalScenario: During coronary artery bypass surgery, harvesting the right internal thoracic artery tears its companion vein, and careful hemostasis is needed before the graft is used.

FJ3059.name: Right lateral basal segmental vein
FJ3059.details: Drains the lateral basal segment (S9) of the right lower lobe; joins the common basal vein, which empties into the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3059.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy planning — precise venous anatomy defines the intersegmental plane for anatomical resection.
FJ3059.clinicalScenario: A patient with a small peripheral lung nodule undergoes CT mapping; the lateral basal segmental vein is traced to plan a safe S9 segmentectomy.

FJ3060.name: Right lateral basal segmental vein
FJ3060.details: Tributary within the basal part of the right lower lobe, running with the lateral basal segmental bronchus and artery in the segment's core.
FJ3060.clinicalCondition: Hemoptysis localization — basal segmental veins help radiologists pinpoint the bleeding segment on CT angiography.
FJ3060.clinicalScenario: A bronchiectatic patient coughs fresh blood; CT angiography localizes hypertrophied vessels around the lateral basal segment, guiding bronchial artery embolization.

FJ3061.name: Right lateral basal segmental vein
FJ3061.details: Part of the basal venous confluence; variations in its junction with the common basal vein are common and relevant to lower lobectomy.
FJ3061.clinicalCondition: Venous congestion after lobectomy — a misplaced staple across a shared basal trunk can congest remaining segments.
FJ3061.clinicalScenario: After right lower lobectomy, imaging shows congestion of a retained basal segment because its draining vein shared a trunk that was divided during surgery.

FJ3062.name: Right lateral basal segmental vein
FJ3062.details: Runs in the intersegmental septum between the lateral and anterior basal segments, serving as the radiological boundary between them.
FJ3062.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein isolation planning — basal tributary anatomy is mapped before ablation to avoid unintended stenosis.
FJ3062.clinicalScenario: Before atrial fibrillation ablation, cardiac CT maps the right inferior pulmonary vein and its basal tributaries so ablation lesions stay clear of the venous ostia.

FJ2201.name: Right lateral circumflex femoral vein
FJ2201.details: Vena comitans of the lateral circumflex femoral artery; drains the lateral thigh and hip region into the femoral or deep femoral vein near the femoral neck.
FJ2201.clinicalCondition: Bleeding during hip surgery — vessels crossing the femoral neck are divided in anterior approaches.
FJ2201.clinicalScenario: During total hip arthroplasty, dissection around the femoral neck injures the lateral circumflex femoral vein, producing bleeding controlled with cautery and ligation.

FJ3611.name: Right lateral sacral vein
FJ3611.details: Accompanies the lateral sacral artery across the sacrum, draining into the internal iliac vein; communicates with the internal vertebral venous plexus through sacral foramina.
FJ3611.clinicalCondition: Presacral hemorrhage during rectal surgery — sacral veins tear when the rectum is mobilized off the sacrum.
FJ3611.clinicalScenario: During total mesorectal excision, the surgeon encounters heavy presacral venous bleeding; thumbtacks and packing are used because the torn sacral veins retract into bone.

FJ2285.name: Right lateral thoracic vein
FJ2285.details: Runs along the lateral chest wall on serratus anterior with the lateral thoracic artery; drains into the axillary vein and connects below with the thoracoepigastric vein.
FJ2285.clinicalCondition: Collateral dilatation in vena caval obstruction — the vein enlarges as part of chest-wall collateral pathways.
FJ2285.clinicalScenario: A patient with inferior vena cava obstruction shows prominent tortuous veins over the lateral chest and abdomen, including a dilated right lateral thoracic vein.

FJ2727.name: Right marginal vein
FJ2727.details: Vein of the heart running along the acute (right) margin with the marginal branch of the right coronary artery; drains into the small cardiac vein or coronary sinus.
FJ2727.clinicalCondition: Venous congestion in inferior myocardial infarction — right coronary occlusion impairs the territory this vein drains.
FJ2727.clinicalScenario: An ECG shows inferior ST elevation; angiography confirms right coronary occlusion in the territory drained by the marginal vein, with right ventricular involvement suspected.

FJ2728.name: Right marginal vein
FJ2728.details: Cardiac vein coursing in the atrioventricular groove region toward the coronary sinus; part of the coronary venous system mapped during device implantation.
FJ2728.clinicalCondition: Cardiac resynchronization therapy planning — coronary venous anatomy determines whether a left ventricular lead can be placed.
FJ2728.clinicalScenario: Before CRT implantation, coronary sinus venography maps the marginal and lateral veins to choose a branch that paces the lateral left ventricular wall.

FJ2729.name: Right marginal vein
FJ2729.details: Small vein draining the right margin of the heart; occasionally opens directly into the right atrium instead of joining the coronary sinus system.
FJ2729.clinicalCondition: Coronary sinus catheterization difficulty — variant venous openings can confuse retrograde cardioplegia delivery in cardiac surgery.
FJ2729.clinicalScenario: During valve surgery, the perfusionist notes poor retrograde cardioplegia distribution; variant coronary venous anatomy, including an anomalous marginal vein opening, is identified.

FJ3054.name: Right medial basal segmental vein
FJ3054.details: Drains the medial basal (cardiac) segment S7 of the right lower lobe; joins the common basal vein to reach the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3054.clinicalCondition: Segmental anatomy in middle and lower lobe surgery — the small medial basal segment is easily congested if its vein is divided.
FJ3054.clinicalScenario: During a right middle lobectomy, the surgeon carefully preserves the medial basal segmental vein to avoid congestion of the adjacent lower lobe segment.

FJ3055.name: Right medial basal segmental vein
FJ3055.details: Small tributary running with the medial basal bronchus medial to the basal trunk; its ostium into the inferior pulmonary vein varies.
FJ3055.clinicalCondition: Preoperative mapping for basal segmentectomy — unrecognized variant drainage risks postoperative segmental congestion.
FJ3055.clinicalScenario: Three-dimensional CT reconstruction before lung surgery reveals the medial basal vein draining separately into the left atrium side of the inferior pulmonary vein, altering the resection plan.

FJ2341.name: Right medial brachial vein
FJ2341.details: One of the paired venae comitantes of the brachial artery on its medial side in the arm; deep vein draining into the axillary vein at the lower border of teres major.
FJ2341.clinicalCondition: Upper-limb deep vein thrombosis — brachial vein clot follows PICC lines or prolonged cannulation.
FJ2341.clinicalScenario: A patient with a peripherally inserted central catheter develops arm ache and swelling; duplex confirms thrombus around the catheter in the right brachial vein.

FJ2202.name: Right medial circumflex femoral vein
FJ2202.details: Vena comitans of the medial circumflex femoral artery; winds around the medial femoral neck, draining the adductor region and hip joint into the deep femoral vein.
FJ2202.clinicalCondition: Bleeding in femoral neck fracture surgery — the vein lies close to the fracture and to fixation screws.
FJ2202.clinicalScenario: During hemiarthroplasty for a fractured neck of femur, bleeding from the medial circumflex femoral vein near the lesser trochanter requires prompt control.

FJ2286.name: Right median antebrachial vein
FJ2286.details: Superficial vein ascending the front of the forearm from the palmar venous plexus; near the elbow it joins the basilic or median cubital vein, often dividing around it.
FJ2286.clinicalCondition: Venous access site — commonly cannulated for intravenous therapy, with thrombophlebitis a frequent minor complication.
FJ2286.clinicalScenario: A dehydrated patient needs fluids; the prominent median antebrachial vein is cannulated, but three days later a tender red cord signals superficial thrombophlebitis.

FJ2287.name: Right median cubital vein
FJ2287.details: Large superficial vein crossing the cubital fossa, connecting cephalic to basilic vein; separated from the brachial artery and median nerve by the bicipital aponeurosis.
FJ2287.clinicalCondition: First-choice venipuncture site — its size and stability make it ideal, though anomalous patterns can endanger deeper structures.
FJ2287.clinicalScenario: A phlebotomist draws blood from a patient's median cubital vein; the bicipital aponeurosis protects the underlying artery and nerve during the puncture.

FJ1996.name: Right musculophrenic vein
FJ1996.details: Vena comitans of the musculophrenic artery along the costal margin; drains the lower anterior intercostal spaces and upper diaphragm into the internal thoracic vein.
FJ1996.clinicalCondition: Collateral pathway in superior vena cava obstruction — flow reroutes through chest-wall and diaphragmatic veins.
FJ1996.clinicalScenario: CT in a patient with SVC syndrome shows opacified musculophrenic and intercostal collaterals bypassing the obstructed vena cava toward the inferior system.

FJ3612.name: Right obturator vein
FJ3612.details: Emerges through the obturator canal with the obturator nerve and artery; drains the medial thigh and hip region into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3612.clinicalCondition: Corona mortis bleeding — an accessory obturator vein anastomosing with the external iliac system can be torn in hernia or pelvic surgery.
FJ3612.clinicalScenario: During laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair, dissection over the pubic ramus injures a corona mortis venous connection, causing bleeding that is controlled with clips.

FJ2290.name: Right palmar metacarpal vein
FJ2290.details: Small deep vein of the palm running in a metacarpal space, draining palmar structures into the deep palmar venous arch.
FJ2290.clinicalCondition: Hand compartment syndrome — bleeding into the interosseous spaces after crush injury raises pressure and threatens intrinsic muscles.
FJ2290.clinicalScenario: A laborer's hand is crushed by machinery; progressive pain and tense swelling lead to fasciotomy of the interosseous compartments to save the intrinsic muscles.

FJ2350.name: Right palmar metacarpal vein
FJ2350.details: Accompanies the palmar metacarpal vessels between the metacarpals; communicates with dorsal veins through perforating channels.
FJ2350.clinicalCondition: Spread of hand infection — deep palmar infections can track along venous channels between palmar and dorsal compartments.
FJ2350.clinicalScenario: A fisherman with a palmar puncture wound develops dorsal hand swelling; infection has tracked through perforating veins from the palmar space to the dorsum.

FJ2353.name: Right palmar metacarpal vein
FJ2353.details: Part of the deep venous network of the palm; its tributaries drain the lumbrical canals and palmar aponeurosis region into the venae comitantes of the ulnar and radial arteries.
FJ2353.clinicalCondition: Palmar hematoma after arterial line or blood gas attempts — venous oozing can mimic arterial injury in the palm.
FJ2353.clinicalScenario: After repeated palmar punctures, a patient develops a painful palmar hematoma; ultrasound confirms venous bleeding without arterial damage, managed conservatively.

FJ2171.name: Right popliteal vein
FJ2171.details: Formed by the union of the anterior and posterior tibial veins at the lower popliteal fossa; lies between the popliteal artery (deep) and tibial nerve (superficial), becoming the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.
FJ2171.clinicalCondition: Deep vein thrombosis — popliteal clot is the classic ultrasound finding in symptomatic leg DVT.
FJ2171.clinicalScenario: After a long flight, a man presents with unilateral calf swelling and pain; compression ultrasound shows a non-compressible right popliteal vein containing thrombus.

FJ1913.name: Right portal vein
FJ1913.details: Right branch of the portal vein formed at the porta hepatis; short trunk entering the right lobe, dividing into anterior and posterior sectoral branches supplying segments V–VIII.
FJ1913.clinicalCondition: Portal vein thrombosis — clot in a branch causes segmental portal hypertension and can complicate cirrhosis.
FJ1913.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic patient develops worsening ascites; Doppler ultrasound shows thrombus occluding the right portal vein, prompting anticoagulation assessment.

FJ2405.name: Right portal vein
FJ2405.details: Carries nutrient-rich venous blood from the gut to the right liver; its branching pattern varies, with trifurcation and early sectoral origins in a significant minority.
FJ2405.clinicalCondition: Tumor invasion by hepatocellular carcinoma — portal branch tumor thrombus worsens staging and limits resection options.
FJ2405.clinicalScenario: Imaging in a patient with hepatocellular carcinoma shows enhancing tumor thrombus expanding the right portal vein, changing the plan from resection to systemic therapy.

FJ3041.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3041.details: Drains the posterior basal segment (S10) of the right lower lobe; runs with the posterior basal bronchus and joins the common basal vein to the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3041.clinicalCondition: Basal segmentectomy planning — this vein forms the intersegmental boundary used to divide S10.
FJ3041.clinicalScenario: A patient with a small S10 nodule has 3D-CT mapping; the posterior basal segmental vein is identified as the landmark for a stapled anatomical segmentectomy.

FJ3043.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3043.details: Tributary of the basal venous system lying in the septum between the posterior and lateral basal segments of the right lower lobe.
FJ3043.clinicalCondition: Hemoptysis work-up — basal venous tributaries help localize the segment responsible for bleeding on CT.
FJ3043.clinicalScenario: A patient with recurrent hemoptysis undergoes CT angiography; congestion around the posterior basal segment directs bronchoscopic inspection to the S10 orifice.

FJ3044.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3044.details: Collects blood from the posterior basal segment, the most dependent part of the lower lobe when supine, and drains into the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3044.clinicalCondition: Aspiration predilection — the posterior basal segment is a common site of aspiration in recumbent patients, mapped by its vessels.
FJ3044.clinicalScenario: An obtunded alcoholic patient develops fever and a right lower lobe infiltrate centered on the posterior basal segment, typical of aspiration pneumonitis.

FJ3045.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3045.details: Runs posteriorly in the basal lower lobe beside the descending basal artery; variations include a separate ostium into the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3045.clinicalCondition: Variant drainage in lobectomy — a separate posterior basal ostium can be injured during inferior pulmonary vein division.
FJ3045.clinicalScenario: During right lower lobectomy, the surgeon finds the posterior basal vein entering the inferior pulmonary vein separately and ligates it individually to avoid tearing.

FJ3046.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3046.details: Part of the common basal confluence; receives intersegmental tributaries that mark the plane between S10 and the superior segment S6.
FJ3046.clinicalCondition: Segmental congestion after basilar resection — dividing shared intersegmental veins can congest the preserved superior segment.
FJ3046.clinicalScenario: After basal segmentectomy, follow-up CT shows a congested superior segment because intersegmental veins draining toward S10 were divided with the specimen.

FJ3047.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3047.details: Small basal tributary demonstrated on contrast CT as part of the inferior pulmonary vein's branching pattern in the right lung base.
FJ3047.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary vein mapping before ablation — basal branches are catalogued so energy delivery avoids venous ostia.
FJ3047.clinicalScenario: An electrophysiologist reviews cardiac CT before ablation and notes the branching of the right inferior pulmonary vein, including the posterior basal tributary, to plan lesion placement.

FJ3048.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3048.details: Drains toward the common basal vein; its caliber increases in pulmonary hypertension as part of basal venous engorgement.
FJ3048.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary venous congestion in left heart failure — engorged basal veins accompany Kerley lines and edema on imaging.
FJ3048.clinicalScenario: A breathless patient with decompensated heart failure has a chest radiograph showing basal venous distension and interstitial edema, improving after diuresis.

FJ3057.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3057.details: Lies adjacent to the posterior basal bronchus in the lung root's lower part; a useful bronchoscopic-anatomical landmark for segment identification.
FJ3057.clinicalCondition: Foreign body localization — posterior basal segments commonly trap aspirated objects in the right lung.
FJ3057.clinicalScenario: A child aspirates a peanut fragment; imaging places it in the posterior basal segment bronchus, and bronchoscopy retrieves it from the S10 airway.

FJ3058.name: Right posterior basal segmental vein
FJ3058.details: Final basal tributary joining the common basal vein; together the basal veins form the lower half of the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3058.clinicalCondition: Pulmonary embolism catheter therapy planning — basal venous anatomy is reviewed alongside arteries before intervention.
FJ3058.clinicalScenario: Before catheter-directed thrombolysis for massive pulmonary embolism, CT venography maps basal pulmonary veins to distinguish vein from clot-filled arteries in the right base.

FJ3022.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3022.details: Drains the posterior segment (S2) of the right upper lobe; joins the apical and anterior segmental tributaries to form the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3022.clinicalCondition: Upper lobe segmentectomy planning — the vein (V2) is the key landmark separating S2 from S1 and S3.
FJ3022.clinicalScenario: For a small apical tumor, 3D reconstruction traces the posterior segmental vein to define the intersegmental plane for an S2 segmentectomy.

FJ3023.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3023.details: Runs in the intersegmental septum below the posterior segment bronchus; its recurrent and central tributaries are constant features in right upper lobe anatomy.
FJ3023.clinicalCondition: Tuberculosis predilection — the posterior segment of the upper lobe is the classic site of reactivation tuberculosis.
FJ3023.clinicalScenario: A patient with chronic cough and weight loss has cavitation in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe, the typical distribution of post-primary tuberculosis.

FJ3024.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3024.details: Tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein; receives blood from the segment supplied by the posterior segmental bronchus B2.
FJ3024.clinicalCondition: Aspiration in the recumbent patient — posterior upper-lobe segments receive aspirated material when lying flat.
FJ3024.clinicalScenario: A sedated patient aspirates during endoscopy; subsequent infiltrates appear in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe, matching its dependent position when supine.

FJ3025.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3025.details: Courses medially across the upper lobe hilum; a central branch may cross behind the upper lobe bronchus, relevant during lobectomy dissection.
FJ3025.clinicalCondition: Venous injury in upper lobectomy — the central posterior segmental tributary can be torn during hilar dissection.
FJ3025.clinicalScenario: During right upper lobectomy for cancer, traction on the lobe tears a posterior segmental tributary; bleeding is controlled with clips before vein division.

FJ3026.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3026.details: Marks the venous watershed between the posterior segment and the superior segment of the lower lobe across the oblique fissure.
FJ3026.clinicalCondition: Localization of lung abscess — posterior segment abscesses follow aspiration and are drained under image guidance.
FJ3026.clinicalScenario: A patient with poor dentition develops a thick-walled cavity in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe; CT-guided drainage treats the lung abscess.

FJ3069.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3069.details: Contributes to formation of the right superior pulmonary vein trunk within the pericardium before it enters the left atrium.
FJ3069.clinicalCondition: Atrial fibrillation ablation anatomy — superior pulmonary vein tributaries are isolated electrically at their ostia.
FJ3069.clinicalScenario: During pulmonary vein isolation, the ablation catheter encircles the right superior pulmonary vein, whose posterior segmental tributary contributes to the arrhythmogenic ostium.

FJ3070.name: Right posterior segmental vein
FJ3070.details: Its tributaries interdigitate with apical segment veins; drainage anomalies include a posterior segment vein crossing to the apical trunk.
FJ3070.clinicalCondition: Variant venous drainage in lung resection — anomalies must be mapped to avoid unexpected bleeding or congestion.
FJ3070.clinicalScenario: Preoperative CT before right upper lobectomy shows the posterior segmental vein joining the apical trunk; the surgeon adjusts the stapling sequence accordingly.

FJ2173.name: Right posterior tibial vein
FJ2173.details: Paired venae comitantes of the posterior tibial artery; formed by the plantar veins behind the medial malleolus, ascend the deep posterior leg and unite with fibular veins to form the popliteal vein.
FJ2173.clinicalCondition: Calf deep vein thrombosis — posterior tibial thrombus is common after stroke, surgery or immobility.
FJ2173.clinicalScenario: A hemiplegic patient recovering from stroke develops calf swelling in the weak leg; duplex confirms thrombus in the right posterior tibial vein.

FJ2296.name: Right radial vein
FJ2296.details: One of the paired venae comitantes of the radial artery in the lateral forearm; drains the lateral hand and forearm into the brachial vein near the elbow.
FJ2296.clinicalCondition: Forearm hematoma after transradial catheterization — venous bleeding contributes to post-procedure forearm swelling.
FJ2296.clinicalScenario: After transradial coronary angiography, a patient's forearm becomes tense and painful; ultrasound excludes compartment syndrome and shows a venous hematoma under observation.

FJ3577.name: Right renal vein
FJ3577.details: Short, wide vein draining the right kidney directly into the inferior vena cava; unlike the left, it receives no gonadal or suprarenal tributaries.
FJ3577.clinicalCondition: Tumor thrombus from renal cell carcinoma — cancer can grow along this vein into the vena cava.
FJ3577.clinicalScenario: A man with hematuria has a right renal mass; MRI shows tumor thrombus filling the right renal vein and reaching the inferior vena cava, guiding surgical planning.

FJ3578.name: Right renal vein
FJ3578.details: Lies anterior to the right renal artery at the hilum; because of its short course, the right kidney is technically harder to mobilize on its vein during donation.
FJ3578.clinicalCondition: Renal vein thrombosis in nephrotic syndrome — hypercoagulability causes flank pain, hematuria and worsening renal function.
FJ3578.clinicalScenario: A patient with membranous nephropathy develops sudden flank pain and macroscopic hematuria; imaging reveals acute thrombosis of the right renal vein.

FJ2176.name: Right small saphenous vein
FJ2176.details: Begins at the lateral dorsal foot, passes behind the lateral malleolus, ascends the posterior calf between the gastrocnemius heads and pierces the deep fascia to join the popliteal vein.
FJ2176.clinicalCondition: Varicose veins of the posterior calf — saphenopopliteal incompetence produces varicosities and pigmentation.
FJ2176.clinicalScenario: A hairdresser complains of aching posterior calf varicosities; duplex shows reflux at the saphenopopliteal junction, and stripping is planned carefully because the sural nerve runs with the vein.

FJ3587.name: Right subclavian vein
FJ3587.details: Continuation of the axillary vein at the first rib; passes behind the clavicle, anterior to scalenus anterior, and joins the internal jugular vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.
FJ3587.clinicalCondition: Effort thrombosis (Paget–Schroetter syndrome) — repetitive arm exertion thromboses the vein at the thoracic outlet.
FJ3587.clinicalScenario: A young weightlifter presents with a swollen, dusky right arm after training; venography confirms acute subclavian vein thrombosis at the costoclavicular space.

FJ1995.name: Right subcostal vein
FJ1995.details: Runs below the twelfth rib with the subcostal nerve and artery along the posterior abdominal wall; drains into the ascending lumbar vein, linking lumbar and azygos systems.
FJ1995.clinicalCondition: Collateral channel in inferior vena cava obstruction — the ascending lumbar route diverts blood toward the azygos system.
FJ1995.clinicalScenario: In a patient with chronic IVC occlusion from old thrombosis, CT shows enlarged ascending lumbar and subcostal veins carrying blood upward to the azygos vein.

FJ2299.name: Right subscapular vein
FJ2299.details: Formed by tributaries accompanying the subscapular artery on the posterior axillary wall; drains the subscapularis and latissimus region into the axillary vein.
FJ2299.clinicalCondition: Bleeding during axillary lymph node clearance — subscapular tributaries are divided during breast cancer surgery.
FJ2299.clinicalScenario: During axillary dissection for breast cancer, the subscapular vein is carefully preserved or ligated to prevent troublesome bleeding near the thoracodorsal pedicle.

FJ3637.name: Right superficial dorsal vein of penis
FJ3637.details: Right-sided component of the superficial penile drainage; runs in the dartos layer draining penile skin and prepuce toward the right external pudendal vein.
FJ3637.clinicalCondition: Penile Mondor disease — thrombophlebitis of the superficial dorsal vein produces a tender dorsal cord.
FJ3637.clinicalScenario: A man notices a firm, cord-like ridge along the dorsum of the penis after vigorous intercourse; ultrasound confirms superficial dorsal vein thrombophlebitis, managed conservatively.

FJ2178.name: Right superficial epigastric vein
FJ2178.details: Superficial vein of the lower anterior abdominal wall accompanying the superficial epigastric artery; drains downward into the great saphenous or femoral vein and links above with thoracoepigastric channels.
FJ2178.clinicalCondition: Flow-direction sign in vena caval obstruction — downward flow in abdominal wall veins indicates inferior vena cava block.
FJ2178.clinicalScenario: Examining a patient with dilated abdominal wall veins, the clinician empties a superficial epigastric vein and finds it refills from above, pointing to inferior vena cava obstruction.

FJ2301.name: Right superficial palmar venous arch
FJ2301.details: Venous network in the superficial palm accompanying the superficial palmar arterial arch; drains palmar skin and fingers toward the ulnar and radial veins.
FJ2301.clinicalCondition: Palmar laceration bleeding — glass injuries divide the arch and bleed freely until compressed.
FJ2301.clinicalScenario: A worker cuts his palm on broken glass and presents with brisk bleeding; direct pressure controls venous hemorrhage from the superficial palmar arch before wound exploration.

FJ3615.name: Right superior epigastric vein
FJ3615.details: Vena comitans of the superior epigastric artery inside the rectus sheath; drains the upper abdominal wall into the internal thoracic vein and anastomoses with the inferior epigastric vein.
FJ3615.clinicalCondition: Collateral pathway between venae cavae — the epigastric anastomosis carries blood when either cava is obstructed.
FJ3615.clinicalScenario: In chronic superior vena cava obstruction, imaging shows blood descending through the superior epigastric vein into the inferior epigastric system to reach the patent inferior cava.

FJ3616.name: Right superior gluteal vein
FJ3616.details: Vena comitans of the superior gluteal artery; passes above piriformis through the greater sciatic foramen to drain the gluteal region into the internal iliac vein.
FJ3616.clinicalCondition: Gluteal bleeding in posterior hip approaches — these vessels are at risk during surgery around the sciatic notch.
FJ3616.clinicalScenario: An anticoagulated patient develops deep buttock pain and a falling hemoglobin after a fall; CT shows hematoma tracking along the superior gluteal vessels above piriformis.

FJ1991.name: Right superior intercostal vein
FJ1991.details: Formed by the union of the second, third and sometimes fourth posterior intercostal veins; arches over the pleura to drain into the right brachiocephalic vein.
FJ1991.clinicalCondition: Collateral enlargement in superior vena cava obstruction — intercostal veins dilate as blood seeks the azygos route.
FJ1991.clinicalScenario: CT in a patient with a mediastinal mass shows a prominent right superior intercostal vein among chest-wall collaterals bypassing the compressed superior vena cava.

FJ3020.name: Right superior pulmonary vein
FJ3020.details: Formed by apical, anterior and posterior segmental veins of the upper lobe plus the middle lobe vein; enters the left atrium carrying oxygenated blood from the right upper and middle lobes.
FJ3020.clinicalCondition: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection — this vein may drain into the superior vena cava with a sinus venosus atrial septal defect.
FJ3020.clinicalScenario: A child with a heart murmur has echocardiography showing a sinus venosus ASD; the right superior pulmonary vein drains anomalously into the superior vena cava.

FJ3050.name: Right superior segmental vein
FJ3050.details: Drains the superior segment (S6) of the right lower lobe; crosses the oblique fissure region to join the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ3050.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy landmark — the vein V6 separates the superior segment from the basal segments.
FJ3050.clinicalScenario: Planning an S6 segmentectomy for a ground-glass nodule, the surgeon traces the superior segmental vein on 3D-CT to define the stapling plane.

FJ3051.name: Right superior segmental vein
FJ3051.details: Runs with the superior segmental bronchus B6 opposite the middle lobe orifice; its tributaries outline the segment's venous drainage.
FJ3051.clinicalCondition: Aspiration localization — the superior lower-lobe segment is dependent in the semi-recumbent position.
FJ3051.clinicalScenario: A stroke patient fed while semi-reclined develops pneumonia localized to the superior segment of the right lower lobe, a classic aspiration site in that posture.

FJ3052.name: Right superior segmental vein
FJ3052.details: Tributary entering the upper part of the inferior pulmonary vein; must be distinguished from basal branches during lower lobectomy.
FJ3052.clinicalCondition: Venous injury during lobectomy — mistaking V6 for a basal branch risks congestion or bleeding.
FJ3052.clinicalScenario: During right lower lobectomy, careful dissection identifies the superior segmental vein entering the inferior pulmonary vein separately, and it is divided under direct vision.

FJ3063.name: Right superior segmental vein
FJ3063.details: Receives intersegmental tributaries from the basal segments, so it partly drains S6 neighbors across segment borders.
FJ3063.clinicalCondition: Postoperative segmental congestion — dividing shared intersegmental veins can impair basal segment drainage.
FJ3063.clinicalScenario: After an isolated S6 resection, imaging shows mild congestion of the adjacent anterior basal segment because shared intersegmental veins were taken with the specimen.

FJ3065.name: Right superior segmental vein
FJ3065.details: Lies posterior to the basal trunk in the lung root; a landmark on cross-sectional imaging for identifying the S6 bronchopulmonary segment.
FJ3065.clinicalCondition: Radiological segment localization — venous landmarks confirm which segment harbors a nodule or infiltrate.
FJ3065.clinicalScenario: A radiologist localizes a cavitating lesion to the superior segment of the right lower lobe by tracing its draining vein toward the inferior pulmonary vein.

FJ3066.name: Right superior segmental vein
FJ3066.details: Part of the inferior pulmonary vein's tributary tree; common trunks with basal veins occur and alter lobectomy technique.
FJ3066.clinicalCondition: Common-trunk variation — a shared trunk with basal veins changes the order of vascular division in surgery.
FJ3066.clinicalScenario: Preoperative imaging shows the superior segmental vein sharing a trunk with the common basal vein; the surgical team plans combined control before parenchymal division.

FJ3580.name: Right suprarenal vein
FJ3580.details: Short single vein emerging from the hilum of the right suprarenal gland and opening directly into the inferior vena cava; receives no significant tributaries.
FJ3580.clinicalCondition: Adrenal vein sampling difficulty — the short right vein is technically hard to cannulate when lateralizing aldosterone excess.
FJ3580.clinicalScenario: Investigating primary hyperaldosteronism, the radiologist struggles to seat the catheter in the short right suprarenal vein before finally obtaining a selective sample.

FJ2302.name: Right suprascapular vein
FJ2302.details: Vena comitans of the suprascapular artery; passes through the suprascapular notch region and drains the supraspinous and infraspinous fossae into the external jugular or subclavian vein.
FJ2302.clinicalCondition: Hematoma in shoulder surgery — vessels at the scapular notch bleed during posterior shoulder approaches.
FJ2302.clinicalScenario: After arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, a patient develops a deep posterior shoulder hematoma attributed to suprascapular venous bleeding near the notch.

FJ3618.name: Right testicular vein
FJ3618.details: Arises from the pampiniform plexus in the spermatic cord, ascends through the inguinal canal and retroperitoneum, and opens directly into the inferior vena cava below the renal vein.
FJ3618.clinicalCondition: Right-sided varicocele red flag — a new isolated right varicocele suggests retroperitoneal mass or caval obstruction.
FJ3618.clinicalScenario: A 55-year-old man presents with a new right varicocele that does not empty when lying down; abdominal imaging is arranged to exclude a retroperitoneal tumor.

FJ2306.name: Right thoracodorsal vein
FJ2306.details: Accompanies the thoracodorsal artery and nerve on the deep surface of latissimus dorsi; drains into the subscapular vein and forms part of the flap's pedicle.
FJ2306.clinicalCondition: Latissimus dorsi flap viability — the thoracodorsal pedicle, including this vein, must be preserved in reconstructive surgery.
FJ2306.clinicalScenario: During breast reconstruction with a latissimus dorsi flap, the surgeon protects the thoracodorsal vein within the pedicle to ensure venous drainage of the transferred flap.

FJ2312.name: Right ulnar vein
FJ2312.details: One of the paired venae comitantes of the ulnar artery; drains the medial forearm and superficial palmar arch region into the brachial vein near the elbow.
FJ2312.clinicalCondition: Forearm hematoma after ulnar arterial puncture — companion veins are easily injured during blood gas sampling.
FJ2312.clinicalScenario: Following repeated ulnar-side punctures for arterial blood gases, a patient develops a tender forearm swelling; ultrasound shows venous hematoma without pseudoaneurysm.

FJ1985.name: Set of anterior intercostal veins
FJ1985.details: Series of small veins draining the anterior ends of the intercostal spaces; they empty into the internal thoracic and musculophrenic veins of each side.
FJ1985.clinicalCondition: Chest-wall collateral dilatation — these veins enlarge visibly in superior vena cava syndrome.
FJ1985.clinicalScenario: A patient with a mediastinal tumor shows engorged anterior intercostal and chest-wall veins among the collateral signs of superior vena cava obstruction.

FJ1994.name: Set of anterior intercostal veins
FJ1994.details: Accompany the anterior intercostal branches of the internal thoracic artery in the upper spaces; valved channels directing flow toward the brachiocephalic system.
FJ1994.clinicalCondition: Bleeding during internal thoracic artery harvest — anterior intercostal tributaries must be clipped as the pedicle is mobilized.
FJ1994.clinicalScenario: During coronary bypass surgery, the surgeon clips several anterior intercostal veins while skeletonizing the internal thoracic artery to prevent postoperative chest-wall hematoma.

FJ2185.name: Set of dorsal digital veins
FJ2185.details: Small veins on the dorsum of the toes draining into the dorsal metatarsal veins and the dorsal venous arch of the foot.
FJ2185.clinicalCondition: Emergency venous access — dorsal foot veins are used for cannulation in infants and shocked children.
FJ2185.clinicalScenario: A dehydrated toddler with collapsed arm veins receives intravenous fluids through a cannula placed in a dorsal digital vein of the foot.

FJ2198.name: Set of dorsal digital veins
FJ2198.details: Form a visible network over the toes and dorsum of the foot; communicate with plantar veins through perforating channels around the foot margins.
FJ2198.clinicalCondition: Dorsal foot vein assessment in edema — engorgement helps distinguish venous insufficiency from lymphatic swelling.
FJ2198.clinicalScenario: Examining a patient with chronic leg swelling, the clinician notes prominent dorsal digital veins and pitting edema, favoring venous rather than lymphatic disease.

FJ2100.name: Set of perforating veins
FJ2100.details: Short veins piercing the deep fascia to connect superficial and deep veins of the leg; their valves normally direct flow inward, from superficial to deep.
FJ2100.clinicalCondition: Incompetent perforators — reversed flow feeds varicose veins and sustains venous hypertension.
FJ2100.clinicalScenario: Duplex scanning in a patient with varicose veins shows an incompetent medial calf perforator jetting blood outward into the great saphenous tributaries during calf compression.

FJ2119.name: Set of perforating veins
FJ2119.details: Includes the medial ankle (Cockett) perforators linking the posterior arch vein to the posterior tibial veins behind the medial malleolus.
FJ2119.clinicalCondition: Venous ulceration at the gaiter area — failed Cockett perforators transmit high pressure to ankle skin.
FJ2119.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman has a chronic ulcer just above the medial malleolus; duplex maps incompetent Cockett perforators beneath the ulcer bed.

FJ2138.name: Set of perforating veins
FJ2138.details: Includes Boyd perforators at the upper medial calf connecting the great saphenous vein to the posterior tibial veins below the knee.
FJ2138.clinicalCondition: Below-knee varicosities from Boyd perforator reflux — a common duplex finding in recurrent varicose veins.
FJ2138.clinicalScenario: After previous varicose vein surgery, a patient returns with new below-knee varicosities; scanning identifies a refluxing Boyd perforator as the source.

FJ2174.name: Set of perforating veins
FJ2174.details: Includes Dodd perforators of the mid-thigh linking the great saphenous vein to the femoral vein through the adductor canal region.
FJ2174.clinicalCondition: Thigh varicosities and recurrence — an untreated incompetent Dodd perforator refills stripped saphenous tributaries.
FJ2174.clinicalScenario: A patient with recurrent mid-thigh varicosities after saphenous ablation is found to have a large incompetent Dodd perforator requiring targeted treatment.

FJ2192.name: Set of perforating veins
FJ2192.details: Posterior calf perforators connect the small saphenous system to the fibular and posterior tibial veins through the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.
FJ2192.clinicalCondition: Post-thrombotic perforator incompetence — valve destruction after DVT drives skin changes and ulceration.
FJ2192.clinicalScenario: Years after a deep vein thrombosis, a patient develops lipodermatosclerosis and a calf ulcer; duplex shows multiple incompetent posterior perforating veins.

FJ2120.name: Set of plantar digital veins
FJ2120.details: Small veins draining the plantar surface of the toes into the plantar metatarsal veins and deep plantar venous arch of the sole.
FJ2120.clinicalCondition: Plantar venous pump function — weight-bearing empties these veins, aiding venous return from the foot.
FJ2120.clinicalScenario: An immobile patient after hip surgery develops dependent foot edema; passive ankle pumps are prescribed to activate the plantar venous pump and assist drainage.

FJ2175.name: Set of plantar digital veins
FJ2175.details: Lie deep in the sole alongside the plantar digital arteries and nerves; drain toward the venae comitantes of the posterior tibial artery.
FJ2175.clinicalCondition: Plantar hematoma in anticoagulated patients — bleeding into the sole causes deep, throbbing foot pain.
FJ2175.clinicalScenario: A patient on anticoagulants steps on a sharp stone and later presents with a tense, painful sole swelling from a plantar venous hematoma.

FJ3639.name: Sigmoid vein
FJ3639.details: Drains the sigmoid colon, following the sigmoid arteries in the sigmoid mesocolon, and empties into the inferior mesenteric vein, hence into the portal system.
FJ3639.clinicalCondition: Pylephlebitis — septic thrombophlebitis of portal tributaries complicating diverticulitis, seeding liver abscesses.
FJ3639.clinicalScenario: A patient treated for sigmoid diverticulitis returns with rigors and jaundice; imaging shows thrombosis extending from the sigmoid vein and multiple small liver abscesses.

FJ2724.name: Small cardiac vein
FJ2724.details: Runs in the coronary sulcus between the right atrium and ventricle with the right coronary artery; drains the right heart borders into the coronary sinus near its termination.
FJ2724.clinicalCondition: Coronary venous mapping for device leads — its course matters when cannulating the coronary sinus.
FJ2724.clinicalScenario: During CRT device implantation, contrast injected into the coronary sinus outlines the small cardiac vein, helping the operator orient within the coronary venous tree.

FJ2731.name: Small cardiac vein
FJ2731.details: Accompanies the right coronary artery from the acute margin of the heart; occasionally drains directly into the right atrium instead of the coronary sinus.
FJ2731.clinicalCondition: Variant drainage in retrograde cardioplegia — anomalous openings reduce cardioplegia delivery to the right heart.
FJ2731.clinicalScenario: During coronary bypass surgery, the surgeon notes poor right-sided cardioplegia distribution and suspects a variant small cardiac vein opening directly into the atrium.

FJ3641.name: Splenic vein
FJ3641.details: Formed by tributaries at the splenic hilum; runs behind the pancreas receiving the inferior mesenteric vein, and joins the superior mesenteric vein behind the pancreatic neck to form the portal vein.
FJ3641.clinicalCondition: Sinistral portal hypertension — splenic vein thrombosis in pancreatitis causes isolated gastric varices with a normal liver.
FJ3641.clinicalScenario: A patient with chronic pancreatitis vomits blood; endoscopy shows isolated gastric fundal varices and splenomegaly from splenic vein thrombosis, with normal liver function.

FJ2208.name: Superficial dorsal vein of penis
FJ2208.details: Midline superficial vein in the dartos layer of the penis draining skin and prepuce; bifurcates toward the external pudendal veins and ultimately the great saphenous veins.
FJ2208.clinicalCondition: Superficial vein rupture mimicking penile fracture — sudden hematoma without tunica albuginea tear.
FJ2208.clinicalScenario: A man presents after intercourse with rapid penile swelling and bruising but no popping sensation; examination suggests ruptured superficial dorsal vein rather than true fracture.

FJ2937.name: Superior lingular vein
FJ2937.details: Drains the superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe; runs below the lingular bronchus and opens into the left superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2937.clinicalCondition: Lingular segmentectomy planning — the vein marks the lower boundary of the lingular division.
FJ2937.clinicalScenario: Before left upper lobe surgery, 3D-CT traces the superior lingular vein to plan a lingulectomy sparing the upper division segments.

FJ2938.name: Superior lingular vein
FJ2938.details: Tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein lying in the fissure between the lingula and the upper division; variable branching is common.
FJ2938.clinicalCondition: Venous variation in left upper lobectomy — unrecognized variant tributaries are a source of hilar bleeding.
FJ2938.clinicalScenario: During video-assisted left upper lobectomy, a variant lingular vein branch is encountered behind the bronchus and clipped carefully before division.

FJ3647.name: Superior mesenteric vein
FJ3647.details: Formed in the root of the mesentery by tributaries draining the midgut; ascends anterior to the third part of the duodenum and joins the splenic vein behind the neck of the pancreas.
FJ3647.clinicalCondition: Mesenteric venous thrombosis — causes bowel ischemia with pain out of proportion to examination findings.
FJ3647.clinicalScenario: A woman with a thrombophilia develops severe central abdominal pain with a benign examination; CT shows superior mesenteric vein thrombosis and thickened jejunal loops.

FJ3030.name: Superior part of medial segmental vein
FJ3030.details: Upper subsegmental tributary of the medial segmental vein of the right middle lobe; drains into the middle lobe vein and thence the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3030.clinicalCondition: Middle lobe segmentectomy planning — subsegmental venous branches define the S5 resection plane.
FJ3030.clinicalScenario: For a small middle lobe nodule, preoperative mapping identifies the superior part of the medial segmental vein to guide a medial segmentectomy.

FJ3027.name: Superior part of right anterior segmental vein
FJ3027.details: Upper tributary of the anterior segmental vein (V3) of the right upper lobe; drains the apex-adjacent part of the anterior segment into the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ3027.clinicalCondition: Anterior segmentectomy anatomy — V3 tributaries cross the intersegmental plane used in S3 resection.
FJ3027.clinicalScenario: Planning an anterior segmentectomy for early lung cancer, the surgeon reviews the branching of V3 on CT to avoid congesting the preserved apical segment.

FJ3648.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3648.details: Small vein draining the superior surface of the diaphragm; accompanies the pericardiacophrenic vessels and empties into the brachiocephalic or internal thoracic vein.
FJ3648.clinicalCondition: Phrenic nerve region surgery — these vessels run with the nerve and bleed during pericardial dissection.
FJ3648.clinicalScenario: During pericardiectomy for constrictive pericarditis, the surgeon controls small superior phrenic veins while carefully preserving the phrenic nerve on the pericardium.

FJ3649.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3649.details: One of several fine veins on the thoracic surface of the diaphragm, forming part of the diaphragmatic venous network linking thoracic and abdominal drainage.
FJ3649.clinicalCondition: Collateral flow in caval obstruction — diaphragmatic veins participate in thoracoabdominal collateral pathways.
FJ3649.clinicalScenario: Imaging in a patient with inferior vena cava occlusion shows enhanced diaphragmatic venous collaterals, including superior phrenic channels, carrying blood toward the thorax.

FJ3650.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3650.details: Travels with the pericardiacophrenic branch of the internal thoracic artery along the lateral pericardium, lateral to the phrenic nerve's terminal branches.
FJ3650.clinicalCondition: Dilated pericardiacophrenic vein mimicking lymphadenopathy — a radiological pitfall on chest CT.
FJ3650.clinicalScenario: A CT report queries an enlarged mediastinal node; review shows the opacity is actually a dilated pericardiacophrenic–superior phrenic vein in a patient with raised central venous pressure.

FJ3651.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3651.details: Drains the central tendon region of the diaphragm; its tributaries communicate with inferior phrenic veins draining to the inferior vena cava.
FJ3651.clinicalCondition: Bleeding in diaphragmatic hernia repair — torn diaphragmatic veins complicate reduction of herniated viscera.
FJ3651.clinicalScenario: Repairing a traumatic diaphragmatic rupture, the surgeon encounters venous bleeding from the torn diaphragmatic edge, controlled with sutures through the muscle.

FJ3652.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3652.details: Minute vein on the diaphragm's thoracic aspect; part of the network anastomosing with intercostal and musculophrenic veins.
FJ3652.clinicalCondition: Venous engorgement in constrictive physiology — raised venous pressures distend diaphragmatic veins visibly at surgery.
FJ3652.clinicalScenario: At operation for constrictive pericarditis, the surgical team notes engorged superior phrenic and pericardial veins reflecting chronically elevated central venous pressure.

FJ3653.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3653.details: Accompanies small arterial twigs to the diaphragm from the pericardiacophrenic and musculophrenic arteries; drains toward the brachiocephalic system.
FJ3653.clinicalCondition: Thoracentesis landmark region — diaphragmatic vessels lie below the safe intercostal approach and are avoided by correct site selection.
FJ3653.clinicalScenario: A trainee performing pleural drainage is reminded to insert above the rib's upper border and stay off the diaphragm, protecting intercostal and diaphragmatic vessels.

FJ3654.name: Superior phrenic vein
FJ3654.details: Contributes to drainage of the fibrous pericardium's diaphragmatic part; its channels cross the central tendon with the phrenic nerve branches.
FJ3654.clinicalCondition: Phrenic nerve injury risk zone — dissection near these veins during cardiac surgery can damage the nerve.
FJ3654.clinicalScenario: After coronary bypass surgery, a patient has an elevated right hemidiaphragm from phrenic nerve injury sustained while dissecting near the pericardiacophrenic vessels.

FJ3657.name: Superior rectal vein
FJ3657.details: Drains the upper rectum and anal canal above the pectinate line into the inferior mesenteric vein; anastomoses with middle and inferior rectal veins, forming a portosystemic shunt.
FJ3657.clinicalCondition: Rectal varices in portal hypertension — this collateral dilates and can bleed massively, distinct from hemorrhoids.
FJ3657.clinicalScenario: A cirrhotic patient passes large-volume rectal blood; colonoscopy reveals bleeding rectal varices supplied through the superior rectal vein, treated with banding and portal pressure reduction.

FJ3645.name: Superior vena cava
FJ3645.details: Formed by the union of the two brachiocephalic veins behind the first costal cartilage; descends about 7 cm, receives the azygos vein, and enters the right atrium at the third costal cartilage.
FJ3645.clinicalCondition: Superior vena cava syndrome — tumor compression causes facial swelling, distended neck veins and venous congestion of the arms.
FJ3645.clinicalScenario: A heavy smoker develops a swollen face, engorged neck veins and headache worse on bending; CT shows a right hilar mass compressing the superior vena cava.

FJ1867.name: Tributary of middle hepatic vein
FJ1867.details: Small intrahepatic branch draining segments IV, V or VIII into the middle hepatic vein, which runs in the main lobar fissure toward the vena cava.
FJ1867.clinicalCondition: Hepatic resection planning — middle hepatic tributaries determine how much drainage the remnant liver keeps.
FJ1867.clinicalScenario: Before an extended right hepatectomy, 3D imaging maps middle hepatic vein tributaries so the left remnant retains adequate venous outflow.

FJ2113.name: Tributary of plantar venous arch
FJ2113.details: Small vein feeding the deep plantar venous arch in the sole; the arch drains into the medial and lateral plantar veins and then the posterior tibial veins.
FJ2113.clinicalCondition: Plantar vein thrombosis — an under-recognized cause of acute plantar foot pain mimicking fasciitis.
FJ2113.clinicalScenario: A runner develops sharp pain along the sole without trauma; ultrasound shows thrombosis in a tributary of the plantar venous arch rather than plantar fasciitis.

FJ2115.name: Tributary of plantar venous arch
FJ2115.details: Part of the deep venous network of the sole compressed during weight-bearing, forming the plantar venous pump that propels blood upward.
FJ2115.clinicalCondition: Venous pump failure in immobility — loss of the foot pump contributes to dependent edema and stasis.
FJ2115.clinicalScenario: A patient in a prolonged bed-rest protocol develops bilateral foot edema; intermittent pneumatic foot compression is used to substitute for the plantar venous pump.

FJ2160.name: Tributary of plantar venous arch
FJ2160.details: Connects the plantar arch with perforating veins to the dorsal foot network, balancing drainage between sole and dorsum.
FJ2160.clinicalCondition: Midfoot injury bleeding — Lisfranc fracture-dislocations tear deep plantar vessels causing compartment-threatening hematoma.
FJ2160.clinicalScenario: After a crush injury with Lisfranc disruption, a patient's midfoot swells tense and painful from deep plantar venous bleeding, prompting urgent compartment assessment.

FJ2165.name: Tributary of plantar venous arch
FJ2165.details: Drains the deep intrinsic muscles of the sole into the plantar arch; valves in the network direct flow toward the posterior tibial system.
FJ2165.clinicalCondition: Diabetic foot venous congestion — microvascular and venous dysfunction worsen healing of plantar ulcers.
FJ2165.clinicalScenario: A diabetic patient with a chronic plantar ulcer shows dusky, congested forefoot skin; vascular review identifies venous insufficiency of the deep plantar network among the causes.

FJ3102.name: Trunk of left portal vein
FJ3102.details: Main stem of the left portal branch, comprising transverse and umbilical parts; runs in the fissure for the ligamentum teres and supplies segments II, III and IV.
FJ3102.clinicalCondition: Rex shunt target — the umbilical part is the recipient vessel in mesenterico-left portal bypass for pediatric portal vein obstruction.
FJ3102.clinicalScenario: A child with extrahepatic portal vein cavernoma and variceal bleeding is assessed for a Rex shunt anastomosing a mesenteric graft to the trunk of the left portal vein.

FJ3031.name: Trunk of right apical segmental vein
FJ3031.details: Main stem draining the apical segment (S1) of the right upper lobe before joining the right superior pulmonary vein; runs below the apical bronchus.
FJ3031.clinicalCondition: Apical segmentectomy planning — the trunk is the venous landmark for isolating S1.
FJ3031.clinicalScenario: For a small apical lung cancer, imaging maps the trunk of the right apical segmental vein so the surgeon can perform a precise S1 segmentectomy.

FJ3122.name: Trunk of right portal vein
FJ3122.details: Short main stem of the right portal branch within the right lobe hilum before it divides into anterior and posterior sectoral branches supplying segments V–VIII.
FJ3122.clinicalCondition: Portal vein embolization — occluding this trunk redirects flow to grow the future liver remnant before major hepatectomy.
FJ3122.clinicalScenario: Before an extended right hepatectomy for colorectal metastases, interventional radiology embolizes the trunk of the right portal vein to hypertrophy the left lobe.

FJ2435.name: Anterior cusp of aortic valve
