FJ1832.details: Septal region beneath the rostrum of the corpus callosum, containing septal nuclei interconnecting hippocampus, hypothalamus, and brainstem; part of the limbic reward and arousal circuitry.
FJ1832.clinicalCondition: Cavum septum pellucidum — a common midline variant of this region, usually incidental but reported more often after repetitive head impacts.
FJ1832.clinicalScenario: A boxer's brain MRI incidentally shows a cavum septum pellucidum; neurologists counsel him about cumulative head-injury risks.

FJ1319.name: Short ciliary nerve
FJ1319.details: Six to ten fine branches radiating from the ciliary ganglion to pierce the sclera around the optic nerve, carrying parasympathetic, sympathetic, and sensory fibers to the globe.
FJ1319.clinicalCondition: Retrobulbar block effect — anesthetic deposited near these nerves produces akinesia and anesthesia of the globe for eye surgery.
FJ1319.clinicalScenario: Before cataract surgery, an ophthalmologist's peribulbar injection bathes the short ciliary nerves, leaving the eye painless and still.

FJ1370.name: Short ciliary nerve
FJ1370.details: Postganglionic branches conveying parasympathetic fibers to sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle, sympathetic fibers to ocular vessels and dilator, plus sensory fibers from the cornea and uvea.
FJ1370.clinicalCondition: Postganglionic tonic pupil — selective injury to these fibers denervates the sphincter, producing Adie pupil supersensitivity to dilute pilocarpine.
FJ1370.clinicalScenario: A dilated pupil that ignores light constricts briskly to weak 0.1% pilocarpine drops, confirming postganglionic denervation.

FJ1825.name: Stria terminalis
FJ1825.details: Principal output tract of the amygdala, arching through the floor of the lateral ventricle's body in the terminal sulcus to reach the septal area, hypothalamus, and bed nucleus.
FJ1825.clinicalCondition: Sustained anxiety circuitry — its bed nucleus mediates long-duration threat responses, a research target in anxiety disorders.
FJ1825.clinicalScenario: A patient with panic disorder shows exaggerated bed-nucleus activation during unpredictable-threat tasks in a research MRI study.

FJ1321.name: Superior branch of left oculomotor nerve
FJ1321.details: Upper division of CN III entering the left orbit through the superior orbital fissure; supplies the superior rectus and levator palpebrae superioris muscles only.
FJ1321.clinicalCondition: Divisional third nerve palsy — isolated superior-division lesions (orbital apex, cavernous sinus) cause ptosis with failure of elevation.
FJ1321.clinicalScenario: A woman with an orbital apex mass cannot lift her left eyelid or look up, while downward gaze and pupil size remain normal.

FJ1372.name: Superior branch of right oculomotor nerve
FJ1372.details: Right upper division of the third nerve; motor supply limited to superior rectus and levator palpebrae superioris, explaining the pattern of divisional palsies.
FJ1372.clinicalCondition: Partial ptosis diagnosis — superior division involvement separates levator weakness from the complete ptosis of a full CN III lesion.
FJ1372.clinicalScenario: A patient after cavernous sinus surgery has a drooping right lid and weak upgaze but normal pupil and other eye movements.

FJ1843.name: Tentorium cerebelli
FJ1843.details: Crescentic dural fold roofing the cerebellum and supporting the occipital lobes; its free edge forms the tentorial notch around the midbrain, and its margins enclose the transverse and superior petrosal sinuses.
FJ1843.clinicalCondition: Uncal (transtentorial) herniation — the temporal uncus forced over its edge compresses CN III and the midbrain, dilating the pupil.
FJ1843.clinicalScenario: A head-injured patient's right pupil suddenly blows and he postures; CT confirms uncal herniation over the tentorial edge from a temporal hematoma.

FJ1780.name: Tuber cinereum
FJ1780.details: Raised area of grey matter in the hypothalamic floor between the optic chiasm and mammillary bodies; the median eminence and pituitary infundibulum arise from it.
FJ1780.clinicalCondition: Hypothalamic hamartoma — congenital mass here causes gelastic seizures and precocious puberty.
FJ1780.clinicalScenario: A five-year-old with brief laughing spells and early puberty has a sessile mass at the tuber cinereum on MRI.

FJ1828.name: Tuber cinereum
FJ1828.details: Part of the floor of the third ventricle behind the infundibulum; hypothalamic tissue regulating autonomic and endocrine function, continuous with the pituitary stalk.
FJ1828.clinicalCondition: Craniopharyngioma — suprasellar tumor compresses this region, causing endocrine failure and visual loss.
FJ1828.clinicalScenario: A teenager with growth failure and bitemporal hemianopia has a calcified suprasellar mass pressing on the hypothalamic floor.

FJ1758.name: White matter of left cerebral hemisphere
FJ1758.details: Myelinated axon tracts: projection fibers (corona radiata, internal capsule), commissural fibers (corpus callosum), and association fibers connecting cortical and subcortical regions.
FJ1758.clinicalCondition: Multiple sclerosis — autoimmune demyelination forms periventricular white-matter plaques.
FJ1758.clinicalScenario: A young woman with optic neuritis and leg weakness shows perivenular left hemispheric white-matter lesions on MRI.

FJ1806.name: White matter of right cerebral hemisphere
FJ1806.details: Myelinated projection, commissural, and association tracts of the right hemisphere; the internal capsule conveys corticospinal fibers, and U-fibers link adjacent gyri.
FJ1806.clinicalCondition: Small-vessel ischemic disease — chronic white-matter rarefaction causes cognitive slowing and gait disturbance.
FJ1806.clinicalScenario: An elderly hypertensive with declining memory has confluent right hemispheric white-matter hyperintensities on MRI.

FJ1282.name: Anterior chamber of left eyeball
FJ1282.details: Space between cornea and iris/lens filled with aqueous humor produced by ciliary processes; drains via trabecular meshwork into canal of Schlemm, maintaining intraocular pressure.
FJ1282.clinicalCondition: Acute angle-closure glaucoma — shallow chamber lets iris block outflow, sharply raising intraocular pressure.
FJ1282.clinicalScenario: A 65-year-old woman has severe left eye pain, haloes around lights, a mid-dilated pupil and a rock-hard eyeball; emergency pressure-lowering treatment follows.

FJ1332.name: Anterior chamber of right eyeball
FJ1332.details: Aqueous-filled space bounded by cornea anteriorly and iris and lens posteriorly; its depth is assessed at the slit lamp and narrows with age and hypermetropia.
FJ1332.clinicalCondition: Hyphema — blunt trauma ruptures iris vessels, layering blood in the chamber with rebleed risk.
FJ1332.clinicalScenario: A teenager struck by a cricket ball has a visible blood level in the right anterior chamber and is nursed head-up to prevent rebleeding.

FJ1755.name: Choroid plexus of cerebral hemisphere
FJ1755.details: Tuft of fenestrated capillaries covered by ependymal epithelium projecting into the lateral ventricle; secretes most cerebrospinal fluid by active transport of ions and water.
FJ1755.clinicalCondition: Choroid plexus papilloma — benign tumor overproducing CSF, causing hydrocephalus especially in young children.
FJ1755.clinicalScenario: A toddler presents with rapidly enlarging head circumference, vomiting and a frond-like intraventricular mass on MRI; excision cures the hydrocephalus.

FJ1803.name: Choroid plexus of cerebral hemisphere
FJ1803.details: The mirror-image plexus of the opposite lateral ventricle, extending from the interventricular foramen through body, atrium and inferior horn; continuous with plexus of the third ventricle.
FJ1803.clinicalCondition: Choroid plexus cyst — common incidental prenatal ultrasound finding, usually transient and clinically insignificant.
FJ1803.clinicalScenario: A routine anomaly scan shows a small cyst within the fetal choroid plexus; follow-up imaging confirms it has resolved without consequence.

FJ2811.name: External ear
FJ2811.details: Auricle of elastic cartilage covered by skin plus the external acoustic meatus leading to the tympanic membrane; collects and funnels sound, supplied by branches of external carotid artery.
FJ2811.clinicalCondition: Otitis externa — infection of canal skin causing pain, discharge and tenderness on tragus pressure.
FJ2811.clinicalScenario: A keen swimmer develops an itchy, painful, discharging ear with exquisite pain when the tragus is pressed; topical drops settle it.

FJ1471M.name: Flexor retinaculum of left wrist
FJ1471M.details: Strong fibrous band (transverse carpal ligament) bridging scaphoid/trapezium to pisiform/hamate, forming the carpal tunnel roof; nine flexor tendons and median nerve pass deep to it.
FJ1471M.clinicalCondition: Carpal tunnel syndrome — median nerve compression beneath the retinaculum causes nocturnal hand paresthesia.
FJ1471M.clinicalScenario: A pregnant woman wakes nightly with tingling in her left thumb, index and middle fingers; splinting and later steroid injection relieve symptoms.

FJ1471.name: Flexor retinaculum of right wrist
FJ1471.details: Fibrous roof of the carpal tunnel on the palmar wrist; the palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve passes superficial to it and is spared in tunnel compression.
FJ1471.clinicalCondition: Carpal tunnel syndrome — dominant hand usually affected first, progressing to thenar wasting if untreated.
FJ1471.clinicalScenario: A typist notices right-hand clumsiness and flattened thenar eminence; nerve conduction studies confirm severe compression and surgical release is performed.

FJ1285.name: Left choroid
FJ1285.details: Vascular, melanin-pigmented layer between sclera and retina containing the choriocapillaris; supplies the outer retina and retinal pigment epithelium and absorbs stray light.
FJ1285.clinicalCondition: Choroidal melanoma — commonest primary intraocular malignancy in adults, risking metastasis to the liver.
FJ1285.clinicalScenario: A pigmented dome-shaped fundus mass with orange pigment is found at a routine eye test; ultrasound confirms melanoma and oncology referral follows.

FJ1286.name: Left choroid
FJ1286.details: Second mesh of the same vascular tunic; its fenestrated choriocapillaris supports the metabolically active photoreceptors, and Bruch's membrane separates it from the pigment epithelium.
FJ1286.clinicalCondition: Choroiditis — inflammatory foci, often granulomatous, damaging overlying retina and blurring vision.
FJ1286.clinicalScenario: A patient with sarcoidosis reports floaters and blurred left vision; fundus examination shows multifocal choroidal granulomas requiring immunosuppression.

FJ1291.name: Left common tendinous ring
FJ1291.details: Annulus of Zinn, a fibrous ring at the orbital apex encircling the optic canal and medial superior orbital fissure; origin of the four rectus muscles.
FJ1291.clinicalCondition: Orbital apex syndrome — apical lesions injure cranial nerves II, III, IV and VI together.
FJ1291.clinicalScenario: A diabetic with invasive fungal sinusitis loses left vision and develops total ophthalmoplegia with a fixed dilated pupil, indicating orbital apex involvement.

FJ1289.name: Left cornea
FJ1289.details: Transparent avascular anterior window of the eye providing about two-thirds of its refractive power; five layers including a non-regenerating endothelium that keeps it dehydrated and clear.
FJ1289.clinicalCondition: Keratoconus — progressive corneal thinning and cone-like ectasia producing irregular astigmatism in young people.
FJ1289.clinicalScenario: A teenager's glasses prescription keeps changing; corneal topography shows steepening and thinning consistent with keratoconus, managed with rigid contact lenses.

FJ1287.name: Left corona ciliaris
FJ1287.details: Ring of roughly seventy radial ciliary processes (pars plicata) whose double epithelium secretes aqueous humor; zonular fibers arise between the processes to suspend the lens.
FJ1287.clinicalCondition: Refractory glaucoma — ablating these processes by cyclophotocoagulation reduces aqueous production when drainage surgery fails.
FJ1287.clinicalScenario: A painful, nearly blind glaucomatous eye with uncontrolled pressure is treated with diode laser cyclophotocoagulation to the ciliary processes, easing pain.

FJ1297.name: Left iris
FJ1297.details: Pigmented muscular diaphragm regulating pupil size: sphincter pupillae driven by parasympathetic fibers of cranial nerve III, dilator pupillae by sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion.
FJ1297.clinicalCondition: Acute anterior uveitis — iris inflammation causing photophobia, miosis and posterior synechiae if untreated.
FJ1297.clinicalScenario: A young man with ankylosing spondylitis has a painful red left eye, small irregular pupil and cells in the anterior chamber; steroids are started.

FJ3265.name: Left lacrimal bone
FJ3265.details: Small thin bone in the anterior medial orbital wall; with the frontal process of maxilla it forms the lacrimal fossa housing the lacrimal sac.
FJ3265.clinicalCondition: Medial orbital wall fracture — the paper-thin bone breaks in trauma, risking sac injury and epiphora.
FJ3265.clinicalScenario: After an assault, a patient has medial orbital crepitus and persistent tearing; CT shows a fractured lacrimal bone with emphysema.

FJ1298.name: Left lacrimal canaliculus
FJ1298.details: Short channel, about 10 mm, running from the lacrimal punctum (vertical then horizontal parts) through the eyelid margin to join the lacrimal sac; conveys tears medially.
FJ1298.clinicalCondition: Canaliculitis — chronic Actinomyces infection producing recurrent conjunctivitis and expressible yellow sulfur granules.
FJ1298.clinicalScenario: A woman with months of unilateral red eye and mattering has gritty concretions expressed from the left upper punctum, confirming canaliculitis.

FJ1299.name: Left lacrimal gland
FJ1299.details: Serous gland in the superolateral orbit, divided by levator palpebrae into orbital and palpebral parts; secretes aqueous tears under parasympathetic control via the pterygopalatine ganglion.
FJ1299.clinicalCondition: Dacryoadenitis — acute gland inflammation causing painful superolateral swelling and an S-shaped eyelid.
FJ1299.clinicalScenario: A young woman develops a tender, swollen outer upper left eyelid with fever after mumps exposure; examination confirms lacrimal gland inflammation.

FJ1301.name: Left lacrimal lake
FJ1301.details: Small pool where tears collect at the medial canthus around the lacrimal caruncle before entering the puncta; the normal endpoint of the tear film's medial drainage sweep.
FJ1301.clinicalCondition: Epiphora — failure of drainage makes the lake overflow, spilling tears onto the cheek.
FJ1301.clinicalScenario: An elderly man complains of constant tearing from the left eye with a visibly brimming medial tear lake; syringing reveals nasolacrimal blockage.

FJ1309.name: Left lacrimal sac
FJ1309.details: Upper dilated end of the nasolacrimal duct lying in the lacrimal fossa below the medial canthal tendon; receives canaliculi and pumps tears downward during blinking.
FJ1309.clinicalCondition: Dacryocystitis — sac infection causing painful swelling below the medial canthal tendon with reflux.
FJ1309.clinicalScenario: A woman presses a tender swelling below her left medial canthus and mucopus refluxes through the punctum, confirming acute dacryocystitis.

FJ1305.name: Left lens
FJ1305.details: Biconvex transparent structure behind the iris, suspended by zonules; ciliary muscle contraction relaxes zonules so the elastic lens rounds up for near accommodation.
FJ1305.clinicalCondition: Cataract — progressive lens opacification, the commonest reversible cause of visual impairment worldwide.
FJ1305.clinicalScenario: A 72-year-old reports painless gradual blurring and glare from headlights; slit-lamp examination shows a dense nuclear cataract in the left eye.

FJ1302.name: Left nasolacrimal duct
FJ1302.details: Membranous channel descending within the bony nasolacrimal canal from sac to open beneath the inferior nasal turbinate at the valve of Hasner; final tear drainage pathway.
FJ1302.clinicalCondition: Congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction — imperforate valve of Hasner causes infant epiphora, usually resolving spontaneously.
FJ1302.clinicalScenario: An eight-month-old has had a watery, sticky left eye since birth; lacrimal sac massage is taught and the tearing resolves by one year.

FJ1317.name: Left sclera
FJ1317.details: Tough white fibrous coat forming the posterior five-sixths of the eyeball; protects the globe, maintains shape and receives insertions of the extraocular muscles.
FJ1317.clinicalCondition: Scleritis — deep, boring ocular pain, often linked to rheumatoid arthritis, threatening vision.
FJ1317.clinicalScenario: A patient with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis describes severe night-time left eye pain radiating to the jaw, with a violaceous scleral hue.

FJ1331.name: Left vitreous body
FJ1331.details: Clear gel of collagen and hyaluronic acid filling the posterior segment behind the lens; attached firmly at the ora serrata, optic disc and macula, maintaining globe volume.
FJ1331.clinicalCondition: Posterior vitreous detachment — age-related gel liquefaction and separation causing floaters and photopsia.
FJ1331.clinicalScenario: A 62-year-old notices a sudden shower of floaters and flashes in the left eye; examination confirms vitreous detachment without retinal tear.

FJ1316.name: Optic part of left retina
FJ1316.details: Light-sensitive retinal layer containing rods and cones, extending from the ora serrata posteriorly to the optic disc; photoreceptors convert photons into signals relayed through bipolar and ganglion cells to the optic nerve.
FJ1316.clinicalCondition: Central retinal artery occlusion — sudden painless monocular blindness with pale retina and cherry-red spot.
FJ1316.clinicalScenario: A 74-year-old with atrial fibrillation loses left vision within seconds; fundoscopy shows a pale swollen retina with a cherry-red macula.

FJ1367.name: Optic part of right retina
FJ1367.details: Photoreceptor-bearing retina of the right eye supplied by the central retinal artery and drained by the central retinal vein; the fovea at its posterior pole mediates acuity.
FJ1367.clinicalCondition: Diabetic retinopathy — chronic hyperglycemia damages retinal capillaries causing microaneurysms, hemorrhages and neovascularization.
FJ1367.clinicalScenario: Screening photographs of a long-standing diabetic reveal blot hemorrhages and hard exudates in the right fundus, prompting laser referral.

FJ1336.name: Right choroid
FJ1336.details: Vascular pigmented tunic of the right eye nourishing the outer retina; choroidal blood flow per gram exceeds that of most tissues, also dissipating heat from photoreceptors.
FJ1336.clinicalCondition: Choroidal metastasis — commonest intraocular malignancy overall, typically seeding from breast or lung primaries.
FJ1336.clinicalScenario: A woman treated for breast cancer reports blurred right vision; fundoscopy shows creamy multifocal choroidal deposits consistent with metastases.

FJ1337.name: Right choroid
FJ1337.details: Second mesh of the right choroid; its large vessels (Haller layer) lie externally, medium vessels (Sattler layer) internally, against Bruch's membrane and the choriocapillaris.
FJ1337.clinicalCondition: Choroidal rupture — blunt trauma tears choroid and Bruch's membrane, causing subretinal hemorrhage and scotoma.
FJ1337.clinicalScenario: After a squash ball injury, a man has reduced right acuity and a crescentic subretinal hemorrhage concentric with the optic disc.

FJ1342.name: Right common tendinous ring
FJ1342.details: Annulus of Zinn at the right orbital apex, giving origin to the rectus muscles; the optic nerve, ophthalmic artery and nerves III and VI pass through it.
FJ1342.clinicalCondition: Superior orbital fissure syndrome — fissure lesions paralyze III, IV, VI and V1 sparing vision.
FJ1342.clinicalScenario: Following facial fractures, a patient has right ophthalmoplegia, ptosis and forehead numbness but normal vision, localizing the lesion to the fissure.

FJ1340.name: Right cornea
FJ1340.details: Avascular transparent dome continuous with the sclera at the limbus; nourished by tears, aqueous and limbal vessels, and densely innervated by the ophthalmic division of trigeminal nerve.
FJ1340.clinicalCondition: Bacterial keratitis — contact-lens-related Pseudomonas ulcer causing pain, infiltrate and threatened perforation.
FJ1340.clinicalScenario: A soft contact lens wearer who sleeps in lenses wakes with a painful red right eye and white corneal infiltrate; intensive antibiotics begin.

FJ1338.name: Right corona ciliaris
FJ1338.details: Ring of ciliary processes of the right eye whose non-pigmented epithelium actively secretes aqueous humor; processes increase surface area and anchor the suspensory zonular fibers.
FJ1338.clinicalCondition: Ciliary body melanoma — hidden tumor behind the iris presenting late with sentinel vessels or glaucoma.
FJ1338.clinicalScenario: Ultrasound biomicroscopy in a man with unilateral right glaucoma and a dilated episcleral vessel reveals a ciliary body melanoma.

FJ1348.name: Right iris
FJ1348.details: Colored diaphragm whose sphincter and dilator muscles set pupil diameter; its posterior pigment epithelium prevents light scatter, and its root inserts into the ciliary body.
FJ1348.clinicalCondition: Horner syndrome — sympathetic interruption produces miosis, mild ptosis and facial anhidrosis.
FJ1348.clinicalScenario: A patient with an apical lung tumor develops a smaller right pupil, drooping lid and dry right face, confirming Horner syndrome.

FJ3371.name: Right lacrimal bone
FJ3371.details: Delicate bone forming the lacrimal fossa with the maxilla in the medial orbital wall; its posterior crest is a surgical landmark for the lacrimal sac.
FJ3371.clinicalCondition: Chronic dacryocystitis — treated by dacryocystorhinostomy, which windows through this bone into the nasal cavity.
FJ3371.clinicalScenario: Recurrent right sac infections lead to endoscopic dacryocystorhinostomy, creating a new drainage opening through the lacrimal bone into the nose.

FJ1349.name: Right lacrimal canaliculus
FJ1349.details: Tiny tear channel from the right upper and lower puncta converging toward the common canaliculus and sac; lies within the eyelid margin near the medial canthus.
FJ1349.clinicalCondition: Canalicular laceration — medial eyelid injuries sever it, requiring microscopic repair over a stent.
FJ1349.clinicalScenario: A dog bite tears a child's right medial lower lid; probing confirms canalicular division, repaired in theater with a silicone stent.

FJ1350.name: Right lacrimal gland
FJ1350.details: Almond-shaped serous gland above the lateral right eye producing the aqueous layer of tears; reflex secretion is driven by corneal sensation via trigeminal afferents and facial parasympathetics.
FJ1350.clinicalCondition: Sjögren syndrome — autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of lacrimal and salivary glands causing severe dryness.
FJ1350.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged woman with gritty right eye discomfort, dry mouth and parotid swelling tests positive for anti-Ro antibodies, confirming Sjögren syndrome.

FJ1352.name: Right lacrimal lake
FJ1352.details: Tear reservoir at the right medial canthus where blinking sweeps the tear film; puncta normally sit immersed in the lake to draw tears into the canaliculi.
FJ1352.clinicalCondition: Involutional ectropion — everted punctum leaves the lake, so tears cannot drain despite patent ducts.
FJ1352.clinicalScenario: An elderly man's everted right lower lid causes constant watering; examination shows the punctum turned away from the tear lake.

FJ1360.name: Right lacrimal sac
FJ1360.details: Blind upper pouch of the nasolacrimal duct cradled in the lacrimal fossa; orbicularis fibers (Horner's muscle) compress it during blinking to propel tears downward.
FJ1360.clinicalCondition: Lacrimal sac mucocele — duct blockage at both ends distends the sac into a painless swelling.
FJ1360.clinicalScenario: A painless, bluish swelling below the right medial canthus with watering proves on imaging to be a mucocoele of the lacrimal sac.

FJ1356.name: Right lens
FJ1356.details: Crystalline lens of layered fibers within an elastic capsule, devoid of blood supply; changes shape for accommodation and filters ultraviolet light protecting the retina.
FJ1356.clinicalCondition: Ectopia lentis — zonular failure in Marfan syndrome subluxates the lens upward and temporally.
FJ1356.clinicalScenario: A tall young man with arachnodactyly shows a superotemporally displaced right lens edge and tremulous iris, prompting cardiac screening for Marfan syndrome.

FJ1353.name: Right nasolacrimal duct
FJ1353.details: Drainage channel from the right lacrimal sac through the nasolacrimal canal to the inferior meatus; tears entering the nose explain why eye drops can be tasted.
FJ1353.clinicalCondition: Neonatal dacryocystocele — distended sac and duct at birth appearing as a bluish medial canthal mass.
FJ1353.clinicalScenario: A newborn has a tense bluish swelling below the right medial canthus and noisy breathing; urgent ENT review excludes intranasal extension.

FJ1368.name: Right sclera
FJ1368.details: Collagenous outer coat of the right globe, thinnest behind rectus insertions and perforated posteriorly at the lamina cribrosa where optic nerve fibers exit.
FJ1368.clinicalCondition: Episcleritis — benign superficial inflammation causing sectoral redness with only mild discomfort.
FJ1368.clinicalScenario: A young woman has a painless red patch on the right eye that blanches with phenylephrine drops, distinguishing episcleritis from scleritis.

FJ1382.name: Right vitreous body
FJ1382.details: Gel occupying about four milliliters of the posterior segment, 99 percent water with collagen fibrils and hyaluronan; formed in fetal life and never regenerated.
FJ1382.clinicalCondition: Vitreous hemorrhage — bleeding from fragile new vessels in proliferative diabetic retinopathy obscures vision.
FJ1382.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man reports a sudden shower of floaters and near-total right vision loss; ultrasound confirms dense vitreous hemorrhage.

FJ1320.name: Suspensory ligament of left lens
FJ1320.details: Zonule of Zinn: radial fibers from ciliary processes to the lens equator; ciliary contraction slackens them, letting the lens round for near focus.
FJ1320.clinicalCondition: Pseudoexfoliation syndrome — fibrillar deposits weaken zonules, risking lens subluxation and difficult cataract surgery.
FJ1320.clinicalScenario: During cataract assessment an elderly patient shows a tremulous left lens (phacodonesis) and white flakes on the pupil margin, warning of zonular weakness.

FJ1371.name: Suspensory ligament of right lens
FJ1371.details: Zonular fiber system anchoring the right lens to the ciliary body, maintaining centration and transmitting accommodative forces; fibers insert into the capsule around the equator.
FJ1371.clinicalCondition: Traumatic zonular dialysis — blunt injury tears fibers, subluxating the lens and causing monocular diplopia.
FJ1371.clinicalScenario: After a fist injury, a man sees double with one right eye alone and the lens edge is visible within the pupil.

FJ1328.name: Tarsal plate of left lower eyelid
FJ1328.details: Dense fibrous plate, about 4 mm high in the lower lid, giving the eyelid rigidity and shape; contains meibomian glands secreting the tear film's oily layer.
FJ1328.clinicalCondition: Chalazion — blocked meibomian gland within the plate forms a chronic painless lid lump.
FJ1328.clinicalScenario: A firm, painless nodule has sat in a woman's left lower lid for six weeks; incision and curettage of the chalazion is arranged.

FJ1324.name: Tarsal plate of left upper eyelid
FJ1324.details: Larger semilunar fibrous plate, about 10 mm high, stiffening the upper lid; its meibomian glands open at the lid margin and its conjunctival surface faces the cornea.
FJ1324.clinicalCondition: Internal hordeolum — acute staphylococcal infection of a meibomian gland produces a painful pointing abscess.
FJ1324.clinicalScenario: A painful swelling develops on the inner surface of a man's left upper lid; warm compresses are advised for the acute stye.

FJ1379.name: Tarsal plate of right lower eyelid
FJ1379.details: Fibrous skeleton of the right lower lid supported by canthal tendons; age-related laxity of plate and tendons destabilizes lid position against the globe.
FJ1379.clinicalCondition: Involutional entropion — lax tarsus and retractors let the lid roll inward, lashes abrading cornea.
FJ1379.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman has constant right eye irritation; her lower lid margin is inverted with lashes touching the cornea, needing surgical correction.

FJ1375.name: Tarsal plate of right upper eyelid
FJ1375.details: Upper tarsal plate of the right lid, attached to levator aponeurosis and Müller muscle; scarring of its conjunctival side distorts lid contour and lash direction.
FJ1375.clinicalCondition: Trachoma — repeated chlamydial infection scars the upper tarsal conjunctiva causing trichiasis and corneal blindness.
FJ1375.clinicalScenario: A patient from an endemic region shows upper tarsal conjunctival scarring (Arlt's line) with inturned lashes abrading a clouded right cornea.

FJ2770.name: Epiglottis
FJ2770.details: Leaf-shaped elastic cartilage behind the tongue root, attached to the thyroid cartilage; folds backward during swallowing to cover the laryngeal inlet; its mucosa is supplied by the internal laryngeal nerve.
FJ2770.clinicalCondition: Acute epiglottitis — rapidly swelling inflamed epiglottis can obstruct a child's airway; the enlarged epiglottis gives the thumbprint sign on lateral neck X-ray.
FJ2770.clinicalScenario: A drooling, febrile 4-year-old sits leaning forward with stridor; the airway is secured in theatre before the swollen epiglottis closes it.

FJ2441.name: Inferior lingular bronchial tree
FJ2441.details: Distal divisions of the inferior lingular segmental bronchus (S5) from the lingular division of the left upper lobe bronchus, ventilating lingular parenchyma against the left heart border.
FJ2441.clinicalCondition: Lingular bronchiectasis — the lingula drains poorly like the middle lobe, so retained secretions cause recurrent infection.
FJ2441.clinicalScenario: A woman with years of productive cough has CT showing dilated, thick-walled bronchi confined to the lingula, treated with airway clearance.

FJ2475.name: Inferior lingular bronchial tree
FJ2475.details: Subsegmental bronchioles of the left inferior lingular segment (S5), branching within the lower lingula; supplied by branches of the left pulmonary artery, draining to the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2475.clinicalCondition: Lady Windermere syndrome — Mycobacterium avium infection favours the lingula and middle lobe in older women who suppress coughing.
FJ2475.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman with chronic cough and weight loss has lingular bronchiectasis on CT; sputum culture grows Mycobacterium avium complex.

FJ2449.name: Lateral segmental bronchial tree
FJ2449.details: Divisions of the lateral segmental bronchus (S4) of the right middle lobe bronchus, which arises from the anterior bronchus intermedius; ventilates the lateral middle lobe segment.
FJ2449.clinicalCondition: Middle lobe syndrome — the long, narrow middle lobe bronchus surrounded by lymph nodes collapses chronically, causing recurrent infection.
FJ2449.clinicalScenario: A child with three episodes of right middle lobe pneumonia has CT showing middle lobe atelectasis with enlarged peribronchial lymph nodes.

FJ2503.name: Lateral segmental bronchial tree
FJ2503.details: Subsegmental bronchi within the lateral segment (S4) of the right middle lobe, running with branches of the right pulmonary artery; the segment lies against the minor fissure.
FJ2503.clinicalCondition: Middle lobe atelectasis — poor collateral ventilation makes this lobe collapse readily when its bronchus is narrowed.
FJ2503.clinicalScenario: An asthmatic teenager's chest film shows a wedge-shaped right middle lobe opacity that fails to clear between exacerbations.

FJ2504.name: Lateral segmental bronchial tree
FJ2504.details: Branching airway tree of the right middle lobe lateral segment (S4); the middle lobe bronchus takes off opposite the superior segmental bronchus of the lower lobe.
FJ2504.clinicalCondition: Post-obstructive pneumonitis — an endobronchial lesion in this bronchus causes recurrent same-site infection until excluded bronchoscopically.
FJ2504.clinicalScenario: A smoker with repeated middle lobe infections undergoes bronchoscopy, which reveals an endobronchial carcinoid narrowing the lateral segmental orifice.

FJ2505.name: Lateral segmental bronchial tree
FJ2505.details: Airway divisions supplying the lateral segment (S4) of the right middle lobe, a bronchopulmonary segment bounded by horizontal and oblique fissures; a surgical unit for segmentectomy or lobectomy.
FJ2505.clinicalCondition: Localised bronchiectasis — disease confined to the middle lobe segments is a classic indication for surgical resection.
FJ2505.clinicalScenario: A young adult with daily purulent sputum from bronchiectasis limited to the middle lobe is booked for middle lobectomy.

FJ2535.name: Left anterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2535.details: Basal airway divisions supplying the anterior basal segment (S8) of the left lower lobe; on the left it usually merges with the medial basal as the anteromedial basal segment.
FJ2535.clinicalCondition: Basal aspiration pneumonia — dependent basal segments receive aspirated material when the patient is upright.
FJ2535.clinicalScenario: An elderly man with poor dentition develops fever and a left basal infiltrate after choking episodes during meals.

FJ2536.name: Left anterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2536.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the left anterior basal segment, part of the basal trunk of the left lower lobe bronchus, lying above the diaphragm behind the heart.
FJ2536.clinicalCondition: Basal bronchiectasis — gravity-dependent basal segments are common sites for bronchiectasis after severe childhood infections.
FJ2536.clinicalScenario: A teenager with cystic fibrosis shows early bronchiectatic change in the basal segments on high-resolution CT.

FJ2538.name: Left anterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2538.details: Terminal bronchial branching within the left anterior basal segment (S8), accompanied by basal branches of the left pulmonary artery and inferior pulmonary vein tributaries.
FJ2538.clinicalCondition: Segmental atelectasis — mucus plugging of a basal segmental bronchus causes lobar-pattern collapse and hypoxemia after surgery.
FJ2538.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient desaturates with a raised left hemidiaphragm; chest imaging shows basal segmental collapse from retained secretions.

FJ2443.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2443.details: Divisions of the anterior segmental bronchus (S3) of the left upper lobe bronchus, supplying the anterior segment facing the anterior chest wall above the lingula.
FJ2443.clinicalCondition: Segmental pneumonia — infection localised to one bronchopulmonary segment follows its bronchial distribution on imaging.
FJ2443.clinicalScenario: A college student with fever and pleuritic pain has a well-demarcated anterior segment infiltrate on her CT chest.

FJ2467.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2467.details: Subsegmental airways of the left anterior segment (S3), one of three upper-division segments of the left upper lobe, running with the anterior segmental pulmonary artery branch.
FJ2467.clinicalCondition: Haemoptysis localisation — bronchoscopy identifies the segmental bronchus bleeding so embolisation or surgery can be targeted.
FJ2467.clinicalScenario: A man coughs up fresh blood; bronchoscopy shows bleeding coming from the left anterior segmental bronchus, guiding bronchial artery embolisation.

FJ2468.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2468.details: Branching tree within the left anterior segment (S3) of the upper lobe; the segment is a discrete surgical unit bounded by intersegmental veins.
FJ2468.clinicalCondition: Early-stage lung cancer — a small peripheral tumour confined to one segment may be treated by anatomical segmentectomy.
FJ2468.clinicalScenario: A 62-year-old has a 1.5 cm nodule confined to the left anterior segment and undergoes segmentectomy, preserving remaining lung.

FJ2469.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2469.details: Airway divisions distal to the left anterior segmental bronchus (S3), aerating parenchyma anterior to the oblique fissure's upper part and medial to the chest wall.
FJ2469.clinicalCondition: Post-obstructive collapse — central tumours obstructing the segmental orifice produce segmental atelectasis with volume loss.
FJ2469.clinicalScenario: A heavy smoker's film shows left upper zone volume loss; bronchoscopy finds tumour occluding the anterior segmental bronchus.

FJ2471.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2471.details: Peripheral bronchioles of the left anterior segment (S3), ending in alveolar ducts; collateral ventilation reaches this segment through pores of Kohn and canals of Lambert.
FJ2471.clinicalCondition: Lung abscess — aspiration into an upper-lobe segment can necrotise into a cavity with an air-fluid level.
FJ2471.clinicalScenario: A man with severe periodontal disease develops a foul-smelling cough and a cavitating lesion in the left anterior segment.

FJ2472.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2472.details: Bronchial subdivisions of the left anterior segment (S3), identifiable at bronchoscopy as the anterior branch of the upper division of the left upper lobe bronchus.
FJ2472.clinicalCondition: Foreign body obstruction — a lodged object causes segmental air trapping or collapse, localised bronchoscopically.
FJ2472.clinicalScenario: A child who choked on a toy part has persistent left-sided wheeze; bronchoscopy retrieves plastic from an upper-lobe segmental bronchus.

FJ2473.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2473.details: The airway tree of the left anterior segment (S3), supplied by the anterior segmental artery and drained by intersegmental tributaries of the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2473.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — irreversibly dilated segmental bronchi cause chronic sputum production and recurrent exacerbations.
FJ2473.clinicalScenario: CT in a woman with daily cupfuls of sputum shows signet-ring dilated bronchi clustered in the left anterior segment.

FJ2474.name: Left anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2474.details: Distal bronchi of the left anterior segment (S3), part of the conducting zone generations 3–8 within the left upper lobe's upper division.
FJ2474.clinicalCondition: Endobronchial tuberculosis — granulomatous narrowing of a segmental bronchus causes distal collapse and bronchiectasis.
FJ2474.clinicalScenario: A young woman treated for pulmonary TB develops left anterior segment stenosis with recurrent distal infections on follow-up imaging.

FJ2444.name: Left apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2444.details: Divisions of the apical part of the left apicoposterior segmental bronchus (S1+2), ventilating the lung apex above the clavicle, near the subclavian vessels and thoracic duct.
FJ2444.clinicalCondition: Reactivation tuberculosis — the apex's high oxygen tension and poor lymphatic drainage favour dormant bacilli reactivating.
FJ2444.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man with night sweats and weight loss has a cavitating infiltrate in the left lung apex on chest radiograph.

FJ2460.name: Left apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2460.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the left apical segment, the highest bronchopulmonary territory, crossed anteriorly by the subclavian artery and vein at the thoracic inlet.
FJ2460.clinicalCondition: Apical fibrosis — healed apical TB scars distort the apex and can harbour aspergilloma in old cavities.
FJ2460.clinicalScenario: A patient with old apical TB cavities presents coughing blood; CT shows a fungal ball within a left apical cavity.

FJ2461.name: Left apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2461.details: Airway branching within the left lung apex (S1), forming the upper part of the combined apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe.
FJ2461.clinicalCondition: Spontaneous pneumothorax — ruptured apical subpleural blebs leak air into the pleural space, typically in tall thin young men.
FJ2461.clinicalScenario: A tall 19-year-old develops sudden pleuritic pain and breathlessness; radiograph shows a left pneumothorax from a ruptured apical bleb.

FJ2462.name: Left apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2462.details: Bronchioles of the left apical segment, whose pleural cupola rises into the neck behind the anterior scalene muscle and first rib.
FJ2462.clinicalCondition: Apical (Pancoast) tumour — a superior sulcus tumour invades nearby roots, sympathetic chain and first ribs.
FJ2462.clinicalScenario: A smoker with left shoulder pain radiating down the arm and a drooping eyelid has an apical mass on imaging.

FJ2463.name: Left apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2463.details: Distal airway tree of the left apical segment (S1), ventilating parenchyma that receives relatively high ventilation but low perfusion when upright.
FJ2463.clinicalCondition: Apical cavitation — post-primary TB classically cavitates in apical and apicoposterior segments, spreading infection via sputum.
FJ2463.clinicalScenario: A homeless man with chronic cough has thick-walled apical cavities and smear-positive sputum, and is started on isolation.

FJ2464.name: Left apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2464.details: Terminal divisions of the left apical segmental bronchus, ending in respiratory bronchioles of the apex; identified at bronchoscopy within the apicoposterior trunk.
FJ2464.clinicalCondition: Segmental resection planning — apical segment anatomy guides apical segmentectomy for localised early tumours or destroyed TB segments.
FJ2464.clinicalScenario: A woman with a destroyed, repeatedly infected left apical segment after TB is referred for apical segmentectomy.

FJ3263.name: Left inferior nasal concha
FJ3263.details: Thin independent bone on the left lateral nasal wall, covered by thick erectile cavernous mucosa; the inferior meatus beneath it receives the nasolacrimal duct opening.
FJ3263.clinicalCondition: Turbinate hypertrophy — swollen erectile mucosa of the inferior concha is the commonest anatomical cause of nasal obstruction.
FJ3263.clinicalScenario: A man with chronic rhinitis and blocked left nostril fails steroid sprays; examination shows a hypertrophied inferior turbinate touching the septum.

FJ2740.name: Left inferior pharyngeal constrictor
FJ2740.details: Origin from the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage and the side of the cricoid; inserts into the median pharyngeal raphe; its cricopharyngeus part forms the upper oesophageal sphincter; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2740.clinicalCondition: Zenker diverticulum — pharyngeal mucosa pouches through Killian's dehiscence between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus, causing dysphagia and regurgitation.
FJ2740.clinicalScenario: An elderly man regurgitates undigested food hours after meals and has halitosis; barium swallow shows a posterior pouch above the cricopharyngeus.

FJ2445.name: Left lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2445.details: Divisions of the lateral basal segmental bronchus (S9) of the left lower lobe, supplying the basal segment on the lateral diaphragmatic surface.
FJ2445.clinicalCondition: Basal segment pneumonia — dependent basal segments are frequent sites for community-acquired consolidation in the elderly.
FJ2445.clinicalScenario: A frail 80-year-old with fever and confusion has consolidation localised to the left lateral basal segment on CT.

FJ2532.name: Left lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2532.details: Subsegmental bronchi within the left lateral basal segment (S9), arising from the basal trunk beside the posterior basal bronchus, accompanied by basal pulmonary artery branches.
FJ2532.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — basal segments commonly develop bronchiectasis from recurrent infection and impaired drainage.
FJ2532.clinicalScenario: A woman with chronic sinusitis and infertility has basal bronchiectasis, raising suspicion of primary ciliary dyskinesia.

FJ2533.name: Left lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2533.details: Airway tree of the left lateral basal segment (S9), a discrete bronchopulmonary unit separated from neighbours by intersegmental veins used in segmentectomy.
FJ2533.clinicalCondition: Localised haemoptysis — a bleeding basal segment identified at bronchoscopy can be resected or embolised selectively.
FJ2533.clinicalScenario: Bronchoscopy localises a patient's bleeding to the left lateral basal segment, and targeted embolisation stops the haemoptysis.

FJ2534.name: Left lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2534.details: Terminal branching of the left lateral basal segmental bronchus, ventilating parenchyma resting on the diaphragm lateral to the posterior basal segment.
FJ2534.clinicalCondition: Aspiration pneumonitis — basal segments receive gastric contents aspirated while upright, classically after vomiting.
FJ2534.clinicalScenario: A patient recovering from anaesthesia vomits and aspirates; imaging later shows a new left lateral basal infiltrate.

FJ2556.name: Left lateral nasal cartilage
FJ2556.details: Upper lateral cartilage supporting the left nasal sidewall, continuous above with the septal cartilage; with the septum it forms the internal nasal valve, the nose's narrowest point.
FJ2556.clinicalCondition: Internal nasal valve collapse — narrowing of this valve after trauma or surgery obstructs airflow despite a straight septum.
FJ2556.clinicalScenario: A boxer breathes poorly through the left nostril since a fracture; inspiration visibly collapses his left nasal sidewall.

FJ2450.name: Left main bronchus
FJ2450.details: About 5 cm long, narrower and more oblique (about 45 degrees) than the right; passes beneath the aortic arch, anterior to oesophagus and thoracic duct, before reaching the left hilum.
FJ2450.clinicalCondition: Left atrial compression — an enlarged left atrium splays the carina and can compress this bronchus, widening the carinal angle.
FJ2450.clinicalScenario: A woman with severe mitral stenosis has a widened carinal angle and left main bronchus compression on her chest imaging.

FJ2442.name: Left medial basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2442.details: Divisions of the medial basal (cardiac) segmental bronchus (S7) of the left lower lobe; on the left it usually shares a trunk with the anterior basal as the anteromedial basal bronchus.
FJ2442.clinicalCondition: Medial basal consolidation — infection here sits against the heart and is easily missed on plain films.
FJ2442.clinicalScenario: CT performed for persistent fever shows a small consolidation in the left medial basal segment hidden behind the heart shadow.

FJ2537.name: Left medial basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2537.details: Subsegmental airways of the left medial basal segment (S7), ventilating parenchyma medially against the pericardium above the diaphragm.
FJ2537.clinicalCondition: Segmental collapse — mucus retention in a small basal bronchus produces segmental atelectasis and postoperative hypoxemia.
FJ2537.clinicalScenario: After upper abdominal surgery, a patient has left basal segmental collapse on imaging that clears with physiotherapy and mobilisation.

FJ2754.name: Left middle pharyngeal constrictor
FJ2754.details: Origin from the greater and lesser horns of the hyoid bone and stylohyoid ligament; fans upward and downward to the median raphe, overlapping the other constrictors; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2754.clinicalCondition: Pharyngeal dysphagia — weak constrictor contraction after stroke or vagal injury leaves residue that is aspirated after swallowing.
FJ2754.clinicalScenario: A post-stroke patient coughs on thin fluids; videofluoroscopy shows weak pharyngeal constriction with residue pooling in the pyriform fossae.

FJ2743.name: Left palatopharyngeus
FJ2743.details: Origin from the palatine aponeurosis and hard palate; descends in the palatopharyngeal arch (posterior tonsillar pillar) to the thyroid cartilage and pharyngeal wall; elevates the pharynx; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2743.clinicalCondition: Tonsillar landmark — the palatine tonsil lies between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches, defining the tonsillectomy dissection planes.
FJ2743.clinicalScenario: During tonsillectomy for recurrent tonsillitis, the surgeon identifies the posterior pillar formed by palatopharyngeus to protect deeper structures.

FJ2446.name: Left posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2446.details: Divisions of the posterior basal segmental bronchus (S10), the continuation of the basal trunk, supplying the segment on the posterior diaphragmatic surface of the left lower lobe.
FJ2446.clinicalCondition: Upright aspiration — the posterior basal segment is the most dependent segment when standing, receiving aspirated material first.
FJ2446.clinicalScenario: A man with bulbar weakness aspirates while eating upright and develops a posterior basal segment pneumonia.

FJ2527.name: Left posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2527.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the left posterior basal segment (S10), running with the posterior basal branch of the left pulmonary artery toward the diaphragm.
FJ2527.clinicalCondition: Basal lung abscess — aspirated anaerobic organisms necrotise dependent basal parenchyma into a thick-walled cavity.
FJ2527.clinicalScenario: An alcoholic man has fever, foul sputum and a thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the left posterior basal segment.

FJ2528.name: Left posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2528.details: Airway tree within the left posterior basal segment, bounded by the oblique fissure anteriorly and intersegmental veins used as surgical planes.
FJ2528.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — posterior basal segments are among the commonest sites of post-infective bronchiectasis.
FJ2528.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged woman with childhood measles pneumonia now has posterior basal bronchiectasis causing daily purulent sputum.

FJ2529.name: Left posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2529.details: Peripheral divisions of the left posterior basal bronchus (S10), supplying parenchyma behind the heart and above the left hemidiaphragm posteriorly.
FJ2529.clinicalCondition: Segmental consolidation — basal posterior infection may present only as fever and raised inflammatory markers in the elderly.
FJ2529.clinicalScenario: An elderly diabetic with unexplained fever has CT showing consolidation isolated to the left posterior basal segment.

FJ2530.name: Left posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2530.details: Bronchioles of the left posterior basal segment, the last basal branch territory; venous drainage passes to the left inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2530.clinicalCondition: Pleural involvement — posterior basal infections abut the diaphragmatic pleura, causing pleuritic pain and small parapneumonic effusions.
FJ2530.clinicalScenario: A patient with left posterior basal pneumonia develops sharp inspiratory pain and a small reactive pleural effusion.

FJ2531.name: Left posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2531.details: Terminal airway branching of the left posterior basal segment (S10); with the other basal segments it forms the pyramid-shaped base of the lower lobe.
FJ2531.clinicalCondition: Chronic aspiration — repeated silent aspiration in reflux or neurological disease scars the basal segments progressively.
FJ2531.clinicalScenario: A patient with advanced Parkinson disease has recurrent left posterior basal infiltrates from chronic silent aspiration.

FJ2447.name: Left posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2447.details: Divisions of the posterior part of the left apicoposterior segmental bronchus (S2 component), supplying the posterior apex region behind the anterior segment.
FJ2447.clinicalCondition: Supine aspiration — posterior upper-lobe segments receive aspirated material when the patient is recumbent.
FJ2447.clinicalScenario: An unconscious overdose patient aspirates supine and develops an infiltrate in the posterior segment of the left upper lobe.

FJ2465.name: Left posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2465.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the left posterior segment, sharing the apicoposterior trunk with the apical division; drained by the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2465.clinicalCondition: Reactivation tuberculosis — apicoposterior segments are favoured sites for post-primary TB cavitation.
FJ2465.clinicalScenario: A miner with silicosis develops a new cavitating lesion in the left apicoposterior segment, and sputum confirms tuberculosis.

FJ2466.name: Left posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2466.details: Airway tree of the left posterior segment (S2 territory), lying posteriorly against the upper thoracic wall beneath the first ribs.
FJ2466.clinicalCondition: Segmental atelectasis — an obstructed posterior segmental bronchus collapses this territory, seen as upper-zone volume loss.
FJ2466.clinicalScenario: Imaging after a mucus plug shows collapse of the left posterior segment in a ventilated ICU patient.

FJ2745.name: Left salpingopharyngeus
FJ2745.details: Slender muscle descending from the torus tubarius at the pharyngeal opening of the auditory tube, blending with palatopharyngeus; elevates the pharynx and helps open the tube; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2745.clinicalCondition: Eustachian tube dysfunction — swelling around the tubal orifice and its fold impairs middle-ear ventilation, causing ear fullness.
FJ2745.clinicalScenario: After an upper respiratory infection, a traveller cannot equalise ear pressure during a flight and develops a retracted tympanic membrane.

FJ2746.name: Left stylopharyngeus
FJ2746.details: Origin from the medial base of the styloid process; passes between the superior and middle constrictors with the glossopharyngeal nerve; inserts into the pharyngeal wall and thyroid cartilage; the only pharyngeal muscle supplied by cranial nerve IX.
FJ2746.clinicalCondition: Jugular foramen syndrome — glossopharyngeal injury weakens pharyngeal elevation and contributes to dysphagia with absent gag reflex.
FJ2746.clinicalScenario: A patient with a skull-base tumour affecting cranial nerves IX to XI has dysphagia and a lost gag reflex.

FJ2747.name: Left superior pharyngeal constrictor
FJ2747.details: Origin from the pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe, mandible and tongue; inserts into the median raphe and pharyngeal tubercle; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus); the gap above it (sinus of Morgagni) transmits the auditory tube and levator veli palatini.
FJ2747.clinicalCondition: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma spread — tumour can extend through the sinus of Morgagni gap above this muscle into the skull base.
FJ2747.clinicalScenario: A man with unilateral ear effusion and blood-stained nasal discharge is found to have a nasopharyngeal mass near the fossa of Rosenmuller.

FJ2448.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2448.details: Divisions of the superior segmental bronchus (S6) of the left lower lobe, arising opposite the lingular bronchus and supplying the segment behind the oblique fissure at mid-thoracic level.
FJ2448.clinicalCondition: Recumbent aspiration — the superior segment is a classic site for aspiration when supine, alongside posterior upper-lobe segments.
FJ2448.clinicalScenario: A patient found unconscious after drinking develops a superior segment infiltrate from aspirating while lying flat.

FJ2479.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2479.details: Subsegmental bronchi within the left superior segment (S6), a discrete bronchopulmonary unit with its own segmental artery, often resected alone.
FJ2479.clinicalCondition: Aspiration lung abscess — anaerobic infection in this dependent recumbent segment forms a cavity with an air-fluid level.
FJ2479.clinicalScenario: A man with poor oral hygiene presents with a foul-smelling cough and an abscess cavity in the left superior segment.

FJ2480.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2480.details: Airway tree of the left superior segment, the first branch of the lower lobe bronchus, arising posteriorly before the basal trunk continues downward.
FJ2480.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy target — a small tumour confined to S6 can be removed by superior segmentectomy, sparing the basal segments.
FJ2480.clinicalScenario: A 58-year-old with a 1.8 cm nodule limited to the left superior segment undergoes S6 segmentectomy.

FJ2482.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2482.details: Peripheral divisions of the left superior segmental bronchus (S6), ventilating parenchyma posterior to the hilum against the paravertebral gutter.
FJ2482.clinicalCondition: Post-obstructive pneumonia — obstruction of this bronchus by tumour or nodes causes recurrent infection in the same segment.
FJ2482.clinicalScenario: A smoker has two infections in the left superior segment within a year; bronchoscopy reveals an obstructing endobronchial lesion.

FJ2483.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2483.details: Bronchial branching inside the left superior segment (S6), accompanied by its segmental pulmonary artery and drained toward the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2483.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — localised S6 bronchiectasis may follow severe necrotising pneumonia in that segment.
FJ2483.clinicalScenario: After severe pneumonia, follow-up CT shows new bronchiectatic change restricted to the left superior segment.

FJ2484.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2484.details: Terminal bronchioles of the left superior segment, accessible at bronchoscopy as the first posterior branch distal to the left upper lobe orifice.
FJ2484.clinicalCondition: Haemoptysis source — bronchoscopic localisation of bleeding to S6 directs embolisation or resection.
FJ2484.clinicalScenario: During bronchoscopy for massive haemoptysis, blood is seen welling from the left superior segmental bronchus.

FJ2485.name: Left superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2485.details: Distal airway divisions of the left superior segment (S6), whose parenchyma lies between the upper lobe anteriorly and basal segments below.
FJ2485.clinicalCondition: Segmental collapse — blockage of the S6 bronchus by mucus or nodes produces a characteristic mid-zone opacity.
FJ2485.clinicalScenario: A ventilated patient's new left mid-zone opacity is traced to a mucus plug occluding the superior segmental bronchus.

FJ2451.name: Medial segmental bronchial tree
FJ2451.details: Divisions of the medial segmental bronchus (S5) of the right middle lobe, supplying the segment against the right heart border, medial to the horizontal fissure.
FJ2451.clinicalCondition: Silhouette sign — medial segment pneumonia touches the right heart border, so consolidation erases that border on the frontal radiograph.
FJ2451.clinicalScenario: A child's chest film shows loss of the right heart border, localising pneumonia to the medial segment of the middle lobe.

FJ2506.name: Medial segmental bronchial tree
FJ2506.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the right middle lobe medial segment (S5), arising with the lateral segmental bronchus from the middle lobe bronchus off the bronchus intermedius.
FJ2506.clinicalCondition: Middle lobe syndrome — chronic collapse of these segments from the narrow, node-surrounded middle lobe bronchus causes recurrent infection.
FJ2506.clinicalScenario: A woman with recurrent right-sided chest infections has a persistently collapsed middle lobe on sequential CT scans.

FJ2507.name: Medial segmental bronchial tree
FJ2507.details: Airway tree within the right middle lobe medial segment, a bronchopulmonary unit bounded by fissures and intersegmental veins, removed with the lobe in middle lobectomy.
FJ2507.clinicalCondition: Localised bronchiectasis — disease confined to the middle lobe is a recognised indication for lobectomy after failed medical therapy.
FJ2507.clinicalScenario: A teenager with bronchiectasis limited to the middle lobe and daily haemoptysis is referred for middle lobectomy.

FJ2508.name: Medial segmental bronchial tree
FJ2508.details: Terminal divisions of the right middle lobe medial segmental bronchus (S5), ventilating parenchyma adjacent to the pericardium and right atrium.
FJ2508.clinicalCondition: Atelectasis in asthma — the middle lobe collapses easily during exacerbations because of its narrow bronchus and poor collateral ventilation.
FJ2508.clinicalScenario: During an asthma admission, a boy's radiograph shows new middle lobe collapse that slowly re-expands over weeks.

FJ2452.name: Right anterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2452.details: Divisions of the anterior basal segmental bronchus (S8) of the right lower lobe, one of five basal branches supplying parenchyma above the diaphragm anteriorly.
FJ2452.clinicalCondition: Basal aspiration pneumonia — upright aspiration gravitates to basal segments, with anterior basal involvement alongside posterior basal disease.
FJ2452.clinicalScenario: A stroke patient who aspirates while seated develops fever and an anterior basal infiltrate on imaging.

FJ2493.name: Right anterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2493.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the right anterior basal segment (S8), running with basal branches of the right pulmonary artery toward the diaphragmatic surface.
FJ2493.clinicalCondition: Basal bronchiectasis — dependent basal segments frequently develop bronchiectasis in chronic suppurative lung disease.
FJ2493.clinicalScenario: High-resolution CT in a man with chronic productive cough shows tram-track bronchiectasis in the right anterior basal segment.

FJ2494.name: Right anterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2494.details: Terminal airway branching of the right anterior basal segment, separated from neighbouring basal segments by intersegmental veins used during basal segmentectomy.
FJ2494.clinicalCondition: Segmental pneumonia — infection confined to this segment produces a basal opacity that can mimic a pleural effusion.
FJ2494.clinicalScenario: Ultrasound distinguishes a suspected effusion from consolidated right anterior basal segment in a febrile patient.

FJ2453.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2453.details: Divisions of the anterior segmental bronchus (S3) of the right upper lobe bronchus, supplying the anterior segment facing the anterior chest wall below the apex.
FJ2453.clinicalCondition: Segmental pneumonia — anterior segment infection gives a triangular opacity abutting the horizontal fissure on the lateral film.
FJ2453.clinicalScenario: A young woman with fever and cough has consolidation sharply limited by the horizontal fissure in the right anterior segment.

FJ2509.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2509.details: Subsegmental airways of the right anterior segment (S3), branching from the anterior division of the upper lobe bronchus with its segmental artery.
FJ2509.clinicalCondition: Post-obstructive pneumonia — a tumour narrowing this bronchus causes repeated infections distal to the blockage.
FJ2509.clinicalScenario: A 65-year-old smoker has three pneumonias in the right anterior segment; bronchoscopy finds an obstructing squamous tumour.

FJ2510.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2510.details: Airway tree within the right anterior segment (S3), a discrete bronchopulmonary unit that can be removed alone in anterior segmentectomy.
FJ2510.clinicalCondition: Early lung cancer — a small ground-glass nodule confined to S3 may be treated with anatomical segmentectomy.
FJ2510.clinicalScenario: Screening CT finds a 1.4 cm ground-glass lesion in the right anterior segment, removed by segmentectomy with clear margins.

FJ2511.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2511.details: Peripheral bronchi of the right anterior segment, ventilating parenchyma between the apical segment above and middle lobe below.
FJ2511.clinicalCondition: Lung abscess — aspiration during recumbency can seed upper-lobe segments and necrotise into an abscess.
FJ2511.clinicalScenario: A man with epilepsy develops a cavitating right anterior segment lesion after a seizure-related aspiration.

FJ2512.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2512.details: Bronchial subdivisions of the right anterior segment (S3), identified bronchoscopically as the anterior branch of the right upper lobe bronchus.
FJ2512.clinicalCondition: Foreign body — an inhaled object in this bronchus causes segmental hyperinflation or collapse depending on the valve effect.
FJ2512.clinicalScenario: A toddler with a persistent right-sided wheeze after choking on a peanut fragment has air trapping of an upper-lobe segment.

FJ2513.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2513.details: Distal bronchioles of the right anterior segment, ending in alveolar ducts; collateral air drift occurs through pores of Kohn between adjacent alveoli.
FJ2513.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — dilated, thick-walled anterior segment bronchi produce chronic sputum and recurrent exacerbations.
FJ2513.clinicalScenario: CT shows signet-ring bronchi clustered in the right anterior segment of a woman with lifelong productive cough.

FJ2514.name: Right anterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2514.details: Terminal airway divisions of the right anterior segment (S3), drained by tributaries of the right superior pulmonary vein crossing between segments.
FJ2514.clinicalCondition: Haemoptysis localisation — identifying this segment as the bleeding source guides targeted bronchial artery embolisation.
FJ2514.clinicalScenario: Bronchoscopy in a patient with haemoptysis shows blood emerging from the right anterior segmental bronchus.

FJ2454.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2454.details: Divisions of the apical segmental bronchus (S1) of the right upper lobe, supplying the lung apex rising above the clavicle, related to the subclavian vessels and first rib.
FJ2454.clinicalCondition: Reactivation tuberculosis — high apical oxygen tension and sluggish lymphatic drainage favour reactivation of dormant bacilli here.
FJ2454.clinicalScenario: An immigrant healthcare worker with cough and night sweats has a cavitating right apical infiltrate; sputum is AFB-positive.

FJ2520.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2520.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the right apical segment (S1), the most superior bronchopulmonary segment, crossed by the subclavian artery and the dome of pleura.
FJ2520.clinicalCondition: Pancoast tumour — an apical tumour invades the lower brachial plexus, sympathetic chain and first two ribs.
FJ2520.clinicalScenario: A smoker with right shoulder and medial arm pain, plus Horner syndrome, has a superior sulcus mass on MRI.

FJ2521.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2521.details: Airway branching within the right lung apex, whose pleural cupola is reinforced by Sibson fascia and related to the stellate ganglion posteriorly.
FJ2521.clinicalCondition: Spontaneous pneumothorax — rupture of apical subpleural blebs is the usual cause in tall, thin young adults.
FJ2521.clinicalScenario: A tall 21-year-old smoker presents with sudden right chest pain; imaging shows a 40 percent pneumothorax from an apical bleb.

FJ2522.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2522.details: Bronchioles of the right apical segment (S1), ventilating parenchyma that extends into the root of the neck medial to the anterior scalene muscle.
FJ2522.clinicalCondition: Apical pleural cap injury — central line insertion through the subclavian or jugular route risks puncturing the pleural dome here.
FJ2522.clinicalScenario: After right internal jugular line placement, a patient becomes breathless and is found to have an iatrogenic pneumothorax.

FJ2523.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2523.details: Distal divisions of the right apical segmental bronchus, accompanied by the apical segmental pulmonary artery and apical venous tributaries.
FJ2523.clinicalCondition: Aspergilloma — a fungal ball forms inside a healed apical TB cavity and can cause major haemoptysis.
FJ2523.clinicalScenario: A man with old apical TB coughs up a cup of blood; CT shows a mobile intracavitary mass with an air crescent.

FJ2524.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2524.details: Terminal airway tree of the right apical segment, the first branch territory of the right upper lobe bronchus ('eparterial' bronchus arising before the pulmonary artery crosses).
FJ2524.clinicalCondition: Apical scarring — fibrotic healing of apical TB distorts bronchi and can cause traction bronchiectasis and volume loss.
FJ2524.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient has upward hilar displacement and apical fibrosis from TB treated forty years earlier.

FJ2525.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2525.details: Peripheral bronchi of the right apical segment (S1), identified at bronchoscopy as the upward first division of the right upper lobe bronchus.
FJ2525.clinicalCondition: Segmental tumour spread — endobronchial tumour in the apical bronchus collapses the apex and mimics pleural thickening.
FJ2525.clinicalScenario: A patient with unexplained right apical shadowing has bronchoscopy showing tumour occluding the apical segmental orifice.

FJ2526.name: Right apical segmental bronchial tree
FJ2526.details: Respiratory bronchioles within the right apical segment, part of the gas-exchange zone where ventilation exceeds perfusion in the upright lung.
FJ2526.clinicalCondition: Apical bullous disease — large apical bullae in emphysema compress adjacent lung and can rupture into pneumothorax.
FJ2526.clinicalScenario: A COPD patient with worsening dyspnoea has giant right apical bullae occupying a third of the hemithorax.

FJ3369.name: Right inferior nasal concha
FJ3369.details: Thin independent bone on the right lateral nasal wall, covered by erectile cavernous mucosa that swells with the nasal cycle; the inferior meatus below receives the nasolacrimal duct.
FJ3369.clinicalCondition: Turbinate hypertrophy — persistent mucosal swelling of this concha blocks airflow and responds poorly once bony enlargement develops.
FJ3369.clinicalScenario: A woman with allergic rhinitis has a bulky right inferior turbinate; she is listed for turbinoplasty after failed medical therapy.

FJ2752.name: Right inferior pharyngeal constrictor
FJ2752.details: Origin from the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage and side of the cricoid; inserts into the median raphe; its cricopharyngeus part forms the upper oesophageal sphincter; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus) and recurrent laryngeal branches.
FJ2752.clinicalCondition: Zenker diverticulum — the pouch herniates through Killian's dehiscence between this muscle's two parts during raised pharyngeal pressure.
FJ2752.clinicalScenario: An 82-year-old with dysphagia and regurgitation of stale food has a barium swallow showing a pharyngeal pouch at C5-C6.

FJ2455.name: Right lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2455.details: Divisions of the lateral basal segmental bronchus (S9) of the right lower lobe, supplying the lateral basal segment above the diaphragm.
FJ2455.clinicalCondition: Basal pneumonia — dependent basal segments are common sites of consolidation in bedridden patients.
FJ2455.clinicalScenario: A bedridden stroke patient develops fever and a right lateral basal consolidation from hypostatic infection.

FJ2490.name: Right lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2490.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the right lateral basal segment (S9), arising from the basal trunk between the anterior and posterior basal bronchi.
FJ2490.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — chronic infection dilates basal segmental bronchi, producing the signet-ring sign on CT.
FJ2490.clinicalScenario: CT in a man with recurrent chest infections shows dilated bronchi with signet rings in the right lateral basal segment.

FJ2491.name: Right lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2491.details: Airway tree within the right lateral basal segment, accompanied by basal pulmonary artery branches and drained by the inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2491.clinicalCondition: Aspiration — material aspirated upright pools in basal segments, and right-sided disease predominates because the right bronchus is straighter.
FJ2491.clinicalScenario: A patient with achalasia aspirates retained food overnight and develops a right lateral basal infiltrate.

FJ2492.name: Right lateral basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2492.details: Terminal branching of the right lateral basal segmental bronchus (S9), supplying parenchyma on the lateral diaphragmatic surface of the lower lobe.
FJ2492.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy planning — intersegmental veins around S9 define resection planes for basal segmentectomy.
FJ2492.clinicalScenario: A patient with a small nodule in the right lateral basal segment is planned for basal segmentectomy using 3D bronchovascular reconstruction.

FJ2558.name: Right lateral nasal cartilage
FJ2558.details: Upper lateral cartilage supporting the right nasal sidewall, fused above with the septal cartilage; together they form the internal nasal valve, the narrowest part of the airway.
FJ2558.clinicalCondition: Nasal valve stenosis — post-traumatic or post-rhinoplasty narrowing here causes obstruction corrected by spreader grafts.
FJ2558.clinicalScenario: After cosmetic rhinoplasty, a woman cannot breathe through the right nostril; examination shows internal valve narrowing on that side.

FJ2539.name: Right main bronchus proper
FJ2539.details: About 2.5 cm long, wider and more vertical (about 25 degrees from midline) than the left; gives off the upper lobe bronchus before continuing as the bronchus intermedius.
FJ2539.clinicalCondition: Foreign body aspiration — inhaled objects preferentially enter this wider, straighter bronchus, especially in children.
FJ2539.clinicalScenario: A 3-year-old who choked on a peanut has right-sided wheeze and air trapping; rigid bronchoscopy removes the fragment.

FJ2456.name: Right medial basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2456.details: Divisions of the medial basal (cardiac) segmental bronchus (S7), first basal branch of the right lower lobe, supplying parenchyma medially against the heart and inferior vena cava.
FJ2456.clinicalCondition: Cardiac segment consolidation — infection here hides behind the heart on frontal films and is best seen on lateral views or CT.
FJ2456.clinicalScenario: A febrile patient's frontal film looks normal, but the lateral view reveals medial basal consolidation behind the heart.

FJ2488.name: Right medial basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2488.details: Subsegmental airways of the right medial basal segment (S7), the only basal segment not reaching the diaphragmatic surface's outer part; it sits on the mediastinal surface.
FJ2488.clinicalCondition: Segmental atelectasis — obstruction of this small bronchus collapses the cardiac segment, sometimes compressing nothing but mimicking mediastinal widening.
FJ2488.clinicalScenario: Postoperative imaging shows a triangular medial basal collapse beside the right heart border that resolves with physiotherapy.

FJ2742.name: Right middle pharyngeal constrictor
FJ2742.details: Origin from the greater and lesser horns of the hyoid and stylohyoid ligament; sweeps to the median raphe, overlapping the superior constrictor above and inferior below; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2742.clinicalCondition: Oropharyngeal dysphagia — weak middle constrictor contraction impairs bolus clearance and risks aspiration in neurological disease.
FJ2742.clinicalScenario: A patient with motor neurone disease has swallow study showing pharyngeal residue and silent aspiration at the hyoid level.

FJ2755.name: Right palatopharyngeus
FJ2755.details: Origin from the palatine aponeurosis; descends within the palatopharyngeal arch (posterior pillar) to the thyroid cartilage; elevates and shortens the pharynx during swallowing; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2755.clinicalCondition: Velopharyngeal dysfunction — palatal muscle weakness, including this muscle, lets air escape nasally and speech become hypernasal, as in cleft palate.
FJ2755.clinicalScenario: A child with a repaired cleft palate has hypernasal speech; nasendoscopy shows poor palatopharyngeal closure.

FJ2457.name: Right posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2457.details: Divisions of the posterior basal segmental bronchus (S10), terminal continuation of the basal trunk, supplying the posterior diaphragmatic segment of the right lower lobe.
FJ2457.clinicalCondition: Upright aspiration — this is the most dependent segment when standing, so aspirated vomit classically lands here first.
FJ2457.clinicalScenario: A man aspirates during a seizure while upright; CT shows a new right posterior basal infiltrate.

FJ2470.name: Right posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2470.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the right posterior basal segment (S10), running with the posterior basal pulmonary artery branch straight down toward the diaphragm.
FJ2470.clinicalCondition: Aspiration lung abscess — anaerobic organisms from the mouth necrotise this dependent segment into a thick-walled cavity.
FJ2470.clinicalScenario: A homeless alcoholic presents with fever, weight loss and a thick-walled cavity with fluid level in the right posterior basal segment.

FJ2481.name: Right posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2481.details: Airway tree within the right posterior basal segment, the largest basal segment, forming much of the posterior diaphragmatic surface.
FJ2481.clinicalCondition: Basal bronchiectasis — posterior basal segments commonly develop bronchiectasis after pertussis or measles pneumonia in childhood.
FJ2481.clinicalScenario: An adult with whooping cough in childhood now has posterior basal bronchiectasis with daily purulent sputum.

FJ2486.name: Right posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2486.details: Peripheral divisions of the right posterior basal bronchus (S10), drained by tributaries of the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2486.clinicalCondition: Parapneumonic effusion — posterior basal pneumonia abutting the pleura frequently produces a small reactive effusion.
FJ2486.clinicalScenario: A patient with right posterior basal pneumonia develops pleuritic pain; ultrasound confirms a small parapneumonic effusion.

FJ2487.name: Right posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2487.details: Bronchioles of the right posterior basal segment, part of the basal pyramid whose segments are separated by intersegmental veins.
FJ2487.clinicalCondition: Chronic aspiration — repeated microaspiration from reflux progressively scars dependent basal segments, especially posterior basal.
FJ2487.clinicalScenario: A woman with severe reflux has recurrent right posterior basal infiltrates that settle once her reflux is controlled.

FJ2489.name: Right posterior basal segmental bronchial tree
FJ2489.details: Terminal airway branching of the right posterior basal segment (S10), the segment first reached by a bronchoscope passed straight down the basal trunk.
FJ2489.clinicalCondition: Segmental resection target — disease localised to S10 can be removed by posterior basal segmentectomy preserving other basal segments.
FJ2489.clinicalScenario: A patient with bronchiectasis destroying only the right posterior basal segment undergoes basal segmentectomy.

FJ2458.name: Right posterior segmental bronchial tree
