FJ2458.details: Divisions of the posterior segmental bronchus (S2) of the right upper lobe, arising from the posterior aspect of the upper lobe bronchus.
FJ2458.clinicalCondition: Recumbent aspiration — posterior upper-lobe segments receive aspirated material when supine, producing characteristic posterior infiltrates.
FJ2458.clinicalScenario: A patient aspirates during general anaesthesia while supine and develops a right posterior segment infiltrate postoperatively.

FJ2515.name: Right posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2515.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the right posterior segment (S2), lying against the posterior chest wall above the horizontal fissure's posterior part.
FJ2515.clinicalCondition: Reactivation tuberculosis — posterior and apical upper-lobe segments are the classic sites for post-primary cavitary TB.
FJ2515.clinicalScenario: A prisoner with chronic cough has a cavitating lesion in the right posterior segment and is isolated for TB workup.

FJ2516.name: Right posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2516.details: Airway tree within the right posterior segment, a discrete surgical unit supplied by the ascending posterior segmental artery branch.
FJ2516.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy target — a small tumour limited to S2 can be excised by posterior segmentectomy, preserving apical and anterior segments.
FJ2516.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old with a 1.6 cm nodule confined to the right posterior segment undergoes S2 segmentectomy.

FJ2517.name: Right posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2517.details: Peripheral bronchi of the right posterior segment (S2), drained by the posterior tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2517.clinicalCondition: Lung abscess — supine aspiration into this segment can necrotise, forming an abscess with an air-fluid level.
FJ2517.clinicalScenario: An unconscious trauma patient later develops fever and a cavity with fluid level in the right posterior segment.

FJ2518.name: Right posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2518.details: Bronchial subdivisions of the right posterior segment, seen at bronchoscopy as the backward branch of the right upper lobe bronchus between apical and anterior divisions.
FJ2518.clinicalCondition: Endobronchial obstruction — tumour or foreign body here causes posterior segment collapse, visible as upper-zone volume loss.
FJ2518.clinicalScenario: A smoker's film shows right upper-zone collapse; bronchoscopy finds tumour blocking the posterior segmental bronchus.

FJ2519.name: Right posterior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2519.details: Terminal divisions of the right posterior segmental bronchus (S2), ventilating parenchyma posterior to the apical segment and above the oblique fissure.
FJ2519.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — post-tuberculous scarring frequently dilates bronchi in posterior and apical segments.
FJ2519.clinicalScenario: A treated TB patient has chronic cough from traction bronchiectasis in the right posterior segment.

FJ2757.name: Right salpingopharyngeus
FJ2757.details: Thin muscle descending from the torus tubarius beside the auditory tube opening, merging with palatopharyngeus; elevates the pharynx and assists tubal opening during swallowing; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus).
FJ2757.clinicalCondition: Middle-ear ventilation — dysfunction around the tubal orifice leaves the middle ear under-ventilated, causing effusion and conductive hearing loss.
FJ2757.clinicalScenario: A child with recurrent otitis media with effusion has nasopharyngeal crowding around the tubal openings from adenoid hypertrophy.

FJ2758.name: Right stylopharyngeus
FJ2758.details: Origin from the medial side of the styloid process base; descends with the glossopharyngeal nerve between the superior and middle constrictors to the pharynx and thyroid cartilage; supplied by cranial nerve IX, uniquely among pharyngeal muscles.
FJ2758.clinicalCondition: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia territory — stylopharyngeus shares CN IX supply, so jugular foramen lesions weaken pharyngeal elevation and swallowing.
FJ2758.clinicalScenario: A patient with a jugular foramen meningioma presents with dysphagia, hoarseness and shoulder weakness from nerves IX to XI involvement.

FJ2759.name: Right superior pharyngeal constrictor
FJ2759.details: Origin from the pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe, mandible and side of tongue; inserts into the median raphe and pharyngeal tubercle; nerve: pharyngeal plexus (vagus); levator veli palatini and the auditory tube pass through the gap above it.
FJ2759.clinicalCondition: Passavant ridge — a ridge formed mainly by palatopharyngeus fibres on the posterior pharyngeal wall (at this muscle's level), meeting the elevated soft palate to seal the nasopharynx during swallowing.
FJ2759.clinicalScenario: A patient with palatal weakness after stroke has nasal regurgitation of fluids because the nasopharyngeal seal fails.

FJ2459.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2459.details: Divisions of the superior segmental bronchus (S6) of the right lower lobe, arising from the posterior bronchus intermedius opposite the middle lobe orifice.
FJ2459.clinicalCondition: Recumbent aspiration — S6 is the classic segment infected when material is aspirated while lying flat.
FJ2459.clinicalScenario: A man found unconscious after an overdose aspirates supine and develops a right superior segment infiltrate.

FJ2495.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2495.details: Subsegmental bronchi within the right superior segment (S6), a discrete bronchopulmonary unit with its own artery, separated from basal segments by an intersegmental plane.
FJ2495.clinicalCondition: Aspiration abscess — anaerobic infection of this dependent recumbent segment forms the textbook lung abscess with air-fluid level.
FJ2495.clinicalScenario: An alcoholic with foul breath and clubbing has a thick-walled cavity in the right superior segment on CT.

FJ2496.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2496.details: Airway tree of the right superior segment, the first and only branch of the lower lobe before the basal trunk, arising at the level of the middle lobe bronchus.
FJ2496.clinicalCondition: Segmentectomy target — tumours confined to S6 are removed by superior segmentectomy, preserving all five basal segments.
FJ2496.clinicalScenario: A 57-year-old with a 2 cm nodule limited to the right superior segment undergoes S6 segmentectomy.

FJ2497.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2497.details: Peripheral divisions of the right superior segmental bronchus (S6), ventilating parenchyma in the paravertebral gutter behind the hilum.
FJ2497.clinicalCondition: Post-obstructive pneumonia — recurrent infection in S6 demands bronchoscopy to exclude an obstructing lesion at its orifice.
FJ2497.clinicalScenario: Two bouts of right superior segment pneumonia prompt bronchoscopy, which reveals a benign endobronchial hamartoma.

FJ2498.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2498.details: Bronchial branching inside the right superior segment (S6), accompanied by the superior segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery.
FJ2498.clinicalCondition: Bronchiectasis — S6 bronchiectasis may follow necrotising pneumonia or chronic aspiration in this segment.
FJ2498.clinicalScenario: A patient with repeated aspiration episodes shows bronchiectatic change localised to the right superior segment.

FJ2499.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2499.details: Terminal bronchioles of the right superior segment, reached at bronchoscopy by directing the scope posteriorly just beyond the middle lobe orifice.
FJ2499.clinicalCondition: Haemoptysis localisation — blood seen emerging from the S6 orifice targets embolisation or resection to that segment.
FJ2499.clinicalScenario: During bronchoscopy for haemoptysis, fresh blood wells from the right superior segmental bronchus of a bronchiectasis patient.

FJ2500.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2500.details: Distal airway divisions of the right superior segment (S6), whose venous drainage passes to the right inferior pulmonary vein.
FJ2500.clinicalCondition: Segmental collapse — mucus plugging of the S6 bronchus after surgery causes a characteristic posterior mid-zone opacity.
FJ2500.clinicalScenario: A postoperative patient's desaturation is explained by a plugged, collapsed right superior segment that re-expands after suctioning.

FJ2501.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2501.details: Conducting bronchi of the right superior segment, generations below the segmental bronchus, ending in respiratory bronchioles and alveolar sacs.
FJ2501.clinicalCondition: Aspiration pneumonitis — chemical injury from gastric contents aspirated while recumbent inflames S6 before infection supervenes.
FJ2501.clinicalScenario: A patient aspirates during emergency induction of anaesthesia and develops a right superior segment chemical pneumonitis.

FJ2502.name: Right superior segmental bronchial tree
FJ2502.details: The airway divisions completing the right superior segment (S6), the segment forming the posterior apex of the lower lobe at the T5-T7 level.
FJ2502.clinicalCondition: Necrotising pneumonia — virulent organisms can destroy this segment's parenchyma, leaving pneumatoceles or a residual cavity.
FJ2502.clinicalScenario: A diabetic with Klebsiella pneumonia develops cavitating destruction of the right superior segment.

FJ2557.name: Septal nasal cartilage
FJ2557.details: Quadrilateral hyaline cartilage forming the anterior nasal septum, articulating with the perpendicular plate of ethmoid and vomer behind; key support for the nasal dorsum and tip.
FJ2557.clinicalCondition: Septal haematoma — trauma collects blood under the perichondrium, starving the cartilage, which necroses and causes saddle-nose deformity if undrained.
FJ2557.clinicalScenario: A boy struck by a cricket ball has bilateral fluctuant septal swellings; the haematoma is drained the same day.

FJ2476.name: Superior lingular bronchial tree
FJ2476.details: Divisions of the superior lingular segmental bronchus (S4) from the lingular division of the left upper lobe bronchus, supplying lingular parenchyma against the left heart border.
FJ2476.clinicalCondition: Silhouette sign — lingular consolidation touches the left heart border, erasing it on the frontal chest radiograph.
FJ2476.clinicalScenario: A teenager's film shows loss of the left heart border, localising her pneumonia to the lingula.

FJ2477.name: Superior lingular bronchial tree
FJ2477.details: Subsegmental bronchi of the left superior lingular segment (S4), the left lung's analogue of the right middle lobe, hanging from the upper lobe bronchus.
FJ2477.clinicalCondition: Lingular syndrome — like the middle lobe, the lingula's dependent drainage predisposes to chronic atelectasis and bronchiectasis.
FJ2477.clinicalScenario: A woman with chronic cough has CT showing a collapsed, bronchiectatic lingula unchanged over two years.

FJ2478.name: Superior lingular bronchial tree
FJ2478.details: Airway tree within the superior lingular segment, running with lingular branches of the left pulmonary artery and draining to the superior pulmonary vein.
FJ2478.clinicalCondition: Lady Windermere syndrome — Mycobacterium avium complex infects the lingula and middle lobe in older women with voluntary cough suppression.
FJ2478.clinicalScenario: An elderly lifelong non-smoker has lingular bronchiectasis and repeated sputum cultures growing Mycobacterium avium complex.

FJ2540.name: Superior lingular bronchial tree
FJ2540.details: Terminal divisions of the superior lingular bronchus (S4), ventilating the upper part of the lingula beside the cardiac notch of the left lung.
FJ2540.clinicalCondition: Localised resection — bronchiectasis destroyed lingula can be removed by lingulectomy, preserving the rest of the upper lobe.
FJ2540.clinicalScenario: A patient with bronchiectasis confined to the lingula and recurrent haemoptysis undergoes lingulectomy.

FJ2541.name: Trachea
FJ2541.details: Fibrocartilaginous airway from C6 to the carina at T4/5, about 10–12 cm long, kept open by 16–20 C-shaped hyaline rings with trachealis muscle posteriorly against the oesophagus.
FJ2541.clinicalCondition: Post-intubation tracheal stenosis — cuff injury scars the trachea, causing progressive stridor weeks after prolonged ventilation.
FJ2541.clinicalScenario: Six weeks after ICU discharge, a patient develops noisy breathing; CT shows a focal tracheal stenosis at the old cuff site.

FJ3072.name: Anterior inferior tributary of right hepatic biliary tree
FJ3072.details: Segmental bile duct draining the inferior right anterior section (segments V/VIII territory inferiorly) toward the right hepatic duct; part of the intrahepatic biliary confluence pattern.
FJ3072.clinicalCondition: Segmental duct injury — unrecognized division during liver or gallbladder surgery causes postoperative bile leak.
FJ3072.clinicalScenario: After right hepatectomy, bilious fluid collects in the drain; imaging shows a leaking divided anterior segmental duct requiring percutaneous drainage.

FJ3071.name: Anterior superior tributary of right hepatic biliary tree
FJ3071.details: Duct draining the superior anterior sector (segment VIII) joining the right hepatic duct system; its branching pattern varies and is mapped preoperatively by MRCP.
FJ3071.clinicalCondition: Variant segment VIII drainage — anomalous joining to the left system changes hepatectomy planes and risks injury.
FJ3071.clinicalScenario: MRCP before living-donor hepatectomy shows segment VIII draining into the left hepatic duct, altering the surgical plan.

FJ2565.name: Appendix
FJ2565.details: Blind vermiform tube arising from the posteromedial cecum below the ileocecal junction, usually near McBurney's point; its mesoappendix carries the appendicular artery from the ileocolic artery.
FJ2565.clinicalCondition: Acute appendicitis — luminal obstruction causes visceral then right iliac fossa pain, fever and peritonism.
FJ2565.clinicalScenario: A 17-year-old has periumbilical pain migrating to the right iliac fossa with guarding at McBurney's point; appendicectomy confirms inflamed appendix.

FJ2566.name: Ascending colon
FJ2566.details: Retroperitoneal segment of large bowel ascending the right flank from cecum to the hepatic flexure; supplied by ileocolic and right colic branches of superior mesenteric artery.
FJ2566.clinicalCondition: Right-sided colon cancer — typically presents insidiously with iron-deficiency anemia rather than obstruction.
FJ2566.clinicalScenario: A 68-year-old with fatigue and microcytic anemia undergoes colonoscopy, revealing an exophytic ascending colon tumor biopsied as adenocarcinoma.

FJ2816.name: Caudate lobe of liver
FJ2816.details: Segment I on the posterior liver between inferior vena cava and fissure for ligamentum venosum; its emissary veins drain directly into the cava, independent of main hepatic veins.
FJ2816.clinicalCondition: Budd–Chiari syndrome — hepatic vein occlusion spares caudate drainage, producing characteristic caudate hypertrophy.
FJ2816.clinicalScenario: A woman with ascites and hepatomegaly has CT showing an enlarged caudate lobe with absent hepatic vein flow, confirming Budd–Chiari syndrome.

FJ1883.name: Caudate lobe tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ1883.details: Small duct draining part of the caudate lobe (segment I) into the left hepatic duct near the hilum; caudate ducts join both right and left systems variably.
FJ1883.clinicalCondition: Hilar tumor staging — caudate duct involvement raises the Bismuth–Corlette class and may preclude resection.
FJ1883.clinicalScenario: Cholangiography in a jaundiced patient shows tumor extending into caudate ducts bilaterally, classifying the hilar cholangiocarcinoma as type IV.

FJ3079.name: Common hepatic duct
FJ3079.details: Formed at the porta hepatis by union of right and left hepatic ducts; descends in the free edge of lesser omentum until joined by the cystic duct.
FJ3079.clinicalCondition: Iatrogenic bile duct injury — clipping or division during cholecystectomy causes jaundice or bile peritonitis.
FJ3079.clinicalScenario: Three days after laparoscopic cholecystectomy a patient is deeply jaundiced; MRCP shows the common hepatic duct clipped and excised.

FJ3080.name: Cystic duct
FJ3080.details: About 3 cm duct linking gallbladder neck to the common hepatic duct, its mucosa folded into spiral valves of Heister; length and insertion vary considerably between individuals.
FJ3080.clinicalCondition: Mirizzi syndrome — an impacted cystic duct stone compresses the common hepatic duct causing obstructive jaundice.
FJ3080.clinicalScenario: A woman with jaundice and gallstones has imaging showing a large stone in the cystic duct compressing the common hepatic duct.

FJ2567.name: Descending colon
FJ2567.details: Retroperitoneal large bowel descending the left flank from splenic flexure to sigmoid colon at the pelvic brim; supplied by left colic branch of inferior mesenteric artery.
FJ2567.clinicalCondition: Left-sided colon cancer — narrowing lumen causes altered bowel habit and eventual large bowel obstruction.
FJ2567.clinicalScenario: A 74-year-old reports months of thinner stools and fresh bleeding; barium imaging shows an apple-core stricture of the descending colon.

FJ2587.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2587.details: Terminal ileum in the right iliac fossa and pelvis, site of vitamin B12–intrinsic factor and bile salt absorption; rich in Peyer's patches and supplied by ileal branches of superior mesenteric artery.
FJ2587.clinicalCondition: Crohn's disease — transmural terminal ileitis with skip lesions, cobblestoning, strictures and fistulas.
FJ2587.clinicalScenario: A 24-year-old has months of right iliac fossa pain, diarrhea and weight loss; colonoscopy shows aphthous ulceration of the terminal ileum.

FJ2588.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2588.details: Second mesh of terminal ileum; its wall contains aggregated lymphoid follicles that sample luminal antigens, and the ileal brake slows transit when fat reaches it.
FJ2588.clinicalCondition: Meckel diverticulum — vitelline duct remnant on the antimesenteric border, classically 2 feet from the ileocecal valve.
FJ2588.clinicalScenario: A 6-year-old passes painless dark-red blood per rectum; a technetium scan shows ectopic gastric mucosa in a Meckel diverticulum.

FJ2589.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2589.details: Segment of distal ileum approaching the ileocecal junction; peristalsis here is regulated to meter chyme into the cecum and limit colonic bacterial reflux.
FJ2589.clinicalCondition: Ileocecal tuberculosis — chronic granulomatous ileitis mimicking Crohn's disease in endemic regions.
FJ2589.clinicalScenario: A migrant worker with night sweats, weight loss and right iliac fossa mass has biopsies showing caseating granulomas of the ileum.

FJ2590.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2590.details: Distal ileal loop commonly lying in the pelvis, where it contacts bladder, uterus or sigmoid colon; inflammation here may irritate neighboring pelvic organs.
FJ2590.clinicalCondition: Gallstone ileus — a large stone eroding through a cholecystoenteric fistula impacts at the ileocecal narrowing.
FJ2590.clinicalScenario: An elderly woman has small bowel obstruction with pneumobilia on CT and an ectopic gallstone impacted in the distal ileum.

FJ2591.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2591.details: Ileal segment whose enteroendocrine cells increase distally; serotonin-secreting enterochromaffin cells here are the commonest source of small bowel neuroendocrine tumors.
FJ2591.clinicalCondition: Ileal carcinoid tumor — small primary causing desmoplastic mesenteric fibrosis and, after liver metastasis, carcinoid syndrome.
FJ2591.clinicalScenario: A man with episodic flushing, watery diarrhea and a spiculated mesenteric mass is found to have a small ileal neuroendocrine tumor.

FJ2592.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2592.details: Mobile distal ileum suspended by the mesentery, free to telescope into the cecum at the ileocecal junction, particularly in infants with hypertrophied lymphoid tissue.
FJ2592.clinicalCondition: Ileocolic intussusception — bowel telescoping causes colicky pain, currant-jelly stool and a sausage-shaped mass.
FJ2592.clinicalScenario: A 9-month-old screams intermittently, draws up his legs and passes red jelly-like stool; ultrasound shows a target sign, reduced by air enema.

FJ2593.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2593.details: Terminal ileum whose resection or disease removes the specialized B12 and bile acid transporters found nowhere else in the gut.
FJ2593.clinicalCondition: Vitamin B12 deficiency — ileal resection causes megaloblastic anemia and potentially irreversible neurological damage.
FJ2593.clinicalScenario: Two years after terminal ileal resection for Crohn's disease, a woman develops macrocytic anemia and glossitis, corrected with parenteral B12.

FJ2594.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2594.details: Loops of distal ileum occupying the lower abdomen, frequently involved in pelvic adhesions after surgery or inflammation, predisposing to mechanical obstruction.
FJ2594.clinicalCondition: Adhesive small bowel obstruction — fibrous bands kink ileal loops causing colicky pain, vomiting and distension.
FJ2594.clinicalScenario: A woman with a previous hysterectomy presents with colicky pain and absolute constipation; CT shows a transition point in a distal ileal loop.

FJ2595.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2595.details: Distal ileum rich in Peyer's patches, which Salmonella typhi invades and ulcerates along the bowel's long axis during enteric fever.
FJ2595.clinicalCondition: Typhoid ileal perforation — ulcerated Peyer's patches perforate in the third week of enteric fever.
FJ2595.clinicalScenario: A traveler with two weeks of stepwise fever develops sudden generalized peritonitis; laparotomy finds a single perforation in the terminal ileum.

FJ2597.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2597.details: Ileal segment within the right lower quadrant where its serosa, wall layers and lacteals make it a recognized site for primary gastrointestinal lymphoma.
FJ2597.clinicalCondition: Ileal lymphoma — mural mass causing obstruction, intussusception or perforation with systemic B symptoms.
FJ2597.clinicalScenario: A man with drenching night sweats and weight loss has CT showing aneurysmal dilatation of an ileal segment, biopsied as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

FJ2598.name: Distal part of ileum
FJ2598.details: Final ileal mesh; pelvic ileal loops lie within the field of pelvic radiotherapy for cervical and prostate cancers and are vulnerable to late radiation injury.
FJ2598.clinicalCondition: Radiation enteritis — late fibrosis and stricturing of pelvic ileum years after radiotherapy.
FJ2598.clinicalScenario: Five years after cervical radiotherapy, a woman has recurrent subacute obstruction from a fixed, narrowed distal ileal stricture.

FJ2611.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2611.details: Jejunum beyond its midpoint, still with tall circular folds and rich villi for absorption; supplied by jejunal branches forming arcades of the superior mesenteric artery.
FJ2611.clinicalCondition: Celiac disease — gluten-driven villous atrophy maximal in proximal small bowel, sampled by jejunal/duodenal biopsy.
FJ2611.clinicalScenario: A woman with iron deficiency and bloating has jejunal biopsies showing subtotal villous atrophy and positive tissue transglutaminase antibodies.

FJ2612.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2612.details: Jejunal wall is thicker and more vascular than ileum, with prominent plicae circulares that slow transit and enlarge absorptive surface area roughly threefold.
FJ2612.clinicalCondition: Jejunal diverticulosis — acquired pulsion diverticula on the mesenteric border causing bacterial overgrowth and malabsorption.
FJ2612.clinicalScenario: An elderly man with bloating, steatorrhea and B12 deficiency has barium imaging showing multiple wide-mouthed jejunal diverticula.

FJ2613.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2613.details: Surgically accessible jejunal loop about 40 cm beyond the ligament of Treitz is the standard site chosen for feeding jejunostomy and Roux limb construction.
FJ2613.clinicalCondition: Feeding jejunostomy — direct jejunal access provides enteral nutrition when the stomach cannot be used.
FJ2613.clinicalScenario: After esophagectomy, a surgical jejunostomy in the proximal jejunum delivers feed while the anastomosis heals.

FJ2614.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2614.details: Intra-abdominal jejunal loops are relatively unprotected by ribs or pelvis, making them vulnerable to blunt compression against the vertebral column.
FJ2614.clinicalCondition: Traumatic jejunal perforation — seat-belt or handlebar compression bursts the bowel causing chemical peritonitis.
FJ2614.clinicalScenario: A cyclist with a handlebar injury develops worsening abdominal tenderness; CT shows free gas and a jejunal wall defect.

FJ2615.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2615.details: Congenital narrowing may persist here as a web or atresia; the apple-peel variant wraps distal bowel around a single mesenteric vessel.
FJ2615.clinicalCondition: Jejunal atresia — congenital discontinuity causing neonatal bilious vomiting and dilated proximal loops.
FJ2615.clinicalScenario: A newborn vomits bile on day one; radiographs show a triple bubble and surgery confirms jejunal atresia.

FJ2616.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2616.details: Submucosal injury from chronic NSAID use can heal as thin circumferential webs (diaphragms) scattered through jejunum and ileum.
FJ2616.clinicalCondition: NSAID diaphragm disease — multiple thin jejunal strictures causing obscure bleeding and subacute obstruction.
FJ2616.clinicalScenario: A long-term diclofenac user has recurrent cramping and iron deficiency; capsule endoscopy shows diaphragm-like jejunal strictures.

FJ2618.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2618.details: Jejunum depends entirely on superior mesenteric arterial flow through its arcades; emboli typically lodge just beyond the middle colic origin, threatening jejunum first.
FJ2618.clinicalCondition: Acute mesenteric ischemia — sudden SMA embolism causes pain out of proportion to examination findings.
FJ2618.clinicalScenario: A man with atrial fibrillation develops severe central abdominal pain with a soft abdomen; CT angiography shows an SMA embolus.

FJ2619.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2619.details: Mesenchymal tumors arising in the jejunal wall grow outward silently, presenting through their rich blood supply rather than obstruction.
FJ2619.clinicalCondition: Jejunal GIST — gastrointestinal stromal tumor causing occult or massive gastrointestinal bleeding.
FJ2619.clinicalScenario: A patient with recurrent melena and normal endoscopies is found on CT enterography to have a vascular jejunal GIST.

FJ2620.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2620.details: Jejunal lamina propria is the diagnostic window for systemic infiltrative diseases; biopsies here capture pathogens that duodenal samples may miss.
FJ2620.clinicalCondition: Whipple disease — Tropheryma whipplei fills jejunal macrophages, causing malabsorption, arthralgia and neurological signs.
FJ2620.clinicalScenario: A middle-aged man with migratory joint pains, diarrhea and weight loss has jejunal biopsy showing PAS-positive macrophage inclusions.

FJ2621.name: Distal part of jejunum
FJ2621.details: After Billroth II gastrectomy the afferent jejunal loop drains bile and pancreatic juice toward the gastric remnant; its obstruction produces a distinct postprandial syndrome.
FJ2621.clinicalCondition: Afferent loop syndrome — post-gastrectomy loop obstruction causing pain relieved by projectile bilious vomiting.
FJ2621.clinicalScenario: Years after Billroth II surgery, a man has post-meal epigastric fullness suddenly relieved by vomiting bile, without food.

FJ2573.name: Duodenum
FJ2573.details: C-shaped first part of small intestine curving around the pancreatic head; receives bile and pancreatic ducts at the ampulla, mostly retroperitoneal, with submucosal Brunner glands.
FJ2573.clinicalCondition: Duodenal ulcer — posterior wall ulcers erode the gastroduodenal artery causing major hemorrhage.
FJ2573.clinicalScenario: A man with food-relieved epigastric pain presents with melena and postural hypotension; endoscopy finds a bleeding posterior duodenal ulcer.

FJ2563.name: Esophagus
FJ2563.details: Muscular tube from cricopharyngeus (C6) to cardia (T11), about 25 cm, with constrictions at cricoid, aortic arch/bronchus and diaphragmatic hiatus; lower sphincter prevents reflux.
FJ2563.clinicalCondition: Esophageal carcinoma — progressive dysphagia, solids before liquids, with marked weight loss.
FJ2563.clinicalScenario: A 68-year-old smoker reports three months of worsening dysphagia and 10 kg weight loss; endoscopy reveals a malignant mid-esophageal stricture.

FJ2817.name: Gallbladder
FJ2817.details: Pear-shaped reservoir under the right liver lobe storing and concentrating bile; fundus, body and neck, with Hartmann pouch near the neck where stones impact.
FJ2817.clinicalCondition: Acute cholecystitis — cystic duct stone obstruction causing right upper quadrant pain and Murphy's sign.
FJ2817.clinicalScenario: A woman has constant right upper quadrant pain, fever and arrest of inspiration on palpation after a fatty meal, confirming acute cholecystitis.

FJ2599.name: Ileocecal junction
FJ2599.details: Junction where terminal ileum opens into the cecum through the ileocecal valve lips; the appendix orifice lies just below, a key colonoscopic landmark.
FJ2599.clinicalCondition: Adult intussusception — usually driven by a lead-point tumor at this junction, unlike childhood cases.
FJ2599.clinicalScenario: CT for intermittent colicky pain shows a target sign at the ileocecal junction with a fat-density lipoma acting as lead point.

FJ3089.name: Lateral inferior tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ3089.details: Duct draining the inferior left lateral section (segment III) toward the left hepatic duct within the umbilical fissure; segment III duct runs a relatively accessible superficial course.
FJ3089.clinicalCondition: Segment III bypass — this duct is anastomosed to jejunum to palliate unresectable hilar obstruction.
FJ3089.clinicalScenario: A patient with unresectable hilar cholangiocarcinoma undergoes segment III cholangiojejunostomy, relieving jaundice and pruritus.

FJ3088.name: Lateral superior tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ3088.details: Duct draining the superior left lateral section (segment II) across the left lobe to join the left hepatic duct; courses near the left triangular ligament.
FJ3088.clinicalCondition: Segmental duct injury — division during left hepatectomy or gastric surgery can cause bile leak or biloma.
FJ3088.clinicalScenario: A subphrenic biloma forms after left hepatectomy; fistulography traces it to a divided segment II duct.

FJ3090.name: Lateral superior tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ3090.details: Second mesh of the segment II duct; isolated obstruction of such a sectoral duct produces segmental cholangitis without jaundice because the remaining liver drains normally.
FJ3090.clinicalCondition: Segmental cholangitis — obstructed undrained segment becomes infected after contrast injection at ERCP.
FJ3090.clinicalScenario: After cholangiography, a patient spikes fevers and rigors from an obstructed, opacified segment II duct that was left undrained.

FJ3094.name: Left duct of caudate lobe of liver
FJ3094.details: Minute duct draining caudate parenchyma into the left hepatic duct close to the confluence; one of several small caudate radicles entering both hepatic ducts.
FJ3094.clinicalCondition: Caudate duct involvement — tumor spread here signals advanced hilar disease affecting resectability decisions.
FJ3094.clinicalScenario: Imaging review for a hilar tumor shows caudate duct dilatation on the left, prompting multidisciplinary discussion about extended resection.

FJ3096.name: Left hepatic duct
FJ3096.details: Formed by segmental ducts within the left lobe, it has a longer extrahepatic course (about 1.7 cm) in the porta hepatis before joining the right duct.
FJ3096.clinicalCondition: Hilar cholangiocarcinoma (Klatskin tumor) — grows at the confluence causing painless progressive obstructive jaundice.
FJ3096.clinicalScenario: A 70-year-old with painless jaundice, pale stools and a non-palpable gallbladder has a stricture at the hepatic duct confluence on MRCP.

FJ2765.name: Left sublingual gland
FJ2765.details: Smallest major salivary gland in the floor of mouth above mylohyoid, draining by multiple ducts of Rivinus along the sublingual fold; produces predominantly mucous saliva.
FJ2765.clinicalCondition: Ranula — mucous extravasation from this gland forming a translucent floor-of-mouth swelling.
FJ2765.clinicalScenario: A teenager has a soft bluish swelling in the left floor of mouth resembling a frog's belly; excision of gland and cyst cures it.

FJ2766.name: Left submandibular gland
FJ2766.details: Mixed salivary gland in the submandibular triangle wrapping the mylohyoid edge; its Wharton duct opens at the sublingual caruncle, with the lingual nerve looping beneath it.
FJ2766.clinicalCondition: Sialolithiasis — alkaline viscous saliva and uphill duct make this gland the commonest stone site.
FJ2766.clinicalScenario: A man gets painful left submandibular swelling at mealtimes that slowly subsides; CT shows a stone in Wharton's duct.

FJ3103.name: Medial inferior tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ3103.details: Duct draining inferior segment IV (quadrate region) into the left hepatic duct near the umbilical fissure; segment IV ducts show frequent branching variants.
FJ3103.clinicalCondition: Aberrant segment IV duct — injury during cholecystectomy or hilar dissection causes postoperative bile collection.
FJ3103.clinicalScenario: Persistent bile drainage after difficult cholecystectomy is traced to an injured low-inserting segment IV duct managed by stenting.

FJ3104.name: Medial superior tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ3104.details: Duct draining superior segment IV toward the umbilical portion of the left hepatic duct; its position defines part of the resection plane in left hepatectomy.
FJ3104.clinicalCondition: Segmental cholangiocarcinoma — peripheral tumors in small ducts stay silent until central spread causes jaundice.
FJ3104.clinicalScenario: An incidental liver mass in segment IV proves to be intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma arising from its draining duct system.

FJ3105.name: Medial superior tributary of left hepatic biliary tree
FJ3105.details: Second mesh of the segment IV superior duct; chronic segmental obstruction upstream produces the atrophy–hypertrophy complex seen in long-standing hilar disease.
FJ3105.clinicalCondition: Atrophy–hypertrophy complex — chronically obstructed segment shrinks while drained segments enlarge compensatorily.
FJ3105.clinicalScenario: CT in chronic hilar obstruction shows a shrunken segment IV with crowding of its ducts and compensatory right lobe hypertrophy.

FJ3396.name: Mesentery of small intestine
FJ3396.details: Fan-shaped double peritoneal fold suspending jejunum and ileum; its root runs 15 cm from the duodenojejunal flexure (L2) to the right sacroiliac joint, carrying vessels, nerves and lymphatics.
FJ3396.clinicalCondition: Mesenteric adenitis — inflamed mesenteric nodes mimic appendicitis in children after viral illness.
FJ3396.clinicalScenario: A 7-year-old with recent cold has right iliac fossa pain but soft abdomen; ultrasound shows enlarged mesenteric nodes and a normal appendix.

FJ3397.name: Mesoappendix
FJ3397.details: Short triangular fold of peritoneum suspending the appendix from the terminal ileal mesentery; transmits the appendicular artery and vein to the appendiceal wall.
FJ3397.clinicalCondition: Appendicular artery thrombosis — end-artery occlusion during appendicitis leads to gangrene and perforation.
FJ3397.clinicalScenario: A delayed-presentation appendicitis patient has a gangrenous black appendiceal tip at surgery, its mesoappendiceal artery thrombosed by inflammation.

FJ2576.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2576.details: Mid-ileum has thinner walls and fewer circular folds than jejunum, with increasing Peyer's patches; Yersinia enterocolitica targets this lymphoid tissue.
FJ2576.clinicalCondition: Yersinia ileitis — infection mimics appendicitis (pseudoappendicitis) with a normal appendix at operation.
FJ2576.clinicalScenario: A young adult undergoes appendicectomy for right iliac fossa pain; the appendix is normal but the ileum is inflamed and nodes enlarged.

FJ2577.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2577.details: Mobile mid-ileal loops lie near the pelvic brim; in infants with malrotation the entire midgut can twist around the superior mesenteric artery pedicle here.
FJ2577.clinicalCondition: Midgut volvulus — malrotation lets bowel twist on a narrow mesenteric base, threatening total midgut infarction.
FJ2577.clinicalScenario: A 3-week-old with bilious vomiting and bloody stool has a whirlpool sign on ultrasound; emergency Ladd procedure untwists the volvulus.

FJ2578.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2578.details: Ileal lumen in children in endemic regions can be obstructed by masses of the roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides tangled at narrower segments.
FJ2578.clinicalCondition: Ascaris bolus obstruction — worm masses block the ileum causing colicky pain and distension.
FJ2578.clinicalScenario: A 5-year-old in a rural area presents with obstruction and palpable mobile masses; imaging shows spaghetti-like worms filling the ileum.

FJ2579.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2579.details: Postoperative ileal motility normally returns last among gut segments (small bowel recovers first, colon last patterns vary); handling and peritonitis prolong adynamic ileus here.
FJ2579.clinicalCondition: Postoperative ileus — functional ileal paralysis causes distension, vomiting and absent bowel sounds after laparotomy.
FJ2579.clinicalScenario: Three days after colectomy, a patient's abdomen is distended and silent with dilated ileal loops but no transition point on CT.

FJ2580.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2580.details: Congenital enteric duplications may share the ileal wall and blood supply, forming cystic or tubular structures along the mesenteric border.
FJ2580.clinicalCondition: Ileal duplication cyst — presents in childhood with pain, palpable mass or bleeding from ectopic mucosa.
FJ2580.clinicalScenario: A toddler with intermittent pain has an abdominal ultrasound showing a cystic structure sharing the ileal wall, a duplication cyst.

FJ2581.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2581.details: The ileal wall is thin enough that sharp ingested objects that pass the stomach and pylorus most often perforate here or at the ileocecal region.
FJ2581.clinicalCondition: Foreign-body perforation — fish bones or toothpicks pierce the ileum mimicking appendicitis or Crohn's disease.
FJ2581.clinicalScenario: An elderly man with right iliac fossa pain has CT showing a linear hyperdensity perforating an ileal loop — a swallowed fish bone.

FJ2582.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2582.details: Healed tuberculous or inflammatory ileal strictures may persist in mid-ileum as short fibrotic narrowings years after the original disease resolves.
FJ2582.clinicalCondition: Benign ileal stricture — fibrotic narrowing causes recurrent subacute obstruction and colicky pain.
FJ2582.clinicalScenario: A woman treated for abdominal TB a decade ago has repeated episodes of post-prandial colic; enterography shows a short mid-ileal stricture.

FJ2583.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2583.details: A segment of ileum is routinely diverted as a urinary conduit (Bricker) after cystectomy; its mucosa continues absorbing urinary solutes from the diverted stream.
FJ2583.clinicalCondition: Ileal conduit metabolic acidosis — absorption of urinary chloride and ammonium causes hyperchloremic acidosis.
FJ2583.clinicalScenario: Years after cystectomy with ileal conduit, a patient develops fatigue and hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis managed with alkalinization.

FJ2584.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2584.details: In ulcerative colitis, severe pancolitis may reflux inflamed content backward, producing a short continuous segment of mild ileal inflammation adjacent to the colon.
FJ2584.clinicalCondition: Backwash ileitis — limited terminal/mid-ileal inflammation accompanying ulcerative pancolitis, not Crohn's disease.
FJ2584.clinicalScenario: Colonoscopy in severe ulcerative colitis shows continuous colonic disease extending a few centimeters into the ileum, judged to be backwash ileitis.

FJ2586.name: Middle part of ileum
FJ2586.details: Submucosal hemorrhage and edema can develop in the ileal wall in small-vessel vasculitis, thickening folds and predisposing to intussusception in children.
FJ2586.clinicalCondition: IgA vasculitis (Henoch–Schönlein) ileitis — mural hematoma causes pain, bleeding and intussusception.
FJ2586.clinicalScenario: A 6-year-old with palpable purpura and joint pains develops colicky abdominal pain; ultrasound shows thickened ileal loops and an intussusception.

FJ2607.name: Middle part of jejunum
FJ2607.details: Mid-jejunum performs the bulk of carbohydrate, amino acid, fat and vitamin absorption through long villi, dense microvilli and high blood flow.
FJ2607.clinicalCondition: Short bowel syndrome — extensive jejunal-ileal resection leaves insufficient absorptive surface, causing diarrhea and malnutrition.
FJ2607.clinicalScenario: After massive resection for mesenteric infarction, a patient with 80 cm of remaining jejunum requires long-term parenteral nutrition.

FJ2608.name: Middle part of jejunum
FJ2608.details: Post-infectious mucosal injury resembling celiac disease can flatten jejunal villi in residents of or travelers to tropical regions.
FJ2608.clinicalCondition: Tropical sprue — post-infective jejunal malabsorption causing steatorrhea, folate and B12 deficiency.
FJ2608.clinicalScenario: A returned traveler has months of fatty diarrhea and glossitis; jejunal biopsy shows villous blunting that responds to tetracycline and folate.

FJ2609.name: Middle part of jejunum
FJ2609.details: In Roux-en-Y reconstruction a jejunal limb carries food while a second limb drains bile; the jejunojejunostomy joins them about 40–60 cm downstream.
FJ2609.clinicalCondition: Roux limb obstruction — adhesions or internal hernia obstruct the jejunal limb after bypass surgery.
FJ2609.clinicalScenario: A post-gastric-bypass patient has severe intermittent epigastric pain; CT suggests an internal hernia at the jejunal mesenteric defect.

FJ2610.name: Middle part of jejunum
FJ2610.details: Chronic reduction of mesenteric flow produces postprandial jejunal ischemia pain (intestinal angina) typically 15–30 minutes after eating, driving food fear and weight loss.
FJ2610.clinicalCondition: Chronic mesenteric ischemia — atherosclerotic stenoses cause postprandial pain, sitophobia and weight loss.
FJ2610.clinicalScenario: An elderly vasculopath loses 12 kg, fearing meals because of predictable postprandial pain; angiography shows severe SMA and celiac stenoses.

FJ2628.name: Middle part of jejunum
FJ2628.details: Hamartomatous polyps grow in the jejunum in Peutz–Jeghers syndrome, acting as lead points while mucocutaneous pigmentation marks the condition externally.
FJ2628.clinicalCondition: Peutz–Jeghers jejunal polyps — cause recurrent intussusception and bleeding from adolescence onward.
FJ2628.clinicalScenario: A teenager with dark lip freckling presents with small bowel intussusception; surgery finds a large pedunculated jejunal hamartoma.

FJ1895.name: Pancreas
FJ1895.details: Retroperitoneal gland at L1–L2 with head cradled by the duodenum, body crossing the aorta, and tail reaching the splenic hilum; combines exocrine acini with endocrine islets.
FJ1895.clinicalCondition: Acute pancreatitis — autodigestion from gallstones or alcohol causing epigastric pain radiating to the back.
FJ1895.clinicalScenario: A man with heavy alcohol use has severe epigastric pain boring through to his back, vomiting and a markedly raised lipase.

FJ1896.name: Pancreatic duct
FJ1896.details: Duct of Wirsung running from tail to head, usually joining the common bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla (of Vater) opening on the major duodenal papilla.
FJ1896.clinicalCondition: Pancreas divisum — failed embryonic duct fusion forces drainage through the minor papilla, predisposing to pancreatitis.
FJ1896.clinicalScenario: Recurrent unexplained pancreatitis leads to MRCP showing a dominant dorsal duct crossing to the minor papilla — pancreas divisum.

FJ2630.name: Pancreatic duct tree
FJ2630.details: Branching network of interlobular ducts converging on the main duct, giving the gland its lobulated drainage pattern mapped by MRCP and pancreatography.
FJ2630.clinicalCondition: Chronic pancreatitis — irregular dilated main duct with side-branch ectasia produces the classic chain-of-lakes appearance.
FJ2630.clinicalScenario: ERCP in a chronic alcoholic with steatorrhea shows a beaded, dilated pancreatic duct with intraductal calculi.

FJ2629.name: Parenchyma of pancreas
FJ2629.details: Lobulated glandular tissue of serous acini secreting digestive enzymes and ducts, interspersed with islets of Langerhans secreting insulin, glucagon and somatostatin into the portal blood.
FJ2629.clinicalCondition: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma — head tumors obstruct the bile duct producing painless jaundice and a palpable gallbladder.
FJ2629.clinicalScenario: A 72-year-old with painless jaundice, pale stools and weight loss has a palpable non-tender gallbladder and a pancreatic head mass on CT.

FJ3108.name: Posterior inferior tributary of right hepatic biliary tree
FJ3108.details: Duct draining the inferior posterior right section (segment VI) into the right posterior sectoral duct; right posterior ducts are notorious for low or ectopic insertions.
FJ3108.clinicalCondition: Aberrant right posterior duct — crossing variants are divided unknowingly at cholecystectomy, leaking bile.
FJ3108.clinicalScenario: Cholangiography after postoperative bile leak shows the segment VI duct joining the common hepatic duct below the clipped stump.

FJ3109.name: Posterior superior tributary of right hepatic biliary tree
FJ3109.details: Duct draining the superior posterior section (segment VII) joining the posterior sectoral duct near the right portal pedicle; identified on segmental cholangiography and MRCP.
FJ3109.clinicalCondition: Segment VII duct injury — unrecognized division during right hepatectomy causes biloma and sepsis.
FJ3109.clinicalScenario: A postoperative biloma is drained and fistulography demonstrates a leaking divided segment VII duct requiring stenting.

FJ3110.name: Posterior superior tributary of right hepatic biliary tree
FJ3110.details: Second mesh of the segment VII duct; long-standing hilar obstruction isolates such posterior ducts, so they must be specifically drained during palliative stenting.
FJ3110.clinicalCondition: Isolated segmental obstruction — undrained posterior segments develop cholangitis despite an apparently patent main stent.
FJ3110.clinicalScenario: A patient with a hilar stent remains septic until imaging shows an isolated obstructed segment VII system needing separate drainage.

FJ2574.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2574.details: Ileum just beyond the jejunoileal transition, with progressively fewer circular folds and thinner wall than jejunum, transitioning in absorption profile along its length.
FJ2574.clinicalCondition: Extensive ileal disease burden — widespread Crohn's involvement here risks malabsorption even without terminal ileal loss.
FJ2574.clinicalScenario: Imaging in a Crohn's patient shows multiple proximal ileal skip strictures with prestenotic dilatation, prompting balloon dilation.

FJ2575.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2575.details: Congenital ileal atresia may occur at this level with a fibrous cord or gap; distal bowel is collapsed and unused in the newborn.
FJ2575.clinicalCondition: Ileal atresia — congenital interruption causing neonatal obstruction with bilious vomiting.
FJ2575.clinicalScenario: A day-old infant with abdominal distension and failure to pass meconium has dilated loops and a microcolon from ileal atresia.

FJ2585.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2585.details: The ileum's antimesenteric border carries prominent aggregated lymphoid follicles (Peyer patches), which sample luminal antigens and form a major gut immune interface.
FJ2585.clinicalCondition: Typhoid fever — Salmonella typhi invades through Peyer patches, which may ulcerate in the third week, causing intestinal hemorrhage or perforation.
FJ2585.clinicalScenario: A traveller returns with step-ladder fever and abdominal tenderness; in the third week he develops peritonitis from a perforated ileal ulcer.

FJ2596.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2596.details: A surgically created blind ileal loop (after bypass or side-to-side anastomosis) stagnates, allowing bacterial overgrowth that deconjugates bile salts and consumes vitamin B12.
FJ2596.clinicalCondition: Blind loop syndrome — bacterial overgrowth in stagnant ileum causing steatorrhea and megaloblastic anemia.
FJ2596.clinicalScenario: Years after bowel bypass, a patient has fatty diarrhea and macrocytosis that resolve with rotating antibiotics.

FJ2600.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2600.details: Ileal loops are the commonest intussuscepting segment in adults as well as children when a mural lesion serves as a lead point.
FJ2600.clinicalCondition: Ileoileal intussusception — transient in adults but persistent forms signal an underlying lesion.
FJ2600.clinicalScenario: CT during pain episodes shows a short ileoileal intussusception that persists on repeat imaging, prompting resection of a small tumor.

FJ2601.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2601.details: An ileal conduit's stomal end can narrow from ischemia or chronic appliance trauma, gradually obstructing urinary drainage upstream.
FJ2601.clinicalCondition: Ileal conduit stomal stenosis — causes recurrent urinary infections and hydronephrosis if unrecognized.
FJ2601.clinicalScenario: A cystectomy patient with recurrent pyelonephritis is found to have a tight conduit stoma and bilateral hydronephrosis.

FJ2602.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2602.details: In cystic fibrosis, abnormally viscid meconium-like content can obstruct the ileum beyond infancy, termed distal intestinal obstruction syndrome, often involving proximal segments too.
FJ2602.clinicalCondition: Distal intestinal obstruction syndrome — inspissated ileal content obstructs the bowel in cystic fibrosis patients.
FJ2602.clinicalScenario: An adolescent with cystic fibrosis presents with right iliac fossa mass and obstruction, relieved by osmotic contrast enema and hydration.

FJ2603.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2603.details: Hookworms (Necator, Ancylostoma) attach chiefly to duodenal and jejunal mucosa; heavy burdens extend into the ileum, feeding on blood and causing chronic iron loss.
FJ2603.clinicalCondition: Hookworm anemia — chronic proximal bowel blood loss produces severe iron-deficiency anemia in endemic areas.
FJ2603.clinicalScenario: A barefoot farmer with profound microcytic anemia and eosinophilia has hookworm ova in stool and improves with albendazole and iron.

FJ2604.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2604.details: Strongyloides larvae mature in proximal small bowel mucosa; in immunosuppressed hosts autoinfection accelerates into hyperinfection involving ileum widely.
FJ2604.clinicalCondition: Strongyloides hyperinfection — steroid-triggered dissemination causing ileus, malabsorption and gram-negative sepsis.
FJ2604.clinicalScenario: A transplant patient started on high-dose steroids develops ileus, diarrhea and E. coli bacteremia; stool shows Strongyloides larvae.

FJ2605.name: Proximal part of ileum
FJ2605.details: The proximal ileum contributes most of the remaining absorptive reserve after jejunal loss; its adaptation (villous hyperplasia) determines survival without parenteral support after resection.
FJ2605.clinicalCondition: Intestinal adaptation failure — after massive resection, remnant ileum cannot adapt enough, causing intestinal failure.
FJ2605.clinicalScenario: A patient left with 60 cm of ileum after volvulus remains dependent on parenteral nutrition despite months of enteral rehabilitation.

FJ2606.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2606.details: Begins at the duodenojejunal flexure suspended by the ligament of Treitz (L2); this landmark divides upper from lower gastrointestinal bleeding sources.
FJ2606.clinicalCondition: Bleeding localization — hemorrhage proximal to Treitz presents as hematemesis; beyond it, usually melena.
FJ2606.clinicalScenario: A bleeding patient is triaged to urgent gastroscopy because hematemesis localizes the source proximal to the ligament of Treitz.

FJ2617.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2617.details: Tallest villi and richest iron and folate transport make proximal jejunum (with duodenum) the principal site of iron absorption.
FJ2617.clinicalCondition: Iron malabsorption — proximal jejunal disease in celiac disease causes iron deficiency before other deficiencies.
FJ2617.clinicalScenario: A woman's refractory iron-deficiency anemia, unresponsive to oral iron, leads to celiac serology and jejunal biopsy confirmation.

FJ2622.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2622.details: Transpyloric nasojejunal tubes are advanced beyond the ligament of Treitz into this segment to feed patients distal to the stomach and pancreas.
FJ2622.clinicalCondition: Post-pyloric feeding — jejunal feeding reduces pancreatic stimulation and aspiration in severe pancreatitis.
FJ2622.clinicalScenario: A nasojejunal tube is placed endoscopically for a patient with necrotizing pancreatitis, allowing early enteral nutrition.

FJ2623.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2623.details: Large true diverticula occasionally form in the proximal jejunum where vessels pierce the muscularis, and may inflame or perforate like their colonic counterparts.
FJ2623.clinicalCondition: Jejunal diverticulitis — perforation of a proximal diverticulum mimics perforated peptic ulcer.
FJ2623.clinicalScenario: An elderly patient with sudden epigastric peritonitis has CT showing a perforated jejunal diverticulum with localized free gas.

FJ2624.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2624.details: Eosinophilic infiltration of the proximal jejunal wall can thicken folds and impair motility and absorption in allergic gastrointestinal disease.
FJ2624.clinicalCondition: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis — jejunal infiltration causing pain, malabsorption and sometimes ascites.
FJ2624.clinicalScenario: A young atopic man with postprandial pain and peripheral eosinophilia has jejunal biopsies packed with eosinophils, responding to dietary exclusion.

FJ2625.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2625.details: In advanced celiac disease, barium studies show loss of proximal jejunal folds with compensatory fold prominence in the ileum (jejunization of ileum pattern).
FJ2625.clinicalCondition: Radiological celiac pattern — jejunal fold atrophy on imaging suggests long-standing mucosal disease.
FJ2625.clinicalScenario: A barium follow-through in a malnourished patient shows a dilated, featureless proximal jejunum with reversed fold pattern, prompting biopsy.

FJ2626.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2626.details: Jejunal loops just beyond Treitz herniate through congenital paraduodenal fossae, the commonest internal hernias, clustering bowel in an abnormal sac.
FJ2626.clinicalCondition: Left paraduodenal hernia — jejunum trapped behind the inferior mesenteric vein causes intermittent obstruction.
FJ2626.clinicalScenario: A young man with recurrent postprandial pain has CT showing clustered jejunal loops encapsulated in the left upper quadrant.

FJ2627.name: Proximal part of jejunum
FJ2627.details: Afferent jejunal loops constructed in gastrojejunostomy lie in this region; kinking at the anastomosis impairs biliopancreatic drainage.
FJ2627.clinicalCondition: Post-gastrectomy jejunal obstruction — kinked afferent loop causes bilious vomiting and risks duodenal stump blowout.
FJ2627.clinicalScenario: A recent Billroth II patient develops severe pain and a rising amylase from an obstructed, distended afferent jejunal loop.

FJ2571.name: Rectum
FJ2571.details: Final 12 cm of large gut from the S3 rectosigmoid junction to the anal canal; its ampulla stores feces, transverse folds (valves of Houston) support the fecal mass.
FJ2571.clinicalCondition: Rectal carcinoma — presents with fresh bleeding, tenesmus and change in bowel habit.
FJ2571.clinicalScenario: A 63-year-old reports tenesmus and blood-streaked stool; rectal examination palpates a hard mass 6 cm from the anal verge.

FJ3123.name: Right hepatic duct
FJ3123.details: Short duct (about 0.9 cm) formed by union of right anterior and posterior sectoral ducts in the right porta hepatis, joining the left duct to form the common hepatic duct.
FJ3123.clinicalCondition: Bile duct injury — sectoral duct variants near Calot's triangle are divided during laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
FJ3123.clinicalScenario: A bile leak after cholecystectomy is shown to come from an aberrant right sectoral duct entering the cystic duct region.

FJ2767.name: Right sublingual gland
FJ2767.details: Mirror gland in the right floor of mouth lying against the mandible's sublingual fossa; its deep ducts open along the sublingual fold beside Wharton's duct.
FJ2767.clinicalCondition: Plunging ranula — sublingual mucus collection herniating through mylohyoid into the neck.
FJ2767.clinicalScenario: A young woman has a right floor-of-mouth swelling plus a soft submandibular neck swelling that cross-fluctuate — a plunging ranula.

FJ2768.name: Right submandibular gland
FJ2768.details: Salivary gland below the mandible whose duct crosses the lingual nerve; facial artery grooves its posterior surface and the marginal mandibular nerve runs superficial to it.
FJ2768.clinicalCondition: Acute bacterial sialadenitis — dehydration and stasis infect the gland in elderly postoperative patients.
FJ2768.clinicalScenario: A dehydrated elderly patient develops a hot, tender right submandibular swelling with pus expressed from the duct orifice.

FJ2564.name: Stomach
FJ2564.details: J-shaped muscular reservoir between esophagus and duodenum with fundus, body, antrum and pylorus; vagal and enteric control of acid secretion and peristaltic mixing.
FJ2564.clinicalCondition: Perforated gastric ulcer — sudden acid spillage causes board-like abdominal rigidity and free subdiaphragmatic gas.
FJ2564.clinicalScenario: An NSAID user collapses with abrupt severe epigastric pain and a rigid abdomen; erect chest film shows gas under the diaphragm.

FJ2568.name: Taenia libera
FJ2568.details: Free (anteroinferior) band of condensed longitudinal muscle running along the colon; all three taeniae converge at the cecal pole onto the appendix base.
FJ2568.clinicalCondition: Surgical landmark — following the taenia libera reliably leads the surgeon to a hidden appendix.
FJ2568.clinicalScenario: During a difficult appendicectomy for a retrocecal appendix, the surgeon follows the anterior taenia of the cecum directly to its base.

FJ2569.name: Taenia mesocolica
FJ2569.details: Posteromedial taenia attached along the transverse mesocolon line of the colon; fat-filled epiploic appendages hang from the colonic wall between the taeniae.
FJ2569.clinicalCondition: Epiploic appendagitis — torsion or venous thrombosis of an appendage causes focal pain mimicking diverticulitis.
FJ2569.clinicalScenario: A man with sharp, well-localized left iliac fossa pain but no fever has CT showing an ovoid fat-density lesion beside the colon.

FJ2570.name: Taenia omentalis
FJ2570.details: Posterolateral taenia to which the greater omentum attaches along the transverse colon; taenial shortening relative to the colonic wall produces the sacculated haustra.
FJ2570.clinicalCondition: Lead-pipe colon — chronic ulcerative colitis destroys haustra, leaving a featureless shortened colon on imaging.
FJ2570.clinicalScenario: Barium enema in a patient with twenty years of ulcerative colitis shows a smooth, ahaustral, narrowed colon resembling a lead pipe.

FJ2761.name: Tongue
FJ2761.details: Muscular organ of intrinsic and extrinsic muscles (all supplied by hypoglossal nerve except palatoglossus); taste from anterior two-thirds via chorda tympani, posterior third via glossopharyngeal nerve.
FJ2761.clinicalCondition: Tongue carcinoma — squamous cancer of the lateral border presenting as a non-healing indurated ulcer.
FJ2761.clinicalScenario: A betel-nut chewer has a three-month non-healing ulcer on the tongue's lateral border with a palpable neck node; biopsy confirms squamous carcinoma.

FJ2572.name: Transverse colon
FJ2572.details: Intraperitoneal colon suspended by the transverse mesocolon, running from hepatic to splenic flexure across the upper abdomen; supplied mainly by the middle colic artery.
FJ2572.clinicalCondition: Toxic megacolon — severe colitis paralyzes and dilates the transverse colon beyond 6 cm, risking perforation.
FJ2572.clinicalScenario: A patient with fulminant ulcerative colitis becomes febrile and distended; plain film shows a grossly dilated transverse colon.

FJ3398.name: Transverse mesocolon
FJ3398.details: Broad peritoneal fold suspending the transverse colon from the anterior border of the pancreas, containing middle colic vessels; its root crosses the duodenum and pancreas.
FJ3398.clinicalCondition: Colon cutoff sign — pancreatic inflammation spreading through this mesocolon abruptly halts colonic gas distension.
FJ3398.clinicalScenario: Abdominal film in acute pancreatitis shows dilated proximal colon ending abruptly at the splenic flexure — the colon cutoff sign.

FJ3145.name: Left kidney
FJ3145.details: Retroperitoneal organ at about T11–L2, slightly higher than the right; hilum transmits vein, artery, and pelvis; related to spleen, pancreatic tail, and colon.
FJ3145.clinicalCondition: Renal cell carcinoma — classically hematuria, flank pain, and a palpable mass.
FJ3145.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old smoker with painless gross hematuria has an enhancing mass in the upper pole of the left kidney on CT.

FJ3144.name: Left ureter
FJ3144.details: Muscular tube, about 25 cm, from renal pelvis to bladder; narrows at the pelviureteric junction, pelvic brim, and vesicoureteric junction; peristalsis propels urine.
FJ3144.clinicalCondition: Ureteric calculus — stones lodge at the constrictions causing colic and hydronephrosis.
FJ3144.clinicalScenario: A man writhing with loin-to-groin pain and microscopic hematuria has a 5 mm stone at the left vesicoureteric junction on CT.

FJ3147.name: Right kidney
FJ3147.details: Retroperitoneal organ lying slightly lower than the left because of the liver; hilum transmits vein, artery, pelvis; related to liver, duodenum, and hepatic flexure.
FJ3147.clinicalCondition: Renal trauma — blunt injury can lacerate the kidney causing hematuria and hematoma.
FJ3147.clinicalScenario: A footballer kicked in the right loin develops gross hematuria; CT shows a right renal laceration with perinephric hematoma.

FJ3146.name: Right ureter
FJ3146.details: Muscular tube, about 25 cm, crossing the pelvic brim at the common iliac bifurcation and running on psoas; enters the bladder obliquely, preventing reflux.
FJ3146.clinicalCondition: Iatrogenic ureteric injury — endangered at hysterectomy where it passes beneath the uterine artery.
FJ3146.clinicalScenario: After total hysterectomy, a woman leaks urine per vaginam; imaging shows an injured right ureter near the cervix.

FJ3148.name: Urethra
FJ3148.details: Conduit from bladder neck to external meatus; male urethra about 20 cm (prostatic, membranous, spongy parts), female about 4 cm, opening before the vagina.
FJ3148.clinicalCondition: Urethral stricture — scarring narrows the lumen causing weak stream and retention.
FJ3148.clinicalScenario: A man with past gonococcal infection reports a thin stream and straining; urethrogram shows a bulbar stricture.

FJ3149.name: Urinary bladder
FJ3149.details: Pelvic urine reservoir with a smooth trigone and detrusor muscle wall; the neck is guarded by the internal sphincter; parasympathetics (S2–4) drive voiding.
FJ3149.clinicalCondition: Bladder carcinoma — transitional cell tumors classically present with painless hematuria.
FJ3149.clinicalScenario: An elderly smoker with painless visible hematuria has a papillary tumor on the bladder's lateral wall at cystoscopy.

FJ3129.name: Left adrenal gland
FJ3129.details: Crescentic gland capping the left kidney; cortex has glomerulosa, fasciculata, and reticularis zones around a medulla; drains via the left adrenal vein to the renal vein.
FJ3129.clinicalCondition: Conn syndrome — aldosterone-secreting adenoma causes hypertension with hypokalemia.
FJ3129.clinicalScenario: A young hypertensive with low potassium and metabolic alkalosis has a 1.5 cm left adrenal adenoma on CT.

FJ1795.name: Pineal body
FJ1795.details: Small midline gland behind the third ventricle above the superior colliculi; secretes melatonin controlling circadian rhythm; calcifies with age, serving as a radiological landmark.
FJ1795.clinicalCondition: Pineal germinoma — tumor compresses the tectum and aqueduct causing Parinaud syndrome.
FJ1795.clinicalScenario: A teenage boy with failure of upward gaze and headaches has a pineal mass obstructing the cerebral aqueduct on MRI.

FJ1796.name: Pituitary gland
FJ1796.details: Pea-sized gland in the sella turcica, stalk-linked to the hypothalamus; anterior lobe secretes GH, prolactin, ACTH, TSH, LH/FSH; posterior lobe releases ADH and oxytocin.
FJ1796.clinicalCondition: Pituitary adenoma — prolactinoma causes amenorrhea-galactorrhea; large tumors compress the optic chiasm.
FJ1796.clinicalScenario: A woman with amenorrhea and milky nipple discharge has a pituitary macroadenoma pressing on the optic chiasm on MRI.

FJ3130.name: Right adrenal gland
FJ3130.details: Pyramidal gland atop the right kidney, related to the IVC and liver; its short central vein drains directly into the IVC, a surgical hazard.
FJ3130.clinicalCondition: Pheochromocytoma — medullary tumor secretes catecholamines causing paroxysmal hypertension and palpitations.
FJ3130.clinicalScenario: A man with episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and blood pressure of 220/120 has a right adrenal mass on CT.

FJ3132.name: Corpus cavernosum of penis
FJ3132.details: Paired dorsolateral erectile columns enclosed in thick tunica albuginea, filled via the deep penile arteries; proximally each forms a crus attached to the pubic ramus.
FJ3132.clinicalCondition: Peyronie disease — fibrous tunica plaque causes painful penile curvature on erection.
FJ3132.clinicalScenario: A 55-year-old diabetic notices a dorsal plaque and upward curvature during erection; examination finds a firm cavernosal nodule.

FJ3133.name: Corpus spongiosum of penis
FJ3133.details: Ventral erectile column surrounding the spongy urethra, expanding into the bulb proximally and the glans distally; stays less rigid, protecting the urethra during erection.
FJ3133.clinicalCondition: Straddle urethral injury — perineal impact ruptures the spongiosum causing hematoma and bleeding.
FJ3133.clinicalScenario: A cyclist falls astride the crossbar, developing perineal bruising and urethral bleeding; urethrogram confirms a spongiosal injury.

FJ3134.name: Glans penis
FJ3134.details: Expanded distal end of the corpus spongiosum with corona and neck; bears the external urethral meatus at its tip; covered by foreskin; richly sensory.
FJ3134.clinicalCondition: Balanitis — glans inflammation, common with diabetes and poor hygiene.
FJ3134.clinicalScenario: A diabetic man presents with an itchy, red, swollen glans and tight foreskin; findings suggest candidal balanitis.

FJ3135.name: Left deferent duct
FJ3135.details: Thick-walled muscular tube, about 45 cm, carrying sperm from the left epididymal tail through the spermatic cord and inguinal canal to the ejaculatory duct.
FJ3135.clinicalCondition: Vasectomy site — the duct is divided through a small scrotal incision for sterilization.
FJ3135.clinicalScenario: A father of three elects sterilization; under local anesthesia his left vas is isolated through a scrotal incision and divided.

FJ3136.name: Left epididymis
FJ3136.details: Tightly coiled duct on the posterolateral surface of the left testis, with head, body, and tail; sperm mature and are stored here before the vas.
FJ3136.clinicalCondition: Epididymitis — infection produces a painful, swollen epididymis eased by scrotal elevation.
FJ3136.clinicalScenario: A young man with urethral discharge develops gradual scrotal pain and fever; examination shows a tender, swollen left epididymis.

FJ3137.name: Left seminal vesicle
FJ3137.details: Lobulated gland behind the bladder, lateral to the vas ampulla; secretes fructose-rich alkaline fluid forming most of semen volume; its duct helps form the ejaculatory duct.
FJ3137.clinicalCondition: Seminal vesiculitis — infection causes perineal pain and blood-stained ejaculate.
FJ3137.clinicalScenario: A man with prostatitis symptoms and hematospermia has an enlarged, inflamed left seminal vesicle on transrectal ultrasound.

FJ3138.name: Left testis
FJ3138.details: Oval gonad suspended in the left scrotum, usually slightly lower than the right; produces sperm and testosterone; venous drainage reaches the left renal vein.
FJ3138.clinicalCondition: Testicular torsion — twisted cord cuts blood flow; a surgical emergency.
FJ3138.clinicalScenario: A teenage boy wakes with severe left scrotal pain and a high-riding testis; Doppler shows absent blood flow.

FJ3139.name: Prostate
FJ3139.details: Fibromuscular gland below the bladder neck surrounding the prostatic urethra; peripheral zone (cancer-prone) and transition zone; adds secretions to semen; palpable per rectum.
FJ3139.clinicalCondition: Benign prostatic hyperplasia — transition-zone growth obstructs outflow causing nocturia and weak stream.
FJ3139.clinicalScenario: A 70-year-old with nocturia and hesitancy has a smooth, enlarged prostate on rectal examination and mildly raised PSA.

FJ3140.name: Right deferent duct
FJ3140.details: Thick-walled muscular tube, about 45 cm, carrying sperm from the right epididymis through the inguinal canal, crossing above the ureter to the ejaculatory duct.
FJ3140.clinicalCondition: Congenital absence of the vas — linked to CFTR mutations, causing infertility.
FJ3140.clinicalScenario: An infertile man with azoospermia has an impalpable right vas deferens; genetic testing confirms a CFTR mutation.

FJ3141.name: Right epididymis
FJ3141.details: Tightly coiled duct on the posterolateral surface of the right testis; its head receives efferent ductules, sperm mature during transit, and the tail continues as vas.
FJ3141.clinicalCondition: Epididymal cyst — benign fluid-filled swelling, separate from the testis, that transilluminates.
FJ3141.clinicalScenario: A man notices a painless lump above his right testis; examination shows a cystic swelling distinct from the testis that transilluminates.

FJ3143.name: Right seminal vesicle
FJ3143.details: Lobulated secretory gland behind the bladder base; its fructose-rich secretion nourishes sperm; its duct unites with the vas to form the right ejaculatory duct.
FJ3143.clinicalCondition: Ejaculatory duct obstruction — vesicle dilation causes low-volume ejaculate and infertility.
FJ3143.clinicalScenario: An infertile man with low-volume acidic ejaculate has a dilated right seminal vesicle on transrectal ultrasound.

FJ3142.name: Right testis
FJ3142.details: Gonad in the right scrotum, usually slightly higher than the left; produces sperm and testosterone; drains via the pampiniform plexus to the IVC; lymph reaches para-aortic nodes.
FJ3142.clinicalCondition: Testicular cancer — painless solid mass; commonest solid malignancy in young men.
FJ3142.clinicalScenario: A 28-year-old finds a painless hard right testicular lump; ultrasound shows a solid intratesticular mass and tumor markers are sent.

FJ3150.name: Left lobe of thymus
FJ3150.details: Left half of the bilobed lymphoid organ in the anterior superior mediastinum behind the sternum; largest in childhood, involutes after puberty; site of T-cell maturation.
FJ3150.clinicalCondition: Thymoma — anterior mediastinal tumor strongly associated with myasthenia gravis.
FJ3150.clinicalScenario: A woman with fatigable ptosis and diplopia has an anterior mediastinal mass arising in the thymus on CT.

FJ3151.name: Right lobe of thymus
FJ3151.details: Right half of the thymus overlying the pericardium and great vessels; medulla contains Hassall corpuscles; progressively replaced by fat with age.
FJ3151.clinicalCondition: Thymic hyperplasia — enlarged thymus in myasthenia gravis may improve after thymectomy.
FJ3151.clinicalScenario: A young man with myasthenia gravis and an enlarged thymus undergoes thymectomy with symptomatic improvement.

FJ2561.name: Spleen
FJ2561.details: Largest lymphoid organ, sheltered under the left 9th–11th ribs; filters blood, removes worn red cells, mounts immune responses; supplied by the splenic artery, draining to portal vein.
FJ2561.clinicalCondition: Splenic rupture — blunt trauma causes intraperitoneal hemorrhage, sometimes delayed.
FJ2561.clinicalScenario: After falling from a height, a man becomes hypotensive with left shoulder-tip pain; CT shows a splenic laceration with hemoperitoneum.

FJ2812.name: Eyebrow
FJ2812.details: Curved rows of coarse hair along the supraorbital ridges diverting sweat from the eyes; moved by frontalis and corrugator muscles; supraorbital vessels and nerve pass nearby.
FJ2812.clinicalCondition: Madarosis — eyebrow hair loss seen in hypothyroidism and leprosy.
FJ2812.clinicalScenario: A woman with weight gain and cold intolerance has thinning of the outer eyebrows; thyroid tests confirm hypothyroidism.

FJ2813.name: Hair of head
FJ2813.details: Scalp hairs grow from dermal follicles through anagen, catagen, and telogen cycles; roughly 100,000 follicles; each follicle has an arrector pili muscle and sebaceous gland.
FJ2813.clinicalCondition: Alopecia areata — autoimmune patchy hair loss with exclamation-mark hairs.
FJ2813.clinicalScenario: A teenager develops smooth round bald patches; examination shows short exclamation-mark hairs at the patch margins.

FJ2814.name: Lip
FJ2814.details: Muscular folds of orbicularis oris guarding the oral opening; the gland-free vermilion meets skin at the vermilion border; labial arteries come from the facial artery.
FJ2814.clinicalCondition: Herpes labialis — HSV-1 reactivation produces painful cold sores at the vermilion border.
FJ2814.clinicalScenario: After a febrile illness, a student develops grouped vesicles with crusting at the corner of the lip.

FJ2815.name: Pubic hair
FJ2815.details: Coarse secondary sexual hair appearing at puberty under androgen stimulation; its pattern and staging (Tanner) mark pubertal development; escutcheon distribution differs between sexes.
FJ2815.clinicalCondition: Pediculosis pubis — crab louse infestation causes intense pubic itching.
FJ2815.clinicalScenario: A young adult with severe pubic itching finds tiny lice and nits attached to the pubic hair shafts.

FJ2810.name: Skin
FJ2810.details: The body's largest organ: epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis providing barrier protection, sensation, thermoregulation, and vitamin D synthesis; cleavage (Langer) lines guide surgical incisions.
FJ2810.clinicalCondition: Basal cell carcinoma — commonest skin cancer; pearly, ulcerating lesion on sun-exposed skin.
FJ2810.clinicalScenario: An elderly farmer has a slowly enlarging pearly nodule with rolled edges on his nose that ulcerates centrally.
